timeline.finding: Site selection for HOXB9 with PBX1a yields ATGATTTACGAC, a PBX half-site next to a new TTAC HOX site. Paralogues 9 and 10 bind cooperatively with PBX1a through a tryptophan N-terminal to the homeodomain; paralogues 11-13 do not, and in the presence of PBX1a they select a TTAC site with no PBX half-site.
timeline.methods: Binding-site selection, EMSA, mutagenesis
timeline.open: Which partner groups 11-13 use in place of PBX.

timeline.finding: HOXA9, HOXA10, HOXA11, HOXD12 and HOXB13 form DNA-binding complexes with MEIS1 on a composite of a MEIS site (TGACAG) and an Abd-B-like site (TTTTACGAC), and slow MEIS1 dissociation. Meis1 and Hoxa9 are co-activated by retroviral integration in mouse myeloid leukemia.

timeline.finding: The 1.9 A HoxA9-Pbx1-DNA structure shows that the posterior hexapeptide adopts a different conformation from the anterior one, and that extra nonspecific contacts and altered DNA conformation account for the stronger affinity and altered specificity of posterior HOX proteins. N-terminal arm residues are needed for correct sequence recognition without contacting bases.

timeline.finding: SELEX-seq with Exd-Homothorax sorts the eight Drosophila Hox proteins into three colinear classes, and DNA-shape predictions indicate that anterior and posterior Hox proteins prefer sites with different minor-groove topographies.

timeline.finding: Genome-wide, Hoxa9 and Meis1 co-bind hundreds of conserved sites in hematopoietic cells, mostly distal enhancers marked by H3K4me1 and CBP/P300 and often shared with PU.1.

timeline.finding: Methylation-sensitive SELEX of 542 human TFs finds many that prefer CpG-methylated sites, most of them extended homeodomain proteins, through hydrophobic contact with the 5-methyl group. This matters here because the posterior HOX site TTTACGAC contains a CpG, and the methyl-HT-SELEX (M) models in this family come from this type of assay.
timeline.methods: Methyl-HT-SELEX, X-ray crystallography
timeline.open: Whether occupied genomic posterior HOX sites are methylated or unmethylated.

open: Whether posterior HOX proteins bind the CpG in TTTACGAC in its methylated form in vivo is unsettled. Methyl-SELEX shows that many homeodomain proteins prefer methylated CpG, but most genomic CpGs are methylated while active regulatory elements are generally hypomethylated, so which state the occupied sites are in has not been established.

For the group-13 proteins the databases disagree: JASPAR models read CCAATAAAA (TTTTATTGG on the other strand) while HOCOMOCO HT-SELEX and methyl-HT-SELEX models read TTTACGAG. Whether the two reflect different assays, methylation states or binding modes is not settled.

How paralogues 11-13, which do not bind PBX1a, are directed to their targets in vivo is incompletely defined: MEIS1 heterodimers on TGACAG-TTTTACGAC composites were shown in vitro, but whether MEIS complexes account for most of their genomic binding has not been established.

families.name: TALE homeodomain (PBX/MEIS/TGIF)
families.def: TGATTGAT and TGACAG. PBX1-4, MEIS1-3, PKNOX1/2, TGIF1/2, TGIF2LX/2LY; PBX-HOX composite sites.
families.short: TALE homeodomain factors - PBX1-4, MEIS1-3, PKNOX1/2 (PREP1/2) and TGIF1/2 with the TGIF2LX/TGIF2LY retrogenes - carry a homeodomain with three extra residues inserted between helices 1 and 2, the Three Amino acid Loop Extension that names the class. That insertion creates a pocket that docks the hexapeptide of HOX proteins, which is how these factors turn otherwise generic HOX binding into specific composite sites. Two cores dominate the family: MEIS, PKNOX and TGIF read TGACAG, usually as the palindrome TGACAGCTGTCA, while PBX proteins read TGAT and assemble PBX-HOX elements (TGATTNAT) and PBX-MEIS elements (TGATTGACAG). These composite sites are the reason HOX and TALE factors have any DNA-level specificity at all.
families.long:
## The factors

The TALE superclass takes its name from a three-residue insertion between helices 1 and 2 of the homeodomain, recognized in 1997 in the MEIS, PBC, KNOX, Iroquois and TGIF groups [PMID:9336443]. The human members here are the PBC class (PBX1-4), the MEIS class (MEIS1-3 and the more distantly related PKNOX1/PKNOX2, also called PREP1 and PREP2), and the TGIF class (TGIF1, TGIF2 and the X- and Y-linked retrogenes TGIF2LX and TGIF2LY). The Iroquois branch is treated separately in this atlas as HD_IRX. Beyond the homeodomain, PBX proteins carry PBC-A and PBC-B domains, and MEIS/PKNOX proteins carry the homologous MEIS/HR domains, through which the two groups heterodimerize with each other [PMID:9336443,16515781]. PBX and MEIS/PKNOX are broadly expressed; TGIF1 and TGIF2 are widely expressed transcriptional repressors that also serve as Smad corepressors, linking the family to TGF-beta and NODAL signaling [PMID:10835638].

## The motif

The extra three residues do two things. They lengthen the loop so that PBX can accommodate an additional fourth helix and, critically, they form part of a hydrophobic pocket that binds the hexapeptide (YPWM-like) motif found N-terminal to the homeodomain in most HOX proteins [PMID:7729685,10052460]. A bare homeodomain reads only a 4-6 bp TAAT-type core, so HOX proteins on their own are nearly indistinguishable [PMID:22153072]. Docking through the TALE pocket assembles a bipartite element: the HOXB1-PBX1 and HOXA9-PBX1 cocrystals show PBX occupying a TGAT half-site and the HOX partner an adjacent TNAT half-site, giving the composite TGATTNATNN, with the identity of the central bases set by the HOX paralogue [PMID:10052460,12923056,22153072]. MEIS, PKNOX and TGIF read a different core, TGACAG [PMID:9343407], and in vitro they bind it overwhelmingly as the head-to-head palindrome TGACAGCTGTCA - the highest-information models in this family, up to 22 bits in JASPAR and CIS-BP, reported for TGIF1, TGIF2, PKNOX2, MEIS2 and MEIS3 alike [PMID:23332764]. PBX-MEIS heterodimers instead give the asymmetric composite TGATTGACAG, seen in the ChIP-derived HOCOMOCO models for PBX1, PBX2, PBX3 and PKNOX1 [PMID:23602564]. Pooled, the family consensus is TGACAGCt with cohesion 0.74; the TGACAG and TGAT branches are readily distinguished from one another, but within each branch the paralogues are not.

## Where it acts

PBX and MEIS/PKNOX sites are found in developmental enhancers, especially in and around the HOX clusters and in hindbrain and limb enhancers, where the composite elements confer the segment specificity that bare HOX motifs cannot [PMID:16515781]. Genome-wide, PKNOX1/PREP1 and MEIS1 occupy largely independent site sets: PREP1 associates with promoters and housekeeping genes, MEIS1 with promoter-remote developmental regions, and HOX-type sequences co-occur with MEIS1 but not PREP1 binding sites, while PBX1 cooperates with both [PMID:23602564]. Composite element names worth searching for are the PBX-HOX or hexapeptide element and the PBX-MEIS/PREP element. Because TGACAG is only 6 bp and TGAT only 4, matches to the half-sites are extremely common; an exact match to the 12-bp TGACAGCTGTCA palindrome, by contrast, is expected by chance only about 150-200 times in 3.1 Gb (3.1e9/4^12 is about 185).

## Biology and disease

PBX1 loss in mouse disrupts skeletal patterning and chondrocyte differentiation [PMID:11566859], and PBX1 haploinsufficiency in humans causes syndromic congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract [PMID:28270404]. MEIS1 is the top locus in genome-wide association studies of restless legs syndrome [PMID:17637780]. In cancer the family is best known for two mechanisms: the t(1;19) fusion E2A-PBX1 in pre-B acute lymphoblastic leukemia [PMID:1967983,1967982], and the collaboration of MEIS1 with HOXA9, where Hoxa9 transforms primary bone marrow cells specifically with Meis1a rather than Pbx1b [PMID:9649441] - a pairing that underlies MLL-rearranged leukemia. Heterozygous TGIF1 mutations cause holoprosencephaly, linking NODAL signaling to human neural axis determination [PMID:10835638].

## Reading a hit

A TGACAGCTGTCA palindrome is strong evidence for a TALE factor but says nothing about which one: TGIF1, TGIF2, TGIF2LX, TGIF2LY, PKNOX1, PKNOX2, MEIS2 and MEIS3 all have essentially this model. A bare TGACAG or TGAT is too short to act on. The most useful reading is compositional: a TGATTNAT composite points to a PBX-HOX pair, and TGATTGACAG to a PBX-MEIS/PREP pair, and those are the hits worth following up. Note that several PBX and PKNOX models in HOCOMOCO are ChIP-only (P grade), so their TGATTGGC and TGATTGACAG variants may partly reflect the partner's contribution rather than PBX alone; one low-information CIS-BP entry in this family (CTAATTAa) has nearest neighbours in the K50 homeodomain group and is best ignored.
families.caveats: Within each branch the paralogues are interchangeable: the TGACAGCTGTCA palindrome is shared by TGIF1/2, TGIF2LX/2LY, PKNOX1/2 and MEIS1-3, and PBX1-4 share TGAT. Treat a hit as "TALE, MEIS/TGIF type" or "TALE, PBX type", not as a named protein. Half-site matches (TGACAG, TGAT) occur far too often to interpret. Several PBX and PKNOX models are ChIP-derived only (HOCOMOCO P grade) and their composite forms may carry a partner's half-site, which is informative but is not evidence that PBX alone binds it. One low-information CIS-BP member resolves to a K50 homeodomain site.

timeline.finding: The 2.35-A HOXB1-PBX1-DNA structure shows the HOXB1 hexapeptide bound in a pocket formed partly by the three-residue TALE insertion, and a fourth helix in PBX1 that stabilizes the complex.
timeline.methods: X-ray crystallography

timeline.finding: The 1.9-A HOXA9-PBX1-DNA structure shows a posterior HOX hexapeptide in an altered conformation, and N-terminal arm residues that set specificity without contacting bases, explaining the different affinity and specificity of posterior HOX-PBX pairs.
timeline.methods: X-ray crystallography, DNA-binding mutagenesis

timeline.finding: SELEX-seq of all eight Drosophila HOX proteins with the Exd-Hth (PBX-MEIS) dimer reveals latent specificities absent from HOX monomers, falling into three classes that follow collinearity and differ in preferred minor-groove shape.
timeline.methods: SELEX-seq, DNA shape modeling
timeline.open: How fully the classes map onto the human HOX-PBX pairs was not tested.

timeline.finding: HT-SELEX of human factors gives the MEIS, PKNOX and TGIF proteins a head-to-head TGACAGCTGTCA palindrome of 18-22 bits, far more informative than the single TGACAG.
timeline.methods: HT-SELEX
timeline.open: Whether the palindrome is used in vivo was not addressed.

timeline.finding: Genome-wide, PREP1 and MEIS1 occupy largely separate site sets with different sequences, PREP1 at promoters and housekeeping genes and MEIS1 at distal developmental elements with HOX-type sequences, revising the in vitro view that the two are interchangeable.
timeline.methods: ChIP-seq, mouse genetics

open: Whether the TGACAGCTGTCA palindrome is a common in vivo site is unresolved: HT-SELEX gives it for the MEIS, PKNOX and TGIF proteins, but every model in these databases that was built with ChIP data for the same factors gives a single TGACAG or a PBX composite instead.

The ChIP-derived MEIS1 and MEIS2 models (JASPAR MA1639.2 and MA1640.2, HOCOMOCO MEIS1.H14CORE.0.P.B) read TGATTTAT, a PBX-HOX composite, rather than MEIS's own TGACAG, and how much MEIS occupancy in vivo is direct DNA binding versus recruitment through PBX-HOX complexes is not settled.

families.name: T-box
families.def: AGGTGTGA half-site, palindromic in TBXT. TBX1-6, TBX10, TBX15, TBX18-21, TBXT/T, TBR1, EOMES, MGA.
families.short: T-box sites are read by the seventeen human T-box proteins - TBXT (Brachyury), TBX1 to TBX6, TBX10, TBX15, TBX18 to TBX22, TBR1, EOMES and MGA - through a ~180-residue T domain that inserts a helix deep into a widened minor groove, a recognition mode found in no other family. The unit of binding is an eight-base half-site, AGGTGTGA, written TCACACCT in the other orientation. Brachyury binds a palindromic pair of half-sites as a dimer; several paralogues occupy single half-sites or tandem repeats instead. These factors specify the notochord, heart, limbs, pharyngeal apparatus and T-helper-1 lineage, and mutations in individual genes cause distinct human malformation syndromes - but the paralogues are essentially indistinguishable from sequence.
families.long:
## The factors

The human genome carries seventeen T-box genes, conventionally grouped into five subfamilies: TBXT (T/Brachyury); the TBX1 subfamily (TBX1, TBX10, TBX15, TBX18, TBX20, TBX22); the TBX2 subfamily (TBX2, TBX3, TBX4, TBX5); the TBX6 subfamily (TBX6 and MGA); and the TBR1 subfamily (TBR1, EOMES, TBX21) [PMID:16285859,25294936]. All share the T domain, about 180 residues of immunoglobulin-like beta-sandwich. The Brachyury T domain-DNA structure showed an unusual recognition mode: a C-terminal helix buries itself in an enlarged minor groove without bending the DNA, and specificity comes from hydrophobic packing and a main-chain carbonyl contact to a guanine as well as conventional major-groove contacts [PMID:9349824]. Expression is mostly narrow and developmental - TBXT in nascent mesoderm and notochord, TBX5 and TBX20 in heart and forelimb, TBX1 in pharyngeal mesoderm, TBR1 and EOMES in cortical neurons and, for EOMES and TBX21, in lymphocytes. One member is a hybrid: MGA combines a T domain with a bHLH-zipper region that heterodimerises with MAX and binds E-boxes, so MGA reads two unrelated motifs [PMID:10601024]. The family splits into activators (TBX5, TBX20, TBX21, EOMES, TBXT) and repressors (TBX2, TBX3) that use the same element.

## The motif

The core unit is the eight-base half-site AGGTGTGA, equivalently TCACACCT on the opposite strand; both orientations are standard and both appear in these databases, a frequent source of confusion when comparing consensus strings. Binding-site selection with Brachyury first defined it; the protein bound as a monomer in that assay [PMID:8344258]. Geometry is where the paralogues differ, insofar as they differ at all. The Brachyury structure used a 24-bp palindrome and found a dimer whose two monomers contact each other [PMID:9349824], whereas the human TBX3 structure on a palindromic duplex found the two sites recognised independently, with no stabilising monomer-monomer interface [PMID:12005433] - different quaternary arrangements within one fold. The data reflect this: the TBXT and TBX19 models here are inverted palindromes (TCACACCTAGGTGTGA), several models are everted pairs (AGGTGTGAAATTCACA), TBX20 models are direct tandem repeats (AGGTGTGAAGGTGTGA), and the majority are plain single half-sites. Beyond geometry, the paralogues are not separable. Across four databases, the primary models for TBX1, TBX2, TBX3, TBX4, TBX5, TBX6, TBX15, TBX18, TBX20, TBX21, TBR1, EOMES, MGA and TBXT are all AGGTGTGA or AGGTGTGAA - character-for-character identical in many cases - and the family's cohesion of 0.86 across 60 motifs is high given how many distinct proteins are involved. High-throughput SELEX reached the same conclusion: homodimer orientation and spacing preferences often carry more information than the core consensus [PMID:23332764]. Treat spacing and orientation, not base identity, as the only thing that might discriminate members, and treat even that as weak. One provenance note: the CIS-BP TBX10 motif is transferred from the mouse protein at 89% DNA-binding-domain identity rather than measured on the human protein.

## Where it acts

T-box sites are predominantly enhancer elements and are not CpG-island features. Occupancy is highly cell-type restricted because expression is: a TBX5 site in a cardiomyocyte and a TBR1 site in a cortical neuron may be the same sequence. In the heart, T-box sites co-occur with GATA4, NKX2-5, MEF2 and SRF sites, and TBX5-GATA4-NKX2-5 co-binding is the best-studied combinatorial arrangement in cardiac enhancers. In lymphocytes, TBX21 sites sit alongside STAT, RUNX and ETS sites at the IFNG locus. The only named heterodimeric element in these collections is MGA::EVX1, a T-box half-site adjacent to a homeodomain TAAT core, which is a composite of two different proteins rather than a T-box variant.

## Biology and disease

Brachyury is required for posterior mesoderm and notochord; homozygous mutants fail axial development [PMID:8344258]. The paralogues map neatly onto human malformation syndromes: TBX5 mutations cause Holt-Oram syndrome, with septal defects and radial-ray limb malformations [PMID:8988165]; TBX3 mutations cause ulnar-mammary syndrome [PMID:9207801]; loss of Tbx1 in mice reproduces the DiGeorge/22q11.2 deletion phenotype [PMID:11242110]; TBX20 mutations cause diverse cardiac pathology including septation and valve defects and cardiomyopathy [PMID:17668378]; TBX19 (TPIT) mutations cause isolated ACTH deficiency; TBX22 mutations cause cleft palate with ankyloglossia; TBX6 variants contribute to congenital scoliosis. TBX21 (T-bet) was isolated as the T-box factor that drives interferon-gamma and commits naive CD4 T cells to the Th1 lineage, and can redirect polarised Th2 cells [PMID:10761931]. In cancer, germline duplication of the TBXT locus confers strong susceptibility to familial chordoma [PMID:19801981], a notochord-derived tumour in which TBXT is also the near-universal lineage dependency; TBX2 and TBX3 are amplified or overexpressed in breast and other carcinomas, where they repress CDKN2A.

## Reading a hit

Assume a T-box hit names the family and nothing more. Models for fourteen or more paralogues are identical, so which protein is responsible must be inferred from expression, not from sequence. An eight-base half-site is also short - AGGTGTGA occurs on the order of tens of thousands of times per genome - so an isolated half-site match is weak. Matches gain weight when the geometry is present: an inverted pair (AGGTGTGA...TCACACCT), an everted pair, or a tandem repeat within a few base pairs is much more likely to be real than a lone half-site. Check provenance before trusting a specific label: the CIS-BP TBX10 model is inherited from mouse, and the Vierstra archetype names (AC0487:TBX/T, AC0490:TBX/EOMES, AC0491:TBX/MGA) list the factor groups whose motifs clustered together, not distinguishable specificities. Two ChIP-derived entries in this family, TBX20.H14CORE.0.P.C and TBX5.H14CORE.1.P.B, read GTGNTGACAG, contain no recognisable T-box core, and have their nearest neighbours outside the family (label agreement 0.1); they are better read as reflecting co-occupancy with another factor than as T-box recognition, and should not be used for scanning.
families.caveats: This family has the paralogue problem in its most extreme form: the primary models for fourteen or more T-box proteins are AGGTGTGA or AGGTGTGAA, identical in many cases, so a hit identifies T-box and nothing finer - the responsible protein follows from which paralogue is expressed. An eight-base half-site is common by chance, so weight matches by geometry: inverted, everted or tandem pairs are far more credible than a single half-site. Two ChIP-derived models here (TBX20.H14CORE.0.P.C, TBX5.H14CORE.1.P.B) read GTGNTGACAG with no T-box core and neighbours outside the family; treat them as co-occupancy signal. The CIS-BP TBX10 motif is transferred from mouse.

timeline.finding: Selection from random oligonucleotides defines a consensus binding site for the Brachyury (T) protein, built on the half-site AGGTGTGA; under the assay conditions the protein binds as a monomer, through a conserved N-terminal domain of 229 residues.
timeline.methods: Binding-site selection from random oligonucleotides; DNA-binding assays
timeline.open: How the domain recognizes DNA, and whether it binds palindromic sites as a dimer, were unknown.

timeline.finding: The structure of the Xenopus Brachyury T domain on a 24-bp palindrome shows a dimer contacting both grooves, with a C-terminal helix embedded in an enlarged minor groove without bending the DNA - a new mode of DNA recognition.
timeline.methods: X-ray crystallography
timeline.open: Whether the contact between the two bound monomers is a general feature of T-box proteins.

timeline.finding: TBX5 mutations are found to cause Holt-Oram syndrome, the first human disease attributed to a T-box gene, followed the same year by TBX3 in ulnar-mammary syndrome.
timeline.methods: Human linkage and mutation analysis

timeline.finding: MGA is identified as a dual-specificity factor that combines a T domain, which binds the Brachyury site, with a bHLHZip domain that binds CACGTG only as a heterodimer with MAX.
timeline.methods: Identification as a MAX-interacting protein; DNA-binding and reporter assays

timeline.finding: The human TBX3 T domain recognizes the two sites of a palindromic duplex independently, without the monomer-monomer interaction seen for Brachyury, so the Brachyury dimer is not a general model for how T-box proteins occupy paired sites.
timeline.methods: X-ray crystallography

timeline.finding: Duplications of a 6q27 region containing TBXT are found in four multiplex chordoma families, identifying TBXT dosage as a major susceptibility factor for this notochord-derived cancer.
timeline.methods: High-resolution array comparative genomic hybridization in families

timeline.finding: HT-SELEX of many T-box proteins recovers the same AGGTGTGA core for nearly all of them, with paralogues differing mainly in the orientation and spacing of paired half-sites.
timeline.methods: HT-SELEX
timeline.open: Whether those geometric preferences discriminate between paralogues at genomic sites.

open: Whether half-site orientation and spacing let T-box paralogues choose different genomic sites is unsettled: HT-SELEX recovers inverted, everted and tandem pairs for different members, but the Brachyury and TBX3 structures disagree on whether two bound monomers interact, and in vivo evidence that geometry selects the paralogue is limited.

What the ChIP-derived GTGNTGACAG models labelled TBX20 and TBX5 represent is unresolved: they contain no T-box core and their nearest neighbours lie outside the family, which points to a co-bound partner - the TGACAG half resembles the TALE homeodomain (MEIS/TGIF) site - but no in vitro evidence identifies which one.

families.name: Other BTB-ZF (ZBTB)
families.def: BTB-domain zinc fingers without a dedicated entry: ZBTB1-6, ZBTB11-49 and relatives. BCL6/BCL6B, HIC1/HIC2, ZBTB17, ZBTB18, ZBTB33, ZBTB7A/B/C and ZBTB48 are covered separately.
families.short: BTB-ZF proteins, also called POZ-ZF, pair an N-terminal BTB/POZ domain, a dimerization module, with a short C2H2 zinc-finger array. This entry collects the 28 less-studied members: ZBTB1 to ZBTB6, ZBTB8A and ZBTB8B, ZBTB11, 12, 14, 16, 20, 22, 24, 26, 32, 37, 40 to 45, 47 and 49, plus myoneurin (MYNN) and ZNF131. The distinctive BTB-ZFs with well-mapped sites, among them BCL6, HIC1/2, ZBTB7A/B, MIZ1, ZBTB18, Kaiso and TZAP, are split into their own entries. It is not a single motif: 60 matrices, cohesion 0.42, median length 10 bp. Several members do read inverted-repeat sites, as obligate dimerization predicts, but the half-sites differ from protein to protein.
families.long:
## The factors

The BTB domain (broad-complex, tramtrack, bric-a-brac), also called POZ (poxvirus and zinc finger), is a protein-protein interaction module with a highly conserved core fold. It was first visualized in the PLZF/ZBTB16 crystal structure (Ahmad et al. 1998) [PMID:9770450], and the PLZF BTB homodimer remains the reference model; surveys of 17 eukaryotic genomes place BTB-ZF among several BTB families and show a large vertebrate expansion (Stogios et al. 2005) [PMID:16207353]. BTB-ZF factors are predominantly transcriptional repressors, with prominent roles in haematopoietic development and malignancy (Kelly and Daniel 2006; de Greef et al. 2011) [PMID:16996269,21596365]. Their C2H2 arrays are short compared with KRAB zinc fingers, typically two to six fingers, which limits how much sequence one monomer can read and is part of why dimerization matters. Twenty-eight gene symbols appear here. Members with distinctive, better-mapped sites are described elsewhere in this atlas: BCL6 and BCL6B, HIC1 and HIC2, ZBTB7A and ZBTB7B, ZBTB17/MIZ1, ZBTB18, ZBTB33/Kaiso, PATZ1 (grouped with MAZ) and ZBTB48/TZAP (grouped with the telobox factors). What remains is deliberately the residue: a few members with good data, a majority with almost none.

## The motif

There is no family consensus; cohesion is 0.42. Median consensus length is 10 bp and median information content 12.7 bits, short and weak beside the KRAB zinc-finger entries; only 2 matrices reach 20 bp and only 7 exceed 20 bits. The clearest structural signature is the dyad an obligate BTB homodimer predicts. ZBTB32 (also TZFP, FAZF) gives TGTACAGTAATACTGTACA at 28.9 bits, an inverted repeat of TGTACAGTA; its half-site ACTGTA is also the entire HOCOMOCO model for ZBTB16/PLZF at 9.4 bits, so at half-site resolution those two are indistinguishable. ZBTB22 gives TCACTATTATAGTGA, a near-perfect inverted repeat of TCACTAT, reproduced independently in CIS-BP and the Vierstra archetype AC0356. ZBTB43 gives GTGCCATANNNNCAGCAC, two half-sites separated by four unconstrained positions. ZBTB20 (CTATACGTT) and ZBTB45 (CACCTATAG, or CTATAGGTG on the other strand) both centre on CTATA and score about 0.96 against each other, so they are not separable. ZBTB14 (ZF5/ZFP161) is GC-rich and appears variously as TGCGCGTGCACGTG, GCGCGTGCGCGCG and CCGCGCAC; its CIS-BP model's nearest neighbour is an E2F matrix at 0.96 and its JASPAR model matches a non-family motif at 1.00, so ZBTB14 hits cannot be separated from the general GC-box and E2F pool. MYNN gives GACTTTTATTTT identically in CIS-BP, HOCOMOCO and the archetype AC0431, one of the few internally consistent models here. ZBTB40 has the best-supported model in the family: AAMAAAACTTTATTGA, 22.7 bits, grade A with ChIP-seq, HT-SELEX and GHT-SELEX evidence [PMID:37971293]. Two members contradict themselves across databases: ZBTB26 appears as TTCTGGA, as a CG repeat, and as TTYAAAANTTTTCTAGAA; ZBTB49 as TTTCGCCTGGCACGTCA and as GTGACCAGCCAGGCMAAAATGG. Neither should be treated as settled.

## Where it acts

Promoters and promoter-proximal regions, mostly; short, moderately informative motifs are typical of factors recruited into promoter complexes rather than of long-range specificity. Genome-wide maps exist for few members. ZBTB11 is found at nuclear respiratory factor 2 (NRF-2/GABP) target promoters, where it facilitates GABP recruitment to genes for respiratory complex I and the mitoribosome (Wilson et al. 2020) [PMID:33122634]. ZBTB24 is required for DNA methylation of juxtacentromeric repeat sequences (de Greef et al. 2011) [PMID:21596365]. ZBTB16/PLZF occupies an extensive transcription-factor poising network in juvenile spermatogonial stem cells (Yi et al. 2025) [PMID:40033150]. For most other members the HOCOMOCO model is the only positional information available.

## Biology and disease

Human phenotypes are established for three members. ZBTB24 mutations cause immunodeficiency, centromeric instability and facial anomalies syndrome type 2, which shares hypomethylation of juxtacentromeric repeats with DNMT3B-mutant ICF1 and involves B cell development (de Greef et al. 2011) [PMID:21596365]. ZBTB20 mutations cause Primrose syndrome (Cordeddu et al. 2014) [PMID:25017102], and Zbtb20 haploinsufficiency reproduces the intellectual disability and autism-like behaviour in mice (Hindermann et al. 2026) [PMID:41729076]. ZBTB11 mutations cause hereditary intellectual disability; the pathogenic substitutions destabilize the protein, lowering its dosage and producing a severe respiratory complex I assembly defect, impaired respiration and cell death (Wilson et al. 2020) [PMID:33122634]. Beyond disease genetics, ZBTB16/PLZF controls juvenile spermatogonial stem cell development (Yi et al. 2025) [PMID:40033150], and myoneurin regulates BMP signalling by competing with PPM1A for SMAD binding (Yang et al. 2022) [PMID:35712083] — several of these proteins act mainly through protein-protein rather than protein-DNA interactions.

## Reading a hit

Because the BTB domain dimerizes, look for the dyad: an inverted repeat of the half-site, with the spacing of the reference matrix. A half-site alone is weak evidence, and half-sites are shared between members, ACTGTA between ZBTB32 and PLZF and CTATA between ZBTB20 and ZBTB45. At a median of 10 bp and 12.7 bits, most of these motifs occur hundreds of thousands of times in the human genome, so a single match without conservation, accessibility or ChIP support supports nothing. Eleven of 60 matrices have their nearest neighbour in another family: three resemble HSF motifs (two ZBTB26 models and the archetype AC0687), two the ZBTB7 motif (ZBTB11 and ZBTB2), two HAND/TWIST (ZBTB42 and AC0074), and one each E2F (ZBTB14), Kaiso/ZBTB33 (AC0312), ZBTB18 (ZBTB42) and HIC (ZBTB43). The ZBTB11 case is instructive: its JASPAR motif CACTTCCGG contains CCGGAAG, the GABP/ETS core, and ZBTB11 is known to recruit GABP to promoters, so the most parsimonious reading is that this matrix records GABP's specificity captured through co-binding rather than ZBTB11's own [PMID:33122634]. Finally, the CIS-BP models for ZBTB1 (CCCGCA) and ZBTB3 (CACTGC) are transferred from mouse orthologues; the domains are 100% identical, so the transfer is sound, but at 6.5 to 6.8 bits they are too weak to scan with.
families.caveats: This is a domain family with several unrelated motifs, not one motif: 28 proteins, 60 matrices, cohesion 0.42, no consensus. The matrices are short (median 10 bp, 12.7 bits), so most match hundreds of thousands of genomic positions and a lone hit means little. Because BTB is a dimerization domain, require the dyad rather than a half-site, and note that half-sites are shared: ACTGTA between ZBTB32 and PLZF, CTATA between ZBTB20 and ZBTB45. Eleven matrices most closely resemble another family's motif, and ZBTB11's is most plausibly GABP's, captured through co-binding. The ZBTB26 and ZBTB49 models contradict each other across databases, and the mouse-derived ZBTB1 and ZBTB3 models carry under 7 bits.

timeline.finding: The 1.9 Angstrom crystal structure of the PLZF/ZBTB16 BTB domain showed a tightly intertwined dimer burying about a quarter of each monomer's surface, the signature of an obligate homodimer, and led to the prediction that full-length BTB-ZF proteins are branched factors carrying two DNA-binding regions.
timeline.methods: X-ray crystallography
timeline.open: Whether two tethered finger arrays actually read two half-sites, and at what spacing, was a prediction rather than an observation.

timeline.finding: A survey of BTB proteins across 17 eukaryotic genomes separated BTB-ZF from the other BTB families, documented a large vertebrate expansion of the group, and showed that the fold is structurally conserved despite widely divergent sequence and several different modes of self-association.
timeline.methods: comparative sequence and structure analysis

timeline.finding: Mutations in ZBTB24 were identified as the cause of ICF syndrome type 2, which shares hypomethylation of juxtacentromeric repeats with DNMT3B-mutant ICF1, giving the first human disease gene and the first chromatin phenotype among the less-studied BTB-ZF members.
timeline.methods: homozygosity mapping, whole-exome and Sanger sequencing in consanguineous families
timeline.open: How a BTB-ZF repressor directs DNA methylation at juxtacentromeric repeats was not established.

timeline.finding: Missense mutations in ZBTB20 were shown to underlie Primrose syndrome, linking the gene to tall stature, macrocephaly, intellectual disability and metabolic features and connecting it to the overlapping 3q13.31 microdeletion syndrome.
timeline.methods: human genetics

timeline.finding: Direct profiling of 131 human C2H2 proteins provided motif models for 78 that had none, including many of the BTB-ZF members here, and found that each protein recruits a largely distinct set of co-activators and co-repressors, so the shared BTB domain does not imply a shared mechanism.
timeline.methods: ChIP-seq, affinity purification-mass spectrometry, knockdown expression profiling
timeline.open: Most of the resulting models were short and derived from ChIP, leaving the direct-versus-indirect question open for each.

timeline.finding: Zbtb11 was shown to facilitate recruitment of NRF-2/GABP to promoters of respiratory complex I and mitoribosome genes, with pathogenic human substitutions destabilizing the protein and causing a complex I assembly defect; this gives a concrete reason to read the ETS-containing ZBTB11 matrix as GABP's specificity captured through co-binding.
timeline.methods: functional genomics, ChIP, biochemistry, modelling of patient mutations

timeline.finding: A Zbtb20-haploinsufficient mouse was characterized as a construct-valid model of Primrose syndrome, with reduced sociability, repetitive behaviour, impaired cognitive flexibility and increased brain volume, and recombinant human erythropoietin was reported to improve the behavioural phenotype.
timeline.methods: behavioural phenotyping, magnetic resonance imaging, treatment trial in mice

open: Whether the ZBTB11 matrix records ZBTB11's own specificity or GABP's is unresolved: the motif contains the CCGGAAG ETS core and ZBTB11 is known to recruit GABP to the same promoters, but no in vitro binding data for ZBTB11 have been published to settle it.

The ZBTB26 and ZBTB49 models contradict each other across databases, ZBTB26 appearing as TTCTGGA, as a CG repeat and as a near-palindromic TTYAAAANTTTTCTAGAA, and no independent assay has been published for either protein.

It is unknown whether proteins that share a half-site, ACTGTA between ZBTB32 and ZBTB16/PLZF and CTATA between ZBTB20 and ZBTB45, occupy the same genomic sites in vivo or are separated by dyad spacing, dimer partner or expression pattern.

Whether ZBTB14 has a specificity distinct from the general GC-box and E2F pool is open, since its models vary between databases and its nearest neighbours are an E2F matrix at 0.96 and a non-family motif at 1.00.

families.name: NKX
families.def: TAAGTG / CACTTAA. NKX1-1/1-2, NKX2-1 to 2-8, NKX3-1/3-2, NKX6-1 to 6-3, plus NKX-like archetypes.
families.short: NKX proteins are homeodomain transcription factors related to Drosophila tinman and vnd, and they are the main exception to the rule that homeodomains read a TAAT core. NKX2-1 (TTF-1), NKX2-2 to NKX2-8, NKX3-1 and NKX3-2 prefer TAAGTG (read as CACTTA on the other strand), a specificity recognized as unusual when TTF-1 was first cloned. The family collects 51 motifs for 16 genes, including NKX1-1/1-2, NKX6-1 to NKX6-3 and NANOG. It is the least cohesive homeodomain family in this atlas because the NKX6 proteins in fact read a conventional TAAT core rather than TAAGTG, so the label covers two different sites.
families.long:
## The factors

NKX genes are the vertebrate NK-class homeobox genes, orthologues of Drosophila tinman (heart) and vnd/NK-2 (ventral nervous system). Sixteen symbols and 51 motifs are grouped here: NKX1-1 and NKX1-2; NKX2-1 (also called TTF-1 or TITF1), NKX2-2, NKX2-3, NKX2-4, NKX2-5, NKX2-6 and NKX2-8; NKX3-1 and NKX3-2; NKX6-1, NKX6-2 and NKX6-3; plus NANOG and unassigned NKX archetypes. Each is restricted to a small number of lineages: NKX2-1 to thyroid and lung, NKX2-5 to heart, NKX2-2 and NKX6-1 to pancreatic endocrine progenitors and ventral neural tube, NKX3-1 to prostate epithelium, NKX3-2 (BAPX1) to axial skeleton, NANOG to pluripotent cells. All bind DNA as monomeric homeodomains; none of them needs a dedicated DNA-binding partner, although NKX2-5 and GATA4 co-activate shared targets.

## The motif

The consensus is TAAGTG. Randomized-site selection with the NKX2-5 homeodomain gave high-affinity sites of the form 5'-TNNAGTG-3' and only intermediate or weak binding to 5'-C(A/T)TTAATTN-3', the conventional TAAT-type site, which is the cleanest demonstration that NKX proteins prefer a different core [PMID:7797561]. The TTF-1/NKX2-1 site is often described by a CAAG core (CAAGTG) [PMID:8890172]. That is not TAAGTG read on the other strand, whose reverse complement is CACTTA, but a one-base variant at the first core position, where NK-2 homeodomains differ among themselves according to N-terminal-arm residues 6-8 [PMID:8890172,18585360].

The structural reason is not position 50. Every NKX homeodomain has glutamine there, the residue that in other families specifies TAATTA [PMID:8692913]; the NMR structure of the vnd/NK-2 homeodomain on DNA confirms Gln50 together with the canonical Asn51 hydrogen bond and minor-groove contacts from Lys3 and Arg5 [PMID:10356327]. What differs is elsewhere in the recognition helix, notably position 54, which is tyrosine in NKX2-1, NKX2-5 and NKX3-1 but methionine in Antp-type and alanine in En-type TAATTA readers. In the fly NK-2 specificity group, Tyr54 specifies the G of TAAG through the complementary C [PMID:18585360], and mutational comparison of the TTF-1, Antennapedia and Engrailed homeodomains ties residue 54 to the base at the 3' end of the core [PMID:8890172]. This is why the position-50 rule, which explains TAATTA versus TAATCC, does not explain TAAGTG.

The family is internally split, and this is its most important practical feature. NKX2-x and NKX3-x models are TAAGTG: NKX3-2 (the medoid, HOCOMOCO NKX32.H14CORE.0.PSM.A) TAAGTG, NKX3-1 TTAAGTGG, NKX2-3 TTAAGTG, NKX2-8 TTAAGTG, NKX2-1 and NKX2-2 TTGAGTG. The NKX6 models are not: NKX6-1 and NKX6-2 give TTAATTA and NKX6-3 gives ATTAATGAC, ordinary TAAT-core sites. NANOG models are TAATGG-like [PMID:18177668]. Family cohesion is accordingly 0.74, the lowest of the homeodomain families here, and NKX6-2's CIS-BP model is flagged as resembling anterior HOX - correctly, since TAATTA is what it is. Within each subgroup the paralogues are indistinguishable: no matrix separates NKX2-1 from NKX2-4, or NKX3-1 from NKX3-2. Several models here are dimeric or extended, such as NKX3-2 TTAAGTGGCACTTAA (two half-sites in inverted orientation) and NKX6-1 ATTAATGGGHWTTTAAT.

## Where it acts

Sites sit in lineage-specific enhancers and in promoters of tissue-defining genes: TTF-1 was purified on thyroid-specific gene promoters [PMID:1976511], NKX2-5 acts on cardiac structural gene enhancers, and NKX6-1 acts downstream of NKX2-2 in beta-cell formation [PMID:11076772]. TAAGTG is a common hexamer, expected on the order of two million times in 3.1 Gb at human base composition, so genome-wide match counts are large and uninformative; accessibility and expression do the work. NKX2-5 sites frequently co-occur with GATA and TBX motifs in cardiac enhancers, NKX6-1 with PDX1 and other pancreatic homeodomain sites.

## Biology and disease

Heterozygous NKX2-5 mutations cause atrial septal defect with progressive atrioventricular conduction block [PMID:9651244], and Nkx2-5 null mouse embryos arrest at the heart-tube stage [PMID:7628699]. NKX2-1 haploinsufficiency causes brain-lung-thyroid syndrome (choreoathetosis, congenital hypothyroidism, pulmonary disease) [PMID:11854319], while the NKX2-1 locus at 14q13 is focally amplified in lung adenocarcinoma [PMID:17982442]. NKX3-1 is a prostate tumor suppressor whose expression is lost early in prostate carcinogenesis [PMID:14648854]. NKX6-1 is required for pancreatic beta-cell formation [PMID:11076772], NKX3-2 for axial skeletal development, and NANOG for maintenance of pluripotency in the epiblast and in embryonic stem cells.

## Reading a hit

A TAAGTG match indicates an NKX2/NKX3-type site and no particular gene. A TAAT-type match labelled NKX6 is a generic homeodomain site and should be read as such. This family also carries the clearest indirect-binding problems in the homeodomain set: 6 of its 17 HOCOMOCO models are ChIP-only, and two of them are flagged as matching other families entirely. The NANOG ChIP-derived model reads CCTTTGTNATGCAAA - the octamer ATGCAAAT, which is the POU/OCT4 motif, exactly what indirect capture of a co-occupied partner looks like for a factor that shares enhancers with OCT4 and SOX2 [PMID:25070602]. An NKX2-5 ChIP model reads GTGHTGACAG and matches the TBX family. Six CIS-BP entries in this family are transferred from mouse orthologues, one of them (NKX2-6) inferred at 93% DNA-binding-domain identity rather than measured. Prefer the HT-SELEX-derived models when testing whether a sequence is an NKX site.
families.caveats: Treat a TAAGTG hit as "an NKX2/NKX3-type site", not as a named factor; paralogues within each subgroup are indistinguishable. The family label spans two different motifs - NKX2 and NKX3 proteins read TAAGTG, but NKX6-1/6-2/6-3 read an ordinary TAAT core - which is why cohesion is only 0.74 and why one NKX6-2 model is flagged as HOX-like. ChIP-only evidence is a real risk here: 6 of 17 HOCOMOCO models are ChIP-derived, and two are flagged as belonging elsewhere, including a NANOG model that is actually the OCT4 octamer. Six CIS-BP motifs are inherited from mouse proteins. Expect roughly two million genome-wide matches, so require accessibility and expression.

timeline.finding: TTF-1 (NKX2-1), a thyroid nuclear factor that binds thyroid-specific promoters, is cloned. Its DNA-binding domain is a homeodomain related to Drosophila NK-2, with a DNA-binding specificity unlike that of other known homeodomains.
timeline.methods: cDNA cloning, DNA-binding assays
timeline.open: The site was known from a few thyroid promoters; whether it was general to NK proteins was not.

timeline.finding: Random-oligonucleotide selection with the NKX2-5 homeodomain gives high-affinity TNNAGTG sites and only intermediate or weak binding to TAAT-type sites, so the NK core differs from the TAATTA consensus.
timeline.methods: Binding-site selection from random oligonucleotides, reporter assays

timeline.finding: Heterozygous NKX2-5 mutations cause congenital heart disease with atrioventricular conduction abnormalities; two of the three mutations are predicted to impair DNA binding.
timeline.methods: Linkage mapping, mutation screening

timeline.finding: The NMR structure of the vnd/NK-2 homeodomain on its 16-bp consensus site confirms the canonical contacts, Asn51 to the second adenine and Lys3 and Arg5 in the minor groove, with Gln50 at the interface. The homeodomain sits on DNA with small but significant differences in orientation from other homeodomains.
timeline.methods: NMR spectroscopy

timeline.finding: Two genome-scale surveys, protein-binding microarrays for 168 mouse homeodomains (at least 65 distinct activities) and bacterial one-hybrid selection for all 84 Drosophila homeodomains (11 specificity groups), resolve NK-type TAAGTG binding as a distinct activity; the fly survey ties it to recognition-helix positions beyond 50, including Tyr54.
timeline.methods: Protein-binding microarrays, bacterial one-hybrid selection

timeline.finding: The crystal structure of the NANOG homeodomain, with binding assays, shows a preference for TAAT(G/T)(G/T) and places NANOG as a distant Q50-type homeodomain, not a TAAGTG reader.
timeline.methods: X-ray crystallography, EMSA with mutant sites and proteins

timeline.finding: Across hundreds of ChIP-seq datasets, peaks carrying motifs of factors other than the one immunoprecipitated make up as much as 45% of a dataset. This is the background for the NANOG and NKX2-5 ChIP models here that read POU and TBX-type sequences.
timeline.methods: Meta-analysis of ChIP-seq datasets

open: NANOG does not read the NK site: its homeodomain behaves as a distant Q50 type and its in vitro models are TAATGG-like. Whether it belongs with the NK family, as its gene classification suggests, or with TAAT-core homeodomains, as its specificity suggests, is a real split in this family's data (cohesion 0.74).

How much NKX2-5 occupancy in the heart depends on its own TAAGTG site, and how much on co-bound partners, is unsettled: the HT-SELEX-supported model is clean TAAGTG, while one ChIP-only NKX2-5 model reads a TBX-type sequence (GTGHTGACAG).

Whether the inverted-repeat models (NKX3-2 TTAAGTGGCACTTAA, NKX6-1 ATTAATGGGHWTTTAAT) reflect cooperative dimer binding used in vivo, or two independent monomer sites recovered together in selection, has not been established.

families.name: PAX paired domain
families.def: Paired-domain site GTCACGC(A/T)TGA; PAX1/9, PAX2/5/8, PAX3/7, PAX4/6 (with and without the homeodomain half-site).
families.short: The paired domain is a bipartite DNA-binding domain, unique to the nine human PAX proteins, that reads an unusually long site: a GTCACGC(A/T)TGA core set inside a footprint of roughly 15 to 20 base pairs. Two helix-turn-helix subdomains, PAI and RED, grip adjacent stretches of the double helix, so the recognition surface is far larger than that of a single homeodomain. PAX3, PAX4, PAX6 and PAX7 additionally carry a complete homeodomain that contributes an independent TAAT half site, making their composite elements longer still. PAX sites are therefore among the most information-rich transcription factor motifs in the genome. These factors specify the eye, thyroid, kidney, pancreatic beta cells, B lymphocytes and muscle progenitors, and paired-domain mutations cause aniridia, Waardenburg syndrome and renal-coloboma syndrome.
families.long:
## The factors

Nine human genes, PAX1 to PAX9, each encode a paired domain of about 128 residues. They fall into four
subgroups by what else they contain: PAX1 and PAX9 (paired domain plus octapeptide), PAX2, PAX5 and PAX8
(plus octapeptide and a vestigial partial homeodomain), PAX3 and PAX7 (plus octapeptide and a complete
homeodomain), and PAX4 and PAX6 (paired domain plus complete homeodomain). The paired domain binds DNA as
a monomer; no dimerisation is required [PMID:7867071]. It is built from two independently folding helix-turn-helix units,
the N-terminal PAI subdomain and the C-terminal RED subdomain [PMID:8406007], joined by a linker that tracks the minor
groove. Expression is tissue-restricted rather than ubiquitous: PAX5 in B lymphocytes, PAX8 in thyroid and
kidney, PAX6 in eye, pancreas and central nervous system, PAX3 and PAX7 in neural crest and muscle
satellite cells, PAX4 in pancreatic beta cells.

## The motif

The core paired-domain site is GTCACGC(A/T)TGA, about 11 bp, sitting inside a 15 to 20 bp contacted
region. Crystal structures of a *Drosophila* Prd paired domain at 2.5 A and of the human PAX6 paired
domain at higher resolution [PMID:7867071,10346815] showed how the information is distributed: the PAI helix 3 inserts into the
major groove and reads the 5' GTCAC half, the beta-hairpin and N-terminal beta-turn make extensive
minor-groove contacts, and the RED subdomain reaches the 3' end of the site [PMID:10346815]. Most of the affinity and most
of the specificity lie in the 5' GTCACGC; RED contributes additional 3' contacts and is dispensable at
some sites [PMID:7867071,8787739]. Alternative splicing of PAX6 exon 5a inserts 14 residues into PAI, inactivates it, and
switches the protein to a RED-dominated specificity, so one gene encodes two different sequence
preferences [PMID:7958875]. The homeodomain of PAX3, PAX4, PAX6 and PAX7 adds a separate TAAT half site and dimerises
cooperatively on palindromic P3-type elements, TAAT-N2/3-ATTA [PMID:7901121]. All three shapes appear in the assembled
data: paired-domain models such as CGTCACGCATGACTGC for PAX9, pure homeodomain palindromes such as
TAATCGATTA for PAX3 and PAX7, and a composite CGTCACGCTWATTA that fuses both in 14 bp. Paralogues within
a subgroup are not separable: PAX1 and PAX9, and PAX2, PAX5 and PAX8, have motifs matching each other at
0.96 or better.

## Where it acts

PAX proteins work at both promoters and distal enhancers, and their long sites make named composite
elements unusually tractable. The best characterised is the B-cell-specific mb-1 (CD79A) promoter, where
PAX5 bound to its paired-domain site recruits ETS-family proteins into a ternary complex on an adjacent
GGAA core; the PAX5 half of that element is degenerate on its own and depends on the partner [PMID:8804314]. PAX6 acts at
lens crystallin promoters and at pancreatic and retinal enhancers. In alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma the
PAX3-FOXO1 fusion occupies myogenic enhancers through the retained paired domain plus homeodomain [PMID:8098985].
Because the full site is long, genome-wide occurrence by chance is low relative to 6 to 8 bp motifs, and
occupancy is strongly cell-type restricted; the same sequence is largely unoccupied in tissues that do not
express the relevant PAX gene.

## Biology and disease

Heterozygous PAX6 loss causes aniridia and a spectrum of anterior-segment eye malformations, and the
mouse *Small eye* mutant is the orthologous allele [PMID:1684738]. PAX3 mutations cause Waardenburg syndrome types 1 and
3 [PMID:1347148]; PAX2 mutations cause renal-coloboma syndrome, optic nerve colobomas with renal hypoplasia and
vesicoureteral reflux [PMID:7795640]; PAX8 paired-domain mutations that reduce DNA binding cause congenital
hypothyroidism from thyroid dysgenesis [PMID:9590296]. Mice lacking Pax5 arrest B-cell development at the pro-B stage and show posterior
midbrain patterning defects [PMID:8001127]. In cancer, t(2;13) and t(1;13) translocations fuse PAX3 or PAX7 to FOXO1 in
alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma [PMID:8098985]; PAX5 is recurrently altered in B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukaemia [PMID:17344859]; PAX8 is
used diagnostically in thyroid, renal and ovarian tumours.

## Reading a hit

A full GTCACGC(A/T)TGA match is one of the more trustworthy motif hits available, because 11 informative
positions are rare by chance. It tells you the subgroup, not the protein: nothing in the sequence
separates PAX2 from PAX5 or PAX8. Short matches are much weaker evidence. The homeodomain-only models are
generic paired-like homeodomain sites: the JASPAR PAX4 entry MA0068.2 is CTAATTAG and its nearest
neighbours across all four databases are PRD-like homeobox motifs, not PAX motifs, and a CIS-BP PAX3 entry
is a bare TAATTG whose neighbours are Q50 homeodomain motifs. Several Vierstra footprint archetypes
labelled PAX carry no paired-domain information at all (GTGCACAC, TCCCCGGGC, CCACCCS, GTTT); these name
the factor group whose footprints clustered, and the cluster can be driven by co-occurring factors [PMID:32728250]. This
is the least cohesive family in the set, at 0.57.
families.caveats: Trust long paired-domain matches; distrust short ones. The family pools three different motif shapes, paired domain, homeodomain half site, and composite, and only the first is PAX-diagnostic. Within the PAX1/PAX9 and PAX2/PAX5/PAX8 subgroups the motifs are interchangeable, so a hit names a subgroup at best. Homeodomain-only models labelled PAX4 or PAX3 are indistinguishable from PRD-like and Q50 homeodomain sites and are flagged in the underlying data as probably belonging elsewhere. Several PAX-labelled footprint archetypes contain no recognisable paired-domain sequence and should not be used to call PAX occupancy. Occupancy is strongly restricted to tissues that express the gene.

timeline.finding: Positional cloning of the aniridia region yields a gene encoding both a paired domain and a homeodomain, PAX6, expressed in exactly the tissues affected in the disease, which ties this domain family to human developmental disease.
timeline.methods: deletion mapping and cDNA cloning in patients
timeline.open: The sequence the paired domain recognizes was not yet defined.

timeline.finding: Alignment of BSAP (PAX5) binding sites, methylation interference and domain swaps define the paired-domain site as two half sites read by two subregions of the domain, and show that natural sites carry compensatory mismatches in one half, which explains the apparently degenerate recognition of Pax proteins.
timeline.methods: binding site selection, methylation interference, in vitro mutagenesis and domain swaps
timeline.open: The subdomain model was inferred from binding data; there was no structure.

timeline.finding: Paired-class homeodomains are shown to bind palindromic sites as cooperative dimers, with affinity raised up to 300-fold, and with residue 9 of the recognition helix setting both the preferred half-site spacing and the central base pairs, which gives PAX3, PAX4, PAX6 and PAX7 a second, homeodomain-based site type.
timeline.methods: in vitro binding and site selection with isolated homeodomains

timeline.finding: The PAX6 exon 5a splice variant, which inserts 14 residues into the PAI subdomain, is shown to bind DNA exclusively through the C-terminal subdomain, so alternative splicing toggles one gene between two different sequence preferences.
timeline.methods: binding assays with splice isoforms and truncated paired domains
timeline.open: Which isoform drives which target genes in vivo was not resolved.

timeline.finding: The crystal structure of the Drosophila Prd paired domain on a 15-bp site at 2.5 A shows two structurally independent helix-turn-helix subdomains, extensive minor-groove contacts from a beta-turn, and a C-terminal subdomain that does not contact the optimized site; all known developmental missense mutations in mammalian paired boxes map to the N-terminal subdomain, most at the protein-DNA interface.
timeline.methods: X-ray crystallography
timeline.open: Left open whether the C-terminal subdomain contacts DNA at other sites or in other Pax proteins.

timeline.finding: Pax proteins are shown to use different combinations of their three helix-turn-helix units at different targets: Drosophila Paired can bind through the PAI subdomain alone, through a homeodomain dimer, or through cooperation between the two, which is why one family produces several distinct motif shapes.
timeline.methods: comparative in vitro binding with domain mutants and in vivo rescue

timeline.finding: The structure of the human PAX6 paired domain on a 26-bp site shows that the linker makes minor-groove contacts over 8 bp and that the C-terminal subdomain makes base-specific major-groove contacts with a docking arrangement nearly symmetric to the N-terminal one, revising the earlier picture in which the C-terminal subdomain was dispensable.
timeline.methods: X-ray crystallography
timeline.open: The relative weight of the two subdomains still varies with the site, so no single consensus length covers the family.

timeline.finding: Genome-scale clustering of DNase footprints into sequence archetypes groups PAX-labeled footprints into clusters named after the factor group rather than a protein, and several PAX archetypes carry no recognizable paired-domain sequence.
timeline.methods: DNase I footprinting across hundreds of cell types with motif clustering
timeline.open: An archetype label does not say which factor made the footprint, so these entries cannot be used to call PAX occupancy.

open: How much of the paired-domain site the C-terminal RED subdomain actually reads is still unsettled: the Drosophila Prd structure found no RED contacts on an optimized site and showed RED to be dispensable for binding, while the PAX6 structure found base-specific RED contacts over the 3' half, and which case applies depends on the site and the protein.

Whether the homeodomain-only models labeled PAX4 and PAX3 belong in this family is doubtful: their nearest neighbours across all four databases are PRD-like and Q50 homeodomain motifs rather than PAX motifs, so the labels may record the protein assayed rather than a PAX-specific preference.

Several footprint archetypes carrying PAX labels contain no paired-domain sequence at all, and it is unresolved whether they reflect an unrecognized PAX binding mode or clustering driven by factors that co-occupy the same footprints.

The in vivo division of labor between the two PAX6 splice isoforms is unknown: the exon 5a insertion switches the protein to a RED-dominated specificity in vitro, but which endogenous targets each isoform occupies, and in which tissues, has not been mapped.

families.name: SCAN-domain zinc fingers (ZSCAN/ZKSCAN)
families.def: SCAN-domain C2H2 factors: ZSCAN and ZKSCAN genes, ZNF24-like SCAN factors.
families.short: The larger, thinner-documented half of the human SCAN-domain zinc fingers: 26 labels including ZSCAN1, 2, 5, 9, 12, 16, 23, 25, 26, 30 and 31, ZKSCAN2, 4, 5, 7 and 8, and the older names ZNF165, ZNF174, ZNF232, ZNF396, ZNF444 and ZNF449. Each combines an N-terminal SCAN domain, an approximately 80-residue leucine-rich module that dimerizes, with a tandem C2H2 finger array; the ZKSCAN members also carry a KRAB domain. This is not a single motif. The 48 matrices here form roughly twenty per-protein groups that do not resemble one another, ranging from ZSCAN16's TGTTAACAGAGCCTC to ZNF444's poly-C run. Functional data exist for only a handful of members.
families.long:
## The factors

The SCAN domain is a conserved, leucine-rich module of about 80 to 84 residues found near the N terminus of a subfamily of C2H2 zinc fingers. It contains three predicted helices and mediates self-association or selective association with other SCAN-bearing proteins (Williams et al. 1999) [PMID:10567577]. The one high-resolution structure, an NMR structure of the MZF1 SCAN domain, is a domain-swapped dimer of five-helix monomers with helix 3 at the core of the interface and a dissociation constant near 600 nM; more than 60 human C2H2 zinc-finger genes carry the domain (Peterson et al. 2006) [PMID:16950398]. SCAN genes sit in clusters, often tandem arrays, carry 3 to 14 fingers, and some combine SCAN with KRAB or SANT domains and generate alternative isoforms (Edelstein and Collins 2005) [PMID:16139965]. Nomenclature has churned: ZNF165, ZNF174, ZNF232, ZNF396, ZNF444 and ZNF449 predate the ZSCAN/ZKSCAN scheme and are the same class of protein. The ZKSCAN members can recruit TRIM28 through their KRAB domain. The atlas places the seven SCAN factors with the best-mapped sites in a separate ZNF24 entry; the members with thinner data are collected here.

## The motif

There is no family consensus; cohesion is 0.39. The 48 matrices have a median consensus length of 14 bp and median information content 16.1 bits, with 15 above 20 bits and a maximum of 32.4 bits (ZSCAN2, AGGTTAGACTTCAGGAAGGACTTCC). Within-family similarity looks high (median 0.95, only 2 of 35 below 0.7), but that is an artefact of redundancy: the close neighbour is almost always the same protein measured again in another database, as for ZNF449 (AGCCCAACC, its reverse complement GGTTGGGCT, and the archetype AC0534) or ZSCAN5C (TTTGTTGACTCAC and TGTGAGTCAATAAA). Between proteins the motifs are unrelated: ZSCAN16 TGTTAACAGAGCCTC at 31 bits with methyl-SELEX support and an agreeing archetype AC0298; ZSCAN23 CATGTGCTAATTACA; ZSCAN31 GCATAACTGCCCTGC; ZSCAN9 TGATTCTTATCTTATCC, a direct TTATC repeat; ZNF174 GGCGAGTGATCGGC, whose CIS-BP model GNCGATCACTTGCC is the same sequence on the opposite strand; ZSCAN5/ZSCAN5A GTCCCCCCCAAA; ZKSCAN5 TCACCTCC; ZNF444 CCCCCTCCCCC. Because the SCAN domain dimerizes, dyadic sites would be a reasonable expectation, and a few models are compatible with one, but most are not obvious inverted repeats and no member has been tested for half-site organization. Do not assume a dyad. Several models are low-complexity rather than specific: the CIS-BP entry for ZSCAN16 (M08377) is a pure (AT)n tract, ZNF444's is a poly-C run flagged as matching the ZNF281 motif, and ZKSCAN2's is a poly-A run whose nearest neighbour outside this family scores 1.00.

## Where it acts

Little systematic mapping has been published. The matrices themselves split into two groups with different expected genomic distributions: the GC- and CT-rich models (ZNF444, ZKSCAN5, ZSCAN25, ZNF165) will fall in promoters and CpG islands, where they are hard to separate from the general GC-box pool, while the longer AT-containing models (ZSCAN2, ZSCAN23, ZKSCAN8, ZNF232) will fall mostly in repeat-rich non-coding sequence. The genes themselves cluster in tandem arrays, several on chromosome 19 (Edelstein and Collins 2005) [PMID:16139965]. Systematic surveys of poorly characterized human transcription factors find that roughly half bind conventional promoters and enhancers while the other half bind repeat-rich closed chromatin at protein-specific sites (Razavi et al. 2026) [PMID:42557260]; most ZSCAN members have not been placed in either group. For ZNF165 the best evidence is that it acts with SMAD3 at TGF-beta target genes rather than autonomously (Gibbs et al. 2020) [PMID:32515734], which matters for how its motif should be read.

## Biology and disease

The functional literature is thin and uneven. ZNF165 is a cancer-testis antigen that elicits antibody responses in hepatocellular carcinoma patients (Dong et al. 2004) [PMID:15354214] and acts as a SMAD3 cofactor coordinating oncogenic TGF-beta signalling in triple-negative breast cancer, where it is required for tumour cell growth (Gibbs et al. 2020) [PMID:32515734]. For most other members, published work is limited to expression surveys and to the systematic screens that generated the motifs in the first place (Najafabadi et al. 2015; Schmitges et al. 2016; Jolma et al. 2026) [PMID:25690854,27852650,42557334]. The KRAB-bearing ZKSCAN members are expected to repress through TRIM28, but this has been shown for very few of them. Absence of a phenotype in this entry reflects absence of study, not a demonstrated lack of function; these are among the proteins the Codebook effort was designed to address.

## Reading a hit

Read a hit as belonging to one named protein: there is no ZSCAN motif. Check the evidence code first. Of the 19 HOCOMOCO models here, 8 are ChIP-only (code P) and the rest carry some in vitro support, with grades splitting 4 A, 7 B and 8 C [PMID:37971293]. Discard the low-complexity matrices for scanning: an (AT)n, poly-C or poly-A model will match millions of positions and carries no factor-specific information. Five matrices have their nearest neighbour in a different family: three are the ZSCAN4/ZNF24 motif (both ZSCAN1 models and the archetype AC0530), one is the ZNF281 poly-C motif (ZNF444), and one is a homeodomain TAATT site (the CIS-BP model for ZSCAN31) — so cross-check before naming a factor. One model, the CIS-BP entry for ZSCAN26, is transferred from the mouse orthologue at 0.89 DNA-binding-domain identity and carries under 10 bits; it should not be used. Finally, because SCAN factors heterodimerize with one another, an occupied site may have been contacted by a partner's fingers rather than by those of the protein whose name is on the motif.
families.caveats: This entry is a structural class, not a motif: 26 proteins, 48 matrices, cohesion 0.39, and no consensus. A hit names one protein at best. Several matrices are low-complexity — an (AT)n tract for ZSCAN16 in CIS-BP, poly-C for ZNF444, poly-A for ZKSCAN2 — and should not be scanned at all. Eight of 19 HOCOMOCO models are ChIP-only, so the enriched sequence may be a partner's; ZNF165 in particular works as a SMAD3 cofactor. The CIS-BP ZSCAN26 model is a mouse transfer carrying under 10 bits. Because SCAN domains heterodimerize, occupancy may reflect a partner's fingers rather than the named protein's.

timeline.finding: The conserved 80-residue leucine-rich region at the N terminus of a subset of C2H2 zinc fingers, named the SCAN box, was shown to function as an oligomerization domain mediating self-association and association with other SCAN-bearing proteins, defining the subfamily by a dimerization module rather than by a shared site.
timeline.methods: yeast two-hybrid, co-immunoprecipitation, in vitro association assays
timeline.open: No DNA sequence was known for any SCAN protein, and it was unclear whether dimerization imposed any site architecture.

timeline.finding: ZNF165 was characterized as a cancer-testis antigen, expressed in testis and in several tumor types and eliciting antibodies in a minority of hepatocellular carcinoma patients, which is still the best-known fact about any member of this entry.
timeline.methods: RT-PCR, real-time PCR, northern blot, western blot on patient sera

timeline.finding: Annotation of the SCAN family established its architecture and genomics: a single SCAN domain combined variously with KRAB or SANT domains and 3 to 14 C2H2 fingers, with the genes clustered in tandem arrays and generating alternative isoforms.
timeline.methods: comparative genome annotation
timeline.open: Function was unknown for most of the family, and remains so for most members of this entry.

timeline.finding: The NMR structure of the MZF1 SCAN domain showed a domain-swapped dimer of five-helix monomers with helix 3 at the core of the interface and a dissociation constant near 600 nM, giving a physical model for SCAN-mediated dimerization across more than 60 human genes.
timeline.methods: NMR spectroscopy, fluorescence polarization, pull-downs
timeline.open: Whether a SCAN dimer contacts two DNA half-sites, and with what spacing, was not tested and still has not been.

timeline.finding: Bulk surveys of C2H2 zinc fingers supplied the first motifs for most members of this entry, by inferring a recognition code from thousands of finger domains and by directly profiling 131 proteins, 78 of which had no prior model; the same work showed that the co-factors these proteins recruit are as diverse as their motifs.
timeline.methods: bacterial one-hybrid, protein-binding microarrays, ChIP-seq, affinity purification-mass spectrometry
timeline.open: Motifs came from screens rather than from study of individual proteins, and almost none were confirmed at a functional target gene.

timeline.finding: ZNF165 was shown to act as a SMAD3 cofactor, with the KRAB zinc finger ZNF446 and TRIM27 as obligate components of the complex, and TRIM27 alone necessary for ZNF165-dependent transcription and tumor growth, so this factor's genomic signal reflects a complex rather than autonomous site recognition.
timeline.methods: co-immunoprecipitation, ChIP-seq, RNA-seq, orthotopic xenografts

timeline.finding: Systematic characterization of poorly characterized human factors produced motifs for 177 of 332 targets and mapped 166 of them in cells, splitting them between promoter-enhancer binders that share conserved motif matches and factors that bind unique repeat sets in closed chromatin; most SCAN members have not yet been assigned to either behaviour.
timeline.methods: multiple in vitro and in vivo binding assays; ChIP-seq in living cells

open: Whether SCAN-mediated dimerization imposes a dyadic site is unresolved: the domain is an obligate dimerization module and a few models here are compatible with two half-sites, but no member has been tested for half-site organization and most matrices are not inverted repeats.
When two different SCAN proteins heterodimerize it is not known whose fingers contact the DNA, so a ChIP-derived motif attributed to one member may record the specificity of its partner.

The two best ZSCAN16 models disagree completely, a 31-bit TGTTAACAGAGCCTC supported by methyl-SELEX against a pure (AT)n tract in CIS-BP, and nothing published says whether this is two binding modes or one unusable model.
Whether ZNF165 recognizes DNA directly at its genomic sites is open, since its transcriptional activity requires SMAD3, ZNF446 and TRIM27, and TRIM27 alone is necessary for that activity.

families.name: IRF
families.def: ISRE/AICE, AANTGAAA repeats. IRF1-9; composite EICE (with SPI1) and AICE (with BATF).
families.short: The nine human interferon regulatory factors, IRF1 through IRF9, bind DNA with an N-terminal winged helix-turn-helix domain studded with five conserved tryptophans. Each domain reads only a short AANTGAAA half-site, so functional elements are tandem repeats of it: the interferon-stimulated response element (ISRE), written RNGAAANNGAAACT or, on the other strand, AGTTTCNNTTTC. The same half-site also appears in two named composites - the EICE with PU.1 or SPIB, and the AICE with BATF-JUN - which is how IRF4 and IRF8, weak DNA binders on their own, reach their targets. IRFs drive the type I and type II interferon responses, myeloid and lymphoid development, and plasma cell differentiation; IRF6 is the non-immune outlier, acting in epithelium, where mutations cause orofacial clefting.
families.long:
## The factors

Nine IRF genes exist in humans, IRF1 to IRF9 [PMID:18303999] (an IRF10 is present in birds and fish but not in
mammals). Each encodes an N-terminal DNA-binding domain of roughly 115 residues characterized by a
cluster of five conserved tryptophans - the "tryptophan cluster" that defines the family - folded as
a variant helix-turn-helix [PMID:9422515]. Most members also carry a C-terminal IRF-association domain that
mediates homodimers, IRF-IRF heterodimers, and complexes with non-IRF partners: STAT2 for IRF9,
BATF-JUN for IRF4 and IRF8, PU.1 and SPIB for IRF4 and IRF8 [PMID:12453417,22983707,29317535]. Functionally the family splits along
lines that sequence does not see. IRF1 and IRF2 are broadly expressed and act as an
interferon-inducible activator/repressor pair on the same sites. IRF3 is constitutive and
cytoplasmic until phosphorylated on virus sensing, whereupon it dimerizes and drives type I
interferon genes; IRF7 amplifies that response and is highly expressed in plasmacytoid dendritic
cells [PMID:18303999]. IRF9 is the constitutive DNA-binding subunit of ISGF3 [PMID:29317535]. IRF4 and IRF8 are lymphoid and myeloid,
with low intrinsic DNA affinity; IRF5 acts in myeloid cells and B cells. IRF6 is the outlier -
epithelial, expressed in skin and oral periderm, with no established role in interferon signaling [PMID:12219090].

## The motif

The unit is a short half-site, AANTGAAA, of which only about four bases (the GAAA) are read
strongly [PMID:9422515,10487755]. The crystal structure of the IRF1 domain on the PRD I element of the interferon-beta
promoter showed why: the recognition helix lies obliquely in the major groove, contacts a short GAAA
core through three of the five conserved tryptophans, and bends the DNA toward the protein [PMID:9422515]. Because
so little sequence is read per domain, affinity and specificity come from repetition, and the IRF2
structure showed cooperative binding to a tandem GAAA repeat driven by DNA distortion [PMID:10487755]. The canonical
element is therefore the ISRE, written RNGAAANNGAAACT [PMID:29317535]; the data consensus for this family,
CGAAACCGAAACT, is the same element read on the opposite strand, whose reverse complement
AGTTTCGGTTTCG is the familiar AGTTTCNNTTTC form. Two composites reuse the same half-site with a
different partner. The EICE, GGAAGTGAAAC, is a PU.1 or SPIB site fused to an IRF half-site [PMID:7797077,12453417]; the
AICE joins an IRF half-site to an AP-1 site, either as AICE1 (TTTCNNNNTGASTCA, four bases of spacer)
or AICE2 (GAAATGASTCA, directly abutting) [PMID:22983707,28346410]. Paralogue resolution from sequence is close to zero: the
in vitro models for all nine IRFs are near-identical GAAA repeats, and what separates them in vivo is
which partner they cooperate with, not which bases they read.

## Where it acts

ISREs sit predominantly in promoters of interferon-stimulated genes, usually within a few hundred
base pairs of the transcription start site, and in virus-inducible enhancers such as the
interferon-beta enhanceosome, where PRD I and PRD III are IRF elements [PMID:9422515]. In lymphoid and myeloid
cells, IRF4 and IRF8 occupancy is overwhelmingly composite: EICEs at immunoglobulin light-chain
enhancers [PMID:7797077], where DNA-bound and Ser148-phosphorylated PU.1 raises IRF4 affinity 20- to 40-fold, and
AICEs with BATF-JUN in T cells and dendritic cells [PMID:22983707]. AICE affinity grades the response to signal
strength: high-affinity AICEs remain occupied under weak T-cell receptor stimulation while
low-affinity ones only under strong stimulation [PMID:28346410]. ISGF3, the STAT1-STAT2-IRF9 trimer, accounts for
most ISRE occupancy in a type I interferon response, with the STAT1-STAT2 pair on the 5' GGAA and
IRF9 on the second repeat [PMID:29317535]. IRF6 works instead in epithelial enhancers of the periderm and keratinocyte programs.

## Biology and disease

IRFs are the transcriptional output of innate immune sensing and are also lineage regulators.
Human IRF8 mutations cause dendritic cell immunodeficiency, with biallelic loss abolishing monocytes
and dendritic cells [PMID:21524210]. IRF4 is required for plasma cell
differentiation, and multiple myeloma lines die when IRF4 is depleted whether or not IRF4 itself is
mutated [PMID:18568025]. A common IRF5 haplotype that alters splicing and expression is a reproducible risk factor
for systemic lupus erythematosus [PMID:16642019]. IRF6 mutations cause Van der Woude syndrome (cleft lip or palate
with lower lip pits) and popliteal pterygium syndrome [PMID:12219090], the clearest case of an IRF acting outside
immunity.

## Reading a hit

A single AANTGAAA half-site is not evidence of anything: with roughly six specified bases it is
expected on the order of a million times per strand in a 3.1-Gb genome. Require the tandem repeat,
or a composite. The most common misreading is confusion with STAT. A STAT homodimer site (GAS) is an
inverted repeat, TTCNNNGAA, with the two half-sites facing each other; an ISRE is a direct repeat,
GAAANNGAAAC, with both half-sites in the same orientation - and its reverse-complement spelling
AGTTTCNNTTTC superficially resembles a GAS. The two families genuinely overlap in biology as well,
because ISGF3 contains STAT1 and STAT2 [PMID:29317535], so ISRE-shaped matrices appear under both labels; one
footprint archetype grouped in this family is named AC0672:IRF/STAT precisely because the clustering
could not separate them. Evidence for this family is comparatively good - most HOCOMOCO models here
carry in vitro HT-SELEX or methyl-HT-SELEX support, and most JASPAR profiles here are SELEX-derived - but two
ChIP-derived entries have absorbed a partner's site. HOCOMOCO's ChIP-based IRF8 model
(IRF8.H14CORE.0.P.B, consensus AGDGGAAGTGAAAGT) contains GGAAGTGAAA, an EICE whose 5' half is a PU.1
site, not an IRF site [PMID:7797077,12453417]; and one CIS-BP model here (M07978, TGHGGAAATGARTCA) is AICE2-shaped, an IRF
half-site abutting an AP-1 heptamer [PMID:22983707], and its best match across the databases lies outside the IRF
family. In
myeloid or B-lineage data, check for an adjacent GGAA or TGASTCA before concluding that an IRF acted
alone.
families.caveats:
A hit identifies an IRF-type element, not an IRF protein: all nine paralogues select
near-identical GAAA repeats in vitro, and their specificity in cells comes from partners (PU.1/SPIB
at an EICE, BATF-JUN at an AICE, STAT2 in ISGF3), not from the bases they read. A lone AANTGAAA
half-site is far too short to be meaningful; insist on a tandem repeat or a composite. Expect
cross-talk with the STAT family in both directions, since ISGF3 contains STAT1 and STAT2 and reads
the ISRE - one footprint archetype here is named IRF/STAT. Most models in this family have in vitro
support, but the ChIP-derived IRF8 model contains an embedded PU.1 half-site and one CIS-BP model in
this family is actually an AICE, half AP-1. Neither should be read as intrinsic IRF specificity.
