timeline.finding: IRF-1 is cloned as the nuclear factor that binds the upstream regulatory region of the interferon-beta gene and mediates its virus-induced transcription; the IRF1 gene is itself virus-inducible.
timeline.methods: cDNA cloning, DNA-binding assays, expression analysis
timeline.open: Which bases IRF-1 read, and how the same factor could act on both interferon-beta and interferon-stimulated genes, was unknown.

timeline.finding: Pip (IRF4) is cloned as the lymphoid partner that binds the immunoglobulin light-chain enhancer composite element only together with DNA-bound, Ser148-phosphorylated PU.1, defining the ETS-IRF composite element.
timeline.methods: cDNA cloning, EMSA, co-transfection reporter assays
timeline.open: How IRF4 targets genes in cells that lack PU.1 or SPIB, such as most T cells, was unexplained.

timeline.finding: The IRF-1 DNA-binding domain on PRD I of the interferon-beta promoter is a new helix-turn-helix that grips DNA through three of the five conserved tryptophans and reads a short GAAA core through an obliquely angled recognition helix while bending the DNA toward the protein.
timeline.methods: X-ray crystallography
timeline.open: The structure suggested, but did not show, why IRF elements are built from GAAA repeats.

timeline.finding: The IRF-2 DNA-binding domain structure gives the recognition sequence AANNGAAA and shows cooperative binding to a tandem GAAA repeat driven by DNA distortion, explaining binding to both single and repeated sites.
timeline.methods: X-ray crystallography

timeline.finding: The PU.1/IRF4/DNA ternary structure shows the composite element contorted into an S shape that juxtaposes the two DNA-binding domains across the central minor groove, explaining cooperativity with IRF4 and IRF8 and anti-cooperativity with IRF1 and IRF2.
timeline.methods: X-ray crystallography

timeline.finding: In T helper 17 cells IRF4 binds AP-1-IRF composite elements (AICEs) cooperatively with BATF-containing AP-1 dimers, resolving how IRF4 and IRF8 find targets without an ETS partner; the same elements operate in TH2, B and dendritic cells.
timeline.methods: ChIP-seq, cooperative DNA-binding assays

timeline.finding: Bases flanking the AICE set the affinity of the BATF-IRF4 complex, and enhancers occupied only at strong T-cell receptor signal are low-affinity AICEs, linking motif affinity to signal strength; a high-affinity AICE2 variant at CTLA4 is associated with resistance to autoimmunity.
timeline.methods: ChIP-seq across stimulation strengths, ChIP-exo, in vitro binding

timeline.finding: Crystal structures of the IRF9 association domain alone and bound to the STAT2 coiled-coil domain explain the selective STAT2-IRF9 pairing in ISGF3, and a model of ISGF3 on an ISRE places the STAT pair on the 5' GGAA repeat and IRF9 on the second GAAA repeat.
timeline.methods: X-ray crystallography, EMSA, structural modeling, cell-based reporter assays
timeline.open: The full ISGF3 complex on DNA has not been solved; its placement on the ISRE is a model.

open: Why in vitro and ChIP-derived IRF models disagree on the base before each GAAA is unresolved: most HT-SELEX and methyl-HT-SELEX models read CGAAACCGAAAC, placing a CpG in each half-site, while ChIP-derived models read TGAAACTGAAA or GAAAGTGAAA, and whether genomic CpG depletion and methylation suppress a genuine in vitro preference or the SELEX enrichment overstates it has not been tested in the sources cited here.

How ISGF3 sits on the ISRE is inferred rather than observed: the STAT2-IRF9 interface has been crystallized, but the placement of the STAT pair on the 5' GGAA and IRF9 on the second repeat comes from a docked model, so which subunit makes which base contacts is not settled.

The databases cannot separate ISRE-shaped STAT models from IRF models (one archetype is named IRF/STAT), and whether ISRE-shaped STAT1 and STAT2 ChIP motifs reflect contacts by IRF9 within ISGF3 or genuine STAT preference for that element cannot be decided from the matrices alone.

families.name: E2F / DP
families.def: TTTSSCGC. E2F1-8, TFDP1/2.
families.short: E2F factors are the transcriptional output of the retinoblastoma (RB) pathway and set the G1/S transition. Eight human genes, E2F1-E2F8, encode a winged-helix DNA-binding domain. E2F1-E2F6 bind DNA only as heterodimers with a DP subunit (TFDP1 or TFDP2); E2F7 and E2F8 carry two tandem winged-helix domains and work without DP. All of them read essentially the same GC-rich eight-base element, written TTTSSCGC and just as often rendered on the other strand as GCGGGAAA. E2F1-E2F3 are activators released when CDKs phosphorylate RB; E2F4-E2F8 repress, E2F4 as part of the DREAM complex that also reads the adjacent CHR element. Sites sit in CpG-island promoters of replication and cell-cycle genes, and the RB-E2F axis is disabled in most human cancers.
families.long:
## The factors

Humans have eight E2F genes and two dimerization partners, TFDP1 and TFDP2 (DP1 and DP2).
E2F1-E2F6 each contribute one winged-helix domain and must heterodimerize with a DP subunit,
which contributes a second winged helix, so the functional unit is a pseudo-symmetric clamp
built from two different proteins. The crystal structure of the E2F4-DP2 DNA-binding regions
on DNA showed both recognition helices inserted into the major groove of one short GC-rich
site [PMID:10090723]. E2F7 and E2F8 are the exceptions: each carries two winged-helix domains in a single
polypeptide, binds as a homodimer or as an E2F7-E2F8 heterodimer, and needs no DP partner [PMID:14633988,18194653].
Function splits along the same lines as pocket-protein binding. E2F1, E2F2 and E2F3a are
activators held inactive by RB [PMID:16360038]; E2F4 and E2F5 are repressors that partner p107 and p130
(RBL1, RBL2) [PMID:17531812]; E2F6 lacks the pocket-protein-binding region and represses as part of a
Bmi1-containing polycomb complex [PMID:11171983]; E2F7 and E2F8 are atypical repressors. E2F1-E2F3 peak at
G1/S, whereas E2F4 is abundant in quiescent cells and accounts for most of the E2F signal in
chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP) experiments, largely through the DREAM complex [PMID:17531812].

## The motif

The literature consensus is TTTSSCGC (S = G or C), eight positions [PMID:10090723]. Because the element is
close to self-complementary at its center, databases write it on either strand: TTTCCCGC,
TTTGGCGC, GCGGGAAA and GGCGGGAA are all the same site. The data consensus here, GGCGGGAA, is
the reverse complement of TTCCCGCC and does not contradict the literature form. In vitro
models from HT-SELEX are longer and palindromic, TTTTGGCGCCAAAA or TTTTGGCGGGAAA, which
reflects two overlapping half-sites and the two-subunit clamp; ChIP-derived models collapse to
the shorter, GC-skewed GGCGGGAA. The information is concentrated in the central GCGC or GCGG,
where the two recognition helices make direct base contacts, and falls off through the flanking
T-rich or A-rich tract [PMID:10090723]. Because the core is GC-rich and contains CGCG or GGCGGG, E2F models
overlap the sequence space of the KLF/SP GC-box (GGGGCGGGG) and of other GC-repeat binders;
the Vierstra archetype AC0552:E2F/ZBTB is effectively a GCGCGCGC repeat whose nearest
neighbours in these data lie outside the family. Across 37 motifs from four databases the
family is cohesive (0.82) and no paralogue is separable: E2F1 through E2F8 and TFDP1 all
converge on one model, and E2F7/E2F8 differ only in showing the doubled form expected from
their tandem domains.

## Where it acts

E2F sites are promoter elements, not typical distal enhancer elements. They cluster within a
couple of hundred base pairs of the transcription start site in CpG islands, upstream of
replication genes (CDC6, the MCM2-7 genes, PCNA, POLA1), nucleotide metabolism genes (TYMS,
RRM2) and the E2F genes themselves. Genome-wide, E2F1, E2F4 and E2F6 occupy largely the same
promoters, which is one reason ChIP data do not separate the paralogues [PMID:17908821], and a large fraction
of occupied regions contain no canonical consensus at all [PMID:18836037]. The best-characterized composite
element is the CDE/CHR module: a GC-rich cell cycle-dependent element (CDE) separated by about
four base pairs from a cell cycle genes homology region (CHR, TTYGAA), found in G2/M promoters
such as CDC25C, CDK1, CCNB2 and PLK1 [PMID:7556094,22064854]. The CHR is bound by LIN54 inside the DREAM/MuvB complex
and the CDE by an E2F-family protein [PMID:22064854,27465258]; the two are functionally coupled [PMID:7556094], and both are needed for
p53-p21-DREAM repression. E2F sites also sit next to NF-Y CCAAT boxes and SP1 GC-boxes [PMID:7556094].

## Biology and disease

Loss of E2F1 in mice produces tumors as well as thymic hyperplasia, combined loss of E2F1-E2F3
blocks proliferation [PMID:19851314], and E2f7/E2f8 double-knockout embryos die with widespread apoptosis [PMID:18194653]. In human cancer the pathway upstream of E2F is disrupted far more often than E2F
itself: RB1 deletion, CDKN2A loss, CCND1 amplification and CDK4/CDK6 activation all converge on
releasing activator E2Fs [PMID:19851314], and CDK4/6 inhibitors work by restoring RB-mediated E2F repression.
Adenovirus E1A, HPV E7 and SV40 large T each dissociate E2F from pocket proteins, and HPV E7
specifically deregulates CDE/CHR-controlled genes. Deregulated E2F1 can also drive apoptosis [PMID:18194653],
which is why E2F activity is not simply pro-proliferative.

## Reading a hit

A single E2F match is weak evidence. The element is eight GC-rich bases with little flanking
information, so it occurs frequently by chance and is especially common in CpG-island promoters,
where base composition alone inflates matches. The match tells you nothing about which member
is bound: all eight E2Fs and both DP proteins share one model, and in a proliferating cell
several are present at once. It also does not tell you whether the site activates or represses,
since activator and repressor E2Fs use the same sequence. Confirm you are not looking at a
KLF/SP GC-box or a generic GC repeat. If the hit is in a G2/M promoter, look for a CHR about
four base pairs downstream, which is stronger evidence than the E2F match alone.
families.caveats: Trust an E2F hit as evidence for "an E2F-family site" and nothing narrower. The 8-bp GC-rich core gives frequent chance matches, especially inside CpG islands, and it overlaps KLF/SP GC-boxes, MAZ and other GC-repeat models. No paralogue is distinguishable from sequence, and neither activator nor repressor identity is readable. HOCOMOCO ChIP-only models (evidence letter P) are shorter and GC-skewed relative to the HT-SELEX and methyl-HT-SELEX models (S, M), which show the longer palindrome; the discrepancy is a difference in method, not in the factor. Roughly a third to a half of genomic E2F occupancy in ChIP experiments falls on regions without a canonical consensus, so absence of a match does not exclude binding.

timeline.finding: A cellular factor that binds the adenovirus E2 promoter, protecting positions -33 to -74, is detected in nuclear extracts; its binding activity rises when the viral E1A gene is expressed. This is the activity named E2F.
timeline.methods: Gel mobility shift, DNase I and exonuclease III footprinting
timeline.open: The protein, its exact recognition sequence and its connection to cell-cycle control were unknown.

timeline.finding: Periodic repression of cdc25C, cyclin A and cdc2 depends on a GC-rich cell cycle-dependent element (CDE) and an adjacent five-base CHR; mutating either one deregulates all three genes in G0.
timeline.methods: Promoter mutagenesis, reporter assays, in vivo DMS footprinting
timeline.open: The proteins occupying the CDE and the CHR were not identified.

timeline.finding: Crystal structure of E2F4-DP2 on DNA: both subunits contribute a winged-helix domain, the central GCGC is read symmetrically by residues conserved across all E2Fs and DPs, and an E2F-specific arginine in the minor groove near the TTT stretch makes the extended site TTTSGCGCS asymmetric.
timeline.methods: X-ray crystallography
timeline.open: Why the heterodimer is preferred over homodimers was inferred from the interface, not measured.

timeline.finding: E2F7 carries two DNA-binding domains in one polypeptide, binds the E2F consensus without DP and represses only a subset of E2F target promoters.
timeline.methods: Cloning, DNA-binding assays, ChIP, RNA interference
timeline.open: What restricts E2F7 to a subset of promoters bearing the same site.

timeline.finding: ChIP-chip of E2F1, E2F4 and E2F6 in five cell types finds most binding within 2 kb of a start site and several E2Fs on the same promoters, with only modest cell-type specificity.
timeline.methods: ChIP-chip on ENCODE and promoter arrays, shRNA knockdown
timeline.open: Most bound promoters lacked a consensus site, leaving open how E2Fs got there.

timeline.finding: Testing isolated fragments in vivo shows that a consensus motif is not sufficient to recruit E2F, that regions lacking one can be bound, and that being an active core promoter is the main determinant of occupancy.
timeline.methods: ChIP-chip, eChIP of isolated fragments
timeline.open: Indirect recruitment, looping and assisted binding to weak sites were not fully separated.

timeline.finding: At cyclin B2 the CHR, not the E2F-bound CDE, is the essential element: DREAM binds the CHR in G0 and the B-Myb-MuvB complex binds it in proliferating cells, and a CDE enhances but is not required for DREAM binding. This revises the earlier view that E2F4 binding to the CDE is central to CDE/CHR regulation.
timeline.methods: Promoter mutagenesis, DNA-affinity purification, ChIP

timeline.finding: Crystal structure of the LIN54 DNA-binding domain on a CHR: two tyrosines insert into the minor groove, and the CHR consensus is defined biochemically as TTYRAA.
timeline.methods: X-ray crystallography, binding assays

open: How E2Fs occupy the many promoters that lack a consensus site is unresolved: in vivo tests point to an active core promoter, not a motif, as the main determinant, but indirect recruitment, looping from a distal site and assisted binding to weak motif-like sequences have not been separated.

Whether individual E2Fs have distinct targets is unsettled: ChIP finds E2F1, E2F4 and E2F6 on largely the same promoters, whereas the activator and repressor classes have distinct functions, so it is open whether any of that specificity is encoded in DNA rather than in partners, timing and pocket-protein binding.

The databases carry two forms of the site: HT-SELEX and methyl-HT-SELEX models give a long palindrome (TTTGGCGCCAAA), ChIP-derived models give the shorter GGCGGGAA, and it has not been settled whether the ChIP form is the preferred in vivo site or a product of CpG-island base composition and indirect binding.

The weight of the E2F-bound CDE in DREAM recruitment is disputed: mutagenesis at cdc25C, cyclin A and cdc2 found the CDE and CHR equally required, whereas work at cyclin B2 found the CHR essential and the CDE only enhancing.

families.name: MAF (MARE)
families.def: Maf recognition element TGCTGAC(G)TCAGCA; large MAFs (MAF, MAFA/B, NRL) and small MAFs (MAFF/G/K).
families.short: Maf proteins are basic region-leucine zipper factors that recognise an unusually long site, the Maf recognition element or MARE: 13 base pairs as TGCTGACTCAGCA, or 14 as TGCTGACGTCAGCA. The MARE is an AP-1 or CRE core with GC extensions added on both sides, and those extensions are read by two residues, an arginine and an asparagine, that are unique to the Maf basic region. The large Mafs - MAF, MAFA, MAFB and NRL - have transactivation domains; the small Mafs - MAFF, MAFG and MAFK - do not, so their homodimers repress and they serve instead as the obligate DNA-binding partners of the CNC and BACH proteins. Family members control lens, pancreatic beta cell, rod photoreceptor and erythroid programs, and are mutated or translocated in retinitis pigmentosa, insulinomatosis, carpotarsal osteolysis and myeloma.
families.long:
## The factors

Two subgroups share this element. The large Mafs - MAF (c-Maf), MAFA, MAFB and NRL - have an N-terminal transactivation domain in addition to the bZIP module, and an extended homology region adjacent to the basic region that contributes to DNA contact [PMID:7936637]. The small Mafs - MAFF, MAFG and MAFK - are bZIP and little else; they have no activation domain, so small Maf homodimers act as repressors [PMID:8107826,27058431]. Their more important role is as partners: the cap-n-collar (CNC) factors NFE2, NFE2L1, NFE2L2 and NFE2L3, and the BTB-bZIP repressors BACH1 and BACH2, cannot bind DNA as monomers, and require a small Maf to form a functional heterodimer [PMID:27058431]. No functional difference is established among MAFF, MAFG and MAFK at the bZIP level [PMID:27058431]. Expression differs a great deal: MAFG and MAFK are broadly expressed, MAFF is stress-inducible, MAFA is largely confined to pancreatic beta cells and lens, MAFB to macrophages, kidney podocytes and hindbrain, and NRL to rod photoreceptors. Maf proteins also heterodimerize with FOS and JUN, and those mixed dimers have binding specificities distinct from either homodimer [PMID:8264639,7936637].

## The motif

The MARE is 13 or 14 bases. Selection with v-Maf recovered two forms at roughly equal efficiency: the T-MARE, TGCTGACTCAGCA, and the C-MARE, TGCTGACGTCAGCA [PMID:8264639]. Strip the flanks from either and you are left with exactly the AP-1 TRE or the CREB/ATF CRE; the Maf-specific information is entirely in the GC pairs added at each end. The crystal structure of MafG on DNA showed how those extensions are read: two well-conserved basic-region residues, Arg57 and Asn61, adopt unusual side-chain orientations and contact the extended GC bases directly, while Maf-specific residues in the N-terminal and basic regions stabilize the complex through backbone phosphate contacts [PMID:19797082]. This is why the MARE is long and why no other bZIP family reads it. Because only one subunit of a heterodimer is a Maf, CNC-Maf and BACH-Maf heterodimers read a half-MARE: GC-extended on the Maf side, AP-1-like on the other side [PMID:7936637]. That element is the antioxidant response element, treated here as the NFE2/BACH family. The 34 models collected for MAF show the split plainly. Full-length models carry both flanks (HOCOMOCO MAFG, MAFK, MAFA and MAFB read AATGCTGACTCAGCA-like sequences), while many others are truncated to one flank, which is why the consensus derived from these models is only the 7 bp TGCTGAC rather than the full 13-mer. Two heterodimer matrices assigned here, JASPAR MAF::NFE2 and MAFG::NFE2L1, read ATGACTCAGCA - GC on one side only - and nine of their ten nearest neighbours across the four databases carry labels from outside this family. Within the family, members are not distinguishable: MAFF, MAFG and MAFK are interchangeable, and the large Mafs differ from them mainly in affinity for degenerate sites. Even the heterodimer distinction is narrow: Nrf2-MafG and MafG homodimers bind the consensus MARE equally well and differ only on suboptimal sequences, traced to Ala502 of Nrf2, where Mafs have tyrosine [PMID:17875642].

## Where it acts

MAREs sit in tissue-specific enhancers and promoters: the alpha-A-crystallin and other crystallin genes in lens, insulin and beta-cell identity genes, rhodopsin and the rod gene set through NRL [PMID:11694879], and the HS2 enhancer of the beta-globin locus, whose NF-E2 site is a tandem MARE. Through CNC-small Maf heterodimers the same family of elements controls the cytoprotective and proteasome gene batteries [PMID:27058431]. Half-MAREs outnumber full MAREs by a wide margin in real genomes, so most Maf-family occupancy in ChIP data reflects heterodimers rather than Maf homodimers. Because small Mafs are obligate partners, their genomic distribution largely follows that of the CNC and BACH proteins.

## Biology and disease

NRL determines rod photoreceptor fate: Nrl-null mice make cones in place of rods [PMID:11694879], and dominant NRL mutations cause autosomal dominant retinitis pigmentosa [PMID:10192380]. A MAFA missense change causes familial insulinomatosis and diabetes in the same pedigrees [PMID:29339498]. Mutations clustering in the N-terminal transactivation domain of MAFB cause multicentric carpotarsal osteolysis [PMID:22387013]. MAF itself is dysregulated by translocation to immunoglobulin loci in a subset of multiple myeloma [PMID:9616139]. Small Maf compound knockouts in mice reproduce aspects of CNC and BACH loss, as expected when the obligate partner is removed rather than the signal-responsive subunit [PMID:27058431].

## Reading a hit

The useful rule is to count the flanks. If your match carries GC extensions on both sides of a TGAC(G)TCA core, a Maf homodimer or large-Maf dimer is the best explanation and AP-1 is not, even though the AP-1 site is literally inside it. If the GC extension is on one side only, you are looking at a CNC-Maf or BACH-Maf half-MARE, that is, the NFE2/BACH family; two matrices assigned to MAF here are exactly that, so the MAF / NFE2-BACH boundary is a labelling convention rather than a separation in sequence space. If there is no GC extension at all, read AP-1 or CREB/ATF instead. Short models are a trap: several HOCOMOCO and CIS-BP entries here are truncated to TGCTGAC, TGCTGA or GTCAGCA, and a 6 or 7 base match of that kind will occur tens of thousands of times genome-wide. No member call is available - not MAFF versus MAFG versus MAFK, not MAF versus MAFA versus MAFB versus NRL, and not whether a Maf is the activating subunit at all. The original selection paper already warned that some sites reported in the literature as TREs are in fact Maf sites [PMID:8264639]; the converse error, calling a MARE an AP-1 site, is the one a motif scanner will make for you.
families.caveats: The full 13 to 14 base MARE is one of the most specific bZIP calls available, because the GC extensions are read by residues no other bZIP family has. Everything short of that is ambiguous. A bare core is AP-1 or CRE; a one-sided GC extension is an antioxidant response element and belongs to NFE2/BACH, where two matrices filed under MAF in fact sit. Several models here are truncated to six or seven bases and should not be used for genome-wide scanning. No member can be inferred: the three small Mafs are interchangeable, the four large Mafs nearly so, and a hit does not say whether the partner subunit is another Maf, a CNC factor or a BACH repressor - which is the difference between activation and repression.

timeline.finding: Selection with v-Maf recovers two long palindromes at similar efficiency, TGCTGACTCAGCA and TGCTGACGTCAGCA, whose centers are exactly the TRE and CRE; Maf also heterodimerizes with Fos and Jun.
timeline.methods: In vitro binding-site selection, EMSA
timeline.open: How a bZIP protein reads the extra GC flanks was unknown.

timeline.finding: MafF, MafG and MafK are identified as the small partner of NF-E2 p45: small Maf homodimers repress through the NF-E2 site, while p45-Maf heterodimers activate.
timeline.methods: Protein interaction, DNA binding and transfection assays
timeline.open: Whether repression or activation dominates in cells was proposed to depend on the relative amounts of p45 and small Maf, which was not measured.

timeline.finding: Maf and Nrl homodimers bind TGC(N)6-7GCA, Fos-Maf and Jun-Nrl heterodimers bind hybrid TGAC(N)3-4GCA sites with each subunit reading one half, and the extended site requires a conserved region N-terminal to the basic domain.
timeline.methods: DNA-binding assays with defined homo- and heterodimers, deletion mutants

timeline.finding: c-maf is dysregulated by t(14;16) and related translocations to immunoglobulin loci in multiple myeloma lines, the first human tumor in which a Maf bZIP acts as an oncogene.
timeline.methods: Breakpoint cloning, expression analysis in myeloma lines

timeline.finding: Nrl-null mice lose rod function and their photoreceptors take on S-cone identity, establishing NRL as the rod-fate determinant among the large Mafs.
timeline.methods: Mouse knockout, electroretinography, retinal expression profiling

timeline.finding: Nrf2-MafG heterodimers and MafG homodimers bind the consensus MARE equally well but differ on degenerate sites, a difference traced to Ala502 of Nrf2 (tyrosine in Mafs) and reflected in different target genes.
timeline.methods: Surface plasmon resonance microarrays, mutagenesis, expression profiling

timeline.finding: The MafG-DNA crystal structure shows that two conserved basic-region residues, Arg57 and Asn61, adopt unusual orientations to contact the GC extensions directly, explaining the long MARE.
timeline.methods: X-ray crystallography

timeline.finding: Human dominant disease maps to the large-Maf activation domain: MAFB mutations clustered in the N-terminal transactivation domain cause multicentric carpotarsal osteolysis, and in 2018 a MAFA Ser64Phe change was found to cause familial insulinomatosis and diabetes.
timeline.methods: Exome sequencing, functional assays in beta-cell lines

open: How often small Maf homodimers repress at genomic MAREs, as opposed to binding as CNC or BACH heterodimers, is not measured: homodimers repress in reporter assays and the balance with partners was proposed to set activation versus repression, but the in vivo proportion of each dimer is unknown.

Where the MAF and NFE2/BACH families divide is a database convention rather than a settled distinction: JASPAR MAF::NFE2 and MAFG::NFE2L1 are filed here but read as one-sided half-MAREs, ATGACTCAGCA, whose nearest neighbours carry NFE2/BACH labels.

Whether the truncated 6 to 7 base models (TGCTGAC, GTCAGCA) reflect a genuine half-site binding mode or are trimming artifacts of motif discovery is not established; they include grade-A HOCOMOCO models for MAF, MAFG and MAFF that have full-length companions in the same database.

families.name: K50 homeodomain (OTX/PITX/CRX-type, TAATCC)
families.def: TAATCC/TAATCY specificity from lysine at homeodomain position 50. The true K50 set: OTX1/2, CRX, DMBX1, PITX1-3, GSC, GSC2. Paired-like factors that carry Q50 and read TAATTA are grouped with HD_Q50 instead, whatever their gene family.
families.short: A small group of homeodomains carries lysine instead of glutamine at position 50 of the domain, and that single substitution changes the two base pairs read 3' of the invariant TAAT core from TA to CC. The result is TAATCC, the bicoid-type site. In human the true K50 set is nine genes: OTX1, OTX2, CRX and DMBX1, PITX1, PITX2 and PITX3, and GSC and GSC2. They are tightly consistent - 34 motifs, all converging on TAATCC, with cooperative dimers on TAATCCGATTA - and unusually well supported in vitro. Paired-like factors that share their gene families but carry glutamine at position 50, such as RAX, VSX2, PHOX2B and NOBOX, read TAATTA and are covered by HD_Q50 instead.
families.long:
## The factors

The homeodomain is a 60-residue three-helix module whose recognition helix sits in the major groove while a flexible N-terminal arm reads the adjacent minor groove. Bicoid, the Drosophila anterior morphogen, is the founding member of the K50 class, defined by lysine at position 50 - the last residue of the recognition helix - and unique among homeodomains in also carrying arginine at position 54, which it needs for RNA binding [PMID:16406070].

In human the class is small and well defined: OTX1, OTX2, CRX and DMBX1 (the OTX group), PITX1, PITX2 and PITX3, and GSC and GSC2. These nine genes contribute 34 motifs across JASPAR, HOCOMOCO, CIS-BP and the footprint archetypes. The only other member is ANHX, a divergent homeobox gene that has alanine rather than lysine at position 50 and whose two reported motifs (TTGACAAG) are not K50 sites at all.

Membership here follows measured specificity, not gene family. Many proteins classified as paired-like alongside OTX, PITX and GSC - VSX1/2, RAX/RAX2, PHOX2A/2B, NOBOX, MIXL1, VENTX, PROP1, DRGX, BSX, OTP and SEBOX - carry glutamine at position 50 and their motifs are TAATTA-type; they are grouped with the Q50 homeodomains in HD_Q50. Expression of the K50 proteins is narrow and lineage-defining: CRX and OTX2 in photoreceptors and retina, OTX1/OTX2 in forebrain and eye, PITX1-3 in pituitary, anterior eye segment and hindlimb, GSC and GSC2 in craniofacial mesenchyme and mesendoderm, DMBX1 in midbrain.

## The motif

The consensus is TAATCC (equivalently GGATTA on the opposite strand). Every homeodomain recognizes the 5'-TAAT-3' core through a hydrogen bond from the invariant Asn51 to its second adenine plus minor-groove contacts from N-terminal arm arginines; residue 50 discriminates the two base pairs immediately 3' of it [PMID:8692913]. Site selection with six different residues at position 50 gave six distinct specificities differing at exactly those positions, through water-mediated hydrogen bonds and van der Waals contacts [PMID:8692913]; lysine contacts the C:G pairs that glutamine cannot [PMID:15895993]. Swapping residue 50 in Bicoid converts it into an Antennapedia-class TAATTA binder [PMID:2500253]; the reverse swap in Paired confers Bicoid specificity [PMID:2572327]. Solution structures of the native Bicoid homeodomain on TAATCC and of PITX2 on DNA show the K50, N51 and R54 side chains remaining mobile within the interface [PMID:16406070,15895993], and the PITX2 structure rationalizes the homeodomain substitutions that cause Axenfeld-Rieger syndrome [PMID:15895993].

Only about six base pairs carry information, so monomeric models are short: all nine genes give 5-7 bp TAATCC/GGATTA matrices, and the family medoid is the footprint archetype AC0061 (PITX/OTX) at exactly TAATCC. This is a tight family: cohesion 0.90, data consensus exactly TAATCC, no member flagged as resembling another family.

The longer models are dimeric. Paired-like homeodomains bind cooperatively on palindromes whose half-sites are three base pairs apart (the P3 site, TAATNNNATTA), and residue 50 sets the central bases [PMID:7901121], so the K50 version is TAATCGGATTA or TAATCCGATTA. That is exactly what the OTX1, OTX2 and OTX archetype models show; the PITX1 and PITX3 models instead carry two GGATTA half-sites. Residue-level rules for cooperativity across the 36 human paired-like factors have recently been derived [PMID:42675056], and blindness-causing CRX homeodomain mutations have been shown to alter cooperative dimerization rather than monomeric affinity [PMID:39715683].

Within the family, individual paralogues are not separable: no matrix distinguishes OTX2 from CRX, or PITX1 from PITX2 from PITX3. K50 versus Q50 is the only specificity distinction that sequence supports.

## Where it acts

These sites concentrate in tissue-specific distal enhancers and in promoters of terminal differentiation genes. The best-mapped case is photoreceptors, where CRX occupies thousands of sites at rod and cone gene promoters and enhancers [PMID:20693478], typically with NRL and NR2E3 motifs nearby. TAATCC is common in absolute terms - roughly two million expected copies in 3.1 Gb at human base composition - so location and cell type do the discriminating, not the 6-mer. The dimeric TAATCCGATTA is about a thousand-fold rarer, with a few thousand expected copies, and is correspondingly more informative.

## Biology and disease

This small family carries a heavy disease load, mostly dominant. CRX mutations cause cone-rod dystrophy [PMID:9390563] and Leber congenital amaurosis; heterozygous OTX2 mutations cause microphthalmia and anophthalmia [PMID:15846561]; PITX2 mutations cause Axenfeld-Rieger syndrome [PMID:8944018]; PITX1 mutation causes asymmetric lower-limb malformation [PMID:18950742]; and homozygous predicted-null GSC mutations or deletion cause the autosomal-recessive SAMS syndrome (short stature, auditory canal atresia, mandibular hypoplasia and skeletal abnormalities) [PMID:24290375]. Many of these substitutions fall inside the homeodomain and alter DNA binding or dimerization directly [PMID:42675056,39715683], which is why the in vitro motifs and cooperativity rules have clinical relevance.

## Reading a hit

A TAATCC match is one of the better-behaved homeodomain calls, but it is still a class-level call: it says a K50 homeodomain could bind, not whether OTX2, CRX, PITX2 or GSC bound it, and in retina at least two of those are usually present. Evidence quality here is uniformly good - all 12 HOCOMOCO models have HT-SELEX or methyl-HT-SELEX support, none is ChIP-only, none of the 34 motifs is a cross-species transfer, and no member is flagged as belonging to a different family. Two things to watch. The ANHX entries read TTGACAAG and should not be scanned as K50 sites. And one CIS-BP CRX model carries only 2.3 bits of information, with consensus TAAT, so it will match almost any AT-rich sequence; prefer the JASPAR or HOCOMOCO CRX models. Finally, if your hit is TAATTA rather than TAATCC, you are looking at the Q50 family - which includes paired-like proteins whose names (RAX, VSX2, PHOX2B, NOBOX, PROP1) might otherwise lead you to expect a K50 site.
families.caveats: A TAATCC match identifies a K50-type homeodomain site, not a protein: OTX1/2, CRX, DMBX1, PITX1-3 and GSC/GSC2 share one motif. Expect roughly two million matches genome-wide, so condition on expression and accessibility; the dimeric TAATCCGATTA is about a thousand-fold rarer and far more informative. Evidence is unusually clean for a homeodomain family - all 12 HOCOMOCO models have in vitro SELEX support, none is ChIP-only, nothing is a cross-species transfer and nothing is flagged as belonging elsewhere. Two exceptions: the ANHX motifs (TTGACAAG) are not K50 sites, and one CIS-BP CRX model carries only 2.3 bits. A TAATTA hit belongs to HD_Q50, which holds the paired-like factors that carry Q50.

timeline.finding: Residue 50 (residue 9 of the recognition helix) is shown to set Bicoid's specificity. One substitution makes Bicoid recognize Ultrabithorax and Fushi tarazu sites, and lysine at residue 50 of Paired confers Bicoid specificity. Lysine 50 becomes the defining feature of the class.
timeline.methods: Yeast transcription-activation assay; in vitro DNA binding of mutant homeodomains
timeline.open: How lysine 50 contacts the bases 3' of TAAT was unknown.

timeline.finding: Paired-class homeodomains bind cooperatively as dimers to palindromic sites, with up to 300-fold enhancement. Residue 50 sets the half-site spacing and the identity of the central base pairs, so the preferred dimer site changes with residue 50.
timeline.methods: Binding-site selection, EMSA

timeline.finding: In vitro selection with six different residues at position 50 gives six distinct specificities differing at the two bases 3' of TAAT, attributed to water-mediated hydrogen bonds and van der Waals contacts.
timeline.methods: In vitro genetic binding-site selection

timeline.finding: The first human K50 disease genes: RIEG (PITX2) mutations cause Rieger syndrome, and in 1997 CRX mutations, including E80A at the first residue of the recognition helix, are found to cause dominant cone-rod dystrophy. The CRX alleles were attributed to haploinsufficiency or a dominant-negative effect.
timeline.methods: Positional cloning, mutation screening
timeline.open: How the homeodomain substitutions change DNA binding was not known.

timeline.finding: The first structure of a native K50 homeodomain on DNA: in PITX2 on TAATCC, lysine 50 contacts the two guanines on the opposite strand next to TAAT, as in the crystal structure of the engineered Engrailed Q50K mutant, but makes fluctuating rather than fixed contacts. The native Bicoid structure (2006) shows K50, N51 and R54 all flexible in the interface.
timeline.methods: NMR spectroscopy
timeline.open: How far native K50 proteins differ in affinity and specificity from the Q50K mutant used as the earlier model.

timeline.finding: CRX ChIP-seq in mouse retina maps thousands of bound regions around photoreceptor genes; bound regions carry several CRX sites whose spacing and orientation tune output, and comparison with Nrl-/- retina separates rod, cone and shared elements.
timeline.methods: ChIP-seq, reporter assays

timeline.finding: Two dominant CRX retinopathy alleles act through cooperativity. E80A keeps binding at monomeric sites but loses cooperative binding at dimeric sites; K88N becomes highly cooperative and moves to ectopic sites rich in dimeric motifs. This gives a specific mechanism for an allele described in 1997 only as haploinsufficient or dominant-negative.
timeline.methods: Quantitative in vitro binding, knock-in mouse models, genomics

timeline.finding: Analysis of the 36 human paired-like homeodomains derives 11 rules for cooperative binding to the P3 site, and 11 of 12 tested disease-associated variants change cooperativity but not DNA-binding affinity.
timeline.methods: Structural, biochemical and bioinformatic analysis; quantitative DNA-binding assays

open: How much K50 function depends on cooperative P3 dimer sites rather than monomeric TAATCC sites is unsettled. The dimeric site is about a thousand-fold rarer than the monomer, yet CRX alleles that change only cooperativity (E80A loses it, K88N gains it) cause dominant retinopathy.

How OTX2 and CRX, which read the same TAATCC site and overlap in the developing retina, divide targets is unresolved: shared sites predict redundancy, and no sequence feature in these models separates the two.

families.name: CREB / ATF (CRE)
families.def: Cyclic-AMP response element TGACGTCA and its half-site. CREB1, CREM, ATF1, ATF2, ATF4, ATF7, CREB5.
families.short: The CREB/ATF group contains the basic region-leucine zipper factors CREB1, CREM, ATF1, ATF2, ATF7, ATF4 and CREB5. They bind the cyclic-AMP response element, the eight-base palindrome TGACGTCA, and its five-base half-site TGACG. The element was defined in the somatostatin promoter as the sequence through which cAMP raises transcription, and CREB1 phosphorylated on Ser133 recruits the coactivators CBP and p300 to it. Unlike the closely related AP-1 site, the CRE carries a central CpG, so its occupancy is sensitive to DNA methylation, and CRE-containing promoters are concentrated in CpG islands. Genome-wide, CREB occupies a few thousand promoters with a profile that is similar across tissues. All members read the same palindrome, so a match identifies the group rather than a single factor.
families.long:
## The factors

Three subgroups share this element. The CREB subgroup - CREB1, CREM and ATF1 - carries a kinase-inducible domain; phosphorylation of CREB1 Ser133 by protein kinase A, calcium/calmodulin kinases and others creates the surface that binds the CBP and p300 KIX domain [PMID:11483993]. CREM is expressed as many isoforms, including activators and the repressor ICER, and a testis-specific form required for spermiogenesis. The ATF2 subgroup - ATF2, ATF7 and CREB5 - is activated instead by the stress-responsive kinases JNK and p38. ATF4 is an outlier: it is regulated translationally, through an upstream open reading frame that is bypassed when eIF2-alpha is phosphorylated during the integrated stress response, and its preferred site is not the plain CRE [PMID:19800252]. All are bZIP proteins, dimerizing through a leucine zipper and reading DNA with a basic region in the major groove. The group was defined as an "extensive family of leucine zipper proteins able to selectively form DNA-binding heterodimers" [PMID:2516827], and cross-family dimers with Jun were reported soon afterwards [PMID:1827203], which is why the CREB/ATF and AP-1 families cannot be cleanly separated at the protein level either.

## The motif

The CRE is the 8 bp palindrome TGACGTCA: two TGAC half-sites related by a two-fold axis, one per subunit [PMID:2875459]. The crystal structure of a CREB bZIP bound to the somatostatin CRE showed the basis for its selective dimerization and a divalent-cation-enhanced mode of DNA binding [PMID:10952992]. Half-site CREs (TGACG, or CGTCA on the other strand) are functional and far more common in promoters than the full palindrome; they bind with lower affinity and with measurably different kinetics [PMID:11134034], which is one reason CREB occupancy and CREB-dependent induction are not the same thing. The feature that distinguishes the CRE from the AP-1 TRE is a single inserted base, giving a central CpG. That CpG is methylatable, and methylation of TGACGTCA abolishes CREB binding and cAMP-dependent activation [PMID:2545524]; genome-wide CREB occupancy tracks both the presence of a consensus CRE and its methylation state [PMID:15753290]. ATF4 is the exception within the family: its selected site is the C/EBP-ATF response element, read as TGATGCAAT or TTGCATCA, one CRE half joined to one C/EBP half [PMID:19800252]. The ATF4 models here (JASPAR MA0833.3, HOCOMOCO ATF4 ChIP and HT-SELEX models) therefore sit closer to C/EBP than to CREB, and their label agreement with the rest of the family is low by construction rather than by error. CREB1, CREM, ATF1, ATF2, ATF7 and CREB5 are not distinguishable from sequence; JASPAR ATF7 MA0834.2 and the CIS-BP ATF7 model are 0.99 similar, and both are within 0.98 of CREB5 and ATF2 models.

## Where it acts

Unlike AP-1, this family is promoter- and CpG-island-biased. Serial analysis of chromatin occupancy in rat PC12 cells recovered 6,302 CREB loci, of which 40% lay within 2 kb of an annotated transcription start site, 49% within 1 kb of a CpG island and 72% within 1 kb of a candidate CRE [PMID:15620361]. In human tissues CREB occupied roughly 4,000 promoter sites, with very similar profiles across tissues, yet only a small fraction of those genes responded to a cAMP agonist, because induction additionally requires CBP recruitment [PMID:15753290]. Half-CRE sites often sit beside other promoter elements rather than in enhancer clusters. Named composite contexts include the CRE-TATA arrangement of the somatostatin promoter, tandem half-CREs in cAMP-inducible promoters, and the amino-acid response elements at which ATF4 acts on ATF3, TRIB3, ASNS and DDIT3 [PMID:19800252].

## Biology and disease

This family is the main route from cAMP and calcium signaling to transcription: gluconeogenic and lipid programs in liver, circadian Per1 induction, activity-dependent transcription and long-term synaptic plasticity in neurons, and hormone-responsive programs in endocrine tissue [PMID:11483993]. ICER provides negative feedback by competing for the same element without activating. ATF2 and ATF7 transmit stress-kinase signaling and have roles in DNA-damage responses. ATF4 is the effector arm of the integrated stress response: it raises amino-acid transporter and aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase expression during amino-acid limitation [PMID:19800252], and together with CHOP it increases protein synthesis during prolonged ER stress to the point of cell death [PMID:23624402]. Loss-of-function phenotypes are generally mild for individual members and severe for combinations, the expected signature of a shared element.

## Reading a hit

A full TGACGTCA is a reasonably specific family call, but not a member call: CREB1, CREM, ATF1, ATF2, ATF7 and CREB5 give the same matrix. A half-site (TGACG) is much weaker evidence and occurs far too often to interpret alone. The CpG matters twice: the 8-mer is rarer than the AP-1 TRE partly because the genome is depleted of CpG, and a match in a methylated region may never be occupied, so pair the hit with methylation or accessibility data where you have it. Boundaries with siblings are real. TGACTCA without the central G is AP-1; TGACGTGG, or CCACGTCA read the other way, is ATF6/CREB3; TTACGTAA is PAR bZIP. If your match is the ATF4-style TGATGCAAT, it is a C/EBP-ATF composite and the C/EBP family is an equally good explanation. Seven of the 13 HOCOMOCO models here carry in vitro evidence, and four of those - ATF2, ATF7, CREB1 and CREM - are grade-A models combining ChIP with both HT-SELEX and methyl-SELEX, which is strong support that these proteins bind this sequence directly.
families.caveats: A full palindromic CRE is one of the better-supported motifs in this collection, with grade-A HOCOMOCO models backed by both ChIP and in vitro selection. What it cannot do is name a factor: six of the seven members are interchangeable at the sequence level, and Jun-family proteins bind the same palindrome, so a CRE hit is genuinely ambiguous between this family and AP-1. Treat the 5 bp half-site as a weak signal. Methylation makes matters worse in one direction and better in another: a methylated CRE is unlikely to be CREB-bound, but is a candidate C/EBP-alpha site. ATF4 models in this family are C/EBP-ATF composites and should not be read as ordinary CREs.

timeline.finding: Deletion mapping of the rat somatostatin promoter locates cAMP responsiveness to a region containing the 8 bp palindrome TGACGTCA, conserved in other cAMP-regulated genes.
timeline.methods: Promoter deletion and reporter assays in PC12 cells
timeline.open: The protein acting on the element was unknown.

timeline.finding: A 43 kDa nuclear protein, CREB, is purified on the somatostatin CRE and is phosphorylated by protein kinase A, linking cAMP signaling to a sequence-specific factor.
timeline.methods: DNase I footprinting, DNA-affinity purification, in vitro phosphorylation
timeline.open: How phosphorylation turns CREB on was unknown; the Ser133-KIX mechanism came later.

timeline.finding: Eight ATF cDNAs define a family of leucine zipper proteins that bind the same site, form selective heterodimers, and differ from the AP-1 site at a single position.
timeline.methods: cDNA cloning, DNA binding, methylation interference

timeline.finding: CpG methylation of TGACGTCA abolishes specific factor binding and transcriptional activation, making the CRE an early example of a methylation-sensitive site.
timeline.methods: Bandshift, methylation interference, reporter assays

timeline.finding: Cross-family heterodimers between Fos/Jun and ATF/CREB proteins have DNA specificities distinct from either parent, so the CRE and TRE families are not separable at the protein level.
timeline.methods: In vitro dimerization and DNA-binding assays

timeline.finding: Crystal structure of the CREB bZIP on the somatostatin CRE identifies a Tyr307-Glu312 contact behind family-selective dimerization and a hydrated Mg2+ ion that enhances binding; mutants show the palindromic and variant CREs are bound by different mechanisms.
timeline.methods: X-ray crystallography, mutagenesis, DNA-binding assays

timeline.finding: Genome-wide occupancy maps show CREB bound at thousands of promoter and CpG-island sites, tracking CRE presence and methylation, but only a small fraction of bound genes respond to cAMP, so occupancy is not activation.
timeline.methods: SACO (ChIP with tag sequencing), ChIP-chip in human tissues
timeline.open: Which partners besides CBP decide which bound promoters respond was not identified.

timeline.finding: Purified bZIP domains show that the earlier HT-SELEX ATF4 motif correlates better with the ATF4-CEBPG heterodimer than with the ATF4 homodimer, suggesting the composite C/EBP-ATF site reflects a partner rather than ATF4 alone.
timeline.methods: SELEX-seq-based cognate site identification with purified bZIP domains
timeline.open: Whether ATF4 homodimers bind CREs in cells, or ATF4 acts almost entirely as a heterodimer, was not resolved.

open: Whether half-site and variant CREs are bound by the same mechanism as the palindrome is unsettled: the Mg2+-dependent enhancement seen on TGACGTCA is absent on variant CREs, suggesting a distinct binding mode, but how that difference shapes occupancy at the many half-site promoters is unmeasured.

Why CREB occupancy at roughly 4,000 promoters yields cAMP induction at only a small subset is only partly explained: preferential CBP recruitment accounts for some of it, and the other partners or promoter features that decide responsiveness are not identified.

What ATF4's own motif is remains contested in the databases: the literature and ChIP-derived models give the C/EBP-ATF composite TGATGCAAT, whereas the highest-information HOCOMOCO ATF4 model, built from HT-SELEX and methyl-HT-SELEX, is a plain CRE, and the purified-domain data attribute the composite to an ATF4-CEBPG heterodimer.

families.name: GATA
families.def: WGATAA. GATA1-6, TRPS1; composite GATA-E-box with TAL1.
families.short: GATA factors are zinc-finger transcription factors that bind the six-base core WGATAA (usually AGATAA or TGATAA) through a single C4-type zinc finger plus a basic tail. Humans have six canonical members, GATA1-6, in two expression groups: GATA1/2/3 in blood, lymphocytes and mammary epithelium, GATA4/5/6 in heart, gut and gonad. The atypical protein TRPS1 carries one GATA-type finger and binds the same core as a repressor. Sites are short and very common, and are often read in pairs or next to an E-box occupied by TAL1. GATA binding sites underlie globin gene switching, cardiac septation and T-helper-2 commitment, and the factors are mutated in congenital heart disease, HDR syndrome and breast cancer.
families.long:
## The factors

Six canonical human GATA proteins (GATA1-6) share a pair of C4-type zinc fingers. Only the
C-terminal finger, with its adjacent basic tail, is required for sequence-specific binding; the
N-terminal finger stabilizes binding to certain palindromic and double sites and is the docking
surface for the cofactors ZFPM1/ZFPM2 (FOG1/FOG2) [PMID:14985365,23142663]. GATA proteins bind DNA as monomers, not as
obligate dimers, although two molecules can occupy adjacent sites on the same or opposite faces
of the helix. Expression splits the family in two: GATA1 (erythroid, megakaryocytic, mast,
eosinophil), GATA2 (hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells, endothelium) and GATA3
(T lymphocytes, mammary luminal epithelium, kidney, parathyroid, inner ear) versus GATA4, GATA5
and GATA6 (heart, endoderm-derived gut, lung, liver, gonad, pancreas). TRPS1 is an outlier: it
has a single GATA-type finger, binds the same core, and represses rather than activates [PMID:11285235]. ZGLP1
is annotated as GATA-like but its measured specificity in these databases (ATGATCGAT) is not the
GATA core, and it clusters here only weakly.

## The motif

The literature consensus is WGATAA, sometimes written (A/T)GATA(A/G) to include the less common
3' G [PMID:8321208,8321207]. The NMR structure of the chicken GATA-1 finger-plus-tail bound to DNA showed that the core
module contacts GAT in the major groove while the basic C-terminal tail wraps into the minor
groove to read the 3' AA and the 5' W [PMID:8332909]; this is why the invariant information sits on GATA and
falls off sharply outside it. Only about 6 bp carry real information, so a GATA PWM is one of the
least specific vertebrate models in routine use. Many database entries are written on the reverse
strand as TTATCT or CTTATCT, which is the same site; the data consensus here, AGATAAg, is simply
the forward-strand form of the same six-base core. Extended versions exist. Tandem sites in the
arrangement GATAA-N(n)-TTATC are common in real regulatory elements and give the double-GATA
archetype seen in footprint clustering. The GATA-E-box composite element places WGATAA 8-10 bp
from a CAGNTG E-box and is bound by the TAL1/E47/LMO2/LDB1/GATA1 pentameric complex [PMID:9214632]; JASPAR
models this as a GATA1::TAL1 dimer motif. Systematic in vitro surveys find near-identical preferences for closely related DNA-binding domains [PMID:23332764,25215497], and the current in vitro and ChIP-derived models for GATA1-6 are effectively the same AGATAA matrix, so the primary site does not distinguish the paralogues. The one reported difference comes from random-site selection with chicken GATA1, GATA2 and GATA3, which recovered an alternative site, AGATCTTA, bound well by GATA2 and GATA3 but poorly by GATA1 [PMID:8321208].

## Where it acts

GATA sites are enhancer elements far more than promoter elements, and they are not associated
with CpG islands. Because WGATAA occurs roughly once every few kilobases by chance, the human
genome contains on the order of a million matches and only a small fraction are occupied in any
cell type. Occupancy is set by chromatin: GATA1 and GATA2 mark erythroid enhancers, GATA3 marks
luminal breast and Th2 enhancers, GATA4 and GATA6 mark cardiac and gut enhancers, and the same
sequence is invisible in the wrong lineage. GATA2 and GATA1 exchange at many of the same sites
during erythroid maturation, the so-called GATA switch. Frequent neighbors are the E-box of TAL1,
KLF1 CACCC boxes, RUNX1, SP1, FOXA1 and estrogen receptor (in breast), and NKX2-5, TBX5 and MEF2
(in heart). GATA3 and GATA4 both behave as chromatin-opening factors at a subset of their sites.

## Biology and disease

Gata1-null mouse embryonic stem cells arrest at the proerythroblast stage and die of apoptosis [PMID:1987478,7568185],
and a megakaryocyte-selective knockdown causes thrombocytopenia. In humans, GATA1 exon 2
mutations producing the short GATA1s isoform cause transient abnormal myelopoiesis and Down
syndrome-associated acute megakaryoblastic leukemia [PMID:12172547]; other GATA1 mutations cause X-linked
dyserythropoietic anemia and thrombocytopenia. GATA2 haploinsufficiency causes MonoMAC syndrome
and familial MDS/AML [PMID:21670465]. GATA3 is required for and sufficient to drive Th2 cytokine expression in
CD4 T cells [PMID:9160750]; heterozygous mutations cause HDR syndrome (hypoparathyroidism, deafness, renal
dysplasia) [PMID:14985365], and GATA3 is one of the most frequently mutated genes in luminal breast cancer.
GATA4 mutations cause septal defects and interact genetically with TBX5 [PMID:12845333]. TRPS1 loss causes
tricho-rhino-phalangeal syndrome [PMID:11285235,12446778]; TRPS1 immunostaining is now used as a breast-carcinoma marker.

## Reading a hit

A WGATAA match tells you the family and nothing about the member. Treat any claim that a site is
"the GATA1 site" rather than "a GATA site" as an inference from expression or ChIP data, not from
sequence. Because the informative core is six bases, isolated matches in a random background are
expected and carry almost no evidence by themselves; a hit becomes interesting when it is
conserved, sits in open chromatin of a tissue that expresses a GATA factor, or is doubled or
paired with an E-box. Two specific confusions are worth knowing. AT-rich homeodomain sites
(TAAT-containing) and the reverse-complement TTATCT can score on loose GATA models, and vice
versa. And the CIS-BP human TRPS1 motif is not measured on human TRPS1: it is transferred from a
Drosophila protein at 63% DNA-binding-domain identity [PMID:25215497], so the model's fine structure should not
be read as TRPS1-specific even though TRPS1 genuinely binds GATA cores. HOCOMOCO GATA models
graded A are backed by both ChIP-seq and in vitro SELEX (evidence codes PSM), which is stronger
support than ChIP alone.
families.caveats: The core is only 6 bp, so chance matches are abundant and a single hit is weak evidence. All six canonical paralogues share one matrix; sequence cannot assign a member, and neither can ChIP-seq in a cell expressing several of them. Reverse-strand renderings (CTTATCT) and AT-rich homeodomain sites are the two commonest misreadings. The CIS-BP TRPS1 model is inferred from a Drosophila protein, and the HOCOMOCO ZGLP1 model does not match the GATA core despite ZGLP1's GATA-like domain annotation. Vierstra archetypes labelled GATA/TAL describe a composite element, not a claim that GATA and TAL1 motifs are separable.

timeline.finding: Disrupting the X-linked Gata1 gene in embryonic stem cells blocks their contribution to mature red cells in chimeric mice, showing that the factor binding erythroid GATA elements is required and that other GATA proteins cannot substitute.
timeline.methods: Gene targeting, chimeric mice
timeline.open: Which GATA elements carry the requirement, and why GATA2 present in the same precursors does not compensate.

timeline.finding: Random-site selection with GATA1, GATA2 and GATA3 confirms the WGATAR consensus and AGATAA as the high-affinity core, but also recovers high-affinity non-consensus sites and partly distinct preferences, notably an AGATCTTA site bound well by GATA2 and GATA3 and poorly by GATA1.
timeline.methods: PCR-based random-site selection (SELEX), EMSA, cotransfection
timeline.open: Whether the paralogue differences seen in vitro are used at genomic sites.

timeline.finding: The NMR structure of the chicken GATA-1 C-terminal finger plus basic tail on DNA shows the zinc module in the major groove and the tail wrapping into the minor groove, with about 8 bp in contact; the tail is an essential determinant of specific binding.
timeline.methods: Multidimensional heteronuclear NMR
timeline.open: The N-terminal finger was absent, so its role in site choice remained unexplained.

timeline.finding: In erythroid cells LMO2 bridges GATA1, TAL1, E2A and LDB1 into one DNA-binding complex that recognizes an E-box followed about 9 bp downstream by a GATA site, defining the GATA-E-box composite element.
timeline.methods: Co-immunoprecipitation, binding-site selection, EMSA, transactivation assays

timeline.finding: Crystal structures of the full GATA3 DNA-binding domain show both zinc fingers wrapping a palindromic GATA site, which raises affinity and kinetic stability, or the two fingers binding GATA sites on separate DNA molecules, a possible basis for DNA looping.
timeline.methods: X-ray crystallography, in-gel FRET
timeline.open: Whether the DNA-bridging mode occurs at endogenous loci.

timeline.finding: High-throughput SELEX and protein-binding-microarray surveys extend measured models across the family and show that closely related DNA-binding domains have near-identical preferences; the GATA1-6 matrices now in JASPAR, HOCOMOCO and CIS-BP converge on AGATAA, and the CIS-BP TRPS1 model is inferred from a Drosophila protein rather than measured.
timeline.methods: HT-SELEX, ChIP-seq, protein-binding microarrays, homology-based inference
timeline.open: The 1993 report of paralogue-specific sites has not been reconciled with these identical matrices.

open: Whether GATA paralogues differ in intrinsic sequence preference is unsettled: 1993 random-site selection found an alternative AGATCTTA site bound well by GATA2 and GATA3 but poorly by GATA1, whereas the HT-SELEX, PBM and ChIP-derived matrices for GATA1-6 in the current collections are effectively identical.

How the N-terminal finger contributes to site choice at genomic double-GATA sites is unresolved: GATA3 structures show it can either wrap a palindromic site together with the C-terminal finger or bind a second DNA molecule, and which mode operates in cells is not known.

ZGLP1 is annotated as GATA-like, yet its in vitro-supported HOCOMOCO model (ATGATCGAT, grade A) does not contain the WGATAA core, so whether it should be read as a divergent GATA-family specificity or a separate one is not settled by the data.

families.name: RFX
families.def: X-box GTTRCC(A/T)3GGYAAC. RFX1-8.
families.short: RFX proteins recognize the X-box, a pseudo-palindrome built from two GTTRCC-like half-sites separated by zero to three bases. The DNA-binding domain is a 76-residue winged helix that reads bases with its beta-hairpin wing rather than with the usual recognition helix, and two domains bind one X-box cooperatively. Humans have eight members, RFX1-RFX8. RFX1-3 form homodimers and heterodimers and drive ciliary gene programs; RFX5 works in a complex with RFXAP and RFXANK to switch on MHC class II genes; RFX6 is restricted to pancreatic islet and enteroendocrine cells. The full 13-14 bp palindrome is one of the most information-rich motifs in vertebrate collections, which makes RFX hits unusually trustworthy.
families.long:
## The factors

The human RFX family has eight genes. All share a highly conserved 76-residue DNA-binding domain
(DBD) [PMID:10706293]; most also carry dimerization domains (B, C and DIM regions) that RFX1, RFX2 and RFX3 use
to form homodimers and heterodimers with each other. RFX1-3 are the ciliogenic branch and are
broadly expressed, with RFX2 and RFX3 concentrated in tissues that build motile cilia. RFX4 is
largely brain- and testis-restricted and produces isoforms lacking parts of the dimerization
region. RFX5 does not dimerize with other RFX proteins; it functions in the RFX (also called
RFXANK-RFXAP-RFX5) complex that, together with the coactivator CIITA, drives MHC class I and
class II transcription [PMID:10779326]. RFX6 is restricted to pancreatic islet and gut enteroendocrine cells and
works downstream of NEUROG3 [PMID:20148032]. RFX7 is broadly expressed and acts downstream of p53 [PMID:34197623]. RFX8 is
poorly characterized in humans, and the CIS-BP human RFX8 entry is not a human measurement at
all: it is transferred from a louse (Pediculus humanus) protein at 55% DBD identity [PMID:29510665,25215497].

## The motif

The literature consensus, from the RFX1 crystal structure, is 5'-GTNRCC(N0-3)RGYAAC-3' [PMID:10706293]. In
practice vertebrate RFX models converge on the tighter form GTTGCCATGGCAAC, which is what the
motif data in this family reports (GTTGCCATGG). The two forms are not in conflict: the databases
are dominated by high-affinity selection experiments that pick GTTGCC as the half-site and a
2-3 bp spacer, while the literature consensus is written loosely enough to cover the weaker,
variably spaced sites found in real promoters. The structural explanation is unusual. RFX1 is a
winged-helix (helix-turn-helix) protein, but instead of inserting a recognition helix into the
major groove it uses a beta-hairpin wing to make the base-specific contacts; two DBDs bind
cooperatively on opposite half-sites of a symmetrical X-box [PMID:10706293]. This is why the informative positions
are the GTT/AAC ends and the CC/GG pair inside them, and why the central spacer bases are almost
free. Half-sites alone are real sites: the RFX6 and RFX7 models in these databases are essentially single half-sites (GTTGCTA, GTTGCCAGG, CCTAGCAAC) with 7-12 bits, whereas the JASPAR models for RFX1-5 are full palindromes of 20-23 bits. RFX5 is in the palindrome group: its HT-SELEX model (JASPAR MA0510.3, 20.2 bits) and its grade-A HOCOMOCO model (18.6 bits) both read GTTGCCATGGCAAC, so RFX1-5 are not separable by these models. Only RFX6 and RFX7 stand apart, by the *absence* of a strong second half-site, and only the RFX7 half-site rests on in vitro data.

## Where it acts

X-boxes are promoter-proximal more often than not, typically within a few hundred bases of the
transcription start site of ciliary genes (IFT and BBS genes, dynein subunits, ciliary membrane
proteins) and of MHC class II genes, where the X box sits next to the X2 box and about 15-20 bp
from the Y box. The Y box is a CCAAT element bound by NF-Y, and RFX5 and NF-Y bind the class II
promoter cooperatively [PMID:10779326]; this is the best-characterized composite element containing an X-box. In
motile ciliated epithelium RFX2 and RFX3 co-occupy promoters with FOXJ1, the forkhead factor that
specifies motile cilia, and in Drosophila the equivalent partnership is Rfx with Fd3F [PMID:22698283]. RFX6 in
islets co-occupies enhancers with NEUROD1, PDX1 and NKX2-2. X-box counts are modest for a
vertebrate motif precisely because the full palindrome is long: genome-wide scans typically
recover a few thousand strong matches, most of them at ciliary and immune loci.

## Biology and disease

Loss of the RFX complex causes MHC class II deficiency (bare lymphocyte syndrome, complementation
groups C, D and E): RFX5, RFXAP or RFXANK mutations remove X-box binding, class II expression
fails, and patients present with combined immunodeficiency [PMID:10779326]. The original RF-X activity was
defined by its absence in such patients' cells [PMID:3133120]. RFX1-3 are the transcriptional core of ciliogenesis across animals [PMID:10882127,32725242]; when X-box control of ciliary genes arose is disputed, with one survey placing it before the origin of metazoans [PMID:20441589] and another early in the animal lineage [PMID:20615967]. Rfx3 mutant mice have laterality defects, hydrocephalus and impaired nodal cilia [PMID:15121860];
combined Rfx1/2/3 loss ablates motile ciliogenesis [PMID:32725242]. RFX6 loss of function causes Mitchell-Riley
syndrome (neonatal diabetes with intestinal atresia) [PMID:20148032]; heterozygous truncating RFX6 variants cause
maturity-onset diabetes of the young with reduced penetrance [PMID:29026101], and Rfx6 is also required to
maintain adult beta-cell identity. RFX7 is recurrently mutated in lymphoid cancers and mediates
part of the p53 response, controlling genes including DDIT4 and PDCD4 [PMID:34197623]. An estrogen-receptor-RFX4
fusion has been reported in breast tumors [PMID:10706293].

## Reading a hit

A full 13-14 bp X-box match is strong evidence, and among vertebrate motifs it is one of the few
where a single high-scoring hit is worth acting on: the palindrome carries about 20 bits, so
chance occurrences in the human genome are rare. What a hit does not tell you is which RFX
protein. RFX1, RFX2, RFX3 and RFX4 are indistinguishable from sequence, and the practical
question is which of them is expressed in your cell type. Half-site-only matches (GTTGC plus a
purine) are a different matter: at 7-9 bits they occur by chance constantly, and they are the form in which the RFX6, RFX7 and RFX8 models are represented here, so hits on those models deserve much more skepticism than hits on the full-palindrome RFX1-5 models. Two provenance problems affect this family in CIS-BP: the
RFX8 motif comes from a louse protein at 55% DBD identity and the RFX6 motif from guinea pig at
71%, so neither is a human measurement. One HOCOMOCO RFX3 secondary model (evidence code S,
grade B) does not resemble an X-box at all and should not be used.
families.caveats: Trust full-palindrome X-box hits; treat half-site hits (GTTGC alone) as near-worthless on their own, because they carry under 9 bits. Nothing in the sequence separates RFX1, RFX2, RFX3 and RFX4, so assign a member from expression, not from the match. The RFX5 models are full palindromes with in vitro support, although in cells RFX5 binds MHC class II X boxes as part of a three-protein complex. In CIS-BP the human RFX8 motif is transferred from a louse protein (55% DBD identity) and the RFX6 motif from guinea pig (71%); neither was measured on the human protein. One HOCOMOCO RFX3 secondary model is not X-box-like and looks unreliable.

timeline.finding: An X-box-binding activity on the HLA-DRA promoter, named RF-X, is missing from B-cell lines of patients with congenital MHC class II deficiency, the first link between the X box and disease.
timeline.methods: EMSA with nuclear extracts from patient-derived B-cell lines
timeline.open: Which protein or proteins made up RF-X, and whether the patients' defect lay in DNA binding itself.

timeline.finding: The single C. elegans RFX factor, DAF-19, is expressed in all ciliated sensory neurons and is required for their cilia; genes shared by all ciliated neurons carry RFX sites in their promoters and depend on DAF-19.
timeline.methods: Worm genetics, promoter analysis, reporter genes
timeline.open: Whether the vertebrate paralogues had kept the ciliary role.

timeline.finding: The 1.5 A structure of two RFX1 DNA-binding domains on a symmetrical X-box shows cooperative binding and base recognition by the beta-hairpin wing instead of the recognition helix, and frames the consensus GTNRCC(N0-3)RGYAAC.
timeline.methods: X-ray crystallography

timeline.finding: RFX5 is the subunit that assembles the RFX5-RFXAP-RFXANK complex on the MHC class II X box, and a separate C-terminal domain makes the complex bind cooperatively with NF-Y on the neighboring Y box.
timeline.methods: Domain mutagenesis, in vitro and in vivo complex assembly, EMSA, complementation of patient cells

timeline.finding: Rfx3-deficient mice have stunted nodal cilia and frequent left-right asymmetry defects, extending the RFX-cilia link from nematodes to mammals.
timeline.methods: Knockout mice, expression analysis

timeline.finding: Rfx6 is required for islet cell differentiation downstream of Neurog3 in mice, and recessive human RFX6 mutations cause a neonatal diabetes syndrome, giving the family its first endocrine role.
timeline.methods: Mouse knockout, human linkage mapping and sequencing

timeline.finding: Two comparative-genomics surveys agree that RFX genes arose independently of cilia, but disagree on when X-box regulation of ciliary genes began: one places the convergence before the first metazoans, the other early in the animal lineage, with X-box footprints found only in animal ciliary genes.
timeline.methods: Comparative genomics, phylogenetic footprinting
timeline.open: Whether choanoflagellate RFX proteins regulate ciliary genes through X-boxes.

timeline.finding: ChIP-seq and RNA-seq in mouse ependymal cells show that RFX1, RFX2 and RFX3 occupy many of the same loci, while only RFX2 and RFX3 act, redundantly, in motile ciliogenesis.
timeline.methods: ChIP-seq, RNA-seq, mouse mutants
timeline.open: What makes shared occupancy produce paralogue-specific function.

open: When X-box control of ciliary genes arose is disputed: Chu and colleagues argue the RFX-ciliary gene convergence predates metazoans because both co-occur in choanoflagellates, while Piasecki and colleagues find X-box footprints only in animal ciliary genes and place the rewiring early in the animal lineage.

How RFX5 reads DNA in its native complex is not settled by the motif data: the in vitro-supported RFX5 models here (JASPAR MA0510.3, HOCOMOCO grade A) are full GTTGCCATGGCAAC palindromes like those of RFX1-3, yet RFX5 does not dimerize with other RFX proteins and binds the MHC class II X box as part of the RFX5-RFXAP-RFXANK complex.

Whether RFX6 and RFX7 genuinely prefer single half-sites is unclear: the RFX7 in vitro model is a half-site (GTTGCYANG), but the RFX6 models are either ChIP-only or inferred from guinea pig, so a weak second half-site could be a property of the protein or of the data.

families.name: MYC / MAX / MXD
families.def: Canonical E-box CACGTG. MYC, MYCN, MAX, MXI1, MXD1-4, MNT, MGA, MLX, MLXIP, MLXIPL.
families.short: MYC, MYCN and their obligate partner MAX bind the canonical E-box CACGTG as bHLH-LZ heterodimers, and the same site is bound by MAX homodimers and by the MAX-associated repressors MXD1-4, MXI1, MNT and MGA, which recruit Sin3-HDAC complexes. The related MLX branch (MondoA, ChREBP) reads an E-box with T/A flanks. The motif is a 6-bp palindrome, two CAC half-sites read by a histidine-glutamate-arginine triad in each basic region. MYC-MAX occupancy is concentrated in CpG-island promoters of already-active genes, which is why MYC is central to the growth program and why it is one of the most frequently activated oncogenes in human cancer. No member of the network can be told from another by sequence alone.
families.long:
## The factors

This family is the MYC/MAX/MXD network: three MYC paralogues (MYC, MYCN, MYCL), their obligate partner MAX, the MAX-binding repressors MXD1-MXD4 (MAD1, MXI1, MAD3, MAD4), MNT and MGA, and the MAX-like hub MLX with its partners MLXIP (MondoA) and MLXIPL (ChREBP). All carry a basic helix-loop-helix leucine zipper (bHLH-LZ) domain: two helices joined by a loop, with the zipper extending helix 2 into a parallel coiled coil that sets dimer choice. MYC proteins do not homodimerize appreciably and reach DNA essentially only as MYC-MAX heterodimers [PMID:2006410]; MAX homodimerizes and is the common partner for MXD proteins, MNT and MGA, which carry a Sin3-interaction domain and convert the same site from activation to repression [PMID:8425218,9000049]. MGA is unusual in combining the bHLH-LZ with a separate T-box DNA-binding domain [PMID:10601024]. MLX heterodimerizes with MondoA and ChREBP [PMID:11073985], which are nutrient sensors rather than growth effectors. MAX, MNT and MLX are broadly expressed; MYC tracks proliferation, MYCN is largely neural and embryonic, MYCL is restricted. The atlas assigns 30 motifs here (9 JASPAR, 12 HOCOMOCO, 8 CIS-BP, 1 Vierstra archetype) across nine symbols with motifs of their own: MAX, MYC, MYCN, MXI1, MXD4, MNT, MLX, MLXIP, MLXIPL. Family cohesion is 0.90 and the medoid is MAX (MA0058.4).

## The motif

The canonical site is the 6-bp palindrome CACGTG, one CAC half-site per monomer [PMID:2251503,8479534]. The Max-DNA co-crystal showed how it is read: each monomer inserts its basic region into the major groove and reads one half-site through a histidine-glutamate-arginine triad [PMID:8479534]. In the Max, Myc-Max and Mad-Max structures the histidine hydrogen-bonds the outer guanine, the glutamate accepts a bond from the cytosine of CAC and packs against the methyl group of the inner thymine, and the arginine hydrogen-bonds the N7 of the guanine in the central CpG while contacting the C5 of its cytosine; methylation of that cytosine lowers MAX affinity for the E-box [PMID:27903915]. The two heterodimers resemble the Max homodimer closely, and partner choice is set by the leucine zipper rather than the basic region, so MYC-MAX, MAX-MAX and MXD-MAX read one motif [PMID:12553908]. Single substitutions in the basic region can switch preference between CACGTG and neighbouring E-boxes, which is why closely related bHLH proteins differ far more in flanks than in core. Information beyond the core sits mainly at the two flanking positions [PMID:25287278]: MYC and MYCN favour C and G immediately outside (CCACGTGG), whereas the MLX branch favours T and A (ATCACGTGAT), the same preference that defines USF and MITF/TFE. Flanking effects are largely a DNA-shape effect rather than direct base contact. The family also tolerates lower-affinity variants - CATGTG, CACGCG, CATGCG - and one HOCOMOCO MAX model is a CATGTG class-A-like variant while another is a CACGTG dimer with a 3-bp gap. ChREBP does not work through a bare E-box at all: its functional element, the carbohydrate response element, is two E-box-like half-sites separated by five base pairs. No member of this family is distinguishable from any other by sequence.

## Where it acts

MYC-MAX occupancy is overwhelmingly promoter-proximal, in CpG islands and nucleosome-depleted, already-active regions rather than distal enhancers [PMID:12695333]; genome-wide mapping in B cells and in fibroblasts found thousands of bound regions strongly enriched for CpG islands, with only a fraction containing a canonical E-box [PMID:17093053,25043028,25287278]. A 6-bp palindrome is expected roughly once every 4 kb, several hundred thousand times in a 3-Gb genome; CpG depletion in mammalian DNA lowers the real CACGTG count, but it remains orders of magnitude above the number of sites any single factor occupies. Occupancy therefore tracks promoter accessibility and MYC dose [PMID:12695333,25287278]. As MYC levels rise it spreads from high-affinity promoters into weaker and more distal sites [PMID:12695333,23021215], the behaviour described as promoter invasion or, in the amplifier model, as general amplification of already-expressed genes [PMID:23021215,23021216].

## Biology and disease

MYC-MAX output is the growth program: ribosome biogenesis, nucleotide and glucose metabolism, and cell-cycle entry, opposed at the same sites by MXD-MAX, MNT-MAX and MGA-MAX repression [PMID:22464321,9000049]. The MLX branch is metabolic: MondoA responds to glucose-6-phosphate, and ChREBP drives hepatic lipogenic genes in response to glucose. MYC is among the most frequently activated oncogenes in human cancer, by IGH translocation in Burkitt lymphoma, by amplification in many carcinomas, and by MYCN amplification in high-risk neuroblastoma [PMID:22464321]. Whether high MYC changes which genes are expressed or mainly how much is a genuine and unsettled disagreement: amplification models argue for near-uniform scaling of active genes [PMID:23021215,23021216], while selective-regulation studies report distinct activated and repressed target sets and tumour-specific profiles [PMID:25043028].

## Reading a hit

A CACGTG match tells you the sequence is a canonical E-box, not that MYC binds it. USF1/2, MITF/TFE3/TFEB, CLOCK-BMAL1, HIF-ARNT, SREBP and BHLHE40/41 all read the same core; flanks shift the odds but do not resolve the factor. Within this family, MYC, MYCN, MAX, MXI1, MXD4 and MNT share one motif, so a hit identifies the network, not the member - which matters because activators and repressors are both in it. MYC ChIP-derived models are additionally biased toward active CpG-island promoters, and a large share of MYC peaks have no E-box at all, so ChIP-only models partly encode promoter context [PMID:17093053,25287278]. Prefer in vitro-supported HOCOMOCO models (S/M evidence) when the question is "does this protein bind this sequence".
families.caveats: CACGTG is short, palindromic and shared across the bHLH class, so a single hit is weak evidence for anything specific. It cannot distinguish MYC from MAX, MXD, MNT or MLX, nor this family from USF, MITF/TFE, CLOCK-BMAL1, HIF-ARNT or SREBP. MYC ChIP-seq peaks are dominated by open, active CpG-island promoters and many contain no E-box, so ChIP-derived MYC models partly capture promoter context rather than intrinsic specificity. The CIS-BP MLXIP model is transferred from the mouse protein at 82% DNA-binding-domain identity, and one secondary HOCOMOCO MYCN model (aCGCGCgc) is not an E-box at all. Treat a hit as 'canonical E-box' and require expression, chromatin and direct binding data to name a factor.
