How far the doubled-site arrangement extends is unresolved: biochemistry shows the CP2-branch factor LSF needs directly repeated elements and binds as a tetramer while Grainyhead binds a single site as a dimer, yet the in vitro-supported HOCOMOCO GRHL1 and GRHL3 models are partly doubled too.

families.name: AP-2 (TFAP2)
families.def: GCCYGCRGGC. TFAP2A-E.
families.short: The five human TFAP2 proteins (TFAP2A-E, historically AP-2 alpha through epsilon) bind a pseudo-palindrome made of GCC and GGC triplets separated by exactly three bases. Each subunit contributes a basic region that inserts a loop into the major groove, and the two subunits are held together by a helix-span-helix domain; the factors are constitutive dimers even off DNA, and all paralogue combinations heterodimerize. The site is GC-rich and sits in GC-rich promoters and neural crest enhancers. TFAP2 factors behave as pioneer factors during neural crest specification, and mutations cause branchio-oculo-facial syndrome (TFAP2A) and Char syndrome (TFAP2B). A hit identifies the family, not a paralogue.
families.long:
## The factors

Five human genes encode this family: TFAP2A, TFAP2B, TFAP2C, TFAP2D and TFAP2E, still widely
called AP-2 alpha, beta, gamma, delta and epsilon. Each protein has an N-terminal proline- and
glutamine-rich activation domain [PMID:3063603,2010091], a basic region, and a C-terminal helix-span-helix (HSH)
dimerization domain: two amphipathic helices separated by a long span. The HSH domain drives
dimerization on its own and can be transplanted onto a foreign basic region, but it cannot bind
DNA without an adjacent basic region [PMID:1998122]. AP-2 is a dimer in solution as well as on DNA [PMID:2010091], and all of
the paralogue pairs can heterodimerize; in neural crest development TFAP2A switches partners from
TFAP2C to TFAP2B as specification proceeds, and the two heterodimers open different sets of
elements [PMID:31848212]. Expression is restricted rather than housekeeping: TFAP2A and TFAP2B in neural crest,
surface ectoderm, facial mesenchyme and kidney [PMID:1989904]; TFAP2C in trophoblast, germ cells and luminal
breast epithelium; TFAP2D mainly in retina and midbrain; TFAP2E in olfactory epithelium. TFAP2D
is the outlier, with a divergent basic region and weaker transactivation.

## The motif

The functional element is a pseudo-palindrome of two triplets, GCC and GGC, with a three-base
spacer: GCC(N3)GGC [PMID:37409559]. SELEX with AP-2 alpha also recovered GCC(N4)GGC and GCC(N3/4)GGG
sites [PMID:10373594], and the older consensus GCCYGCRGGC is an N4 form. The database 9-mers (GCCTGAGGC,
GCCTCAGGC) are N3; the longer models are not that core plus flanks, since the extra C and G sit inside
the triplets: GCCCYAGGGC is GCC(N4)GGC, and GCCCTBAGGGC reads as GCC(N4)GGG. The data consensus,
GCCTCAGGGCA, is a longer form (GCC(N4)GGC, or GCC(N3)GGG), so it differs from the literature's
GCC(N3)GGC in spacing, not only in flanks.
The crystal structure of the TFAP2A DBD-HSH tandem domain on DNA explains the geometry: the two
flat amphipathic HSH helices stack against each other through hydrophobic contacts, and a
stabilized loop from each DBD inserts into one of two neighboring major grooves [PMID:37409559]. Because the two
loops are a fixed distance apart, spacer length, not just spacer sequence, determines binding: a
three-base gap is strongly preferred: TFAP2A bound a four-base spacer about 18-fold more weakly and two-
or five-base spacers barely at all [PMID:37409559]. This makes the informative
positions the GCC and GGC triplets, with the central three bases nearly free (commonly written
YAG or TCA/TGA). The five paralogues are not separable from sequence. Every model in this family's
data carries the same GCC and GGC/GGG triplets (7.5-14.5 bits); they differ in spacer length, but
TFAP2A, TFAP2B and TFAP2C each have models of more than one spacing.

## Where it acts

AP-2 sites are GC-rich, so they are enriched in GC-rich and CpG-island promoters, where they can
be hard to distinguish from SP/KLF GC-boxes on loose models. The functionally important sites,
however, are largely distal: TFAP2A occupies thousands of enhancers at the neural plate border and
in specified neural crest, acting as a pioneer factor that remodels chromatin ahead of the
lineage program [PMID:31848212]. In melanocytes TFAP2 paralogues bind in parallel with MITF at pigmentation genes [PMID:28249010].
In luminal breast cancer cells TFAP2C co-occupies enhancers with estrogen receptor and FOXA1 and
regulates ESR1 itself [PMID:24469049]. Co-occurring motifs therefore depend on the tissue: SOX and PAX motifs in
neural crest, MITF E-boxes in melanocytes, ERE and forkhead sites in breast. AP-2 sites are common
enough in GC-rich sequence that a genome-wide scan returns very large numbers of matches; the
constraint on real occupancy is TFAP2 expression, which is narrow.

## Biology and disease

Tfap2a-null mice fail cranial neural tube closure and have severe craniofacial defects, matching
AP-2's expression in ectoderm and migrating cranial neural crest [PMID:8622765,1989904]. In humans, heterozygous TFAP2A
mutations, mostly missense changes in the basic region and HSH domain, cause branchio-oculo-facial
syndrome: cervical and infra-auricular skin defects, ocular anomalies, cleft lip or palate, and
sometimes inner ear malformation and deafness [PMID:18423521]. Mutations in TFAP2B cause Char syndrome, a dominant
condition combining patent ductus arteriosus, a distinctive face and hand anomalies, with a
genotype-phenotype relationship that tracks with how much DNA binding is lost [PMID:10802654]. TFAP2C is amplified
and overexpressed in a subset of breast cancers, where it governs the luminal epithelial phenotype
and hormone response and higher expression predicts worse outcome on anti-hormonal therapy [PMID:24469049].
TFAP2A and TFAP2C are also required in trophoblast and germ cell programs. A structural survey of
disease mutations concluded that reduced or abolished DNA binding is the primary mechanism in
TFAP2-associated disease [PMID:37409559].

## Reading a hit

A GCC(N3)GGC match tells you that a TFAP2 dimer could bind, and nothing about which one. The five
paralogues share one matrix; assign a member from expression, and remember that the biologically
active species is often a heterodimer, so the question may have no single answer. Check the spacer
before believing a match: two bases is a poor site, while four binds more weakly than three in vitro
but was recovered by SELEX and is common in the models here, so it is weaker evidence, not a non-site
[PMID:37409559,10373594]. Permissive scanners report all of these spacings. Because
the site is GC-rich, the main false-positive risk is confusion with other GC-binding families. A
loose AP-2 model will score on SP1/KLF GC-boxes (GGGGCGGGG) and on CpG-island sequence generally;
conversely, GC-box models score on AP-2 sites. Require the discontinuous GCC...GGC arrangement
rather than a continuous GC run before calling a hit AP-2. The evidence base here is comparatively
clean: HOCOMOCO models for AP2A and AP2C are grade A with combined ChIP-seq and in vitro selection
(PSM), and the AP2B and AP2E models rest on in vitro selection alone (SM), so the family's
specificity does not depend on ChIP data. The one provenance caveat is the CIS-BP TFAP2D entry,
which is transferred from a mouse protein at 80% DNA-binding-domain identity [PMID:25215497].
families.caveats: All five TFAP2 paralogues share one matrix and heterodimerize freely, so a hit identifies the family only. Spacer length is part of the motif: three bases is the canonical, tightest-binding form, four is weaker but was recovered by selection and appears in many models here, and two is a poor site. The biggest practical risk is GC-richness. AP-2 models cross-score with SP/KLF GC-boxes and with CpG-island sequence, so a GC-rich promoter hit needs the discontinuous GCC...GGC arrangement to be credible. Genome-wide matches vastly outnumber occupied sites because TFAP2 expression is narrow. In vitro evidence supports the core specificity; the CIS-BP TFAP2D model is inferred from mouse at 80% domain identity.

timeline.finding: SELEX and missing-phosphate analysis of AP-2 alpha show a flexible protein-DNA complex that accepts three related site classes, GCC N3 GGC, GCC N4 GGC and GCC N3/4 GGG, rather than a single fixed spacing.
timeline.methods: SELEX, missing-phosphate and nucleotide competition analysis

timeline.methods: X-ray crystallography, binding assays with spacer variants, mutant analysis
timeline.open: How the strict-spacer model accommodates the N4 and GGG-type sites selected in 1999.

open: How strict the spacer is remains disputed: the 2023 TFAP2A structure and binding data favor a fixed three-base spacer, while 1999 SELEX with AP-2 alpha recovered GCC N4 GGC and GCC N3/4 GGG sites as well, and the extended database models (GCCCTBAGGGC) read as GCC N4 GGG rather than GCC N3 GGC.

Whether TFAP2 heterodimers differ in DNA specificity is unknown: TFAP2A/B and TFAP2A/C heterodimers occupy different elements in neural crest, but every measured paralogue model is the same matrix, so the difference may come from partner availability and chromatin rather than sequence.
TFAP2D has a divergent basic region, yet its only model here is inferred from a mouse protein at 80% domain identity, so whether TFAP2D shares the family specificity has not been measured.

families.name: MYB / MYB-like
families.def: MBS YAACKG. MYB, MYBL1, MYBL2; plus Myb/SANT archetypes (SNAPC4, MYPOP, TERF1/2 telobox).
families.short: MYB factors bind the Myb binding site (MBS), a six-base element written YAACKG, through two or three imperfect ~52-residue repeats that each fold into a helix-turn-helix-like unit. Humans have three true MYB proteins: MYB (c-Myb), MYBL1 (A-Myb) and MYBL2 (B-Myb). Only repeats R2 and R3 are required for sequence-specific binding, and their recognition helices sit side by side in one major groove. MYB proteins control hematopoietic progenitor expansion, spermatogenesis and, for MYBL2, mitotic gene expression through the MuvB complex. MYB is duplicated in T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia and fused to NFIB in adenoid cystic carcinoma. This family key also collects Myb/SANT-fold archetypes whose proteins are not MYB factors and do not bind the MBS, which is the main source of confusion here.
families.long:
## The factors

Three human genes encode true MYB transcription factors: MYB (c-Myb), MYBL1 (A-Myb) and MYBL2
(B-Myb); HOCOMOCO labels them MYB, MYBA and MYBB, and the Vierstra archetypes use the group
name MYBL. Their DNA-binding domain is built from three imperfect repeats of about 52 residues,
R1, R2 and R3, each containing three regularly spaced tryptophans and folding into a
helix-turn-helix-related unit [PMID:8415700,7954830]. R1 is dispensable: R2 and R3 alone give specific binding [PMID:8415700,7954830], which is
why plant and fungal homologues are usually R2R3 proteins. MYB is expressed in immature
hematopoietic cells, colonic crypt epithelium and some neural progenitors; MYBL1 is highest in
testis and germinal-center B cells; MYBL2 is a cell-cycle gene, rising in S phase and peaking at
G2/M. This atlas key is deliberately broader than the three MYB proteins, because the Myb/SANT
fold is reused by proteins that are not MYB factors. In the current data those extras are DMTF1
(DMP1, a cyclin D-binding Myb-like protein) [PMID:8887674], MYPOP (a Myb-related protein that partners profilin)
and TTF1 (the RNA polymerase I transcription termination factor, not the thyroid factor NKX2-1,
which is unfortunately also called TTF-1) [PMID:7597036]. TERF1 and TERF2, whose telobox is a Myb-like repeat,
are held in a separate TELOBOX family here; SNAPC4, which uses Myb repeats to bind the snRNA
proximal sequence element, has no motif in these databases. The SANT domain itself, found in
chromatin remodelers and corepressors, has the Myb fold but is thought to read histone tails
rather than DNA sequence [PMID:15040448].

## The motif

The literature consensus for the MBS is YAACKG, six bases, usually quoted as PyAAC(G/T)G [PMID:3185713]. The
invariant part is AAC followed by G or T then G; the identity comes from the recognition helix of
R3 inserting into the major groove with R2 packed alongside, so the two repeats read one
continuous site [PMID:7954830,8415700] and the cavity in R2 rearranges on binding. Database renderings differ mainly by
strand and by doubling. JASPAR MYB (MA0100.4) and the corresponding CIS-BP model give CAACTG,
which is YAACKG with Y=C and K=T; the HOCOMOCO ChIP model GGCAGTTG is the same site read on the
other strand. The data consensus for the family as a whole, CCGTTA, is the reverse complement of
TAACGG, again the same core. In vitro selection on MYBL1 and MYBL2 returns longer, near-palindromic
models such as AACCGTTAACGG and CCGTTAAACSG [PMID:23332764]: these are two MBS half-sites in inverted orientation
and reflect how the isolated domains bind selected DNA, not a different specificity. Within the
three MYB proteins nothing is separable by sequence. The non-MYB members are separable, and they
are not MBS models: DMTF1's grade-A model, backed by ChIP-seq and four in vitro assays, is CCCGGATG [PMID:8887674], MYPOP's is GCGCAA, and
TTF1's is the rDNA Sal box terminator [PMID:7597036], recognizable by its internal GACCAG. Their nearest
neighbours across the four databases fall outside this family, and the family's cohesion (0.72
over 22 motifs) is lower than for a single-specificity family for exactly that reason.

## Where it acts

MYB sites are short and occur in both promoters and enhancers. In hematopoietic cells c-Myb
occupies thousands of sites and cooperates with CEBP factors, RUNX1, GATA2 and the coactivators
CBP/p300; classic targets include MYC, KIT, CCNB1 and, in T cells, TCR genes. MYBL2 behaves
differently: it is recruited to mitotic promoters mainly as a subunit of the MYB-MuvB (MMB)
complex, which hands over from the repressive DREAM complex at G1/S [PMID:22391450], and MuvB's own sequence
anchor is the CHR element read by LIN54, not the MBS [PMID:22064854]. Consequently much of the MYBL2 signal in
chromatin immunoprecipitation sits on CHR-containing promoters where the underlying sequence is
not a Myb site at all [PMID:22064854,22391450]. TTF1 sites are confined to the rDNA repeat, where the Sal box terminates
Pol I transcription [PMID:7597036], so its motif is genomically almost absent outside the rDNA and its
nucleolar-organizer copies.

## Biology and disease

Mice lacking c-Myb die around embryonic day 15 with a failure of fetal hepatic hematopoiesis [PMID:1709592], the
sharpest demonstration that MYB is needed for progenitor expansion rather than for lineage
identity. Mybl1-null male mice are sterile with a meiotic arrest, and Mybl2 loss is lethal at the
blastocyst stage. In cancer, MYB is more often amplified, translocated or driven by a new enhancer
than mutated: tandem duplication of MYB occurs in T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia [PMID:17435759], and a
recurrent MYB-NFIB fusion defines most adenoid cystic carcinomas of salivary gland and breast [PMID:19841262].
MYBL2 overexpression is a component of proliferation signatures in many tumors and is largely a
readout of cell-cycle activity.

## Reading a hit

A YAACKG match is six informative bases and will occur by chance roughly every few hundred base
pairs on either strand, so a single hit is close to meaningless without other evidence. The three
MYB proteins cannot be separated from sequence, so a hit means "a MYB-family site" at best, and
expression context is what narrows it: MYB in immature hematopoietic cells, MYBL1 in testis and
germinal centers, MYBL2 in cycling cells. The bigger hazard in this key is the label. Several
members are Myb/SANT-fold proteins that do not bind the MBS, and a match scored against the
DMTF1, MYPOP or TTF1 models is a match to an unrelated sequence that happens to share the family
key. For MYBL2, treat ChIP-derived enrichment with care: recruitment through MuvB to CHR
elements means a B-Myb peak often marks a LIN54 site rather than a Myb site [PMID:22064854].
families.caveats: Two problems compound here. First, the MBS is six bases, so chance matches are abundant and the three MYB paralogues are indistinguishable by sequence. Second, this key is a fold class, not a single specificity: DMTF1 (CCCGGATG), MYPOP (GCGCAA) and TTF1 (the rDNA Sal box) are Myb/SANT-fold proteins whose motifs are unrelated to the MBS, and the CIS-BP MYPOP model is transferred from mouse. The family cohesion of 0.72 reflects this mixture. For MYBL2, ChIP-derived signal is frequently recruitment through the MuvB complex onto LIN54's CHR element rather than direct MBS binding, so a B-Myb peak is not evidence of a Myb site.

families.name: NFE2 / NRF / BACH (ARE)
families.def: Antioxidant/electrophile response element TGACTCAGC. NFE2, NFE2L1/L2/L3, BACH1, BACH2.
families.short: This family covers the cap-n-collar (CNC) basic region-leucine zipper activators NFE2, NFE2L1 (NRF1) and NFE2L2 (NRF2) together with the BTB-bZIP repressors BACH1 and BACH2. None of them binds DNA alone: each must heterodimerize with a small Maf protein (MAFF, MAFG or MAFK). The resulting element is the antioxidant or electrophile response element, TGACTCAGCA, an AP-1-like TGAC half-site read by the CNC or BACH subunit joined to a GC-extended half read by the small Maf. It is therefore a one-sided version of the Maf recognition element. NRF2 drives the cytoprotective gene battery and is constitutively activated by KEAP1 loss in several cancers; NFE2 is required for platelet formation; BACH1 is a heme sensor and BACH2 a lymphocyte regulator. Members cannot be distinguished from sequence.
families.long:
## The factors

The CNC subfamily takes its name from the Drosophila cap-n-collar protein and comprises NFE2 (p45), NFE2L1 (NRF1), NFE2L2 (NRF2) and NFE2L3 (NRF3). The BTB-bZIP proteins BACH1 and BACH2 read the same element but carry a BTB domain and act as repressors. A defining property of both sets is that they cannot bind DNA as monomers or as homodimers: every functional complex is a heterodimer with one of the small Maf proteins, which supply half of the DNA contact [PMID:8107826,8887638]. Regulation differs by member. NRF2 is continuously ubiquitinated through a KEAP1-CUL3 complex and degraded; electrophiles and oxidants modify reactive KEAP1 cysteines, NRF2 escapes degradation and accumulates in the nucleus [PMID:9887101,29717933]. BACH1 is a heme sensor: heme displaces Bach1 from MafK-occupied enhancers, after which NRF2 binds the same sites [PMID:14747657], and it also triggers Crm1-dependent nuclear export of Bach1 [PMID:15175654]. Expression is uneven. NFE2 is restricted to erythroid and megakaryocytic cells, NFE2L1 and NFE2L2 are broad, BACH1 is broad, and BACH2 is concentrated in B and T lymphocytes. NFE2L3 has no motif model in any of the four source collections and so appears nowhere in this atlas. One naming hazard: NFE2L1 is routinely called NRF1, but an unrelated factor, nuclear respiratory factor 1 (gene symbol NRF1), shares that abbreviation and binds a GC-rich palindrome unrelated to this element.

## The motif

The element was originally defined functionally, as the core required for antioxidant-inducible transcription of rat glutathione S-transferase Ya and NAD(P)H:quinone reductase: 5'-(A/G)GTGACNNNGC-3' [PMID:1646813]. In the sequences that actually occur, the variable middle is almost always TCA, giving the 10 or 11 base consensus TGACTCAGCA, sometimes written with the 5-prime A as ATGACTCAGCA. Read the other way round it is TGCTGAGTCAT, the consensus derived from the 21 models collected here: the same element on the opposite strand, with models differing in how much flank they retain. The small Maf subunit reads the GC extension through Arg57 and Asn61 of the Maf basic region, the same residues that read both flanks of a full MARE [PMID:19797082]. The CNC subunit reads the other half, and the residue that makes the difference is Ala502 of NRF2, which sits where Maf proteins have a tyrosine; replacing it with tyrosine makes NRF2-MafG bind like a MafG homodimer and shifts its target gene set [PMID:17875642]. So the ARE is a MARE with one flank removed, and a single residue in the CNC partner explains why. Common variants include an AT-rich 3-prime extension (GCATTT or GCANTTT) present in many small-Maf-partnered models, and a truncated TGACTCAT form that is simply the AP-1 TRE and carries no Maf-side information at all. JASPAR BACH1 MA1633.2 and the CIS-BP NFE2L1 model are of this second kind, which is why their nearest neighbours fall outside the family. No member is distinguishable: NFE2, NFE2L1, NFE2L2, BACH1 and BACH2 give one motif, and the small Maf partner is likewise unidentifiable.

## Where it acts

AREs occur at promoters and enhancers of the cytoprotective battery: NQO1, GCLC and GCLM, HMOX1, TXN, GPX2, SLC7A11, glutathione S-transferases, and proteasome subunit genes [PMID:29717933]. ChIP-seq of Nrf2 in Keap1-null mouse embryonic fibroblasts, integrated with expression data, defined 645 basal and 654 inducible direct targets with 244 in common [PMID:20460467], so the responsive set is a few hundred genes rather than thousands. The erythroid NF-E2 site of the beta-globin HS2 enhancer is a tandem ARE and MARE [PMID:7937919]. The same elements are occupied competitively: a BACH-small Maf dimer keeps them repressed until heme or an electrophile replaces the repressor with an activator [PMID:14747657], so occupancy and output are decoupled. Co-occurrence with AP-1 sites is common because the core is shared.

## Biology and disease

NRF2 is the main transcriptional response to electrophiles and oxidants, and the pathway protects against chemical carcinogenesis, emphysema and inflammatory injury in mouse models [PMID:20460467]. The same pathway is subverted in tumours: KEAP1 mutations and NFE2L2 mutations in the KEAP1-binding Neh2 domain constitutively activate NRF2 in non-small-cell lung cancer and elsewhere, where it supports growth and confers chemotherapy and radiation resistance [PMID:17020408,29717933]. NFE2/p45-null mice fail to produce platelets despite intact thrombopoietin signaling [PMID:7774011], and somatic NFE2 mutations occur in myeloproliferative neoplasms [PMID:23589569]. BACH2 haploinsufficiency causes a human immunodeficiency with defective B and T cell function, a phenotype linked to loss of a super-enhancer-driven expression level [PMID:28530713].

## Reading a hit

Every model in this family is, by construction, a heterodimer motif: the CNC and BACH proteins cannot bind DNA alone, so roughly half the information in any NRF2 or BACH1 matrix belongs to a small Maf. A ChIP-derived NRF2 motif is therefore not evidence that NRF2 contacts those GC bases. The practical test is the 3-prime GC. TGACTCAGC is an ARE; TGACTCA alone is an AP-1 TRE and cannot be assigned here; GC on both sides is a full MARE and belongs to MAF. Because the families are nested this way, a 7 or 8 base match is not separable among AP-1, NFE2/BACH and MAF. Two entries in this collection carry motifs that do not belong: CIS-BP M08184, labelled BACH1, is a CACGTG E-box whose nearest neighbours are USF motifs, and JASPAR BACH2 MA1470.2 is a long CRE-like AANCATGACGTCATGNTT that matches outside the family. Six of the eight HOCOMOCO models here are ChIP-only (evidence P, grade B); only the NFE2 and BACH2 models add in vitro support. Finally, a hit says nothing about direction: the same element is bound by BACH1 or BACH2 to repress and by NRF2 or NFE2 to activate, and sequence cannot tell you which is present.
families.caveats: Read every matrix in this family as a heterodimer motif, because the CNC and BACH proteins do not bind DNA without a small Maf; half of the information is the partner's. The family is nested between two siblings: remove the 3-prime GC and you have an AP-1 TRE, add GC on the 5-prime side and you have a full MARE, so short matches cannot be assigned. Member identity is unavailable, and so is direction, since activators (NFE2, NRF1, NRF2) and repressors (BACH1, BACH2) compete for the same sites. Two entries here carry motifs that belong elsewhere, one an E-box and one a long CRE. NFE2L3 has no model in any source database, and NFE2L1 shares the abbreviation NRF1 with an unrelated factor.

open: Whether CNC and BACH proteins bind DNA without a Maf partner is in doubt: the obligate-heterodimer view holds that they cannot, yet the HT-SELEX models for NFE2 and BACH2 here, and JASPAR NFE2 MA0841.2 and BACH2 MA1101.3, recover a palindromic ATGASTCATG with no Maf-side GC extension, so whether such homodimer-like binding happens in cells or only in selection assays is unresolved.

families.name: Steroid receptors (GR/MR/PR/AR)
families.def: Inverted repeat of AGAACA (ARE/GRE) spaced by 3 bp. NR3C1/GR, NR3C2/MR, PGR, AR.
families.short: The steroid receptors - glucocorticoid receptor (GR/NR3C1), mineralocorticoid receptor (MR/NR3C2), progesterone receptor (PGR) and androgen receptor (AR) - are hormone-activated transcription factors that bind DNA as homodimers on a 15 bp inverted repeat: two copies of the hexamer AGAACA facing each other across a 3 bp spacer, written AGAACAnnnTGTTCT. All four receptors read essentially the same element, so a match identifies the steroid-receptor group and not a particular receptor. Which receptor occupies a site in a given cell is decided by hormone availability, receptor expression, pioneer factors such as FOXA1 and pre-existing chromatin accessibility, not by sequence. These elements carry the transcriptional response to cortisol, aldosterone, progesterone and androgens, and they are the DNA end of drugs from dexamethasone to the antiandrogens used in prostate cancer.
families.long:
## The factors

Four receptors share this element: GR (NR3C1), MR (NR3C2), PGR and AR, the oxosteroid branch of the nuclear receptor superfamily. Each has an N-terminal activation region, a C4 double-zinc-finger DNA-binding domain (DBD), a flexible hinge and a C-terminal ligand-binding domain that binds cortisol, aldosterone, progesterone or dihydrotestosterone respectively. DNA binding is by a homodimer: the first zinc finger contributes the recognition helix that enters the major groove of one half-site, and a loop in the second zinc finger (the D-box) forms the interface between the two subunits [PMID:1865905]. GR and MR are expressed in most tissues; PGR is largely restricted to uterus, breast, ovary and parts of the brain, AR to prostate, seminal vesicle, muscle, skin and bone. The four collections here contribute 21 models, labelled AR, NR3C1, NR3C2 and PGR.

## The motif

The response element is an inverted repeat of a hexamer with a 3 bp spacer, abbreviated IR3: AGAACA nnn TGTTCT, 15 bp and almost exactly palindromic [PMID:2891134,20304998]. Information is concentrated in the two hexamers; the three spacer bases are weakly constrained but not free, and selection in a receptor-competitive setting showed that spacer and flanking positions are chosen asymmetrically and contribute to receptor preference rather than to raw affinity (Nelson et al. 1999) [PMID:10598584]. The crystal structure of the GR DBD dimer on DNA established how the recognition helix reads the half-site (Luisi et al. 1991) [PMID:1865905]. Which hexamer a receptor reads is set by three residues in the first zinc finger: swapping them converts GR specificity to that of the estrogen receptor, which reads AGGTCA instead, while five residues in the stem of the second finger set the tolerated half-site spacing (Umesono and Evans 1989) [PMID:2500251].

The models here have a systematically degenerate 5' half-site. The GR and MR matrices from JASPAR and HOCOMOCO read AG(A/T)ACAnnnTGTTCC, often written in the literature as GGTACAnnnTGTTCT, which is why the family's data consensus is AGWACAtnaTGTtCc rather than the symmetrical form quoted above; both describe the same element, one from selected high-affinity sites and one from averaged genomic occupancy. AR has one partly private variant: some natural androgen-selective elements are direct rather than inverted repeats of the hexamer with a 3 bp gap (ADR3), and the AR DBD binds them head-to-head using an extended dimer interface (Shaffer et al. 2004; Denayer et al. 2010) [PMID:15037741,20304998]. In practice this discriminates weakly. Single base changes inside the hexamer alter GR conformation and activity, not only affinity, so the element behaves as a sequence-specific allosteric ligand (Meijsing et al. 2009; Weikum et al. 2017) [PMID:19372434,28053348]. Several HOCOMOCO models here are single half-sites (TGTTC, AGAACA, GWACA) carrying 4-8 bits; alone they have almost no specificity.

## Where it acts

Steroid receptor sites are overwhelmingly distal enhancers rather than promoters, and are strongly cell-type restricted. Up to 95% of de novo GR binding after hormone falls in chromatin that was already accessible, so the cistrome is largely pre-specified by cell identity, with sequence a secondary contribution (John et al. 2011) [PMID:21258342]. AR occupancy depends on tissue-specific pioneer factors: FOXA1 both opens AR sites and masks others, and its depletion redistributes AR binding wholesale (Sahu et al. 2011; Pihlajamaa et al. 2014) [PMID:21915096,24451200]. Composite arrangements are common - a GRE next to AP-1, NF-kB, STAT5 or FOX sites, and in liver next to CEBP and HNF4 motifs. GR also represses genes from a distinct negative element (nGRE) that is not an IR3 and is bound by two non-dimerizing monomers (Hudson et al. 2013) [PMID:23222642], and can act without touching DNA by tethering to AP-1 and NF-kB [PMID:28053348].

## Biology and disease

These elements carry the metabolic and anti-inflammatory programs of cortisol, salt and water handling by aldosterone, the uterine and mammary response to progesterone, and male sexual development and prostate growth. GR-null mice die perinatally from failure of lung maturation. Loss-of-function NR3C1 variants cause generalized glucocorticoid resistance; NR3C2 loss causes pseudohypoaldosteronism type 1, and an NR3C2 gain-of-function variant causes early-onset hypertension. AR loss-of-function causes androgen insensitivity syndrome, and CAG-repeat expansion in AR causes spinal and bulbar muscular atrophy. In cancer, AR amplification, point mutation and the AR-V7 splice variant drive castration-resistant prostate cancer, PGR status is a standard breast cancer biomarker, and glucocorticoids acting through GR remain part of lymphoid leukemia regimens.

## Reading a hit

A match says a steroid receptor could bind, not which one. The full-length GR, MR, PGR and AR matrices in this collection mostly sit within 0.89-1.00 of each other, so sequence cannot assign the receptor; ligand, receptor expression, cell type and cofactors can. Because roughly 10-12 of the 15 positions carry information, exact consensus IR3s are rare (order 10^2 per haploid genome) but sites within one or two mismatches number in the tens of thousands, far more than are occupied in any one cell type, so intersect hits with accessibility data. Check the evidence code on HOCOMOCO models: in vitro entries (S, M, SM) support direct binding, while ChIP-only entries (P) can absorb neighbouring signal - ANDR.H14CORE.2.P.B here is a single half-ARE fused to an AT-rich element and matches other families better than its own. A GR or AR ChIP peak with no IR3 is not necessarily a failure: tethering to AP-1 and NF-kB is a documented mode of action.
families.caveats: Trust a good IR3 hit as evidence for the family, not for a receptor: the GR, MR, PGR and AR matrices here are near-identical, and even AR's direct-repeat preference separates them only weakly. Because the element tolerates mismatches, near-consensus sites occur tens of thousands of times genome-wide while only a fraction are ever bound, so a scan hit without accessibility, hormone treatment or ChIP support is weak evidence. Half-site-only models (TGTTC, AGAACA) should not be scanned genome-wide. ChIP-derived models can include a partner's signal, and these receptors also regulate genes by tethering to other factors, so motif presence is neither necessary nor sufficient.

timeline.finding: A 15 bp partially symmetric sequence from the tyrosine aminotransferase GRE is sufficient to confer both glucocorticoid and progesterone induction on a heterologous promoter, and point mutations affect both responses alike: the first evidence that two steroid receptors read one element.
timeline.methods: Oligonucleotide reporter assays, point mutagenesis
timeline.open: Whether androgen and mineralocorticoid receptors use the same element, and how receptors sharing it achieve distinct target genes.

timeline.finding: Three residues at the base of the first zinc finger (the P-box) convert GR target specificity to that of the estrogen receptor, and five in the second finger change half-site spacing preference, localizing the determinants of hexamer identity and spacing.
timeline.methods: Domain-swap mutagenesis, transactivation assays

timeline.finding: Crystal structures of the GR DNA-binding domain show a DNA-induced dimer in adjacent major grooves; with one extra spacer base, one subunit binds specifically and the other nonspecifically, making the 3 bp spacing part of the element's identity.
timeline.methods: X-ray crystallography
timeline.open: Did not explain how GR, MR, PGR and AR, which share the recognition residues, select different genes.

timeline.finding: The AR DBD binds a selective direct-repeat element (ADR3) head-to-head through an extended dimer interface; PGR was later shown to read these elements too, but GR and MR do not.
timeline.methods: X-ray crystallography; mutational and binding analyses
timeline.open: How much of AR selectivity in tissues is due to ADR3-type elements rather than to chromatin context.

timeline.finding: GR binding sequences differing by a single base pair induce different receptor conformations and regulatory activity, so the element acts as an allosteric ligand and not only a docking site.
timeline.methods: X-ray crystallography, biochemical and cell-based reporter assays

timeline.finding: Genome-wide maps show that most de novo GR binding falls in chromatin that was already accessible, and that AR binding depends on the pioneer factor FOXA1; occupancy is set largely by cell identity rather than by sequence.
timeline.methods: DNase-seq, ChIP-seq, FOXA1 knockdown

timeline.finding: A negative GRE unrelated to the IR3 is bound by two GR monomers on a single site with strong negative cooperativity, a second DNA-binding mode that prevents dimerization and mediates direct repression.
timeline.methods: X-ray crystallography, binding thermodynamics
timeline.open: What fraction of glucocorticoid-repressed genes uses this element rather than tethering to AP-1 or NF-kB.

timeline.finding: In live cells, DNA binding triggers GR tetramerization on a tandem array of response elements, revising the long-held dimer model of the DNA-bound receptor.
timeline.methods: Number-and-brightness fluorescence imaging in live cells
timeline.open: How a tetramer is arranged on a single 15 bp element is not shown by any of the DNA-bound structures, which are dimers or monomers.

open: How AR achieves androgen-selective binding is disputed: structural and mutational work points to direct-repeat ADR3 elements read through an extended dimer interface, whereas genome-wide studies attribute most of the tissue-specific AR cistrome to pioneer factors such as FOXA1 and to pre-existing accessibility.

The oligomeric state of GR on chromatin is unsettled: crystal structures show a dimer on the IR3 and monomers on the negative GRE, while live-cell imaging indicates that DNA binding converts GR into a tetramer.

How much glucocorticoid repression goes through DNA binding is contested: tethering to AP-1 and NF-kB was the textbook mechanism, direct binding of GR monomers to negative GREs was later proposed as a widespread alternative, and the share of repressed genes explained by each is not agreed.

Selected high-affinity sites give a symmetric AGAACAnnnTGTTCT, whereas the genome-derived GR and MR models in the databases have a degenerate 5' half-site (AGWACA, often GGTACA); whether that asymmetry reflects a functional preference of natural elements or averaging over weaker occupied sites is not settled.

families.name: COUP-TF (NR2F)
families.def: DR1 AGGTCAAAGGTCA. NR2F1/2/6.
aka: chicken ovalbumin upstream promoter transcription factor
families.short: COUP-TFI (NR2F1), COUP-TFII (NR2F2) and EAR2 (NR2F6) are orphan nuclear receptors that bind DNA as homodimers, most often on a DR1: two AGGTCA half-sites in the same orientation separated by one base pair. Their distinguishing property is not a private consensus but promiscuity - the same dimer accommodates direct repeats with several spacings, plus inverted and everted arrangements of the same hexamer - which is how COUP-TFs compete with vitamin D, thyroid hormone and retinoic acid receptors for shared elements and repress them. The three paralogues share one motif and are also not separable from RXR homodimers, HNF4/TR2-TR4 or ERR sites. COUP-TFII specifies venous identity and is required for angiogenesis; NR2F1 mutations cause an optic atrophy and intellectual disability syndrome.
families.long:
## The factors

Three paralogues: NR2F1 (COUP-TFI, EAR3), NR2F2 (COUP-TFII, ARP1) and NR2F6 (EAR2). COUP-TF was purified as a factor binding upstream of the chicken ovalbumin gene and cloned as a member of the steroid receptor superfamily (Wang et al. 1989) [PMID:2739739]; NR2F1 and NR2F2 are among the most conserved nuclear receptors known (Lin et al. 2011) [PMID:21257780]. Each has a C4 double-zinc-finger DNA-binding domain (DBD) with a C-terminal extension and a ligand-binding domain; they bind as homodimers and can heterodimerize with RXR [PMID:1324415,1311101]. The ligand-free COUP-TFII ligand-binding domain, solved at 1.48 A, is in an autorepressed conformation, with helix alpha10 folded into the ligand pocket and the activation function-2 helix occupying the coactivator groove; retinoic acid at concentrations above physiological levels releases this, so COUP-TFII is ligand-regulatable but has no established endogenous ligand (Kruse et al. 2008) [PMID:18798693]. NR2F1 is expressed in brain, eye, inner ear and neural crest derivatives, NR2F2 in mesenchyme, venous endothelium and reproductive tract, NR2F6 broadly including lymphocytes. Twenty-one models fall in this family (JASPAR 7, HOCOMOCO 8, CIS-BP 3, Vierstra 3).

## The motif

The core arrangement is a DR1: AGGTCA-n-AGGTCA, 13 bp, seen in the data as AGGTCAAAGGTCA (JASPAR NR2F1 MA1537.2, HOCOMOCO COT1.H14CORE.1.PSM.A). The family's data consensus is the shorter AaAGGTCA, an extended single half-site, because many models here are half-sites with a 5' A or AA rather than full dimeric elements.

A counting convention trips people up constantly and is worth stating plainly. The original characterisation described COUP-TF elements as direct repeats of GGTCA with a 2 bp spacing [PMID:1324415]; modern usage calls the identical element a DR1, a direct repeat of AGGTCA with a 1 bp spacing [PMID:1311101]. The two descriptions differ only in whether the half-site is defined as a 5-mer or a 6-mer. Compare like with like before concluding that two sources disagree.

The real signature of this family is tolerance of geometry. Aligning natural COUP-TF elements showed that besides the predominant direct repeat, functional sites vary in both orientation and spacing of the GGTCA motif; the functional DNA-binding form is a dimer needing two half-sites, and the dimer undergoes a substantial structural adaptation to accommodate these variants. The consequence is that COUP-TF can occupy the response elements of the vitamin D, thyroid hormone and retinoic acid receptors and down-regulate their hormonal induction (Cooney et al. 1992) [PMID:1324415]. The models in this collection reproduce that range: DR1 (NR2F1 MA1537.2), DR2 (NR2F6 MA0728.1, gAGGTCAAaAGGTCA), IR1 (NR2F1 MA1538.1 and NR2F6 MA1539.1, aAGGTCAnTGACCTt), IR2 (NR2F6.H14CORE.3.SM.B, AAGGTCAatGacC) and bare half-sites (AGGTCA, AAGGTCA).

Nothing here separates the paralogues: NR2F1, NR2F2 and NR2F6 models are 0.96-0.99 similar to each other. Worse, they are barely separable from other families - members' best match outside this family runs 0.89-0.98, and two of the three Vierstra archetypes assigned here are labelled NR2F/RXRG and NR2F/RXRA because COUP-TF and RXR footprints cluster together. Protein-binding microarrays did detect a polarity preference within the DR1 for COUP-TFII, as for HNF4A and RXRA homodimers (Fang et al. 2012) [PMID:22383578], but that is a quantitative preference, not a discriminator you can apply to a single hit.

## Where it acts

Mostly distal enhancers in mesenchyme and endothelium, with NR2F2 marking venous rather than arterial endothelium [PMID:15875024]. Functionally many COUP-TF sites are repressive, and the mechanism documented in detail is competition: occupying a DR element that another receptor needs (Cooney et al. 1992) [PMID:1324415,1311101]. COUP-TF motifs co-occur with SOX, FOX and GATA sites in neural and cardiovascular enhancers, and because the element is a plain DR1 they overlap physically with RXR-heterodimer and HNF4 elements in the same regions.

## Biology and disease

Nr2f2-null mouse embryos die around E10.5 with defective angiogenesis and heart development (Pereira et al. 1999) [PMID:10215630]. Deleting COUP-TFII in endothelium makes veins acquire arterial characteristics, including neuropilin 1 and Notch pathway markers, while ectopic expression fuses veins and arteries - COUP-TFII maintains vein identity by repressing Notch signalling (You et al. 2005) [PMID:15875024]. In tumour models COUP-TFII promotes growth and metastasis by supporting tumour angiogenesis (Qin et al. 2010) [PMID:20133706]. In humans, heterozygous NR2F1 point mutations and deletions cause Bosch-Boonstra-Schaaf optic atrophy syndrome, combining optic atrophy or hypoplasia with developmental delay and intellectual disability (Bosch et al. 2014) [PMID:24462372], and rare NR2F2 variants cause congenital heart defects, notably atrioventricular septal defects (Al Turki et al. 2014) [PMID:24702954].

## Reading a hit

A DR1 hit licenses very little. It does not name the paralogue, and it does not even name the family: RXR homodimers, PPAR:RXR, HNF4A and the TR2/TR4 heterodimer all use DR1, and their matrices in this atlas sit within 0.89-0.98 of the models here. Report the geometry you actually see - spacing and orientation - and state the counting convention you used, because a DR1 under one convention is a 2 bp-spaced repeat under another. Given about 11 informative positions in a 13 bp element, near-consensus DR1s occur tens of thousands of times per haploid genome, far more than any COUP-TF cistrome. Half-site-only models (eight of the twenty-one here read AGGTCA, gGGTCa, AAGGTCA or AaAGGTCA) should not be scanned genome-wide. Evidence codes help a little: NR2F1 and NR2F6 have grade A HOCOMOCO models with combined ChIP, HT-SELEX and methyl-SELEX support (PSM), so direct binding is not in doubt; what a hit cannot tell you is which NR2F protein, or whether a different DR1-binding receptor was there instead.
families.caveats: This is one of the least discriminating motifs in the atlas. NR2F1, NR2F2 and NR2F6 models are 0.96-0.99 similar to each other, and their best matches outside the family run 0.89-0.98 - RXR homodimers, PPAR:RXR, HNF4A and TR2/TR4 all bind the same DR1. Two of the three Vierstra archetypes here are named NR2F/RXRG and NR2F/RXRA for that reason. Eight of the twenty-one models are single half-sites. COUP-TF also binds DR, IR and everted arrangements with several spacings, so geometry constrains the candidates less than it does for most nuclear receptor families. Treat a hit as evidence that some DR1-binding nuclear receptor could bind, and use expression and chromatin data to go further.

timeline.finding: COUP-TF, a factor required for chicken ovalbumin promoter transcription that also binds the rat insulin promoter, is cloned and found to be a member of the steroid/thyroid hormone receptor superfamily.
timeline.methods: Protein purification and cDNA cloning, cell-free transcription
timeline.open: Its DNA-binding rules, and why two dissimilar promoter sites both bind it.

timeline.finding: RXR and COUP-TF both bind preferentially to a DR1, form heterodimers on it in vitro, and COUP-TF fully represses RXR-mediated activation in cells, filling the DR1 slot left by the 3-4-5 rule.
timeline.methods: In vitro DNA binding, cotransfection reporter assays

timeline.finding: COUP-TF binds as a dimer needing two GGTCA half-sites, but tolerates direct repeats and palindromes with different spacings, which lets it occupy vitamin D, thyroid hormone and retinoic acid receptor elements and repress their induction.
timeline.methods: In vitro binding to spacing and orientation variants, reporter assays
timeline.open: How a single dimer accommodates so many half-site geometries at the structural level.

timeline.finding: Deleting Nr2f2 is embryonic lethal with failed remodeling of the primitive capillary plexus and atria and sinus venosus arrested at the primitive tube stage, with Angiopoietin-1 down-regulated.
timeline.methods: Mouse knockout, histology, expression analysis

timeline.finding: COUP-TFII is expressed in venous but not arterial endothelium; removing it gives veins arterial markers and Notch signalling, and ectopic expression fuses veins and arteries, so vein identity is actively specified rather than a default state.
timeline.methods: Endothelial conditional knockout, transgenic ectopic expression

timeline.finding: The 1.48 Å ligand-free structure of the COUP-TFII ligand-binding domain is autorepressed, with helix alpha10 bent into the pocket and the AF-2 helix in the coactivator groove; retinoic acid releases it, but only above physiological concentrations.
timeline.methods: X-ray crystallography, mutagenesis, coactivator recruitment and reporter assays
timeline.open: Whether an endogenous ligand exists at all, and why the receptor is constitutively active in cell lines despite the autorepressed structure.

timeline.finding: Protein-binding microarrays comparing COUP-TFII with HNF4A and RXRA detect a previously unrecognized polarity preference within the DR1 for all three homodimers, while only HNF4A has a private element.
timeline.methods: Protein-binding microarrays

timeline.finding: Heterozygous NR2F1 mutations and deletions cause optic atrophy with intellectual disability (Bosch-Boonstra-Schaaf syndrome), and rare NR2F2 variants cause congenital heart defects, establishing both paralogues as human disease genes.
timeline.methods: Exome sequencing and copy-number analysis in patient cohorts

open: Whether COUP-TFs have an endogenous ligand is unresolved: the COUP-TFII ligand-binding domain crystallizes in an autorepressed conformation that retinoic acid can release, but only at concentrations above physiological levels, while the receptor is constitutively active in cell lines.

How COUP-TFs repress most of their targets is not settled: competition for shared DR elements, sequestration of RXR into heterodimers, and active repression through the receptor's own repression domains have all been documented, and their relative contribution across the genome is unknown.

families.name: NFI (CTF/NF-1)
families.def: Palindromic TTGGC(N5)GCCAA. NFIA, NFIB, NFIC, NFIX.
families.short: Nuclear factor I proteins bind a 15-bp palindrome, TTGGC followed by five variable bases and GCCAA. Four human genes, NFIA, NFIB, NFIC and NFIX, encode DNA-binding domains that are about 85% identical, so they bind as homodimers or heterodimers in any combination and cannot be told apart from sequence. The domain adopts a SMAD MH1-like fold with a bound zinc ion, which is why the family is classified with SMAD rather than with any CCAAT-box factor. The full palindrome is highly informative, but NFI also occupies single TTGGC half-sites. NFI factors keep stem cell populations in glia, retina, skin and muscle on track, and are mutated in human overgrowth and brain malformation syndromes.
families.long:
## The factors

Four human genes, NFIA, NFIB, NFIC and NFIX, each produce several splice isoforms [PMID:10831836]. The
N-terminal region carries both the DNA-binding and the dimerization functions; the C-terminal
regions differ and carry the transactivation or repression activity [PMID:10831836]. Because the DNA-binding
domains are roughly 85% identical [PMID:41261119], all six pairwise heterodimers form in addition to the four
homodimers, and the effective factor in a cell is usually a mixture. A crystal and solution study
of NFI-X bound to its consensus palindrome showed a MH1-like fold with a structural Zn2+ site, an
obligate dimeric assembly, and the base contacts that set specificity; the authors present it as
prototypic for the whole family given the DBD identity [PMID:41261119]. This places NFI in the same structural
class as the SMADs, which is why TFClass and the archetype labels used here call the group
"SMAD/NF-1". Expression is broad but graded: NFIA and NFIB dominate in developing CNS and glia,
NFIX in neural stem cells, muscle and hematopoiesis, NFIC in tooth and kidney. NFI was originally
purified as a host factor required for adenovirus type 2 DNA replication, and independently as
"CTF" (CCAAT box transcription factor) and as the chicken "TGGCA protein"; all three are the same
family [PMID:4040852,3398920].

## The motif

The consensus is the 15-bp palindrome TTGGC(N5)GCCAA, equivalently written TGGC(N5)GCCA [PMID:4040852,3039460]. Each
monomer reads one TTGGC half-site, so the information sits almost entirely on the two half-sites;
the five central bases are a spacer and contribute little. Spacing matters more than spacer sequence,
though it is not rigid: early binding studies accepted 6- or 7-bp gaps between the motifs TGG and
GCCAA, 6 bp being the canonical spacing in that notation [PMID:3039460], and a later oligonucleotide study described a flexible binding mode that lets site length
vary [PMID:10736221]. The NFI-X structure explains the strong preference for TTGGC(N5)GCCAA: the five-base
spacer places both DNA-binding domains on the same side of the DNA, and with a spacer one base shorter
only a single monomer bound, at one half-site [PMID:41261119]. All the
JASPAR and HOCOMOCO full-site models fix the five-base spacer and run 14-17 columns with the spacer
degenerate. Full-site models reach 15-26 bits, among the most informative in these collections.
Half-site models also exist and are legitimate: NFI binds single TTGGC/TGCCAA sites with lower
affinity, and several database entries for all four paralogues are 5-7 bp half-sites carrying only
8-12 bits. No paralogue is distinguishable from any other by sequence. The name "CCAAT box
transcription factor" is a historical trap: the NFI half-site GCCAA contains the letters of a
CCAAT box read on one strand, and NFI was long listed among CCAAT-binding proteins [PMID:3398920], but NFI and
NF-Y are unrelated proteins with different folds and different optimal sites. If a scan returns
both, they are separate hypotheses, not confirmations of each other.

## Where it acts

NFI sites are found at promoters and at enhancers, and NFI proteins are enriched at distal
regulatory elements in stem and progenitor populations. NFI binding is closely tied to chromatin
accessibility: in skin stem cells NFI factors occupy super-enhancers and provide access for
lineage factors while suppressing alternative fates [PMID:32393888], and in retinal progenitors NFI factors
control mitotic exit and late-born cell specification [PMID:31128945]. NFI also binds nucleosomal DNA more
readily than many factors, consistent with a role early in opening elements. Recurring partners
include FOXA1 in prostate, the glucocorticoid and progesterone receptors at the MMTV promoter
(where NFI and the receptor compete for overlapping DNA) [PMID:2162764], SOX factors in glia, and MYOD in
muscle. Because the full palindrome is long, genome-wide scans recover a manageable number of
strong matches, but half-site matches are effectively everywhere.

## Biology and disease

Mouse knockouts give distinct phenotypes despite the shared motif: Nfia loss causes corpus
callosum agenesis and hydrocephalus, Nfib loss impairs lung maturation and forebrain
development, Nfic loss blocks tooth root formation [PMID:12529411], and Nfix loss affects brain, muscle and
hematopoiesis. The human syndromes mirror them. NFIA haploinsufficiency causes a CNS malformation
syndrome with corpus callosum hypoplasia, macrocephaly and urinary tract defects [PMID:17530927]. NFIX variants
cause two different disorders depending on whether the transcript escapes nonsense-mediated
decay: missense or deletion alleles affecting the DNA-binding/dimerization domain cause Malan
(Sotos-like) overgrowth syndrome, while alleles producing stable truncated protein cause
Marshall-Smith syndrome [PMID:20673863]. NFIB is amplified and drives progression and metastasis in small cell
lung cancer [PMID:27373156], and NFIB works with CARM1 in that setting; NFIB fusions also occur in adenoid cystic
carcinoma via MYB-NFIB translocation.

## Reading a hit

A full TTGGC(N5)GCCAA match is good evidence that some NFI dimer can bind, and it is specific
enough that chance matches are uncommon. It is no evidence at all about which paralogue, and
because heterodimers are the rule, "which paralogue" may not even be a well-posed question in a
cell expressing three of them; assign from expression data. Half-site hits are a different
proposition: TTGGC or TGCCAA alone carries under 12 bits and will occur by chance many times in
any window you look at, so half-site models should be treated as weak. Two confusions are worth
flagging. First, the GCCAA half-site overlaps the letters of a CCAAT box, and NFI's old name CTF
invites the false inference that an NFI hit is an NF-Y hit; the true NF-Y site is CCAAT read in a
different context and the proteins are unrelated. Second, NFI's MH1-like fold means archetype and
class labels place it with SMAD, which can look like a mislabeling but is structurally correct [PMID:41261119].
HOCOMOCO NFI models graded A generally rest on both ChIP-seq and in vitro selection (evidence
codes PS or PSM), so the full-site matrices here are well supported.
families.caveats: The four paralogues share one matrix and freely heterodimerize, so a hit identifies NFI, never NFIA versus NFIB versus NFIC versus NFIX. Full-palindrome matches are trustworthy; half-site models (TTGGC or GCCAA alone, under 12 bits) are not, and several database entries for this family are half-sites. Spacer length matters more than spacer sequence: a gap one base shorter than TTGGC(N5)GCCAA supports only half-site binding, and how well other gaps are tolerated is less clear. Do not equate the GCCAA half-site with the CCAAT box of NF-Y despite NFI's historical name CTF; the two proteins are unrelated. The SMAD/NF-1 class label reflects the shared MH1-like fold and is not an error.

timeline.finding: Nuclear factor I, a HeLa protein that stimulates adenovirus DNA replication, protects nucleotides 19-42 of the adenovirus 2 terminal repeat, and deletion mapping places its minimal recognition site at 15-16 bp.
timeline.methods: DNase I footprinting, filter binding with deletion mutants, in vitro replication
timeline.open: Which bases inside the site were read, and whether the site was symmetrical.

timeline.finding: Binding to synthetic and selected sites defines the NFI site as two motifs, TGG and GCCAA, separated by a 6- or 7-bp spacer, with spacer-position biases that differ between the two spacings.
timeline.methods: Selection from degenerate oligonucleotide libraries, binding assays
timeline.open: Whether the 7-bp spacing is a genuine second site class used in cells.

timeline.finding: Cloning shows that the transcription factor CTF and the replication factor NF-I are one family of differentially spliced proteins that bind GCCAAT-containing sites and act both as promoter-selective activators and as replication initiation factors.
timeline.methods: cDNA cloning, expression and functional assays
timeline.open: The CCAAT-box label grouped NFI with unrelated CCAAT-binding proteins such as NF-Y.

timeline.finding: At the MMTV promoter NFI is needed for efficient hormone-induced transcription, yet purified NFI and the glucocorticoid or progesterone receptor compete for overlapping DNA rather than binding cooperatively.
timeline.methods: Cotransfection, DNase I footprinting with purified and recombinant proteins

timeline.finding: Haploinsufficiency for NFIA in five individuals causes corpus callosum hypoplasia or agenesis, hydrocephalus or ventriculomegaly and urinary tract defects, matching the Nfia knockout mouse and giving the first human NFI syndrome.
timeline.methods: Cytogenetics and microdeletion mapping in patients, mouse genetics

timeline.finding: Ablating NFIB and NFIX in hair follicle stem cells decommissions the super-enhancers of stem cell identity genes and de-represses other lineages, casting NFI as a chromatin-access factor.
timeline.methods: Conditional knockout, single-cell RNA-seq, ATAC-seq, ChIP-seq

timeline.finding: Structures of the NFI-X DNA-binding domain, alone and on its palindromic site, reveal an MH1-like fold with a structural Zn2+ site and a dimeric assembly, placing NFI structurally with the SMADs; the authors present it as prototypic for all four paralogues.
timeline.methods: X-ray crystallography and solution structural methods
timeline.open: How heterodimers and alternative spacings are accommodated was not addressed.

open: Whether NFI has a second spacing class is unresolved: binding studies in 1987 recovered TGG...GCCAA sites with either 6-bp or 7-bp spacers and a 2000 study described a binding mode flexible enough to accommodate variation in site length, whereas the NFI-X structure explains a strong preference for TTGGC(N5)GCCAA (the 6-bp form in the 1987 notation), the only spacing that the full-site models in the current collections use.

Why NFIA, NFIB, NFIC and NFIX knockouts differ so sharply despite one shared motif is not settled: the NFI-X structure is presented as prototypic for all four DNA-binding domains, which points to expression, heterodimer composition and C-terminal domains rather than DNA specificity, but paralogue-specific binding has not been excluded directly.

How much genomic NFI binding uses single half-sites rather than full palindromes is not established; half-site models (TGCCAA, TTGGCA) exist for all four paralogues, including in vitro-supported ones, alongside full-site models above 15 bits.

families.name: MBD and CxxC readers
families.def: Methyl-CpG and unmethylated-CpG readers. MECP2, MBD1-3, CXXC1/4/5, KDM2A/B, TET1/3, DNMT1, KMT2A/B.
families.short: This family puts two opposite kinds of reader in one place. MBD proteins - MECP2, MBD1, MBD3 - bind CpG that is methylated. ZF-CxxC proteins - CXXC1/CFP1, CXXC4, CXXC5, KDM2A, KDM2B, FBXL19, TET1, TET3, DNMT1, KMT2A, KMT2B - bind CpG that is not. Neither group has a sequence-specific site in any useful sense. The single most important thing to know about this page is that its motifs are essentially measurements of CpG density: the family consensus is literally CG, eight of the twenty-one models carry two to four bits of information, and the representative model is a two-base-pair CG. Treat a MECP2 motif in particular with real scepticism.
families.long:
## The factors

Two unrelated protein modules are collected here because they do the same job from opposite directions. The methyl-CpG binding domain was defined in 1998 as the shared feature of a small mammalian family - MeCP2 plus MBD1, MBD2, MBD3 and MBD4 - that binds DNA containing methylated CpG [PMID:9774669]; MeCP2 then recruits a Sin3A and histone deacetylase complex, which was the first mechanistic link from DNA methylation to repressive chromatin [PMID:9620804]. The zinc-finger CxxC domain does the reverse: it binds CpG only when the cytosine is unmethylated, and it appears in a striking list of chromatin enzymes - CXXC1 (CFP1), CXXC4 and CXXC5, the H3K36 demethylases KDM2A and KDM2B, FBXL19, the 5-methylcytosine dioxygenases TET1 and TET3, the maintenance methyltransferase DNMT1, and the H3K4 methyltransferases KMT2A and KMT2B [PMID:23697932]. In every case the domain is a targeting device attached to a catalytic or scaffolding protein, not a transcription factor in its own right.

Because methylation is almost entirely restricted to CpG in mammalian somatic cells, and because CpG islands are by definition the unmethylated CpG-dense regions, the two groups partition the same dinucleotide between them according to its modification state rather than according to its sequence context.

## The motif

There is no motif in the ordinary sense, and the atlas data say so plainly. The family consensus is CG. The representative model, CIS-BP M01919 for CXXC1, is a two-base-pair CG carrying 4.0 bits. Eight models - those for CXXC1, CXXC5, KMT2A, KDM2A, KDM2B, FBXL19, TET1 and DNMT1 - are CG or CGG at 1.5 to 4.5 bits. The MECP2 model in CIS-BP, M00806, is the dinucleotide Ac at 1.8 bits. The slightly longer models add at most one or two informative flanking positions: TACG for FBXL19, TaCGc for KDM2A, TaCGT for CXXC4, GCGch for MBD1, CCGCcG for CXXC1 in HOCOMOCO. Structural work on human CXXC domains shows exactly this - the CpG is read directly and the domains differ modestly in which bases they tolerate immediately around it - so the flanking preferences in these models are real but small [PMID:29276034].

The long models are a different problem. HOCOMOCO's KMT2A model, CcCcGCCgCCGCCGCCGCCgCC, and its KMT2B model, GCGGCGGC, are ChIP-derived (evidence code P, grade B) CGG-repeat and GC-rich patterns; the MBD3 model, GGAGCgcaGsngGsgggrgvg, is likewise ChIP-only. These describe the base composition of CpG-island promoters, which is where the proteins sit, not a site the proteins select. The Vierstra archetype for MECP2, cCCGGag, and for MBD1, gGgCCGGag, are footprint archetypes over the same GC-rich compartment. Only TET3's tACGTaagGggggg has grade A multi-assay support, and it is dominated by an ACGT core plus a G-tract.

One statistic deserves attention. The short CG models have high label agreement, 0.5 to 0.8, meaning their nearest neighbours in other databases really do carry family labels - but their bestOther scores are also 0.85 to 0.95, meaning they are nearly identical to models in unrelated families. When both numbers are high for a two-bit model, the model is not discriminating anything.

## Where it acts

CpG islands, and methylated CpG everywhere else. CFP1/CXXC1 occupancy tracks unmethylated CpG islands and shapes their chromatin [PMID:20393567], and KDM2A is recruited to CpG islands by its CxxC domain to remove H3K36 methylation there [PMID:20417597]. TET1 acts genome-wide on 5-methylcytosine and 5-hydroxymethylcytosine, with CpG islands and their shores prominent [PMID:21514197]. MeCP2, by contrast, is not localised in the usual sense at all: in neurons it is present at levels approaching those of the histone octamer and tracks methylated CpG across the whole genome [PMID:20188665], and it represses the rate of transcriptional initiation of long, highly methylated genes rather than acting at discrete sites [PMID:31784358].

## Biology and disease

MECP2 is the Rett syndrome gene - mutations in the X-linked gene cause the classic neurodevelopmental disorder in girls [PMID:10508514], and duplication of the locus causes a distinct syndrome in boys. This is a very well-understood gene with a very poorly defined binding motif, and the contrast is instructive. KMT2A rearrangement defines a major class of acute leukaemia; DNMT1 mutations cause hereditary sensory neuropathy with dementia; TET2, a relative of the TET1/TET3 proteins filed here, is one of the most commonly mutated genes in myeloid malignancy. In none of these cases does a motif model contribute to interpretation.

## Reading a hit

Do not treat a match in this family as a binding site. If you must use these models, read them as a CpG-density statistic and check whether your region is a CpG island. Then ask which direction of methylation sensitivity matters: a CXXC protein requires the CpG to be unmethylated, an MBD protein requires it to be methylated, and the motif model cannot tell you which state your sequence is in - you need methylation data for that. Be most sceptical of MECP2. Its CIS-BP model is 1.8 bits, its Vierstra archetype is a generic GC-rich footprint, and the biology says MeCP2 coats methylated CpG genome-wide rather than occupying motifs [PMID:20188665]. A MECP2 motif hit is not a MeCP2 site. The same applies to the ChIP-derived KMT2A, KMT2B and MBD3 models, which report the composition of CpG-island promoters.
families.caveats: These are not sequence-specific motifs. The family consensus is CG, the representative model is a two-base CG, and eight of twenty-one models carry under 4.5 bits; they measure CpG density, not a site. Methylation state, which is what actually determines binding and which is opposite for the MBD and CxxC halves of the family, is invisible to a sequence scan. The long KMT2A, KMT2B and MBD3 models are ChIP-only (grade B) and describe the GC-rich composition of CpG-island promoters. MECP2 deserves particular scepticism: its CIS-BP model is 1.8 bits, and MeCP2 binds methylated CpG genome-wide at near-nucleosomal abundance rather than at discrete sites. Two CIS-BP models are cross-species transfers.

timeline.finding: MBD2, MBD3 and MBD4 were identified by their shared methyl-CpG binding domain; MBD2 and MBD4 bound methyl-CpG in vitro and colocalized with methylated satellite DNA in cells, whereas MBD3 bound methylated DNA neither in vitro nor in vivo.
timeline.methods: cDNA identification, in vitro binding assays, GFP localization in methylation-deficient cells
timeline.open: What, if anything, MBD3 recognizes on DNA.

timeline.finding: De novo MECP2 mutations were found in 5 of 21 sporadic Rett syndrome patients, missense changes in the methyl-binding domain and truncations of the transcription-repression domain, identifying the first disease-causing mutations for Rett syndrome.
timeline.methods: Systematic gene screening in patients and families

timeline.finding: The crystal structure of the MeCP2 methyl-binding domain on methylated DNA showed the methyl groups contacting a mostly hydrophilic surface with tightly bound water, so MeCP2 reads hydration of the methylated major groove rather than the methyl groups themselves, revising the hydrophobic-patch model of specificity.
timeline.methods: X-ray crystallography

timeline.finding: Neuronal MeCP2 was measured at nearly histone-octamer abundance, its genome-wide binding tracked methyl-CpG density, and its loss raised histone acetylation and doubled histone H1, arguing against MeCP2 as a gene-specific repressor that occupies discrete sites.
timeline.methods: Protein quantification, ChIP-seq, chromatin analysis in neurons and glia

timeline.finding: Two studies showed that unmethylated CpG islands recruit ZF-CxxC proteins: Cfp1 bound non-methylated CpGs and promoter-free artificial CpG clusters inserted into the mouse genome recruited Cfp1 and created new H3K4me3 peaks, and KDM2A was recruited through its CxxC domain with binding blocked by CpG methylation.
timeline.methods: ChIP-seq, in vitro binding, integrated artificial CpG clusters, depletion experiments
timeline.open: Whether CpG density alone, or additional sequence, decides which CxxC protein occupies a given island.

timeline.finding: A genome-wide, length-dependent rise in gene expression in Mecp2 mutant mice and human Rett brains was attributed to MeCP2 binding at methylated CA sites within long genes, extending MeCP2's substrate beyond methyl-CpG.
timeline.methods: Transcriptomics in mouse models and human brain, methylation and binding analyses
timeline.open: The relative contributions of methylated CA and methylated CG to MeCP2 function.

timeline.finding: The DNA-binding selectivities of all known human CXXC domains were measured with several assays and explained by a series of crystal structures, yielding a classification of CXXC domains by DNA selectivity in which the CpG is read directly and flanking-base preferences differ between domains.
timeline.methods: Multiple in vitro binding assays, X-ray crystallography

timeline.finding: Measuring transcription rates directly in the brain showed that MeCP2, through the NCoR co-repressor, lowers the rate of Pol II initiation, not elongation, at highly methylated long genes, a model in which MeCP2 binds broadly across methylated DNA but acts at transcription start sites.
timeline.methods: Nascent transcription and initiation-rate measurements in mouse brain

open: Whether MBD3 has any intrinsic DNA preference is unsettled: it fails to bind methylated DNA in vitro or in vivo, a reported preference for 5-hydroxymethylcytosine was not borne out by later binding studies, and its only model here is ChIP-derived and reflects the GC-rich promoters NuRD occupies.

How MeCP2's specificity should be described is not settled: it was defined as a methyl-CpG reader, but in neurons it also binds methylated CA, and the relative contribution of the two marks to long-gene repression is still argued; neither is captured by a sequence motif.

Whether the TET1 CXXC domain discriminates methylation state is unresolved: genome-wide work in embryonic stem cells reported that it binds CpG-rich DNA whether the cytosine is unmodified, methylated or hydroxymethylated, unlike the methylation-blocked CxxC domains of CFP1 and KDM2A.

It is open whether the modest differences in flanking-base preference measured between CXXC domains, rather than the partner proteins and catalytic activities attached to them, decide which CpG islands each CxxC protein occupies.

families.name: SIX
families.def: MEF3 element, read as TGATAC / GTATCA (the two strands of one extended site). SIX1/2/4 and SIX3/6 select the same core in vitro and differ in cofactor use rather than in sequence.
families.short: The six human SIX genes encode homeodomain proteins with an additional SIX domain that recruits the EYA family of transcriptional coactivators. Their shared DNA core is TGATAC (GTATCA on the other strand), usually embedded in a longer element written GTAACCTGATAC, which on the opposite strand contains the MEF3 site TCAGGTT first defined in the myogenin promoter. SIX1, SIX2 and SIX4 partner with EYA proteins and activate transcription; SIX3 and SIX6 instead recruit Groucho/TLE corepressors and repress. The family builds muscle, kidney, inner ear and eye: SIX1 mutations cause branchio-oto-renal syndrome, SIX3 mutations cause holoprosencephaly, and SIX1 with EYA is re-activated in several carcinomas.
families.long:
## The factors

Six human genes - SIX1, SIX2, SIX3, SIX4, SIX5 and SIX6 - encode the vertebrate relatives of *Drosophila* sine oculis [PMID:10878574,18989625]. Each protein carries a homeodomain preceded by a roughly 110-residue SIX domain, which is the family's second functional module: together with the homeodomain it is required for specific DNA binding [PMID:10878574], and it provides the interaction surface for the EYA coactivators. The crystal structure of human SIX1 (SIX domain plus homeodomain) bound to the EYA2 Eya domain shows how that interface is organized, and suggests that the last helix of the SIX domain, where BOR syndrome mutations that abolish DNA binding cluster, could contact the major groove [PMID:23435380]. The family splits on cofactor use rather than on sequence. SIX1 binds EYA1 and EYA2 [PMID:15141091,23435380], and SIX2, SIX4 and SIX5 bind EYA1-3 and carry them into the nucleus [PMID:10490620]; EYA has intrinsic protein tyrosine phosphatase activity and its recruitment converts a SIX-DACH complex from repressing to activating, so the same site can give opposite outputs depending on which partner is present [PMID:14628042]. SIX3 does not bind EYA [PMID:10490620,12050133]; SIX3 and SIX6 instead bind Groucho-related corepressors, SIX3 through an eh1-like motif in its SIX domain, and SIX3 then acts as a repressor [PMID:12050133]. SIX1 and SIX4 are expressed in somites, muscle satellite cells, kidney and otic placode; SIX2 in nephron progenitors; SIX3 and SIX6 in the anterior neural plate, retina and hypothalamus. SIX5 is a family member with no motif model in any of the four collections used here.

## The motif

All SIX models in these databases converge on a GATAC core. The HT-SELEX and methyl-SELEX models - SIX1.H14CORE.1.SM.B, SIX2.H14CORE.2.SM.B, SIX3.H14CORE.0.SM.B, SIX6.H14CORE.0.SM.B and two CIS-BP models - reduce to tGATAC, 6-9 bits. The ChIP-derived and longer JASPAR models extend it: SIX1 and SIX2 give tGaAAcyTGAtac, JASPAR SIX1 gives GtAACCTGA, JASPAR SIX2 TGAAACCTGAt, SIX4 TGtAAccTGAcACC, and the Vierstra archetype AC0459 GtAACcTGAta. Read the long version on the opposite strand and the classical name appears: GTAACCTGATAC is GTATCAGGTTAC reversed, and TCAGGTT is the MEF3 motif identified in the myogenin promoter as the site through which Six1 and Six4 activate myogenin during somitogenesis [PMID:9826681]. So the family has one site described under two names and two strand conventions; the pooled consensus here, GtaACgcGATACc, is the long form. Two caveats about the split written into this family's definition. First, SIX3 and SIX6 are sometimes described as preferring a TAAT-type site rather than the MEF3 site, but in these four databases their in vitro models give the same TGATAC core as SIX1/2/4, and the JASPAR Six3 model (AtaGGGTATCA) is the GTATCA form [PMID:18585359] - so the SIX1/2/4 versus SIX3/6 division is a cofactor distinction, not one you can make from sequence. Second, one CIS-BP member of this family reads GAgTTGTAGT and has nearest neighbours among the ETS factors; it should not be used as a SIX motif.

## Where it acts

SIX sites occur in tissue-specific enhancers and promoters: the myogenin promoter MEF3 element [PMID:9826681], nephron progenitor enhancers for SIX2, otic and branchial arch enhancers for SIX1, and forebrain and retinal enhancers for SIX3 and SIX6 [PMID:12569128]. The functional unit is usually a SIX site plus its cofactor complex rather than a cluster of different motifs, which is why composite element names are rare for this family. Because the core is only 6 bp, exact TGATAC matches number on the order of 10^6 genome-wide and carry almost no information alone; the 11-13 bp extended form is far more discriminating. Note that the short models will also match GATA-like sequence by coincidence - one Vierstra archetype in this family is labelled SIX/GATA for that reason.

## Biology and disease

Heterozygous SIX1 mutations cause branchio-oto-renal syndrome by disrupting EYA1-SIX1-DNA complexes [PMID:15141091], and Six1 loss in mouse impairs kidney, muscle and inner ear development [PMID:14628042]; Six4-null mice have no developmental defect, but removing Six4 as well as Six1 aggravates the Six1 phenotype, with general muscle hypoplasia and impaired expression of the myogenic regulatory factors [PMID:15788460]. SIX2 is required to maintain nephron progenitors [PMID:17036046]. Mutations in the SIX3 homeodomain cause holoprosencephaly [PMID:10369266], and Six3 represses Wnt signaling in the anterior neuroectoderm, which is required for forebrain formation [PMID:12569128]; SIX6 lies in a chromosome 14 cluster and is associated with eye malformation [PMID:10512683] and, in common variation, with optic disc and glaucoma phenotypes [PMID:24875647]. The SIX1-EYA complex is re-expressed in breast, ovarian and other carcinomas, where it promotes migration and metastasis, and is being pursued as a drug target [PMID:23435380].

## Reading a hit

A bare TGATAC hit is close to meaningless: 6 bp, high genomic frequency, and shared by every SIX paralogue. Insist on the extended GTAACCTGATAC / MEF3 form before calling a site. Even then the hit identifies the family and not the member, and it does not tell you the output, because SIX1/2/4 with EYA activate while SIX3/6 with Groucho repress at what looks like the same sequence. The SIX1, SIX2 and SIX4 models graded P in HOCOMOCO come from ChIP alone and their 5' extension may reflect co-bound partners; the SM-graded models are the in vitro evidence and are the short GATAC form.
families.caveats: The GATAC core is only 6 bp and is shared by all SIX paralogues, so short matches are uninformative and will also pick up GATA-like sequence - one Vierstra archetype here is labelled SIX/GATA. Use the extended 11-13 bp MEF3 form. A hit cannot distinguish SIX1, SIX2, SIX3, SIX4 or SIX6, and cannot predict activation versus repression, since that depends on whether EYA or Groucho is recruited. SIX5 has no model here at all. One CIS-BP member of the family reads an ETS-like sequence (GAGTTGTAGT) and is flagged as belonging elsewhere; the longer SIX1/2/4 models are ChIP-derived and may include partner contributions.
