timeline.finding: Mutating the MEF3 motif (TCAGGTT) in a 184-bp myogenin promoter fragment abolishes correct transgene expression in the embryo, and the MEF3-binding activity in muscle is identified as Six1 and Six4, which transactivate MEF3 reporters.
timeline.methods: Transgenic promoter mutagenesis, EMSA with specific antibodies, transfection
timeline.open: Whether the other SIX proteins read the same site was not addressed.

timeline.finding: Six2, Six4 and Six5, but not Six3, bind EYA proteins and carry them into the nucleus, and Six-Eya combinations synergistically activate the myogenin promoter and multimerized Six4 sites; the SIX domain plus homeodomain is necessary and sufficient.
timeline.methods: Cotransfection, coimmunoprecipitation, yeast two-hybrid

timeline.finding: Six3 and Six6 instead bind the Groucho-related corepressors Grg4 and Grg5 through an eh1-like motif in the SIX domain, and Six3 acts as a potent repressor; a PCR-selected Six3 binding site is reported.
timeline.methods: Protein interaction assays, site selection, retinal and lens overexpression
timeline.open: Whether the Six3-selected site and the MEF3 site are distinct specificities or one site read by both subclasses was not settled.

timeline.finding: EYA is shown to be a protein phosphatase whose activity switches SIX1-DACH from repression to activation, and Six1 is shown to be required for kidney, muscle and inner ear development.
timeline.methods: Mouse genetics, phosphatase assays, coactivator recruitment assays

timeline.finding: SIX1 mutations cause branchio-oto-renal and branchio-otic syndromes; all three disrupt EYA1-SIX1 interaction, and the two in the homeodomain also abolish specific DNA binding.
timeline.methods: Human genetics, protein-protein and protein-DNA binding assays

timeline.finding: Protein-binding microarrays for 168 mouse homeodomains resolve at least 65 distinct binding activities; the Six3 model reads GGTATCA, the reverse complement of the TGATAC core that later in vitro models give for SIX1, SIX2, SIX4 and SIX6 alike.
timeline.methods: Universal protein-binding microarrays

timeline.finding: The 2.0-A structure of SIX1 bound to the EYA2 ED domain shows that SIX1 contacts EYA mainly through a single helix; one substitution in it disrupts the complex, SIX1-driven epithelial-mesenchymal transition and metastasis in mice.
timeline.methods: X-ray crystallography, mutagenesis, mouse metastasis models
timeline.open: No SIX protein has been solved on DNA, so how the SIX domain and homeodomain divide the extended site remains structural inference.

open: Whether the SIX domain contacts DNA is unsettled: reviews describe both the SIX domain and the homeodomain as required for specific DNA binding, the SIX1-EYA2 structure was read as suggesting a new DNA-binding mode, but without a SIX-DNA structure it is unknown how the two domains share the extended GTAACCTGATAC site.

The databases disagree over site length: the HT-SELEX and methyl-HT-SELEX models give only the 6-bp TGATAC core, while the ChIP-derived models give the 11-13 bp MEF3 form, and it is not resolved whether the 5' AACC extension is read by the SIX protein itself or reflects co-bound factors in ChIP.

Whether SIX3 and SIX6 prefer a site different from SIX1, SIX2 and SIX4 is unsettled: the subclasses differ clearly in cofactor (EYA versus Groucho), but the systematic in vitro models for all five paralogues in these databases give the same TGATAC core.

families.name: SMAD
families.def: SBE GTCT/AGAC and GC-rich SMAD motifs. SMAD1-5, SMAD9.
families.consensus: GTCT / AGAC (palindrome GTCTAGAC); also the 5-bp GC motif GGC(GC/CG)
families.short: SMAD proteins are the intracellular effectors of TGF-beta family signaling. Their MH1 domain inserts a beta-hairpin into the major groove and reads just four bases, GTCT or its reverse complement AGAC, often written as the CAGAC box or as the 8-bp palindrome GTCTAGAC. SMAD3, SMAD4 and the BMP-activated SMAD1/5/9 also bind a separate 5-bp GC-rich element, GGCGC or GGCCG. Both elements are far too short to be informative alone, and genome-wide SMAD occupancy is set mainly by whichever lineage-determining factor is present, so most SMAD ChIP peaks are better explained by a partner's motif than by an SBE. This is a family where a motif hit needs corroboration more than almost any other.
families.long:
## The factors

Eight human SMADs fall into three groups. The receptor-regulated R-SMADs are SMAD2 and SMAD3
(phosphorylated by TGF-beta and activin receptors) and SMAD1, SMAD5 and SMAD9/SMAD8
(phosphorylated by BMP receptors). SMAD4 is the shared co-SMAD. SMAD6 and SMAD7 are inhibitory
and are not sequence-specific activators. DNA contact is made by the N-terminal MH1 domain, a
compact domain with a bound zinc ion whose 11-residue beta-hairpin inserts into the major groove [PMID:9741623];
the C-terminal MH2 domain mediates trimerization, so the functional unit on DNA is normally a
trimer of two R-SMADs plus SMAD4, giving two or three DNA-contacting hairpins [PMID:29234012]. One paralogue is a
special case: wild-type SMAD2 carries a 30-residue insert encoded by exon 3 immediately before the
hairpin that blocks direct DNA binding [PMID:9873005]. Full-length SMAD2 reaches DNA through partners, most
clearly the forkhead protein FOXH1/FAST1 [PMID:9702197,9873005]; the naturally occurring SMAD2 delta-exon-3 splice form
does bind DNA, like SMAD3 [PMID:9873005].

## The motif

The classical Smad-binding element is 4 bp, GTCT, read on the other strand as AGAC and usually
quoted with a flanking base as CAGAC ("CAGA box") or CAGACA. Zawel and colleagues showed that
SMAD3 and SMAD4 both recognize an identical 8-bp palindrome, GTCTAGAC [PMID:9660945], and the Smad3 MH1 crystal
structure explained why: the hairpin reads GTCT and two hairpins from a trimer can occupy the two
halves of the palindrome [PMID:9741623]. Real promoters usually contain tandem CAGA repeats rather than a perfect
palindrome; the TGF-beta response element of the PAI-1/SERPINE1 promoter is the canonical example [PMID:9606191].
Separately, SMADs bind a 5-bp GC-rich element with consensus GGC(GC) or GGC(CG). This was first
described as a BMP-responsive element for SMAD1/5 [PMID:10679014], but structural work showed that SMAD3 and SMAD4
bind the same 5GC motifs, and that these motifs occur in clusters in SMAD-bound regions
genome-wide [PMID:29234012]. So the family has two chemically distinct consensus sequences, not one; a database
entry showing GTCTAGAC and one showing a GC-rich string can both be correct. The data for this
family reflects that split, and its cohesion (0.76) is the lowest in this batch. The CAGAC-type
and 5GC-type models do not interconvert, and paralogues are not separable from sequence within
either type. The CIS-BP SMAD9 entry is a GC-rich model transferred from a Drosophila protein at
91% MH1 identity, not a human measurement.

## Where it acts

SMAD sites are distributed across promoters and enhancers with no CpG-island preference for the
CAGAC form, while 5GC clusters are by definition GC-rich and promoter-biased. What matters more is
that SMAD occupancy is almost entirely conditional. Smad3 ChIP-seq in three different cell types
recovers three largely non-overlapping site sets, each co-occupied by that cell type's
lineage-determining factor: OCT4 in embryonic stem cells, MYOD1 in myotubes, PU.1 in pro-B cells [PMID:22036565].
In other systems the recurring partners are FOXH1 and other forkhead proteins, RUNX1/2, AP-1
(JUN/FOS), TEAD, and the repressors TGIF1, SKI and SnoN. Named composite elements include the
activin-responsive element of the Mix.2 promoter (a forkhead site next to a SMAD site) [PMID:9702197,9873005] and the
BMP-responsive elements of the Id1 and Smad7 promoters. In practice a SMAD peak set looks like the
partner's peak set with a weak SBE enrichment layered on top.

## Biology and disease

TGF-beta/BMP signaling through SMADs controls epithelial growth arrest, extracellular matrix
production, epithelial-mesenchymal transition, regulatory T cell induction, bone and cartilage
formation, and left-right and dorsoventral patterning. Smad3-null mice die within months from
impaired mucosal immunity with defective T cell responses to TGF-beta [PMID:10064594]. SMAD4 was identified as
DPC4, a candidate tumor suppressor at 18q21.1 that was homozygously deleted in 25 of 84 pancreatic
carcinomas (about 30%), with potentially inactivating mutations in 6 of 27 of the others [PMID:8553070]; germline SMAD4 mutations cause juvenile polyposis and, with an overlapping
phenotype, hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia [PMID:9582123,15031030]. SMAD4 and SMAD2/SMAD3 are also recurrently
mutated in colorectal cancer, and loss of SMAD signaling converts TGF-beta from a growth
suppressor to a driver of invasion and immune evasion [PMID:37714133]. SMAD9 mutations cause a form of pulmonary
arterial hypertension, consistent with the BMP9/BMPR2 axis [PMID:19211612].

## Reading a hit

Treat an isolated SBE match as essentially no evidence. GTCT or AGAC occurs about once every 128
bases on either strand, so a 4-bp core appears tens of millions of times in the human genome; even
the 8-bp palindrome GTCTAGAC is expected tens of thousands of times by chance. A SMAD hit becomes
meaningful only in one of three forms: several CAGA repeats within a short window, a cluster of
5GC motifs, or an SBE within a few base pairs of a validated partner site (a forkhead, RUNX,
AP-1 or TEAD motif). The second problem is that ChIP-derived SMAD motifs in these collections are
contaminated by indirect binding almost by construction, since SMAD complexes are recruited by
lineage factors. Every HOCOMOCO SMAD2 model here rests on ChIP-seq only (evidence code P), and
wild-type SMAD2 cannot bind DNA directly [PMID:9873005], so those matrices describe the composition of SMAD2
peaks rather than SMAD2's own specificity. Finally, do not use a hit to name a paralogue. CAGAC
does not mean TGF-beta rather than BMP, because SMAD1/5 bind CAGAC-type sites too and SMAD3/4 bind
GC-type sites; the original "TGF-beta uses CAGAC, BMP uses GC" division does not survive the
structural and genome-wide data [PMID:29234012,33510867].
families.caveats: The lowest-confidence family in this batch. A 4-bp SBE is not a finding; even the 8-bp palindrome is common by chance. The family has two unrelated consensus sequences (CAGAC-type and 5GC-type), so conflicting database entries may both be right, and paralogues are not separable within either. Most SMAD ChIP peaks are explained by a partner's motif, not by an SBE, and all HOCOMOCO SMAD2 models here are ChIP-only while full-length SMAD2 cannot bind DNA directly. The CIS-BP SMAD9 model is transferred from Drosophila. Use SMAD hits only as supporting evidence alongside a partner site or experimental occupancy.

timeline.finding: SMAD3 and SMAD4 each recognize the same 8-bp palindrome, GTCTAGAC, and tandem copies confer TGF-beta responsiveness that is lost in SMAD4-deleted cells, establishing SMADs as sequence-specific DNA-binding factors.
timeline.methods: Binding-site selection from random oligonucleotides, reporter assays, SMAD4-null cells

timeline.finding: Three CAGA boxes in the PAI-1/SERPINE1 promoter are bound directly by SMAD3 and SMAD4, are required for TGF-beta induction, and respond to TGF-beta and activin but not BMP; recombinant SMAD1 and SMAD2 do not bind them.
timeline.methods: Promoter mutagenesis, EMSA with recombinant proteins and nuclear extracts, reporter assays
timeline.open: What, if anything, the BMP-activated SMADs bind directly.

timeline.finding: The 2.8 A structure of the SMAD3 MH1 domain on DNA shows that base-specific recognition is made entirely by a conserved 11-residue beta-hairpin in the major groove.
timeline.methods: X-ray crystallography

timeline.finding: Wild-type SMAD2 does not bind DNA directly because of the exon 3 insert before the hairpin; it reaches target promoters with SMAD4 through the forkhead partner FAST/FOXH1, whereas the delta-exon-3 isoform and SMAD3 bind DNA themselves.
timeline.methods: EMSA, reporter assays, splice-variant comparison

timeline.finding: BMP-activated SMAD1 with SMAD4 binds the GC-rich GCCGnCGC element first defined for Drosophila Mad, weakly and only with multiple repeats, and GCCG reporters respond to BMP but not TGF-beta, supporting a split between GC-type BMP sites and CAGA-type TGF-beta sites.
timeline.methods: EMSA, multimerized reporter assays, mutagenesis
timeline.open: Whether the GC versus CAGA division reflected intrinsic specificity or the reporter contexts tested.

timeline.finding: SMAD3 ChIP-seq in embryonic stem cells, myotubes and pro-B cells gives largely distinct site sets, each co-occupied with and dependent on that cell's lineage-determining factor (OCT4, MYOD1, PU.1); inducing MYOD1 redirects SMAD3.
timeline.methods: ChIP-seq, knockdown and ectopic expression

timeline.finding: Structures of SMAD3 and SMAD4 on goosecoid promoter DNA define the 5-bp GC motif GGC(GC)|(CG) as a site for TGF-beta-activated, BMP-activated and common SMADs alike, and 5GC clusters are frequent in SMAD-bound regions genome-wide. This overturns the view that CAGAC is the TGF-beta site and GC-rich elements the BMP site.
timeline.methods: X-ray crystallography, binding assays, ChIP-seq motif analysis

timeline.finding: SMAD5 and SMAD8 MH1 structures show all MH1 domains bind 5GC motifs similarly, but SMAD2/3/4 MH1 domains bind as monomers while SMAD1/5/8 form helix-swapped dimers, and site clustering and spacing in ChIP-seq peaks differ between BMP- and TGF-beta-responsive genes.
timeline.methods: X-ray crystallography, NMR, chimeric domains, ChIP-seq motif analysis
timeline.open: Whether monomer-versus-dimer propensity actually drives pathway-specific target selection in cells.

open: How TGF-beta and BMP SMADs reach different targets is unresolved now that both bind CAGAC-type and 5GC sites: one proposal is that MH1 monomer (SMAD2/3/4) versus helix-swapped dimer (SMAD1/5/8) propensity sets site spacing and clustering, the alternative is that partner factors such as FOXH1 or lineage-determining factors choose the sites and the SMAD motif contributes little.

The ChIP-derived HOCOMOCO SMAD2, SMAD3 and SMAD4 models (for example tGTCTGdCACc and AGGTGncAGACA) do not match the in vitro palindrome GTCTAGAC, and it is not settled whether they describe composite SMAD-partner sites or simply peak composition shaped by recruiting factors.

families.name: DMRT (DM domain)
families.def: DM element, palindromic ACAWTGTW. DMRT1-3, DMRTA1/2, DMRTB1, DMRTC2.
families.short: DMRT proteins are the DM-domain transcription factors, named after Drosophila Doublesex and C. elegans MAB-3, the sexual regulators in which the domain was found. Humans have seven well-studied genes, DMRT1, DMRT2, DMRT3, DMRTA1, DMRTA2, DMRTB1 and DMRTC2, plus DMRTC1 paralogues. The DM domain is not a classical zinc finger: two zinc ions are chelated by an intertwined arrangement of cysteines and histidines that cannot be split into independent fingers, and the module ends in a recognition helix. The proteins bind a pseudopalindromic element built from two ACA/TGT half-sites, canonically ACAWTGTW, as dimers and higher-order oligomers. DMRT1 is required for testis differentiation and sustains it after birth; it is the sex-determining gene in chicken, and the 9p24 region containing it is deleted in human 46,XY sex reversal.
families.long:
## The factors

The DM domain was identified in Drosophila Doublesex (DSX) and C. elegans MAB-3 and is conserved
across animals [PMID:9490411]. Vertebrates have a small family: the seven human genes usually discussed are
DMRT1, DMRT2, DMRT3, DMRTA1 (DMRT4), DMRTA2 (DMRT5), DMRTB1 (DMRT6) and DMRTC2 (DMRT7), with
additional DMRTC1 paralogues that also have measured binding. Outside the DM domain the proteins
share almost no sequence [PMID:17605809], so the family is defined by its DNA-binding module and not by any
common architecture. That module is structurally unusual. Rather than the independent zinc
fingers of C2H2 or GATA proteins, the DM domain chelates two zinc ions through an intertwined
set of cysteine and histidine ligands that cannot be separated into discrete fingers, followed by
a C-terminal recognition helix and a basic tail [PMID:10898790,26005864]. DMRT proteins do not bind as simple monomers:
the crystal structures of human DMRT1 on DNA show tetrameric, trimeric and dimeric modes on the
same kind of site, and ChIP with exonuclease treatment indicates that several of these modes are
used in cells [PMID:26005864]. Expression is restricted. DMRT1 is essentially gonad-specific (Sertoli cells and
germ cells) [PMID:9490411,20616082]; DMRT2 acts in somites; DMRT3 is in spinal interneurons and gonad; DMRTA2 is in
developing cortex; DMRTB1 and DMRTC2 are germ-cell proteins.

## The motif

The element is a pseudopalindrome assembled from two trinucleotide half-sites that are reverse
complements of one another, ACA and TGT, separated by one or two variable bases [PMID:17605809,26005864]. Written as the
literature usually does, the core is ACAWTGTW; the equivalent forward-strand rendering with the
half-sites in the other order is TGTWACA, and this is what the data consensus here,
AATGTAACAA, represents. The two are the same element, not a disagreement. Information is
concentrated on the two ACA/TGT triplets; the spacer base and the flanks are weakly constrained,
which is why individual database models range from a bare six-base TGTADC to a full 13-base
AATGTATCAATTT. Structurally, the early NMR work on the DSX DM domain described contacts in the
minor groove of an undistorted duplex [PMID:10898790], whereas the later crystal structures of DMRT1 showed two
adjacent antiparallel recognition helices inserted into a widened major groove making
base-specific contacts [PMID:26005864]; the current picture is major-groove reading with minor-groove
stabilization, and this shift is worth knowing when reading older descriptions. In vitro
selection across six of the seven vertebrate proteins returned sites resembling the DSX site for
all of them, differing only in efficiency and in preference at individual positions [PMID:17605809]. The family
is correspondingly cohesive here (0.86 across 20 motifs) and no paralogue is separable by
sequence. Some DMRT models drift toward pure AT-richness: the Vierstra archetype
AC0092:DMRT/HOXB is an ATATATT-like model shared with HOXB, and its nearest neighbours lie
outside the family, a reminder that AT-rich DM sites and AT-rich homeodomain sites are hard to
tell apart.

## Where it acts

DMRT1 occupancy in mouse testis is largely promoter-proximal and promoter-distal in roughly equal
measure, with thousands of sites, and the strongest targets are genes of the male pathway
(SOX9, PTGDS) and genes that DMRT1 must keep off (FOXL2, and the retinoic-acid-responsive meiotic
initiator STRA8). DMRT1 works with and against other gonadal regulators: it opposes FOXL2 and
ESR1/ESR2 in the ovarian program [PMID:21775990], and cooperates with SOX9 and SF1/NR5A1 in the testis. DMRT3
acts in the spinal cord in circuits that coordinate limb movement [PMID:22932389]. Because the factors are
tissue-restricted, the genomic distribution of DM sites is much broader than the set that is
ever occupied: in a cell that expresses no DMRT protein, the sequence is inert.

## Biology and disease

Dmrt1-null mice have severely dysgenic testes [PMID:11040213], and postnatal loss of DMRT1 in Sertoli cells
reprograms them toward granulosa cells with activation of FOXL2 and ESR2, so DMRT1 is needed
continuously, not just at the sex-determining step [PMID:21775990]. In chicken, the Z-linked DMRT1 is the male
sex-determining gene, and knockdown feminizes male gonads [PMID:19710650]. In humans, deletions of distal 9p
that remove DMRT1 cause 46,XY gonadal dysgenesis and sex reversal [PMID:9490411,11040213], and point mutations in
residues that contact DNA have the same effect [PMID:26005864]; common variants near DMRT1 are associated with
testicular germ cell tumor risk [PMID:20543847]. Outside sex determination, a premature stop codon in horse
DMRT3 underlies the ability to perform alternate gaits, and the same mutation modeled in mice
disturbs spinal circuit function [PMID:22932389].

## Reading a hit

The element is short and AT-rich in its flanks, so chance matches are common and the AT-rich
tails are readily confused with homeodomain and other minor-groove AT binders. A match cannot
be assigned to a paralogue: the seven vertebrate DM proteins select nearly the same sequence in
vitro [PMID:17605809], and most models in these databases come from HT-SELEX or methyl-HT-SELEX on isolated
domains [PMID:23332764], which measure intrinsic specificity and cannot distinguish family members. The strongest
interpretive constraint is expression: DM sites are only meaningful in tissues where a DMRT
protein is present, which for DMRT1 means gonad. Note also that the JASPAR mouse Dmrt1 matrix
MA1603.2 (TACAAAGT) is an outlier here, with nearest neighbours outside the family, so a hit
scored against that specific model deserves a second look.
families.caveats: The informative part of a DM site is two ACA/TGT triplets separated by one or two bases, so an effective width of about seven bases plus AT-rich flanks: chance matches are frequent. All seven vertebrate paralogues select nearly identical sequences in vitro, so a hit identifies the family, never the member, and expression is the only practical discriminator. AT-rich renderings of the site overlap homeodomain space, which is visible in the Vierstra AC0092:DMRT/HOXB archetype. Most models here derive from in vitro selection on isolated DM domains, which supports the sequence preference but says nothing about genomic occupancy. The JASPAR mouse Dmrt1 model MA1603.2 does not match the family consensus.

timeline.finding: The C. elegans male regulator mab-3 is related to Drosophila doublesex; their shared DNA-binding motif is named the DM domain, and a human DM gene (DMT1, now DMRT1) is testis-specific and maps to distal 9p, a region implicated in XY sex reversal.
timeline.methods: Gene cloning, sequence comparison, cross-species transgene expression
timeline.open: What DNA sequence the domain reads, and whether vertebrate DM genes act in sex development.

timeline.finding: NMR structure of the DSX DM domain: an intertwined CCHC/HCCC zinc module with a disordered tail that acts as a nascent recognition helix, described as binding the minor groove without sharp DNA bending.
timeline.methods: NMR spectroscopy, mutagenesis
timeline.open: How a minor-groove binder achieves the unusually high sequence specificity measured for DSX and MAB-3.

timeline.finding: Dmrt1-null mice fail postnatal testis differentiation, with phenotypes like those of human 9p deletions, while ovaries develop normally: the first functional evidence for a vertebrate DM gene in male development.
timeline.methods: Mouse gene targeting

timeline.finding: Random-oligonucleotide selection on six of the seven vertebrate DMRT proteins returns DSX-like sites for all of them, differing in efficiency and per-position preference, and some DMRTs bind DNA as heterodimers.
timeline.methods: In vitro selection, gel mobility shift, transfection assays
timeline.open: How paralogues with near-identical sites reach different targets.

timeline.finding: ChIP in juvenile mouse testis identifies almost 1,400 DMRT1-bound promoter-proximal regions, enriched for a motif closely resembling the in vitro site; DMRT1 activates some targets and represses others, differently in germ cells and Sertoli cells.
timeline.methods: ChIP-chip, conditional knockouts, expression profiling

timeline.finding: Deleting DMRT1 in Sertoli cells, even in adults, activates Foxl2 and reprograms them into granulosa-like cells, so testis identity has to be maintained continuously.
timeline.methods: Conditional mouse knockout

timeline.finding: Crystal structures of DMRT1 on DNA show two adjacent antiparallel recognition helices in a widened major groove making base-specific contacts, with tetramer, trimer and dimer binding modes, and ChIP-exo suggests several modes are used in vivo. This replaced the minor-groove picture drawn from the DSX NMR structure.
timeline.methods: X-ray crystallography, ChIP-exo, analysis of fly and human mutations
timeline.open: Which stoichiometry operates at which genomic sites.

open: Which binding stoichiometry operates at functional sites is unresolved: DMRT1 binds DNA as a tetramer, trimer or dimer in crystals and ChIP-exo suggests more than one mode in testis, but which mode a given genomic site uses, and whether the mode changes the transcriptional outcome, is not known.

How DMRT paralogues with near-identical in vitro preferences reach different targets is unclear: the proposed explanations, subtle per-position preferences and DMRT heterodimers, compete with the simpler view that non-overlapping expression does all the work.

The JASPAR mouse Dmrt1 matrix MA1603.2 (TACAAAGT) breaks the second half-site of the pseudopalindrome (ACAAAGT against ACAWTGT) and its nearest neighbours lie outside the family; whether it records a real in vivo variant of the site or a misassigned motif is not settled by the data.

families.name: Chromatin regulators without a classical DBD
families.def: Motifs attributed to cofactors, readers and writers that have no sequence-specific DBD of their own: BPTF, PHF1, PHF21A, DPF1/2, MYSM1, SETBP1, TOPORS, GATAD2A, ZFPM1, ZZZ3, GLYR1, TCF20, SP140L, NAIF1, ARID1A.
aka: Chromatin regulators without a classical DBD
ChIP-derived motifs of readers and writers
families.short: A deliberate holding bucket, and the place to learn why a ChIP-derived motif may not belong to the protein it is labelled with. The twenty motifs here are attributed to chromatin readers, writers and scaffolds that have no sequence-specific DNA-binding domain: BPTF, PHF1, PHF21A, DPF1, MYSM1, SETBP1, TOPORS, GATAD2A, ZFPM1, ZZZ3, GLYR1, MTF2, TCF20, SP140L, NAIF1 and ARID1A. Cohesion is 0.38, the lowest in the atlas, and six models are explicitly flagged as resembling another family. The clearest case is ZFPM1/FOG-1, which binds GATA-1's zinc finger rather than DNA, yet carries a GATA motif. Read this page as a warning list.
families.long:
## The factors

Curation of the human transcription factors draws a line between proteins that carry a recognised sequence-specific DNA-binding domain and the much larger set of chromatin-associated proteins that reach DNA only through partners [PMID:29425488]. Everything in this family is on the wrong side of that line. BPTF is the largest subunit of the NURF remodelling complex, a PHD-finger and bromodomain histone reader. PHF1 and MTF2 are Polycomb-like accessory subunits of PRC2. DPF1 is a BAF subunit with a double PHD finger, GATAD2A (p66alpha) a NuRD subunit, ZFPM1 is FOG-1, and ZZZ3 belongs to the ATAC acetyltransferase complex, where its ZZ-type zinc finger binds the histone H3 N-terminus [PMID:30217978]. GLYR1 is a nucleosome-destabilising PWWP protein, PHF21A is BHC80 of the LSD1-CoREST complex, MYSM1 a histone H2A deubiquitinase, and ARID1A the BAF subunit whose ARID domain binds DNA with no sequence preference [PMID:14982958]. SETBP1, TCF20, TOPORS, SP140L and NAIF1 are scaffolds and modifiers.

Several do touch DNA - SETBP1 through AT-hooks, ZZZ3 through a Myb/SANT-like region, SP140L through a SAND domain, DPF1 through a Kruppel-like zinc finger - so "no classical DNA-binding domain" is not "no DNA contact". What none has is a demonstrated, discriminating, sequence-specific site. MTF2 is the instructive exception: it binds DNA directly and recruits PRC2 to CpG islands, but what it reads is helical shape, not sequence [PMID:29808031].

## The motif

A ChIP-seq experiment reports where a protein is crosslinked, not what it recognizes. If the protein is carried to chromatin by a sequence-specific partner, de novo motif discovery on its peaks returns the partner's motif, reproducibly, and the result is then filed under the wrong name. This is not a rare accident: non-targeted transcription factor motifs are a systemic component of ChIP-seq datasets [PMID:25070602], active promoters generate false-positive "phantom peaks" independent of the antigen [PMID:26117547], and high-occupancy target regions accumulate signal for many proteins at once [PMID:31114922,24173036]. A survey of 208 chromatin-associated proteins in one human cell type found exactly that pattern [PMID:32728244].

The atlas exposes it mechanically, through the resembles flag and by comparing each model's best within-family match against its best out-of-family match. Six models are flagged, and the cases are concrete:

ZFPM1 (FOG1.H14CORE.0.I.C) reads TTATCt, is flagged as resembling GATA, and has an out-of-family similarity of 0.98. FOG-1 was characterised in 1997 as a multitype zinc finger protein that acts as a cofactor for GATA-1 by binding GATA-1's own zinc finger [PMID:9230307]. It does not bind DNA sequence-specifically. The motif is GATA's. GATAD2A gives the same answer from another complex: its P66A model, tCTTATCTcthtthhnatctt, is flagged as resembling GATA, and its out-of-family similarity (0.858) exceeds its within-family one (0.813) - NuRD is recruited to GATA sites, and the motif came along for the ride. ARID1A's TTTTATtGg is ChIP-only, graded C, flagged as resembling the posterior HOX family, and scores 0.944 against another family; the ARID domain of BAF subunits binds DNA without sequence specificity [PMID:14982958]. PHF1 (tCGG) and NAIF1 (CGTA) are flagged as resembling the CpG readers and are essentially CpG dinucleotides. MTF2's CCCGaCGg is flagged as resembling MTF1 - a different protein with a similar name - at 0.98.

Three more deserve naming. The family's highest-information model, Vierstra archetype AC0442 [PMID:32728250] labelled TOPORS with function "Unknown", is a 17-base-pair, 31.5-bit consensus TCCCAAAGTAGCTGGGA that closely matches a segment of the Alu consensus: it reads as repeat sequence, not a factor site. SP140L's tACGTcA is a fragment of the canonical CRE, TGACGTCA. DPF1 is the genuine near-miss: its HOCOMOCO and CIS-BP models (CaCCTATAG, CTATAGGtG) have in vitro selection support and agree at 0.97, but their best out-of-family similarity is 0.996 and the Vierstra archetype carrying them is labelled DPF/ZBTB and classed as C2H2 - so even here the model cannot be assigned to DPF1 rather than a ZBTB protein. The rest (SETBP1's A-rich aCgvaaAAaaaA, TCF20's gAdTataT, GLYR1's four-base AAAT, PHF21A's rcaaAaAcA, BPTF's AtAACA at 5.4 bits) are short and uninformative; SETBP1's is consistent with its AT-hooks, which give affinity without specificity.

## Where it acts

Wherever the recruiting factor acts. GATAD2A and ZFPM1 signal at GATA sites in erythroid and megakaryocytic cells; PRC2 accessory subunits at CpG islands; BAF and NURF subunits at active promoters and enhancers, which is also where phantom peaks and high-occupancy regions live. The useful statement is always about the complex and its recruiter, not about a sequence.

## Biology and disease

These are important genes. PHF21A disruption in the Potocki-Shaffer region causes intellectual disability with craniofacial anomalies [PMID:22770980]; de novo SETBP1 mutations cause Schinzel-Giedion syndrome [PMID:20436468]; ARID1A is among the most frequently mutated genes in human cancer, and TCF20 and BPTF are established disease genes too. None of that makes their motif models usable. Clinical importance and motif quality are independent.

## Reading a hit

Do not attribute a hit in this family to the labelled protein. Instead, use the entry backwards: if a scan returns a hit for one of these names, identify which real family the model belongs to and read that entry. For ZFPM1 and GATAD2A, go to GATA. For PHF1 and NAIF1, go to MBD_CXXC. For ARID1A, go to the posterior HOX family. For SETBP1 and PHF21A, go to HMGA and read what an AT-hook does. Check TOPORS against repeat annotation. And apply the general rule beyond this page: whenever a motif is attributed to a cofactor, reader, writer or remodeller, ask whether the ChIP experiment that produced it was measuring the protein or its recruiter.
families.caveats: Nothing in this family should be scanned with the intention of finding sites for the named protein. These are chromatin proteins without sequence-specific DNA-binding domains, and their models are best explained as the motifs of the sequence-specific factors that recruit them, as phantom peaks over active promoters, or as repeat sequence. Cohesion is 0.38, the lowest in the atlas; six of twenty models are flagged as resembling another family, and several score higher against other families than within this one. The NAIF1 model is a Gallus gallus transfer at 74 percent domain identity. Even DPF1, the only member with in vitro support and internal agreement, is 0.996 similar to a ZBTB C2H2 model and cannot be attributed.

timeline.finding: FOG (ZFPM1) was isolated in a two-hybrid screen with the GATA-1 zinc finger and shown to act as a cofactor that binds GATA-1 rather than DNA, the clearest early case of a nuclear protein whose chromatin localization is entirely borrowed from a sequence-specific partner.
timeline.methods: Yeast two-hybrid, expression analysis, transcription and differentiation assays
timeline.open: Whether such cofactors would be distinguishable from direct binders in genome-wide assays, which did not yet exist.

timeline.finding: The ARID-containing SWI/SNF subunit p270 (ARID1A) was shown to bind DNA without regard to sequence, excluding the idea that its DNA-binding domain recruits the remodeller to specific promoter sequences.
timeline.methods: In vitro DNA-binding assays, substitution mutagenesis

timeline.finding: Highly expressed loci in yeast were found to be 'hyper-ChIPable': the Sir silencing complex, an unrelated transcription factor, a centromeric protein and even nuclear GFP were all apparently enriched there, and the signal scaled with transcription, showing that ChIP enrichment need not reflect binding at all.
timeline.methods: ChIP-seq and ChIP-qPCR with control proteins and inducible genes
timeline.open: How much of the human ChIP-seq catalog is affected.

timeline.finding: Across hundreds of human ChIP-seq datasets, a small set of motifs (CTCF-like, ETS-like, JUN-like and THAP11) were repeatedly enriched in experiments that did not target those factors; peaks carrying such a 'zinger' motif and lacking the assayed factor's own motif made up as much as 45% of a dataset.
timeline.methods: Motif enrichment analysis across hundreds of ChIP-seq datasets
timeline.open: Whether these peaks reflect tethering, co-occupancy or an immunoprecipitation artifact.

timeline.finding: ChIP-seq profiles for two Drosophila remodelers were reproduced in mutant embryos that do not express the antigen, identifying about 3,000 mostly active-promoter loci prone to non-specific enrichment, and the same 'phantom peaks' were found across many epigenetic-regulator profiles.
timeline.methods: ChIP-seq with knockout chromatin and multiple antibodies, reanalysis of published profiles
timeline.open: Which published cofactor motifs are phantom-peak artifacts rather than tethering.

timeline.finding: A curated catalog of over 1,600 human transcription factors formalized the distinction between proteins with a recognized sequence-specific DNA-binding domain and chromatin-associated proteins without one, giving the criterion by which a motif attributed to a reader or writer is suspect.
timeline.methods: Manual curation of DNA-binding domains and motif evidence

timeline.finding: MTF2, a PRC2 accessory subunit with no classical DNA-binding domain, was shown to bind DNA directly and recruit PRC2 to CpG-dense regions of reduced helix twist, demonstrating that a chromatin protein can select targets by DNA shape rather than by base sequence - a mode no position weight matrix represents.
timeline.methods: In vitro DNA binding, knockout cells, genome-wide EZH2 and H3K27me3 mapping

timeline.finding: ChIP-seq of 208 chromatin-associated proteins in one human cell line confirmed the pattern at scale: motifs of other factors were co-enriched in the peaks of many proteins, FOX-family motifs appearing in those of 37 of them, and high-occupancy regions contained motifs for only a minority of the proteins found there.
timeline.methods: ChIP-seq of 208 proteins in HepG2 with motif analysis
timeline.open: How to assign a co-enriched motif to tethering, co-binding or artifact in any individual case.

open: For each model here it is unresolved which of three explanations applies - tethering by a sequence-specific partner, a phantom peak over an active promoter, or genuine low-specificity binding - and no published experiment distinguishes them protein by protein; the GATA-like ZFPM1 and GATAD2A models are the only ones where the partner is named with confidence.

Whether DPF1 has a site of its own is open: its HOCOMOCO and CIS-BP models have in vitro selection support and agree with each other at 0.97, yet they are 0.996 similar to a C2H2 ZBTB model and the archetype that carries them is labelled DPF/ZBTB, so in vitro support does not settle which protein the site belongs to.

How many chromatin proteins resemble MTF2 - binding DNA directly but selecting targets by shape or CpG density rather than base sequence - is unknown, and such binding would be invisible to the position weight matrices this atlas is built from.
Whether the ARID1A model, flagged as resembling the posterior HOX motif, reflects tethering of BAF by a homeodomain factor or the AT-rich preference of a non-specific ARID domain has not been tested.

families.name: HIF / ARNT
families.def: Hypoxia response element (A/G)CGTG. HIF1A, EPAS1/HIF2A, HIF3A, ARNT, ARNT2.
families.short: The hypoxia response element is the site read by HIF, a heterodimer of an oxygen-labile alpha subunit (HIF-1alpha, HIF-2alpha/EPAS1, HIF-3alpha) and the constitutive beta subunit ARNT (HIF-1beta) or its paralogue ARNT2. Both partners are bHLH-PAS proteins. The element is an asymmetric E-box half-site pair: ARNT reads the 3' GTG and the alpha subunit reads a 5' half that is usually TAC or GAC, giving the five-base core (A/G)CGTG, most often written in context as ...TACGTGC... When oxygen is plentiful the alpha subunits are prolyl-hydroxylated and destroyed by the VHL ubiquitin ligase, so occupancy of these sites is a direct readout of oxygen availability. HIF drives erythropoietin, VEGFA and the glycolytic genes, and the pathway is constitutively active in VHL-mutant kidney cancer.
families.long:
## The factors

HIF is an obligate heterodimer of one oxygen-regulated alpha subunit and one constitutive beta subunit. The alpha subunits are HIF-1alpha (*HIF1A*), HIF-2alpha (*EPAS1*) and HIF-3alpha (*HIF3A*, which produces several splice isoforms, some of them dominant-negative); the beta subunits are ARNT (also called HIF-1beta) and the brain- and kidney-enriched paralogue ARNT2. All are bHLH-PAS proteins: a basic helix-loop-helix domain followed by PAS-A and PAS-B. Alpha-subunit prolines are hydroxylated by the PHD enzymes, creating the binding site for the VHL ubiquitin ligase; a separate asparagine hydroxylation by FIH blocks p300/CBP recruitment (Kaelin and Ratcliffe 2008) [PMID:18498744]. HIF-1alpha is close to ubiquitous; HIF-2alpha is enriched in endothelium, kidney interstitium, lung and sympathoadrenal tissue. ARNT is the shared partner of the whole bHLH-PAS class: it also dimerizes with AHR, SIM1/2 and NPAS factors, and forms homodimers. Loss of *Arnt* in mice is embryonic lethal around E10.5 with defective angiogenesis and placental vascularization (Maltepe et al. 1997) [PMID:9121557]. HIF-1 was first defined as the hypoxia-inducible activity at the erythropoietin enhancer (Semenza and Wang 1992) [PMID:1448077] and then identified as a bHLH-PAS heterodimer (Wang et al. 1995) [PMID:7539918].

## The motif

The core is (A/G)CGTG, conventionally written RCGTG. Unlike the palindromic E-box CACGTG, the HIF site is an asymmetric pair of half-sites: selection experiments assign the 3' half-site GTG to ARNT, while the 5' half comes from the partner (AHR prefers T(C/T)GC and SIM prefers GT(G/A)C, so ARNT is the constant element in all of them) (Swanson et al. 1995) [PMID:7592839]. For HIF the 5' half is usually TAC or GAC, so the full site reads TACGTGC or GACGTGC. One substitution, C to T at the first position, is therefore all that separates an HRE from a canonical E-box. Crystal structures of mouse HIF-2alpha-ARNT and HIF-1alpha-ARNT bound to an HRE show ARNT spiraling around the outside of the alpha subunit; the DNA-reading head rotates and extends and cooperates with a distal PAS domain, and cancer-associated alpha-subunit mutations map to residues that establish DNA binding (Wu et al. 2015) [PMID:26245371]. Systematic measurements across the family find 12-15 bp footprints in which flanking-base preferences, not the core, distinguish members that share a core (Bersten et al. 2026) [PMID:41495897]. The consensus computed from the 19 members here is ACGTGc, core plus a 3' C preference, matching the compiled consensus HRE (Wenger et al. 2005) [PMID:16234508]. Nothing in the sequence distinguishes HIF-1alpha from HIF-2alpha (Smythies et al. 2019) [PMID:30429208]. Two entries need care: JASPAR EPAS1 (MA2325.1) is written GCACGTAC, the reverse complement of GTACGTGC, so it is the same site on the other strand; JASPAR Arnt (MA0004.1) is an ARNT-homodimer palindrome, not an HRE.

## Where it acts

RCGTG is expected several million times per strand in a 3-Gb genome, and only a small fraction is ever occupied. Chromatin is the dominant filter: occupancy is enriched roughly 20-fold at DNase-hypersensitive sites that were already open in normoxia, irrespective of distance from promoters (Schodel et al. 2011) [PMID:21447827]. Confirmed sites number in the hundreds to low thousands per cell type and often lie far from the genes they regulate. The two isoforms partition consistently: HIF-1 is biased toward promoter-proximal sites and HIF-2 toward promoter-distant sites, each with a cell-type-specific repertoire that does not redistribute with hypoxia severity or duration (Smythies et al. 2019) [PMID:30429208]. Because the core contains a CpG, HREs cluster with CpG-rich promoters and are sensitive to DNA methylation. Functional HREs generally need neighboring sequence, historically called the HIF ancillary sequence, and commonly co-occur with CREB/ATF, SP1 and AP-1 sites (Wenger et al. 2005) [PMID:16234508].

## Biology and disease

HIF targets include *EPO*, *VEGFA*, the glucose transporter *SLC2A1*, *LDHA*, *PDK1* and *CA9*, coordinating oxygen delivery with a shift to glycolysis. Biallelic *VHL* loss in clear-cell renal carcinoma leaves HIF-2 constitutively active, which made the PAS-B pocket seen in the HIF structures a drug target (Wu et al. 2015; Kaelin and Ratcliffe 2008) [PMID:26245371,18498744]. Somatic gain-of-function *EPAS1* mutations that block hydroxylation cause paraganglioma with polycythemia (Zhuang et al. 2012) [PMID:22931260], and *EPAS1* carries the strongest selection signal in Tibetan high-altitude adaptation (Yi et al. 2010) [PMID:20595611]. The pathway is also the target of prolyl-hydroxylase inhibitors used for renal anemia.

## Reading a hit

An RCGTG match on its own licenses almost no conclusion: five informative base pairs occur millions of times, and the great majority are never bound. Treat it as a candidate only in accessible chromatin, and preferably with hypoxia-responsive expression nearby. A hit cannot tell you which alpha subunit bound, and it barely distinguishes HIF:ARNT from the other ARNT complexes: AHR:ARNT prefers GCGTG, SIM:ARNT GT(G/A)CGTG, and ARNT homodimers the palindromic CACGTG, so the discriminating information sits in one or two weakly constrained positions. Evidence is skewed: eight of the ten HOCOMOCO models here are ChIP-only (letter P) at grade B or C, supporting "this region was occupied in cells" rather than "this protein binds this sequence"; the one HT-SELEX model, ARNT2.H14CORE.2.S.C, is a palindromic CACGTGAC of the kind an ARNT2 homodimer makes. The CIS-BP ARNT entry M01719_2.00 is transferred from mouse at 100% DNA-binding-domain identity: safe, but not a human measurement. The Vierstra archetype AC0072:HIF1A/ARNT is named after the factors whose motifs clustered together and is not a claim that HIF1A and ARNT can be told apart.
families.caveats: The core is only five informative base pairs, so chance matches vastly outnumber real sites and a hit is close to uninformative without chromatin or expression evidence. HIF-1alpha and HIF-2alpha share one consensus and cannot be distinguished by sequence; neither can HIF:ARNT be cleanly separated from AHR:ARNT, SIM:ARNT or ARNT homodimers, since all read CGTG with differences at one or two flanking positions. Most HOCOMOCO models here are ChIP-only at grade B or C, so they reflect occupied regions and may include indirect binding; ChIP peaks lacking any RCGTG are well documented. The ARNT entries in JASPAR and CIS-BP include palindromic E-boxes that are homodimer, not HIF, motifs, and one JASPAR entry is written on the opposite strand.

timeline.finding: A hypoxia-inducible nuclear activity was mapped to a short element in the 3' enhancer of the human erythropoietin gene that is required for its transcriptional induction, defining the hypoxia response element operationally before any protein was known.
timeline.methods: Electrophoretic mobility shift, enhancer mutagenesis in reporter assays
timeline.open: The identity of the binding protein and the generality of the element beyond the EPO locus.

timeline.finding: HIF-1 was purified and shown to be a heterodimer of two bHLH-PAS proteins, an oxygen-regulated alpha subunit and the constitutive beta subunit now called ARNT, explaining why the element is an asymmetric pair of E-box half-sites.
timeline.methods: Protein purification, peptide sequencing, reconstitution

timeline.finding: Binding-site selection with AHR, ARNT and SIM established the pairing rules for the class: ARNT reads the 3' GTG half-site in every complex while the partner supplies the 5' half, so the few bases 5' of CGTG carry almost all of the discriminating information.
timeline.methods: In vitro binding-site selection (SELEX) with recombinant proteins
timeline.open: Whether one or two weakly constrained positions suffice to separate HREs from AHR and SIM sites in genomic sequence.

timeline.finding: Prolyl hydroxylation of the alpha subunits by the PHD enzymes followed by VHL-dependent degradation, with a separate asparaginyl hydroxylation blocking coactivator recruitment, was consolidated as the mechanism that makes occupancy of these sites a readout of oxygen tension rather than of sequence.
timeline.methods: Review of biochemistry, genetics and structural work

timeline.finding: Genome-wide ChIP-seq showed that HIF binding is concentrated at sites already DNase-hypersensitive in normoxia, roughly 20-fold enriched there and largely independent of distance from promoters, so chromatin rather than the five-base core is the main filter on which matches are used.
timeline.methods: ChIP-seq in human cells with DNase-hypersensitivity comparison
timeline.open: Why many accessible RCGTG matches nonetheless stay unbound.

timeline.finding: Crystal structures of mouse HIF-2alpha-ARNT and HIF-1alpha-ARNT bound to an HRE showed ARNT spiraling around the outside of the alpha subunit, with the DNA-reading head rotated and cooperating with a distal PAS domain, and placed cancer-associated alpha-subunit mutations at residues that establish DNA binding.
timeline.methods: X-ray crystallography

timeline.finding: HIF-1 and HIF-2 were shown to partition consistently in chromatin, HIF-1 toward promoter-proximal and HIF-2 toward promoter-distant sites, with cell-type-specific repertoires that do not redistribute with the severity or duration of hypoxia, although neither isoform has a distinguishable consensus.
timeline.methods: ChIP-seq across cell types and hypoxic conditions
timeline.open: What establishes the isoform partition, given an identical core preference.

timeline.finding: Systematic binding measurements across bHLH-PAS proteins reported footprints of 12-15 bp in which preferences for bases flanking the shared core, rather than the core itself, separate members, revising the long-standing description of these sites as 5-6 bp elements.
timeline.methods: High-throughput in vitro binding across family members
timeline.open: Whether the flanking preferences are strong enough to assign genomic matches to one complex.

open: What makes HIF-1 favor promoter-proximal sites and HIF-2 promoter-distant ones is unresolved: the two share one consensus and the partition is stable across hypoxic conditions, so the explanation has been sought in chromatin context and cofactors rather than in sequence, without a settled answer.

Whether the flanking-base and DNA-shape preferences measured in vitro can actually separate HIF:ARNT from AHR:ARNT, SIM:ARNT and ARNT homodimers in genomic sequence is untested; the recent biophysics says the information exists outside the core, while every motif model in this family still encodes little more than RCGTG.

The functional role of HIF-3alpha remains disputed, with some isoforms described as dominant-negative competitors for ARNT and others as transcriptionally active on HRE-like sites; the HIF3A models here are ChIP-only and do not settle it.

It is not known what fraction of HIF ChIP peaks lacking any RCGTG reflects indirect binding through partner factors as opposed to occupancy of degenerate sites that current models score too low to recover.

families.name: HNF4
families.def: DR1 with strong 5' extension. HNF4A, HNF4G, NR2C1/2 (TR2/TR4).
families.short: HNF4A and HNF4G are nuclear receptors that bind DNA only as homodimers, on a DR1: two hexameric half-sites in the same orientation separated by exactly one base pair. Their preferred half-site drifts away from the superfamily's AGGTCA towards AG(G/T)CCA, which is why the databases render the HNF4 motif as CAAAGTCCA, or at full length as a 13 bp DR1. That drift is real specificity: the HNF4-specific binding motif is bound by HNF4A and not by other nuclear receptors tested in vivo. The same family here also holds NR2C1 and NR2C2 (TR2/TR4), whose models are generic AGGTCA DR1s and are not distinguishable from RXR or COUP-TF. HNF4A is the central regulator of hepatocyte, islet and intestinal gene expression and the MODY1 gene.
families.long:
## The factors

HNF4A (NR2A1) and HNF4G (NR2A2) are C4 double-zinc-finger nuclear receptors, discovered as a liver-enriched activator and immediately recognised as a steroid-receptor-superfamily member (Sladek et al. 1990) [PMID:2279702]. HNF4A is expressed in hepatocytes, pancreatic islet beta cells, intestine, kidney proximal tubule and stomach; HNF4G overlaps, weighted towards intestine and stomach. Unlike most of the superfamily they do not use RXR: HNF4A recognises its target genes exclusively as a cooperative homodimer (Lu et al. 2008) [PMID:18829458]. Fatty acyl-CoA thioesters have been proposed as ligands, but HNF4 is usually treated as constitutively active, regulated through coactivators and isoform choice (P1 versus P2 promoters).

This family also contains NR2C1 (TR2) and NR2C2 (TR4), broadly expressed orphan receptors that homodimerize and heterodimerize with each other [PMID:12093744]. They are grouped here because their motif models are DR1 elements in the same frame, not because they are HNF4 paralogues. The family holds 18 models in total (JASPAR 6, HOCOMOCO 6, CIS-BP 4, Vierstra 2).

## The motif

The architecture is a DR1: two hexamers on the same strand with a single base between them, generically AGGTCAxAGGTCA (Khorasanizadeh and Rastinejad 2001) [PMID:11406412]. HNF4 departs from that hexamer. Its models read AGKCCA-A-AGTCCA at full length (CIS-BP M08219, HOCOMOCO HNF4A.H14CORE.0 gGtyCAAAGTcC, JASPAR MA1494.2 ggGTCCAAAGGTCA), and the short JASPAR models for both paralogues (MA0114.5, MA0484.3) give only the 9 bp core CAAAGTCCA, covering the spacer and the 3' half-site.

Protein-binding microarrays comparing HNF4A, RXRA and COUP-TFII resolved this into a named element: the HNF4-specific binding motif, H4-SBM, xxxxCAAAGTCCA [PMID:22383578]. ChIP data indicated the H4-SBM is bound by HNF4A and not by ten other nuclear receptors in vivo, and the specificity maps to Asp69 and Arg76 in the DNA-binding domain, a residue combination unique to HNF4 among human nuclear receptors [PMID:22383578]. The same study reported a previously unrecognised polarity in the classical DR1 for HNF4A, RXRA and COUP-TFII homodimers (Fang et al. 2012) [PMID:22383578]. The 2.0 A structure of the HNF4A DBD on the HNF1A promoter element shows the cooperative homodimer and the contacts that give this element its strong 5' extension (Lu et al. 2008) [PMID:18829458].

So the family splits into two unequal halves. HNF4A and HNF4G carry the AGTCCA-flavoured signature and are partly distinguishable from the rest of the superfamily - but not from each other, their models being 0.999 similar. NR2C1 and NR2C2 models are either the bare hexamer AGGTCA (four of the eighteen models here) or a generic AGGTCAxAGGTCA DR1, and are not distinguishable from RXR homodimers or COUP-TF. That is why the family's data consensus is GgTcAAAGGTCA, the generic DR1, rather than the H4-SBM quoted above, and why the family's medoid model (HOCOMOCO NR2C2.H14CORE.1.PS.A) matches motifs outside this family better than inside it, 0.985 against 0.86. The disagreement is not an error in either source: it reflects a family that contains one receptor pair with a private motif and one without.

## Where it acts

HNF4A occupies promoters and enhancers across the hepatocyte, islet, intestinal and renal gene programs. Promoter-occupancy mapping in human liver and pancreatic islets placed HNF4A in tissue-specific circuits with HNF1A and HNF6/ONECUT1 (Odom et al. 2004) [PMID:14988562], and combining protein-binding microarrays with expression and ChIP data extended the human target list (Bolotin et al. 2010) [PMID:20054869]. HNF4 motifs are among the most enriched in liver open chromatin and co-occur with HNF1A/HNF1B, FOXA1/FOXA2, CEBPA/CEBPB, ONECUT1 and NR5A2 sites. On the NR2C side, the best-characterised sites are DR1 elements in the embryonic and fetal beta-type globin promoters, where the TR2/TR4 heterodimer forms the core of a repressor complex (Tanabe et al. 2002) [PMID:12093744].

## Biology and disease

Heterozygous HNF4A mutations cause maturity-onset diabetes of the young type 1 (Yamagata et al. 1996) [PMID:8945471], and some of the same alleles cause transient neonatal hyperinsulinism and macrosomia. Germline Hnf4a loss is embryonic lethal: without HNF4A in the visceral endoderm, embryonic ectoderm dies at E6.5 and gastrulation is impaired [PMID:7958910]. Liver-specific deletion in adult mice causes hepatic lipid accumulation, low serum cholesterol and triglycerides and raised serum bile acids, traced to reduced apolipoprotein B and microsomal triglyceride transfer protein and to reduced basolateral bile-acid transporters (Hayhurst et al. 2001) [PMID:11158324]. HNF4A is required for intestinal and hepatic differentiation, and its loss or isoform switching is seen in hepatocellular carcinoma and colorectal cancer. TR2/TR4 repression of the fetal globin genes makes NR2C1 and NR2C2 candidate targets for induction of fetal hemoglobin in sickle-cell disease and beta-thalassemia [PMID:12093744].

## Reading a hit

This family contains the one place in the nuclear receptor superfamily where a matrix does come close to naming a receptor. A clean CAAAGTCCA or full AGTCCA-type DR1 is reasonable evidence for HNF4A or HNF4G, given that the H4-SBM was bound by HNF4A and not by ten other nuclear receptors tested (Fang et al. 2012) [PMID:22383578]. It still does not separate HNF4A from HNF4G; use expression, since the two rarely overlap strongly outside intestine and stomach. A generic AGGTCAxAGGTCA hit tells you much less: RXR homodimers, PPAR:RXR, COUP-TF/NR2F and TR2/TR4 all use DR1. Scale matters too: a 9-mer like CAAAGTCCA occurs on the order of 10^4 times per haploid genome by chance, comparable to the number of HNF4A ChIP peaks recovered in liver, so the motif alone over-calls heavily outside hepatic and intestinal chromatin. Finally, one CIS-BP model labelled NR2C2 in this family, M07990 (abcaCTTCCGGGtC), contains a CTTCC/GGAA core and its nearest neighbours across all four databases are ETS motifs; the family data flags it with altFamily ETS_EHF. Treat it as indirect or misassigned rather than as evidence that TR4 binds an ETS site.
families.caveats: Two different things live in this family. An HNF4-flavoured site (CAAAGTCCA, or a DR1 whose half-sites read AGTCCA) is genuinely informative for HNF4A/HNF4G, though it cannot separate those two paralogues. A generic AGGTCAxAGGTCA DR1 - which is what the NR2C1 and NR2C2 models here are, four of them being the bare hexamer - is shared with RXR homodimers, PPAR:RXR and COUP-TF, and the family's own medoid matches other families better than its own. One CIS-BP model labelled NR2C2 (M07990) is an ETS-like matrix flagged as belonging elsewhere. A 9-mer occurs roughly 10^4 times per genome, so pair hits with liver or intestinal accessibility data.

open: Whether HNF4A has a physiologically regulated ligand is unresolved: fatty acyl-CoA thioesters were proposed as ligands and fatty acids such as linoleic acid are found in the ligand-binding pocket, but whether pocket occupancy changes HNF4A activity in vivo, or the receptor is effectively constitutive, is disputed.

No sequence feature is known that separates TR2/TR4 DR1 sites from those of RXR homodimers or COUP-TF, so whether the NR2C receptors have a private element, as HNF4 does with the H4-SBM, is open; this is why the family's data consensus is the generic DR1 GgTcAAAGGTCA rather than the literature's HNF4 element.

families.name: MEF2
families.def: AT-rich CTA(A/T)4TAG. MEF2A/B/C/D.
families.short: MEF2 sites are bound by the four MADS-box factors MEF2A, MEF2B, MEF2C and MEF2D, which act as obligate dimers. The element is an A/T-rich decamer, CTA(A/T)4TAG, and is easy to confuse with ordinary AT-rich sequence: the information sits almost entirely in the flanking CTA and TAG. MEF2 and SRF share the MADS fold but not the site - SRF requires the CC and GG of a CArG box where MEF2 requires TA and TA. The four paralogues have the same sequence preference and overlapping expression, so which one acts at a given element is decided by cell type and by chromatin rather than by DNA. MEF2 factors drive muscle differentiation, cardiac morphogenesis and activity-dependent programmes in neurons.
families.long:
## The factors

MEF2A, MEF2B, MEF2C and MEF2D each carry a MADS box - a 56-58 residue domain shared with SRF and with the plant and yeast MADS proteins [PMID:7744019] - immediately followed by a MEF2-specific extension of about 30 residues. The two regions together form the DNA-binding and dimerisation surface; MEF2 proteins bind only as homodimers or as heterodimers among themselves [PMID:1748287]. The crystal structure of the MEF2A core on DNA at 1.5 A resolution and an NMR structure of the same complex showed that MEF2 lacks the N-terminal extension SRF uses, and that the MEF domain C-terminal to the MADS box adopts a conformation substantially different from the equivalent region in SRF and yeast MCM1 - the structural basis for a different sequence preference and a different degree of DNA bending within one fold [PMID:10715212,10835359]. All four genes are broadly expressed with different emphases: MEF2A and MEF2D are near-ubiquitous, MEF2C is prominent in brain, cardiac and skeletal muscle and in B lymphocytes, MEF2B in germinal-centre B cells [PMID:23974956]. Activity is regulated post-translationally rather than by abundance: class IIa histone deacetylases (HDAC4, HDAC5, HDAC7, HDAC9) bind the MADS/MEF2 domain and repress it until calcium-CaMK signalling drives their nuclear export, and p38 MAPK, ERK5, sumoylation and the corepressor CABIN1 tune the same surface [PMID:17959722,23974956].

## The motif

The consensus came with the cloning of the three human SRF-related proteins, later named MEF2, which recognize CTA(A/T)4TAG, distinct from the SRF site CC(A/T)6GG [PMID:1748287]. Site selection with anti-MEF2A antibodies and skeletal muscle, heart and brain extracts later returned the same core, 5'-CT(A/T)(A/T)AAATAG-3' [PMID:7559475]; it is now written CTA(A/T)4TAG or YTA(A/T)4TAR, a 10-bp near-palindrome. Each MADS monomer reads one half, contacting the bases through an antiparallel coiled coil of two alpha-helices laid in the widened major groove, with basic residues gripping the flanking phosphates [PMID:10715212,10835359]. Because the centre is a run of A and T, essentially all the sequence information lives in the outer CTA and TAG - which is why an A/T-rich stretch with the wrong flanks scores poorly, and why MEF2 sites are easy to over-call in AT-rich genomes. That same selection experiment found that MEF2 complexes from brain extracts imposed additional constraints outside the decamer, a tissue effect that has never been resolved into a distinct PWM [PMID:7559475]. The four paralogues are not separable: in these databases the JASPAR and CIS-BP models for MEF2A, MEF2B, MEF2C and MEF2D are nearly identical (family cohesion 0.86), and no in vitro study has reported a usable difference [PMID:23332764]. One real complication is visible in the data. Alongside the canonical CTATTTTTAG models sits a second flavour - CCAAATATGG, CCNAATTTGGAA and similar - which comes almost entirely from HT-SELEX and methyl-HT-SELEX experiments and which is, read literally, a CArG box: CC plus an A/T core plus GG. These entries have lower label agreement (0.6-0.7) and their nearest non-MEF2 neighbours are MADS-box motifs from SRF. Whether this is a genuine secondary MEF2 specificity or an artefact of selection is unsettled; either way, scanning with those models partly scans for SRF.

## Where it acts

MEF2 motifs are enhancer elements, not promoter elements, and are depleted from CpG islands - unsurprising for an A/T-rich site. In differentiating muscle they mark the same enhancers as the myogenic bHLH factors MYOD1 and MYF5, and MEF2-E-box pairs are the canonical muscle enhancer architecture [PMID:17959722]; MEF2 does not have a named composite element of its own but the MEF2-plus-E-box arrangement is close to one. In neurons MEF2 sites mark activity-regulated enhancers; in cardiomyocytes they co-occur with GATA4, NKX2-5, TBX20 and SRF sites. Paralogue occupancy is largely redundant where two MEF2 proteins are co-expressed, and which paralogue compensates at a given site depends on the local chromatin environment [PMID:31722213].

## Biology and disease

MEF2 factors are required for differentiation rather than for lineage specification. Mef2c-null mouse embryos fail cardiac morphogenesis, with a single ventricular chamber and absent right ventricle, and die around E9.5 [PMID:9162005]. In neurons, activity-dependent MEF2 activation restricts excitatory synapse number, so MEF2 acts in synapse elimination rather than formation [PMID:16484497]. In humans, MEF2C haploinsufficiency - by 5q14.3 microdeletion or point mutation - causes severe intellectual disability with stereotypic movements, epilepsy and absent speech [PMID:19592390]. MEF2B is somatically mutated in roughly 11% of diffuse large B-cell lymphomas and 12% of follicular lymphomas; the mutations increase MEF2B activity, either by disrupting its interaction with the corepressor CABIN1 or by escaping inhibitory phosphorylation and sumoylation, and deregulate the proto-oncogene BCL6 [PMID:23974956]. MEF2D fusions define a subtype of B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia [PMID:27824051], and a 21-bp MEF2A deletion was reported to cause an autosomal dominant form of coronary artery disease [PMID:14645853], a link not supported by later resequencing: in about 300 patients with premature disease no causative mutations were found, the same deletion appeared in unaffected controls, and it did not cosegregate with disease [PMID:15841183].

## Reading a hit

The main risk here is the base composition of the genome, not the paralogue problem. An A/T-rich decamer is common in intergenic and intronic DNA, so scan with a model that actually constrains the CTA and TAG flanks and check the flanks in the match itself; a hit on a poly-A or poly-T stretch with soft flanks is almost certainly noise. A hit identifies MEF2, not MEF2A versus MEF2B, MEF2C or MEF2D - there is no reported sequence-level discrimination, and expression plus chromatin decide the occupant. Be explicit about which model you used, because the collections contain two incompatible flavours: canonical CTA(A/T)4TAG models, and CArG-like CCAAATATGG models from in vitro selection whose nearest neighbours are SRF motifs. If a putative MEF2 hit came from the second kind, consider SRF as an equally good explanation. The ChIP-derived MEF2A and MEF2C models here are grade B and reflect occupancy in specific cell types; because MEF2 sits beside E-boxes at muscle enhancers, E-box information can leak into ChIP-derived MEF2 models and vice versa.
families.caveats: Two distinct problems. First, base composition: the site is an A/T-rich decamer whose only real information is the CTA and TAG flanks, so AT-rich sequence throws false positives unless the flanks are genuinely constrained - inspect them in every hit. Second, the databases carry two incompatible model flavours for this family: canonical CTA(A/T)4TAG, and a CArG-like CCAAATATGG form from HT-SELEX whose nearest neighbours are SRF motifs. A hit from the second kind is as consistent with SRF as with MEF2. No model separates MEF2A, MEF2B, MEF2C and MEF2D, so report MEF2-family and let expression and chromatin decide the member.

families.name: CUX (CUT homeodomain)
families.def: ATCGAT / ATCRAT. CUX1, CUX2, SATB1, SATB2.
families.short: CUX1, CUX2 and the SATB proteins SATB1 and SATB2 bind DNA with two kinds of domain at once: CUT repeats, each an independent ~70-residue DNA-binding module, plus a homeodomain. The combination shifts the preferred site away from the generic TAAT core of other homeodomain proteins toward ATCGAT, usually embedded in a longer near-palindrome such as TAATCGATTA. CUT repeats also bind CCAAT boxes, which is how CUX1 earned its older name, CCAAT displacement protein. SATB1 and SATB2 use their CUT-like domain differently, recognizing AT-rich matrix-attachment regions rather than ATCGAT. CUX1 is a haploinsufficient tumor suppressor in myeloid and other cancers, and SATB1 and SATB2 organize chromatin over long distances in T cells and bone.
families.long:
## The factors

Four human proteins make up this family. CUX1 (also CDP, CUTL1, CASP, Clox) and CUX2 each carry three evolutionarily conserved 73-residue CUT repeats followed by a CUT-type homeodomain [PMID:7905452,11403998]. SATB1 and SATB2 carry a CUT-like domain of two repeats plus a homeodomain [PMID:12915443], and additionally an N-terminal ubiquitin-like dimerization domain, so they act as oligomers. CUX1 is broadly expressed and produces multiple isoforms by alternative splicing and proteolytic processing, which changes how many CUT repeats a given isoform contains and therefore how it binds DNA [PMID:11403998]. CUX2 is largely neural. SATB1 is highest in thymocytes and T cells [PMID:1505028]; SATB2 is expressed in osteoblasts, cortical neurons and intestinal epithelium, where it is used clinically as a lineage marker [PMID:39029534].

## The motif

The defining feature is that the homeodomain does not work alone. In vitro selection with the mammalian Cut proteins returned the palindromic consensus (t/a)(a/t)tATCGATTAt(t/c)(t/g)(t/a) - an ATCGAT core with a homeodomain ATTA motif adjacent - and showed that CUT repeat 2 binds DNA independently of the homeodomain, preferring CCAAT boxes and an ATTA core, and that the repeat and the homeodomain interact even without DNA, greatly increasing the affinity of the pair [PMID:7905452,7904999]. A separate study of CUT repeats 1 and 3 found broad, overlapping specificities, binding as dimers, with flanking sequence contributing measurably, and concluded that the native human Cut-like protein prefers a site with an ATCGAT core flanked by G/C-rich sequence rather than one built around ATTA [PMID:7799919]. Both pictures are visible in the pooled data here: the family consensus is TaATCGATa, JASPAR gives CUX1 TAATCGATA and CUX2 TaATCGATa [PMID:23332764], HOCOMOCO HT-SELEX models give TATCGATTA, and two Vierstra archetypes recover tandem ATCGAT (ATCgATaannttATCGAT) and, strikingly, CCAATAATCGAT - a CCAAT box abutting the homeodomain site, exactly the arrangement the biochemistry predicts [PMID:7905452]. ATCGAT contains a CpG, and because CpG is depleted several-fold in the human genome outside CpG islands, exact matches are considerably rarer than a naive 6-mer calculation suggests; they are also candidates for methylation-sensitive binding. Note that the SATB1 models in this family look different: the ChIP-derived HOCOMOCO entries read ataATtAwtAcTAATAAtt and tACTAATAATtA, and the JASPAR model CTAATAA - AT-rich rather than ATCGAT.

## Where it acts

CUX1 and CUX2 sites occur in promoters, where CUT-repeat binding to CCAAT elements displaces CCAAT-box activators, and in enhancers of differentiation genes [PMID:7905452,11403998]. SATB1 and SATB2 bind base-unpairing regions - AT-rich stretches with an ATC sequence context, one strand rich in A, T and C but not G - that occur in matrix- or scaffold-attachment regions [PMID:1505028]. SATB1 anchors such regions into a cage-like nuclear structure and recruits chromatin remodelling activity [PMID:12374985] to regulate genes tens of kilobases away, most clearly across the T-helper-2 cytokine locus [PMID:17057718] and the MHC class I region. So although the two halves of this family share a domain architecture, they occupy different kinds of sequence: CUX hits tend to be discrete ATCGAT-containing sites, SATB hits broad AT-rich regions.

## Biology and disease

Inactivating CUX1 mutations behave as haploinsufficient tumor-promoting events across cancer types [PMID:24316979], and CUX1 lies in the commonly deleted 7q22 region of myeloid malignancy [PMID:11403998,24316979]. SATB1 overexpression was reported to reprogram gene expression and promote breast tumor growth and metastasis in xenograft models [PMID:18337816], but an independent study using the same kinds of aggressive and non-aggressive lines found no effect on tumor formation or metastasis and no association of SATB1 expression with outcome across 1,170 patients [PMID:20595686]. Heterozygous disruption of SATB2 causes cleft palate [PMID:12915443] and, more broadly, the SATB2-associated syndrome; SATB2 immunohistochemistry is standard in distinguishing colorectal from other adenocarcinomas [PMID:39029534]. Mouse Cux1 mutants show hair follicle and immune defects, and Satb1-null mice have a severe block in thymocyte development [PMID:12374985].

## Reading a hit

A TAATCGATTA-type match is reasonably specific because ATCGAT is CpG-containing and therefore uncommon, but it does not distinguish CUX1 from CUX2, whose models are the same. Do not use an ATCGAT hit as evidence for SATB1 or SATB2: their functional target is an AT-rich base-unpairing region, and the SATB1 motifs in these databases are ChIP-derived (P grade) AT-rich models that may partly reflect the sequence composition of matrix-attachment regions rather than a crisp binding site. Also be careful with short fragments: four CIS-BP and Vierstra members of this family reduce to ATCG or ATTG, which is too short to be informative. Finally, one Vierstra archetype in this family is labelled CUX/ONECUT, a reminder that ATCGAT is shared with the ONECUT factors covered separately.
families.caveats: CUX1 and CUX2 are indistinguishable from sequence. SATB1 and SATB2 belong to the same domain family but do not share the ATCGAT preference; their models here are ChIP-derived, AT-rich, and better understood as matrix-attachment/base-unpairing regions than as a defined site, so do not infer SATB binding from an ATCGAT hit or vice versa. ATCGAT is also the preferred core of the ONECUT factors, and one Vierstra archetype in this family is explicitly labelled CUX/ONECUT, so an ATCGAT hit cannot be assigned to CUX over ONECUT without expression context. Several members reduce to 4-bp fragments that carry almost no information.
