timeline.finding: CUT repeats are shown to be DNA-binding domains in their own right; in vitro selection gives CDP and Clox one palindromic site, (t/a)(a/t)tATCGATTAt(t/c)(t/g)(t/a), with CCAAT boxes in 37% of selected sequences, and CUT repeat 3 plus the homeodomain binds with a Kd near 4 x 10^-11 M, about 200-fold tighter than CUT repeat 3 alone.
timeline.methods: In vitro site selection, EMSA, DNase footprinting, affinity measurements

timeline.finding: Random-oligonucleotide selection with CUT repeats 1 and 3 finds broad, overlapping specificities and dimeric binding, and concludes that native human CDP prefers an ATCGAT core flanked by G/C rather than a site built around the ATTA homeodomain motif, contradicting the 1994 consensus.
timeline.methods: PCR-mediated site selection, EMSA, DNase footprinting, dissociation constants
timeline.open: Which of the two descriptions applies to the full-length protein in cells was left unresolved.

timeline.finding: SATB1 recruits the NuRD deacetylase and the ACF1/ISWI remodelers to a bound site in the IL-2Ra locus and controls histone acetylation and nucleosome positioning over several kilobases; Satb1-null thymocytes misexpress many genes and T-cell development arrests.
timeline.methods: ChIP, chromatin assays, mouse gene targeting

timeline.finding: SATB1 knockdown in aggressive breast cancer cells, and overexpression in non-aggressive cells, is reported to reverse or confer tumor growth and metastasis in xenografts, and SATB1 expression is reported as prognostic.
timeline.methods: RNA interference, ectopic expression, xenografts, tumor immunohistochemistry

timeline.finding: Repeating the SATB1 manipulations in aggressive and non-aggressive breast cancer lines finds no effect on transformed phenotype, tumor formation or metastasis, and no association of SATB1 expression with outcome across 1170 patients, contradicting the 2008 result.
timeline.methods: shRNA knockdown, ectopic expression, orthotopic and tail-vein xenografts, microarray meta-analysis

timeline.finding: HT-SELEX gives human CUX2 the site TaATCGATa, combining the ATCGAT core of the 1995 study with the flanking ATTA homeodomain element of the 1994 consensus.
timeline.methods: HT-SELEX

timeline.finding: Inactivating CUX1 mutations occur in about 1-5% of 7,651 cancers and are associated with poor survival in myeloid malignancy; CUX1 loss raises PI3K signaling through reduced PIK3IP1, and it is validated as a tumor suppressor in mouse and Drosophila models.
timeline.methods: Cancer genome analysis, transposon mutagenesis in mice, Drosophila models

open: What flanks the CUX core in vivo is unsettled: in vitro selection with CDP/Clox gave ATCGATTA with an adjacent ATTA homeodomain motif, a study of the native human protein favored ATCGAT flanked by G/C, and the HT-SELEX models (TATCGATTA) side with the first.

The best-supported CUX1 model in HOCOMOCO (CUX1.H14CORE.0.PM.A, ChIP plus methyl-HT-SELEX) reads ATTGAT rather than ATCGAT, the same core as the ONECUT factors, and it is unresolved whether CUX proteins in cells mainly use this CpG-free form or whether the model reflects ONECUT-like sites in the ChIP data.

Whether SATB1 has a sequence-specific site at all is open: biochemistry describes recognition of an unpairing-prone ATC context through the minor groove with little base contact, and the only SATB1 models in these databases are ChIP-derived AT-rich patterns.

Whether SATB1 drives breast cancer progression is disputed: knockdown and overexpression in xenografts supported it in 2008, but a 2010 study with the same kinds of cell lines found no effect on tumor formation or metastasis and no association with outcome in 1170 patients.

families.name: ONECUT (HNF6)
families.def: TATTGATTT. ONECUT1/2/3.
families.short: ONECUT1 (HNF6), ONECUT2 and ONECUT3 bind DNA with a single CUT domain joined to a divergent homeodomain, and the two modules together read TATTGATT, often followed by a run of T. The same proteins also bind ATCGAT, the core preferred by the CUX proteins, and both forms appear across JASPAR, HOCOMOCO and CIS-BP. This is the most internally consistent family in the CUT class: cohesion is 0.92 and the three paralogues cannot be told apart from sequence. ONECUT1 is a liver, pancreas and biliary factor whose loss disrupts bile duct and endocrine pancreas development and causes human diabetes; ONECUT2 has become a target of interest in treatment-resistant and neuroendocrine prostate cancer.
families.long:
## The factors

Three human genes: ONECUT1 (HNF6, HNF-6alpha), ONECUT2 (OC-2) and ONECUT3 (OC-3). ONECUT1 was identified as a liver-enriched factor with an architecture no other homeodomain protein had at the time - a single CUT domain rather than the three CUT repeats of CUX1, followed by a homeodomain of a novel type [PMID:8790352]. The ONECUT homeodomain differs from the canonical fold at positions that normally contact DNA, and it depends on the CUT domain for high-affinity binding, so the functional unit is bipartite [PMID:8790352,17223534]. ONECUT1 is expressed in hepatocytes, biliary epithelium, pancreas and parts of the nervous system; ONECUT2 overlaps in liver and pancreas and is also expressed in retina and prostate; ONECUT3 is the least studied and is largely neural. The three are partly redundant, most clearly in retina, where Onecut1 and Onecut2 together, but neither alone, are required for early retinal cell fates [PMID:25228773].

## The motif

The crystal structure of the bipartite DNA-binding domain of ONECUT1 bound to the HNF6 site of the transthyretin promoter shows the CUT domain and the homeodomain engaging adjacent stretches of the duplex, and the comparison with the DNA-free protein and with the OCT1 POU domain explains how the same protein can bind DNA in two distinct modes that use different coactivators [PMID:17223534]. That structural duality shows up directly in the motif data. One set of models reads TATTGATT with a 3' T-rich extension - HOCOMOCO HNF6.H14CORE.0.PM.A gives TATTGATT, ONEC3.H14CORE.0.S.B gives TATtGATTT, and the JASPAR ONECUT1 and ONECUT3 models are the reverse complements AAATCAATA and AAAAATCAATAa. A second set reads ATCGAT, sometimes doubled: HNF6.H14CORE.2.S.B gives tATCGATcGAT, ONEC2.H14CORE.2.S.B gives TATCGATCG, and the JASPAR ONECUT2 model is GATCGATA. A ChIP-derived ONECUT2 model even resolves into six tandem ATTGAT repeats at 28 bits, which reflects clustered sites rather than a single long element. The pooled consensus is TATTGATT with cohesion 0.92, the highest in the CUT class. No position distinguishes ONECUT1, ONECUT2 and ONECUT3.

## Where it acts

ONECUT1 sites sit in liver and pancreas promoters and enhancers. Promoter-array location analysis in human hepatocytes and pancreatic islets placed ONECUT1/HNF6 in one network with HNF1A and HNF4A: HNF1A and HNF4A occupy each other's promoters, and HNF6 heads feed-forward loops - for example binding the HNF4A P2 promoter and, with HNF4A, PCK1 - involving more than 80 genes in each tissue [PMID:14988562]. The arrays covered only about 900 bp around each start site, so they show co-occupied promoters, not how close ONECUT, HNF1 and HNF4 sites lie to one another. In the developing pancreas, ONECUT1 acts upstream of NEUROG3 [PMID:10825208]. Because the informative core is about 8 bp and AT-rich, exact TATTGATT matches are expected on the order of 10^5 times in 3.1 Gb; the ATCGAT form is rarer, since CpG is depleted several-fold in the genome outside CpG islands. Tandem arrangements of ATTGAT, as in the archetype and ChIP-derived models, are a more distinctive signal than a single copy.

## Biology and disease

Hnf6-null mice fail to form a normal biliary tract, with gallbladder agenesis and abnormal intrahepatic bile ducts [PMID:11934848], and show disrupted pancreatic endocrine differentiation through loss of Ngn3 expression [PMID:10825208]. In humans, biallelic ONECUT1 mutations cause recessive syndromic diabetes with pancreatic hypoplasia and gallbladder agenesis or hypoplasia [PMID:34663987], confirmed as a cause of neonatal diabetes in a larger cohort [PMID:37639628]. Heterozygous rare variants were proposed to define a dominant early-onset, non-autoimmune form [PMID:34663987], but that cohort found no enrichment of ONECUT1 variants among 484 unexplained MODY cases and associated only heterozygous null variants, not missense ones, with type 2 diabetes [PMID:37639628]. ONECUT2 has emerged as a driver in prostate cancer: it suppresses the androgen receptor program and promotes neuroendocrine differentiation, and it is the target of active inhibitor development in castration-resistant and neuroendocrine disease [PMID:30478421,30655535]. In retina, combined loss of Onecut1 and Onecut2 depletes horizontal cells and alters retinal ganglion cell production [PMID:25228773].

## Reading a hit

A TATTGATT match, and especially a tandem ATTGATTGAT arrangement, is good evidence for a ONECUT factor, but it cannot say which of the three; the in vitro models are interchangeable. An ATCGAT-only match is genuinely ambiguous between ONECUT and CUX, and one Vierstra archetype is labelled CUX/ONECUT for exactly that reason [PMID:32728250] - resolve it with expression data, not with the motif. Evidence quality here is good: the HOCOMOCO A-grade models HNF6.H14CORE.0.PM.A and ONEC2.H14CORE.1.PM.A carry methyl-HT-SELEX (M) support, so the sequence claim does not rest on ChIP alone. Be cautious with the 28-bit tandem-repeat model, which will only match clustered sites and will miss ordinary single occurrences.
families.caveats: The three ONECUT paralogues share one motif, so a hit identifies the family only; use tissue expression to guess which one. ONECUT and CUX both prefer ATCGAT, and one Vierstra archetype is labelled CUX/ONECUT, so an ATCGAT-only match cannot be assigned between the two families. The TATTGATT core is short and AT-rich, giving roughly 10^5 expected chance matches genome-wide, so a single hit without footprint or expression support is weak. One ChIP-derived ONECUT2 model is a six-fold tandem repeat and behaves very differently from the single-site models - check which model produced your hit before interpreting its score.

timeline.finding: HNF6 is cloned as the prototype of a sixth family of liver-enriched factors, with two DNA-binding domains: a single CUT domain and a homeodomain of a new type.
timeline.methods: cDNA cloning, sequence analysis, promoter assays
timeline.open: The sequence HNF6 reads, and how its two domains share it, were not yet defined.

timeline.finding: Hnf6-null embryos have impaired pancreatic endocrine differentiation with Ngn3 expression almost abolished, HNF6 binds and stimulates the Ngn3 promoter, and adult mutants are diabetic.
timeline.methods: Mouse gene targeting, promoter binding and reporter assays

timeline.finding: Hnf6-null mice lack a gallbladder and have abnormal extra- and intrahepatic bile ducts, with HNF1B downregulated, placing HNF6 upstream of HNF1B in biliary development.
timeline.methods: Mouse gene targeting, histology, promoter assays

timeline.finding: The crystal structure of the HNF6 CUT domain plus homeodomain on the transthyretin promoter site, compared with the DNA-free protein and OCT1, shows how the bipartite domain engages DNA and gives a structural basis for two DNA-binding modes.
timeline.methods: X-ray crystallography
timeline.open: Which genomic sites use which binding mode was not mapped.

timeline.finding: Onecut1 and Onecut2 single knockouts reduce only horizontal cells, but the double knockout loses horizontal cells entirely and impairs cones, retinal ganglion cells and starburst amacrine cells, showing redundancy between the paralogues.
timeline.methods: Mouse single and double knockouts, RNA-seq

timeline.finding: ONECUT2 is identified as a driver of castration-resistant and neuroendocrine prostate cancer that suppresses the androgen-receptor program and FOXA1, and a small-molecule inhibitor reduces metastasis in mice; a 2019 study independently links it to neuroendocrine plasticity through hypoxia signaling.
timeline.methods: Network analysis, functional genomics, xenografts, small-molecule inhibition

timeline.finding: Biallelic ONECUT1 mutations cause recessive syndromic diabetes with pancreatic hypoplasia and gallbladder agenesis, rare heterozygous variants are proposed to define an early-onset non-autoimmune subgroup, and loss of ONECUT1 in stem-cell-derived pancreatic progenitors impairs the endocrine program.
timeline.methods: Human genetics, directed differentiation of pluripotent stem cells, chromatin profiling

timeline.finding: Large monogenic cohorts and UK Biobank confirm biallelic ONECUT1 variants as a cause of neonatal diabetes but find no enrichment of heterozygous variants in unexplained MODY; heterozygous null, not missense, variants associate with type 2 diabetes, revising the 2021 proposal of a MODY-like dominant form.
timeline.methods: Sequencing of monogenic diabetes cohorts, rare-variant burden testing in >400,000 individuals

open: Why ONECUT models split into two forms is unresolved: every ATCGAT model in these databases comes from in vitro selection on unmethylated DNA (HT-SELEX or CAP-SELEX), while every model built with ChIP or methyl-HT-SELEX reads ATTGAT, so it is open whether the split reflects the two binding modes inferred from structure or simply that genomic CpGs are depleted and methylated.
Whether ONECUT and CUX sites can be told apart at all is open: both families give ATCGAT in HT-SELEX, and the best-supported CUX1 model in HOCOMOCO reads ATTGAT, the main ONECUT core.

Whether heterozygous ONECUT1 variants cause a dominant MODY-like diabetes is disputed: the 2021 report proposed it from rare coding variants, but a 2023 analysis of 484 unexplained MODY cases found no enrichment, and only heterozygous null variants were associated with type 2 diabetes.

families.name: TCF/LEF (HMG box)
families.def: WNT response element CTTTGWW. TCF7, TCF7L1, TCF7L2, LEF1.
families.short: TCF/LEF proteins are the DNA-binding end of the canonical Wnt pathway. Humans have four: TCF7 (TCF-1), TCF7L1 (TCF-3), TCF7L2 (TCF-4) and LEF1. Each binds DNA through a single SRY-type HMG box plus an adjacent basic region, reading the minor groove of the Wnt response element CTTTGWW and bending the helix sharply. None activates transcription on its own: an N-terminal domain recruits beta-catenin, which supplies the coactivators, and without nuclear beta-catenin the same proteins repress through TLE/Groucho. Wnt response elements control intestinal crypt renewal, hair follicle and limb development, and T cell differentiation; they are constitutively occupied in APC-mutant colorectal cancer, and an intronic variant at TCF7L2 is the largest-effect common risk allele for type 2 diabetes.
families.long:
## The factors

Four human genes encode TCF/LEF proteins: TCF7 (originally TCF-1), TCF7L1 (TCF-3), TCF7L2
(TCF-4) and LEF1. Each carries one HMG box of the same SRY-related, sequence-specific type used
by SOX proteins, together with an adjacent basic region. The HMG box binds entirely in the minor
groove and bends DNA sharply; the LEF-1 solution structure showed the box in a widened minor
groove of a markedly distorted helix, with the basic region lying across the narrowed major
groove and adding to recognition [PMID:7651541]. Because of that geometry these proteins were first described
as architectural factors that bring proteins at flanking sites into contact, the original
example being Ets-1, RUNX and ATF/CREB at the TCR-alpha enhancer [PMID:7651541]. Transcriptional output comes
from partners rather than from the HMG box: an N-terminal domain binds the armadillo repeats of
beta-catenin, whose groove accommodates the extended TCF peptide [PMID:11136974], and without nuclear beta-
catenin the same proteins repress through TLE/Groucho and histone deacetylases. Alternative
splicing produces "E-tail" isoforms of TCF7 and TCF7L2 carrying a 30-residue cysteine clamp
(C-clamp), a second and independent DNA-binding module [PMID:17893322]. TCF7 and LEF1 are highest in T
lymphocytes and progenitors, TCF7L1 is broad and prominent in embryonic stem cells, and TCF7L2
is broad with high levels in intestine, pancreatic islets and brain.

## The motif

The Wnt response element, also called the TCF binding element, is written CTTTGWW (W = A/T),
most often CTTTGAT or CTTTGAA, and AWWCAAAG on the opposite strand [PMID:1639073]. The medoid of the 18 models
collected here is AGATCAAAG, the reverse complement of CTTTGATCT; the databases differ in which
strand they display, not in what they measured. Cyclic selection with full-length LEF-1 and
TCF-1E gave the extended element TYYCTTTGATSTT [PMID:17893322]. The invariant part is the CTTTG pentamer, where
the HMG box inserts into the minor groove [PMID:1639073]; the two positions after it are read with help from
the basic region and from residues C-terminal to the box, and site selection on Tcf1 showed the
functional element to be about 12 base pairs, not the 6-8 usually assumed for an HMG box [PMID:10867006]. E-tail
isoforms additionally bind a GC-rich helper element, RCCG, near the core [PMID:17893322]. The C-clamp does not
change which WRE is recognized, but it restricts occupancy to sites carrying the extra block [PMID:17893322],
and that is visible here: the two longest models (HOCOMOCO TCF7L1, CAGCGCCTCGATGT, 18.0 bits;
Vierstra AC0308 LEF/TCF, CAGCGCCCCGATG, 17.4 bits) pair a GC-rich block with the core instead of
extending the AT-rich flanks. All four proteins give the same motif - cohesion 0.84, the
tightest family in the HMG class - so sequence cannot separate TCF7, TCF7L1, TCF7L2 and LEF1,
and the archetypes are named "LEF/TCF" and "TCF7L/LEF". The boundary that does matter is with
SOX: the reverse complement of CTTTGWW is WWCAAAG, and the SRY/SOX consensus is WWCAAWG,
identical except that SOX tolerates T where TCF/LEF requires A [PMID:1639073,7774012].

## Where it acts

Wnt response elements are predominantly distal. Genome-wide mapping of TCF7L2 in colorectal
cancer cells placed most occupied sites well away from transcription start sites, often in
clusters of several elements per responsive gene, and recovered the CTTTG core as the enriched
motif [PMID:18268006]. Canonical targets include AXIN2, LGR5, ASCL2, SP5, NKD1, CDX1, MYC and LEF1 itself [PMID:18268006,16413481]. In
intestinal epithelium TCF7L2 sites co-occur with CDX2, HNF4A, GATA6 and SOX9 sites; in T cells
TCF7 sites co-occur with RUNX and GATA3. With two degenerate positions, CTTTGWW is expected on
the order of 1.5 million times in a 3.1 Gb double-stranded genome, so the element is not what
limits output - nuclear beta-catenin level, chromatin state and the presence of a C-clamp helper
site are.

## Biology and disease

TCF/LEF proteins convert Wnt signaling into transcription. Beta-catenin was shown to bind LEF-1
and convert it into an activator [PMID:8757136], and the Drosophila experiment with Armadillo and dTCF
established that this is the pathway's output step [PMID:9118222]. In colorectal cancer with APC loss, beta-
catenin accumulates and forms a constitutive complex with TCF7L2 that holds Wnt targets on [PMID:9065401];
activating CTNNB1 mutations produce the same result. LEF1 is required for hair follicle, tooth
and limb development; TCF7 for thymocyte development, and TCF1 marks the stem-like CD8 T cell
population that responds to checkpoint blockade; TCF7L1 restrains differentiation in embryonic
stem cells. The intronic TCF7L2 variant rs7903146 was identified as a common risk allele for
type 2 diabetes [PMID:16415884] and remains the largest-effect common variant for that disease, acting through
islet function.

## Reading a hit

A CTTTGWW match identifies a Wnt response element, not which TCF/LEF protein uses it: all four
are identical on DNA. Choosing among them needs expression data; deciding whether the site is
active needs evidence about beta-catenin. The bigger practical hazard is the SOX family:
CTTTGTT-type sequences satisfy both consensuses, several HOCOMOCO SOX models (SOX4, SOX11,
SOX13, one SOX2 model) read CCTTTGTT, and there is no sequence-only way to resolve them - an AT-
rich flank leans SOX, a GC-rich RCCG block leans an E-tail TCF. The element is common enough to
occur by chance more than a million times, so isolated matches are weak evidence. Three of the
seven HOCOMOCO models here are ChIP-only; prefer the HT-SELEX and methyl-HT-SELEX models when
the question is whether a protein binds a sequence. Finally, do not read the GC-rich block of
the long TCF7L1 models as a WRE - it is the helper site, and alone it is not a TCF/LEF motif.
families.caveats: Good confidence that a CTTTGWW match is a Wnt response element; none at all about which of TCF7, TCF7L1, TCF7L2 and LEF1 binds it, since all four share one motif (cohesion 0.84) and the archetypes are named "LEF/TCF". The element overlaps the SOX consensus at all but one position, so CTTTGTT-type hits cannot be assigned to TCF/LEF rather than SOX from sequence alone. Roughly 1.5 million matches are expected by chance genome-wide. Occupancy depends on nuclear beta-catenin and, for E-tail isoforms, on a nearby GC-rich helper site; the GC block in the longest TCF7L1 and LEF/TCF models is that helper, not the core element.

timeline.finding: The HMG boxes of TCF-1 and SRY are shown to recognize the heptamer (A/T)(A/T)CAAAG through contacts in the minor groove, with no major-groove guanine contacts: the first definition of the element now called the Wnt response element.
timeline.methods: Methylation and carbethoxylation interference footprinting, base-analogue substitution
timeline.open: Nothing yet connected the site to a signaling pathway; TCF-1 was a T cell factor of unknown input.

timeline.finding: The solution structure of the LEF-1 HMG box with its adjacent basic region shows the box in a widened minor groove of a sharply bent helix and the basic region across the narrowed major groove, supporting an architectural role in assembling the TCR-alpha enhancer complex.
timeline.methods: NMR

timeline.finding: TCF/LEF proteins are established as the output step of Wnt signaling: beta-catenin binds LEF-1 and converts it to an activator, Armadillo does the same for dTCF in Drosophila, and APC-mutant colon carcinoma cells carry a constitutive beta-catenin-TCF4 complex.
timeline.methods: Yeast two-hybrid, reporter assays, Drosophila genetics, cell-line reconstitution

timeline.finding: Two complementary results: site selection shows Tcf1 reads a 12-base-pair element rather than the 6-8 bases assumed for an HMG box, and the beta-catenin/Tcf3 crystal structure shows the TCF peptide extended along the armadillo-repeat groove.
timeline.methods: Binding-site selection and footprinting; X-ray crystallography

timeline.finding: An intronic microsatellite at TCF7L2, tagging rs7903146, is identified as a common type 2 diabetes risk allele, replicated in three cohorts, which makes this the only TCF/LEF gene with a large common-variant disease signal.
timeline.methods: Linkage follow-up and association genotyping

timeline.finding: The C-clamp of E-tail TCF7 and TCF7L2 isoforms is shown to be a second DNA-binding module: cyclic selection gives the same core element, TYYCTTTGATSTT, with or without it, but wild-type sites are additionally enriched for a GC-rich RCCG block.
timeline.methods: CASTing, surface plasmon resonance, reporter and growth assays
timeline.open: The helper block's own sequence requirements, and whether LEF1 and TCF7L1 compensate for lacking a C-clamp, were not settled.

timeline.finding: Genome-wide mapping of TCF7L2 occupancy in colorectal cancer cells finds 6,868 sites, mostly far from transcription start sites and clustered around responsive genes, with ACA/TTCAAAG recovered as the occupied motif.
timeline.methods: ChIP-chip, motif discovery, reporter assays

timeline.finding: In liver tumor organoids, beta-catenin occupies largely distinct genomic regions depending on whether it partners LEF1 or TCF7L2, and the TCF7L2-specific regions are marked by a longer GC-rich helper motif, GGRCCRTACCAC, rather than by extra copies of the classical element, which complicates the view that the four paralogues are interchangeable on DNA.
timeline.methods: CUT&RUN, single-cell RNA-seq and ATAC-seq, motif enrichment
timeline.open: Whether TCF7L2 contacts this helper sequence directly through its C-clamp or is brought there by cofactors is untested.

open: Whether the four TCF/LEF proteins are genuinely interchangeable on DNA is now in question: all four give one motif in these databases (cohesion 0.84), but CUT&RUN in liver tumor organoids puts LEF1 and TCF7L2 at largely separate sites distinguished by a GC-rich helper motif, and it is unresolved whether that reflects intrinsic DNA preference or partner-driven recruitment.

The sequence of the C-clamp helper site is not agreed: selection with TCF-1E gave the short RCCG block, genome-wide analysis in DLD1 colorectal cells gave GCCGCCR, and the liver organoid work gives the longer GGRCCRTACCAC, so a GC-rich block near a WRE cannot yet be scored against one definition.

CTTTGTT-type matches cannot be assigned between TCF/LEF and SOX: the two consensuses differ at a single position, several HOCOMOCO SOX models read CCTTTGTT, and no sequence feature has been shown to separate a SOX-occupied from a TCF/LEF-occupied site.

families.name: SNAIL / SCRATCH
families.def: E-box CAGGTG. SNAI1-3, SCRT1/2.
families.short: The SNAIL/SCRATCH proteins - SNAI1 (Snail), SNAI2 (Slug), SNAI3 (Smuc), SCRT1 and SCRT2 - are C2H2 zinc-finger repressors that read the E-box CAGGTG, the same 6 bp core that basic helix-loop-helix activators use. They carry no HLH domain; specificity comes from four or five zinc fingers, and repression from an N-terminal SNAG peptide that recruits LSD1/CoREST. SNAI1 and SNAI2 repress E-cadherin and drive epithelial-mesenchymal transition in gastrulation, neural crest migration, fibrosis and carcinoma; SCRT1 and SCRT2 do related work in neurons. SCRATCH sites carry an extra CAAC, giving the only sequence feature that separates part of this family. SNAI2 deletion causes Waardenburg syndrome type 2D and piebaldism.
families.long:
## The factors

Five human proteins fall in this family: SNAI1 (Snail), SNAI2 (Slug), SNAI3 (Smuc) and the more distant SCRT1 and SCRT2 (Scratch). All are small, 250-330 residue proteins with four to five C-terminal C2H2 zinc fingers and an N-terminal SNAG domain [PMID:11994736] - a short, highly conserved peptide that docks into the substrate pocket of the histone demethylase LSD1 and so brings the LSD1/CoREST corepressor complex to DNA [PMID:20389281]. They bind DNA as monomers; there is no dimerization interface, and no HLH or leucine zipper. SNAI1 is labile, phosphorylated by GSK3-beta and degraded by beta-TrCP, which makes its protein level a signaling readout rather than a transcriptional one [PMID:15448698]. SNAI1 and SNAI2 are expressed in mesoderm, neural crest, and in mesenchymal and carcinoma cells; SNAI3 is largely restricted to hematopoietic tissue and muscle; SCRT1 and SCRT2 are neural [PMID:11274425]. The superfamily is ancient - Snail and Scratch orthologues are present throughout bilaterians, with the SNAG domain a vertebrate/arthropod-shared feature [PMID:19427053] - and the Drosophila Snail protein that gave the family its name performs the same kind of repression in dorsoventral patterning.

## The motif

The defining site is the E-box CAGGTG (CACCTG on the other strand). It was mapped for Drosophila SNAIL by random-site selection as 5'-(G/A)(A/T)(G/A)A-CAGGTG-(C/T)AC-3', with a highly conserved 6 bp core; the same study noted that the core is identical to the bHLH binding core and that SNAIL bound CAGGTG far better than other CANNTG boxes [PMID:8371971]. Vertebrate SNAI1/2/3 models agree: HOCOMOCO and JASPAR render them gCAGGTG, ggCAGGTGc or gCACCTGT, 10-14 bits, and they are mutually indistinguishable (pairwise similarities 0.95-0.99). The SCRATCH paralogues are the exception worth knowing: SCRT1 and SCRT2 models are consistently GCAACAGGTG, 16-18 bits, with a 5' CAAC that adds real information and separates them from the SNAI models (best similarity to a SNAI motif only 0.80-0.84). Structurally the fingers contact the major groove over the core; because the flanks in the SNAI models are weak, essentially all the discriminating power is in the six core bases plus, for SCRATCH, the upstream CAAC. The family data also contains a Vierstra archetype, AC0083:SNAI/TCF:bHLH, in which SNAIL motifs cluster with TCF (E-protein) motifs and the cluster is labelled bHLH - a direct demonstration that these C2H2 motifs are not separable from bHLH motifs by sequence.

## Where it acts

SNAI sites are classically proximal-promoter elements. The human CDH1 promoter carries three E-boxes, including the E-pal element, and both SNAI1 and SNAI2 bind them [PMID:10655586,10655587]; other epithelial targets (CLDNs, OCLN, KRT8) follow the same pattern. Beyond promoters, SNAI1 occupies thousands of enhancers in mesenchymal cells. CAGGTG contains no CpG, is not CpG-island-restricted, and occurs on the order of a million times in the human genome by chance, so genome-wide occupancy is chromatin- and cofactor-limited. SNAI factors co-occur with ZEB1/ZEB2 on the same boxes (the two families cooperate sequentially in EMT, with SNAI1 induction preceding ZEB1), with TGF-beta-driven SMAD complexes, and with LSD1/CoREST and PRC2. SCRT1/SCRT2 act at neuronal promoters, where SCRT2 represses miR-25 [PMID:23516276].

## Biology and disease

Snai1-null mouse embryos die during gastrulation with a mesodermal layer that fails to complete EMT and retains E-cadherin [PMID:11689706]. Snai2-null mice are viable with pigmentation and hair defects, and in humans heterozygous or homozygous SNAI2 deletions cause Waardenburg syndrome type 2D and piebaldism, a neural crest phenotype [PMID:12444107]. SNAI1 also blocks the cell cycle and confers resistance to apoptosis, which is part of why EMT and proliferation are often anticorrelated [PMID:15155580]. Sustained SNAI1 expression in kidney tubular epithelium produces a partial EMT that drives renal fibrosis and is reversible in mice [PMID:26236989]. In carcinoma, SNAI1 and SNAI2 are induced at invasive fronts and correlate with loss of E-cadherin, but the degree to which a complete EMT occurs in human tumors, and its necessity for metastasis, remains disputed; consensus guidelines now favor describing hybrid intermediate states and caution against inferring EMT from any single marker [PMID:32300252].

## Reading a hit

A CAGGTG hit tells you that an E-box is present, not which protein family reads it. The candidate list includes the bHLH factors (TCF3/4/12, MYOD, TWIST, NEUROD, MAX, USF), ZEB1/ZEB2, INSM-related repressors and ZBTB18, alongside SNAI1-3. E-box does not mean bHLH. Within this family, SNAI1, SNAI2 and SNAI3 cannot be told apart from sequence; a hit identifies "a SNAIL-family site" at best. SCRT1/SCRT2 are the one real discrimination available: if the match extends to GCAACAGGTG, SCRATCH becomes the better guess, and the neural expression restriction helps. Evidence codes matter here. The HOCOMOCO SNAI1, SNAI2, SCRT1 and SCRT2 models are grade A with PSM evidence, meaning they are supported by ChIP-seq plus HT-SELEX and methyl-HT-SELEX, so "this protein binds this sequence" is on firm in vitro ground. SNAI3 rests on HT-SELEX alone at grade C, and the JASPAR SNAI2 (MA0745.3) and SCRT1 (MA0743.3) matrices are ChIP-seq-derived from ReMap, where indirect binding through a partner on the same E-box cannot be excluded.
families.caveats: The core is 6 bp, CpG-free, and shared with bHLH activators as well as with ZEB, INSM and ZBTB18, so an unqualified CAGGTG match supports "E-box" only; expect roughly a million chance occurrences genome-wide. SNAI1, SNAI2 and SNAI3 are indistinguishable from each other. SCRT1/SCRT2 are separable only because of the 5' CAAC extension. One Vierstra archetype in this family (AC0083:SNAI/TCF:bHLH) merges SNAIL with E-protein motifs and is labelled bHLH, which should be read as a statement about clustering, not about biology. ChIP-derived matrices here (JASPAR SNAI2, SCRT1) can reflect a partner bound to the same box.

timeline.finding: Random-site selection with recombinant Drosophila SNAIL defined the binding repertoire as a 6 bp CAGGTG core with weakly specified flanks, and showed that SNAIL bound CAGGTG better than other CANNTG boxes although the core is the same word bHLH proteins read.
timeline.methods: random-oligonucleotide site selection, EMSA, transfection reporters
timeline.open: Whether vertebrate Snail proteins use the same site, and how a zinc-finger protein and a bHLH protein share a core without interfering.

timeline.finding: Two groups independently showed that Snail represses E-cadherin by binding E-boxes in the CDH1 promoter and that its expression converts epithelial cells to an invasive mesenchymal phenotype, establishing the motif as the entry point of an epithelial repression program.
timeline.methods: promoter reporters, EMSA, ectopic expression and knockdown in cell lines

timeline.finding: Snail-null mouse embryos were shown to form a mesoderm layer that keeps epithelial junctions and E-cadherin, giving the family an in vivo requirement in gastrulation; in parallel, mammalian Scratch was identified as a neural-restricted family member that antagonizes proneural bHLH factors at E-boxes.
timeline.methods: mouse gene targeting with electron microscopy, cDNA cloning and reporter assays

timeline.finding: Homozygous SNAI2 deletions were found in patients with Waardenburg syndrome type 2, tying loss of a SNAIL-family factor to a human neural crest pigmentary and auditory phenotype.
timeline.methods: patient genotyping, mouse genetic interaction

timeline.finding: Snail was shown to attenuate the cell cycle and to confer resistance to apoptosis, which separated the invasive program it drives from proliferation and explained why EMT markers and proliferation markers are often anticorrelated in tumors.
timeline.methods: ectopic expression in epithelial cells and chick embryos, survival assays

timeline.finding: The SNAG domain was shown to resemble a histone H3 tail and to act as a hook that docks into the amine oxidase pocket of LSD1, recruiting LSD1/CoREST; repression by SNAIL is therefore a property of the recruited complex rather than of the zinc fingers.
timeline.methods: interaction mapping, competition with H3 peptide and LSD1 inhibitors, chromatin immunoprecipitation

timeline.finding: Snail1 reactivation in mouse renal tubular epithelium was shown to drive fibrosis through a partial transition in which cells signal to the interstitium without themselves becoming myofibroblasts, and the disease was reversible when Snail1 was switched off.
timeline.methods: conditional mouse alleles, lineage tracing, obstructive nephropathy model
timeline.open: Whether the partial state seen in mouse kidney is the same state described in human carcinoma.

timeline.finding: A consensus statement redefined EMT as a spectrum of partial states and advised against inferring a transition from a single marker, which revised the earlier reading of SNAI1 or SNAI2 expression in a tumor as evidence of a completed EMT.
timeline.methods: consensus guidelines

open: What keeps SNAIL factors and bHLH activators off each other's boxes in vivo is unresolved: selection experiments show SNAIL prefers CAGGTG over other CANNTG boxes, while genome-wide data place SNAI peaks on the same boxes that E-proteins occupy, and no study has shown whether flanking sequence, chromatin state or relative abundance decides.

Whether SNAI1, SNAI2 and SNAI3 have genuinely distinct direct target sets is unknown, because their motifs are 0.95-0.99 similar and reported target differences could equally reflect their different expression domains and cofactor availability.

The Vierstra archetype AC0083:SNAI/TCF is labelled bHLH, and it is unsettled whether SNAIL and E-protein motifs are truly inseparable or whether the archetype clustering is simply too coarse to resolve the modest flanking differences the HT-SELEX models show.

Whether a complete EMT occurs in human carcinomas, and whether it is required for metastasis, remains disputed: culture and developmental systems support a full transition, while consensus guidelines for human tumors describe partial, reversible states.

families.name: Myogenic bHLH (MyoD)
families.def: Muscle E-box CAGCTG with AT-flank preference. MYOD1, MYF5, MYF6, MYOG, MSC, MYOR.
families.short: The four myogenic regulatory factors — MYOD1, MYF5, MYF6 (MRF4) and MYOG — plus the related repressor MSC (musculin/MyoR) are class II basic helix-loop-helix proteins restricted to the skeletal muscle lineage. They bind DNA as heterodimers with the ubiquitous class I E-proteins TCF3, TCF4 and TCF12, reading the E-box CAGCTG with a preference for A/T-rich flanks (AACAGCTGTT). MYOD1 was the first transcription factor shown to reprogram cell identity: transfecting it alone converts fibroblasts into myoblasts. Whether a myogenic bHLH activates muscle genes depends less on where it binds than on three residues in its basic region — the "myogenic code" — so an occupied E-box and an active one are not the same thing.
families.long:
## The factors

Four myogenic regulatory factors (MRFs) define this family: MYOD1, MYF5, MYF6 (MRF4) and MYOG (myogenin). The atlas also places MSC (musculin, also called MyoR and ABF-1) here, on motif similarity. All are class II bHLH proteins of about 68 residues in the DNA-binding domain, and all work as heterodimers with the broadly expressed class I E-proteins TCF3 (E12/E47), TCF4 and TCF12; MYOD1 can homodimerise in vitro, but the heterodimer is the active species in cells. MYOD1 and MYF5 act as determination factors and are largely interchangeable for that job, while MYOG and MYF6 act later in differentiation. Expression is restricted to the skeletal muscle lineage: MYF5 in early somitic and satellite-cell progenitors, MYOD1 in activated myoblasts and satellite cells, MYOG and MYF6 in differentiating and mature fibres. MSC is the odd member — a muscle-restricted bHLH that antagonises MyoD rather than cooperating with it, so a site assigned to this family can be an activating or a repressing site depending on which protein is present. MYOD1's historical importance is that transfecting it alone converts fibroblasts into myoblasts, the first demonstration that one transcription factor can switch cell identity [PMID:3690668].

## The motif

The core is the E-box CANNTG, and the myogenic version is CAGCTG, usually written with its A/T-rich flanks as AACAGCTGTT. The data agree: the representative model is the Vierstra archetype `AC0075:MYOD/MYOG:bHLH` with consensus AACAGCTGTC, and JASPAR MSC, MYF6 and CIS-BP MYOG models all read AACAGCTGTT. Each monomer reads one CAN half-site through a basic-region glutamate and arginine, which is why CA...TG is fixed while the central two bases are loosely specified. Binding-site selection with MyoD and E2A complexes showed exactly this: both recognise CA--TG but differ in their flanking and internal preferences, consistent with independent half-site recognition [PMID:2174572].

The interesting part of the myogenic story is not the sequence but three residues in the protein. Replacing MyoD's helices or loop with the equivalent *Drosophila* achaete-scute sequence leaves both DNA binding and muscle-gene activation intact; replacing the basic region preserves DNA binding but abolishes activation [PMID:2155707]. Transferring just three MyoD residues (Ala114, Thr115 and Lys124) into E12 confers myogenic specificity [PMID:1317057]. The crystal structure of the MyoD bHLH-DNA complex then showed that Ala114 and Thr115 are buried at the protein-DNA interface, not exposed for coactivator contacts, and may instead fix the conformation of Arg111 [PMID:8181063]. So the "myogenic code" is a DNA-proximal effect, and binding is necessary but not sufficient: functional selection of transcriptionally active MyoD sites recovered sequences resembling real muscle promoters rather than the optimal in vitro binding site [PMID:8668207].

Two caveats about CAGCTG follow from this. First, genome-wide comparison of MYOD and NEUROD2 found CAGCTG shared between them, with CAGGTG (CACCTG on the other strand) as the MYOD-preferred motif and CAGATG as the NEUROD2-preferred one, and only the factor-specific sites tracked with transcription [PMID:22445365]. JASPAR's MYOD1 MA0499.3 is indeed a GCACCTGTC-type model. Second, none of the four MRFs is distinguishable from the others: cohesion is 0.88 and the family is one motif.

## Where it acts

MRF sites sit in distal muscle enhancers and promoters — the MCK enhancer, the myogenin promoter, desmin, myosin heavy-chain and troponin loci — and are AT-rich rather than CpG-island-associated. Genome-wide, MYOD1 occupies far more sites than it activates, including many in non-muscle chromatin [PMID:20412780], and occupancy is largely limited to E-boxes that are already accessible; the cell's chromatin state, not the motif, picks the target set. Characteristic co-occurring motifs are MEF2 (an A/T-rich site often within a helical turn or two of the E-box in muscle enhancers), SRF/CArG, TEAD/MCAT, SIX and PBX/MEIS; MYOD1 also binds with PBX1 at some promoters. A "muscle E-box pair" of two CAGCTG sites is common in MRF-dependent enhancers but has no fixed spacing rule.

## Biology and disease

Mice lacking both *Myod1* and *Myf5* form no skeletal muscle and no myoblasts, whereas single mutants are near-normal, showing the two are redundant determination factors [PMID:8269513]. *Myog*-null mice reach birth but have a severe deficit of differentiated fibres and die perinatally [PMID:8393145]. MSC/MyoR was identified as a muscle-restricted bHLH that inhibits MyoD-driven myogenesis [PMID:9892671]. In human disease, the MRFs are both markers and drivers of rhabdomyosarcoma: MYOD1 and MYOG immunostaining is diagnostic, and a recurrent somatic MYOD1 p.Leu122Arg substitution defines an aggressive subset of embryonal/spindle-cell tumours [PMID:24793135]. That mutation is instructive for motif work — it lies in the basic region and redirects MYOD1 to MYC consensus sequences, converting a differentiation factor into a proliferative one [PMID:24793135].

## Reading a hit

A CAGCTG match with A/T flanks is consistent with an MRF site but cannot name the factor, and cannot separate MRFs from E-protein homodimers, ASCL1/2, NHLH1/2, ATOH8, TCF21 or TWIST2, all of which give CAGCTG models. The A/T flank preference is real but worth only a bit or two. The strongest in vitro support in this family is `MYOD1.H14CORE.1.PSM.A` (grade A, ChIP plus HT-SELEX plus methyl-SELEX), so "MyoD binds CAGCTG" is well grounded; the MSC label is shakier, because the HOCOMOCO in vitro model `MUSC.H14CORE.0.SM.B` reads CATATGGT, a NeuroD/Atonal-type site, and is flagged as matching the TWIST/HAND family instead. One CIS-BP MYF5 model is inferred from the mouse protein (90% DBD identity), which is benign but should be noted. Because CAGCTG is one of the commonest six-mers in the genome, treat an isolated hit as a hypothesis requiring muscle expression, accessibility or conservation.
families.caveats: CAGCTG is among the most frequent six-mers in mammalian genomes and is read by E-protein homodimers, ASCL1/2, NHLH1/2, ATOH8, TCF21 and TWIST2 as well as by the MRFs, so a match places a site in the broad class II bHLH space rather than in muscle. The four MRFs share one motif and cannot be distinguished; nor can the activator MYOD1 be distinguished from the repressor MSC, whose in vitro model in HOCOMOCO is a CATATG site that clusters with TWIST/HAND instead. Binding also does not imply activation: the myogenic code governs activation, not affinity. Muscle-lineage expression and open chromatin are required to make a hit meaningful.

timeline.finding: A single transfected cDNA, MyoD, converts fibroblasts into myoblasts, the first demonstration that one transcription factor can switch a cell's identity.
timeline.methods: subtractive cloning and transfection of 10T1/2 fibroblasts
timeline.open: No DNA sequence was yet attributed to the protein.

timeline.finding: Binding-site selection shows MyoD and E2A complexes both read a CA--TG core with different flanking and internal preferences, implying independent half-site recognition, while domain swaps place the determinant of myogenic activation in the basic region rather than in the helix-loop-helix.
timeline.methods: in vitro binding-site selection; chimeric proteins in conversion assays
timeline.open: Why a DNA-binding segment, rather than an activation domain, should carry the myogenic code.

timeline.finding: Substituting three MyoD residues (Ala114, Thr115 and Lys124) into E12 is enough to confer myogenic specificity, defining a minimal 'myogenic code'.
timeline.methods: site-directed mutagenesis and myogenic conversion assays
timeline.open: Whether those residues work by contacting DNA or by presenting a surface to coactivators.

timeline.finding: Mice lacking both Myod1 and Myf5 form no skeletal muscle and no myoblasts while single mutants are near-normal, and Myog-null mice make myoblasts but few differentiated fibres, splitting the family into redundant determination factors and a non-redundant differentiation factor.
timeline.methods: mouse gene targeting

timeline.finding: The MyoD bHLH-DNA crystal structure shows Ala114 and Thr115 buried at the protein-DNA interface rather than exposed to coactivators, so the myogenic code acts through the DNA contact surface, possibly by fixing the conformation of Arg111.
timeline.methods: X-ray crystallography
timeline.open: How a buried residue converts into transcriptional output was left as a proposal.

timeline.finding: Functional random-sequence selection for transcriptionally active MyoD sites recovers sequences that resemble real muscle promoters rather than the highest-affinity in vitro site, separating binding requirements from activation requirements.
timeline.methods: functional random sequence selection in cells

timeline.finding: Genome-wide mapping shows MyoD constitutively occupies thousands of sites well beyond muscle genes, and a side-by-side comparison with NEUROD2 then separates a shared CAGCTG site from factor-specific sites (CAGGTG for MYOD, CAGATG for NEUROD2), with transcription following only the specific sites and occupancy limited to E-boxes in accessible chromatin.
timeline.methods: ChIP-seq in myoblasts and myotubes; cross-lineage ChIP-seq and expression profiling
timeline.open: Occupancy and activation remain only loosely coupled, so the determinants of a productive MyoD site are still not predictable from sequence.

timeline.finding: A recurrent somatic MYOD1 p.Leu122Arg substitution in embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma, in the basic region, blocks wild-type MYOD1 and redirects binding to MYC consensus sequences, turning a differentiation factor into a proliferative one.
timeline.methods: whole-exome sequencing of tumours, interpreted against earlier mutagenesis

open: Occupancy and activation are still not reconciled: MyoD binds thousands of E-boxes that it does not activate, and whether productive sites are picked by flanking sequence, by E-box pairing, by cofactors such as MEF2 and PBX, or only by pre-existing chromatin accessibility remains contested.

Which CAGCTG matches belong to the myogenic program cannot be decided from sequence, because E-protein homodimers, ASCL1/2, NHLH1/2, ATOH8, TCF21 and TWIST2 give indistinguishable models, and the A/T flank preference reported for MRFs is worth only a bit or two of information.

The placement of MSC/musculin in this family is doubtful: its HOCOMOCO in vitro model reads the NeuroD/Atonal-type site CATATGGT and is flagged as matching TWIST/HAND, so whether MSC shares the MRF site or has its own is unresolved by the current data.

How the buried myogenic residues Ala114 and Thr115 convert into transcriptional activation is still a structural proposal rather than a demonstrated mechanism, since the crystal structure placed them at the DNA interface instead of on a coactivator-binding surface.

families.name: TEAD
families.def: MCAT element GGAATG. TEAD1-4.
families.short: The four human TEAD proteins (TEAD1-4, formerly TEF-1, TEF-4, TEF-5 and TEF-3) bind the MCAT element GGAATG, read on the other strand as CATTCC. The DNA-binding TEA domain is a three-helix bundle with a homeodomain-like fold, and two TEADs load cooperatively onto tandem MCAT sites. TEADs have no activation domain of their own: they are the DNA-binding platform for the Hippo pathway coactivators YAP and TAZ, and for the VGLL proteins that compete with them. The motif is therefore the readout of Hippo signaling status on chromatin. TEAD sites drive muscle gene expression, trophectoderm specification and organ size control, and are central to YAP-driven cancers.
families.long:
## The factors

Four human genes, TEAD1, TEAD2, TEAD3 and TEAD4, share an N-terminal TEA (also called ATTS) DNA
binding domain and a C-terminal YAP-binding domain. TEAD1 (TEF-1) and TEAD3 (TEF-5) are broadly
expressed with enrichment in muscle and placenta, TEAD2 (TEF-4) in neural and embryonic tissue,
TEAD4 (TEF-3) in skeletal muscle, trophectoderm and many carcinomas. TEADs bind DNA as monomers
but load cooperatively onto tandem sites via a loop in the TEA domain [PMID:2843293,17085591]. They carry no intrinsic
transactivation domain, so their output depends entirely on which partner occupies the
YAP-binding domain: YAP or TAZ (WWTR1) when Hippo signaling is off, or a VGLL protein
(VGLL1-VGLL4) competing for the same surface [PMID:18579750,22632831]. Structures of the YAP-TEAD, TAZ-TEAD and VGLL1-TEAD
complexes show how the same interface is reused [PMID:20123905,22632831]. TEADs are also palmitoylated on a conserved
cysteine in a hydrophobic central pocket; this auto-palmitoylation is required for stability and
for YAP/TAZ binding [PMID:26724994,31043565], and it is the target of the current generation of TEAD inhibitors [PMID:33850002].

## The motif

The literature name is the MCAT (muscle CAT) element, GGAATG, equivalently CATTCC on the opposite
strand [PMID:17962623]; older papers also call it the GT-IIC element of the SV40 enhancer [PMID:2843293,1851669]. TEF-1 was purified as a protein binding both GT-IIC and a
second SV40 motif, Sph, but the two are unrelated in sequence, so Sph is not another name for the MCAT site [PMID:2843293].
Six bases carry essentially all the information, with the GGAAT core most constrained. The solution
structure of the TEA domain showed a three-helix bundle with a homeodomain fold, and revealed that
the L1 loop is what allows two TEAD molecules to load cooperatively onto tandemly duplicated MCAT
sites [PMID:17085591]. That explains the pattern in this family's data: single-site models span 6-9 columns with
10-13 bits, while the most informative models (up to 21 bits) are tandem pairs such as
CATTCC-N(2)-CATTCC, which represent the cooperative arrangement rather than a longer monomer
footprint. Database models divide simply into the forward-strand rendering (GGAATG, GGAATGT) and
the reverse rendering (ACATTCC, CATTCCA); they are the same motif and the family is one of the
most cohesive in these collections. No TEAD paralogue is distinguishable from another by sequence.
An in vitro microarray study also found that the isolated TEA domain binds a broader set of
sequences than the sites recovered with the full-length protein, so the narrow GGAATG consensus
partly reflects constraints outside the DNA-binding domain [PMID:17085591].

## Where it acts

TEAD/YAP sites are overwhelmingly enhancer elements, not promoters. YAP-TEAD complexes occupy
thousands of distal enhancers and act largely through enhancer-promoter contacts [PMID:26258633] and release of
paused RNA polymerase; TEAD motifs are among the most enriched motifs in the accessible chromatin
of proliferating and mechanically stimulated cells. The classic promoter-proximal cases are
muscle: MCAT elements in the cardiac troponin T, beta-myosin heavy chain and smooth muscle
alpha-actin promoters [PMID:17962623]. Recurrent co-occurring motifs are AP-1 (JUN/FOS), which forms functional
composite TEAD-AP-1 enhancers in many YAP-driven contexts [PMID:26258633], plus RUNX, MYOD E-boxes in muscle, and
CDX2/GATA3 in trophectoderm. Because GGAATG is only 6 bp, chance matches are extremely numerous;
occupancy is set by chromatin state and by whether YAP/TAZ are nuclear.

## Biology and disease

TEAD4 specifies the trophectoderm lineage in the mouse preimplantation embryo [PMID:17913785], and its activity is
restricted to outer cells by Hippo signaling through LATS and YAP [PMID:19289085], making this the earliest known
cell-fate decision read out through a TEAD motif. In muscle, MCAT elements coordinate the
cardiac and smooth muscle differentiation programs. A missense mutation in TEAD1 that weakens its
interaction with YAP and TAZ causes Sveinsson chorioretinal atrophy, a dominant retinal
degeneration [PMID:15016762,17689488], and is the clearest human germline TEAD disease. In cancer, TEAD activity is the
effector of Hippo pathway loss: NF2 (merlin) inactivation in mesothelioma and schwannoma, LATS1/2
loss, and YAP1 or WWTR1 fusions all converge on TEAD-driven transcription, and YAP1-TFE3 and
TAZ-CAMTA1 fusions in epithelioid hemangioendothelioma retain the TEAD-binding function.
Small-molecule inhibitors of TEAD auto-palmitoylation selectively suppress NF2-deficient
mesothelioma in preclinical models [PMID:33850002] and have entered clinical testing. VGLL4 acts as a tumor
suppressor by competing with YAP for the same TEAD surface.

## Reading a hit

GGAATG is 6 bp and occurs on the order of a million times in the human genome, so an isolated
match is close to meaningless. Three things upgrade a hit: a tandem pair of MCAT sites within
about 15 bp, which is the cooperative binding arrangement; an adjacent AP-1 site, which marks the
functional TEAD-AP-1 composite enhancers; and open chromatin in a cell with nuclear YAP or TAZ. A
hit never identifies a paralogue; TEAD1 through TEAD4 share one matrix, and in most tissues more
than one is expressed. Equally important, a TEAD motif hit says nothing about the direction of the
output, because the same site is bound by TEAD with YAP/TAZ (activating) or with VGLL4
(repressing), and TEAD occupancy in the absence of a coactivator does little. ChIP-derived TEAD
motifs are reasonably trustworthy here: HOCOMOCO grade-A models for TEAD1-4 combine ChIP-seq with
in vitro selection (evidence codes PS or PSM), so direct binding is independently supported. The
converse caution applies to the reverse: YAP and TAZ ChIP-seq recovers the TEAD motif even though
YAP and TAZ do not touch DNA [PMID:26258633], a textbook case of a coactivator "having" the motif of the protein
that recruits it. If a database entry attributes GGAATG to YAP1, WWTR1 or a VGLL protein, that is
indirect binding.
families.caveats: GGAATG carries about 6 bits, so single hits are expected by chance and are not evidence on their own; tandem MCAT pairs and neighboring AP-1 sites are what make a hit credible. TEAD1-4 share one matrix and cannot be separated by sequence. A hit does not indicate activation: the same site is used by TEAD-YAP/TAZ and by repressive TEAD-VGLL4 complexes, and TEAD without a coactivator is largely inert. Any GGAATG motif attributed to YAP1, WWTR1/TAZ or a VGLL protein is indirect, since those proteins do not contact DNA. TEAD's own models are supported by in vitro selection as well as ChIP-seq.

open: Whether TEAD has a second binding specificity is unresolved: purified TEF-1 bound two SV40 motifs of unrelated sequence (GT-IIC and Sph) and the isolated TEA domain binds a broader set of elements on microarrays, yet every database model here reduces to the single GGAATG/CATTCC site.

How much genomic TEAD binding uses the cooperative tandem arrangement is not established: the most informative in vitro models (HT-SELEX TEAD1 and TEAD3) are paired CATTCC sites, whereas the ChIP-supported models are single sites.

families.name: IRX (TALE, Iroquois)
families.def: ACA-rich TALE sites. IRX1-6.
families.short: IRX1 through IRX6, with the related factor MKX (Mohawk), form the Iroquois branch of the TALE homeodomain superclass - homeodomains carrying three extra residues between helices 1 and 2. Unlike most homeodomain proteins they do not read a TAAT core. Their recognition unit is a short ACA, and the functional site is an inverted repeat of it, so models in these databases range from the half-site CATGT up to long palindromes such as ACATGnnnnnCATGT. The IRX genes sit in two clusters, IRX1/2/4 and IRX3/5/6, and pattern the heart, limb, kidney and nervous system. IRX3 is best known outside developmental biology as the gene connected by long-range enhancer contacts to the obesity-associated variants inside FTO.
families.long:
## The factors

The Iroquois genes are one of the five branches of the TALE superclass, which is defined by a three-amino-acid insertion between helices 1 and 2 of the homeodomain [PMID:9336443]. Humans have six, arranged in two clusters that arose by duplication: IRX1, IRX2 and IRX4 on chromosome 5, and IRX3, IRX5 and IRX6 on chromosome 16 [PMID:11532909]. Each protein carries a TALE homeodomain plus a C-terminal Iro box [PMID:9336443]. MKX (Mohawk) is an IRX-related TALE homeodomain protein assigned to this family in the motif data; it acts as a repressor and recruits the Sin3A/HDAC corepressor complex [PMID:19235719]. Iroquois proteins form homodimers and heterodimers, which is part of how a very short recognition core is turned into a usable site [PMID:16203991]. Expression is broad but regional: IRX1/2/4 and IRX3/5 are prominent in heart, limb bud, kidney, lung and neural tube, with IRX4 largely ventricle-specific; MKX is expressed in tendon and the precursors of skeletal muscle, cartilage and bone [PMID:22923612].

## The motif

This family is the clearest example in the atlas of a homeodomain that has abandoned the TAAT core. In vitro site selection with *Drosophila* Mirror defined an Iroquois-binding sequence recognized by the other fly Iroquois proteins and by vertebrate IRX factors, and used in vivo to mediate repression [PMID:16203991]. Bacterial one-hybrid selection with the mouse MKX homeodomain gave a monomeric core of just three bases, A-C-A, and the minimal Mohawk response element in the Mkx promoter is a conserved inverted repeat of that core [PMID:22923612] - the same architecture the human IRX models show. Because the reverse complement of ACA is TGT, the inverted repeat is ACA-TGT, most compactly ACATGT, which is itself palindromic. The databases capture this at several spacings: CIS-BP M05319 gives tACAtGaatattCaTGTa and HOCOMOCO IRX3.H14CORE.2.S.C gives ACAtGnaaaaaCATGTa (ACATG and CATGT separated by five to seven bases), the Vierstra archetype AC0476 gives ACacGawaawtCaTGT, AC0460 gives the tandem ACAtgACA, and the shortest models collapse to the half-site CATGTt or aACATG. The pooled consensus is therefore the half-site CATGTt with cohesion 0.77 - a number that reflects spacer variability, not disagreement about the core. Two methyl-HT-SELEX models for IRX3 and IRX5 instead read ACGCGTaA, a CpG-containing palindrome, so methylation status may matter for a subset of sites [PMID:28473536]. IRX1-6 are not distinguishable from one another by sequence.

## Where it acts

IRX sites occur in developmental enhancers rather than housekeeping promoters, and because the core is 3 bp the useful signal is always the paired arrangement plus its spacing. An exact ACATGT is expected on the order of 10^6 times in 3.1 Gb, so single-half-site matches should not be acted on. The longer palindromic forms with a 5-7 bp AT-rich spacer are much more discriminating. The best-documented regulatory context is the FTO/IRX3 locus, where obesity-associated variants in FTO introns make long-range functional contacts with the IRX3 promoter, so IRX3 rather than FTO is the effector gene [PMID:24646999,26287746]. In heart, Irx3 and Irx5 act on conduction-system and repolarization genes and have both cooperative and antagonistic roles, giving a regional readout from the same motif [PMID:22992950].

## Biology and disease

Irx3/Irx5 double mutants in mouse have cardiac morphogenetic defects and abnormal postnatal cardiac physiology [PMID:22992950], and Irx4 loss affects ventricular identity. Homozygous loss-of-function mutations in human IRX5 cause Hamamy syndrome, with craniofacial anomalies and impaired germ cell migration attributable to reduced SDF1/CXCL12 [PMID:22581230]. Variants in the FTO first intron act on IRX3 to influence body mass [PMID:24646999], and IRX3 and IRX5 have also been implicated in adipocyte browning [PMID:26287746]. Mkx-null mice have tendon hypoplasia, and MKX loss de-represses Sox6 and shifts skeletal muscle away from slow fiber gene expression [PMID:22923612].

## Reading a hit

Treat a bare CATGT or ACATG match as noise: 5 bp is not enough, and CATG is also the core of several unrelated motifs. What is interpretable is a paired ACATG...CATGT arrangement, ideally with the AT-rich spacer the high-information models show. The hit identifies the Iroquois branch, not a paralogue - all six IRX models are the same. Two members of this family in CIS-BP are cross-species transfers, one from *Drosophila melanogaster* at 98% DNA-binding-domain identity and one from mouse, and both are extremely low information (aAACA and AcA); do not treat them as independent human evidence. The MKX model here is graded A in HOCOMOCO with ChIP-seq and four in vitro assays behind it (HT-SELEX, GHT-SELEX, SMiLE-seq and PBM) but is still only five informative bases.
families.caveats: The recognition core is three bases, so short matches are essentially uninformative and only paired ACATG...CATGT arrangements with their AT-rich spacer are worth interpreting. IRX1-6 share one model, so a hit identifies the Iroquois branch and never a paralogue. Two CIS-BP members are inherited from non-human proteins (one from Drosophila at 98% DBD identity, one from mouse) and carry almost no information. Spacer length varies between models, so scores depend heavily on which matrix you used. Because the CATG core is shared with unrelated motifs, expect a high false-positive rate without footprint or expression support.

open: Whether IRX proteins act mainly as monomers on ACA half-sites or as dimers on paired ACATG...CATGT sites is unresolved: the same factors yield both half-site models and inverted-repeat models with a 5-7 bp spacer, and which spacing is used in vivo has not been established.

The methyl-HT-SELEX models for IRX3 and IRX5 read a CpG-containing ACGCGTAA that differs from the unmethylated ACATGT core, and it is not known whether methylated sites are a real class of IRX targets in cells.

Whether MKX shares the IRX site is open: it is grouped here by motif data, but its best-supported model (HOCOMOCO grade A) is only five informative bases (aTGTA), too little to show that it reads the paired Iroquois arrangement.

families.name: CDX / PDX / anterior gut HD
families.def: TTTATG / CTTTAT. CDX1/2/4, PDX1, and related ParaHox factors.
families.short: This family groups the caudal-related factors CDX1, CDX2 and CDX4 with PDX1, all encoded by ParaHox genes - an ancient cluster that is the evolutionary sister of the Hox cluster. The CDX proteins read TTTATG, usually extended to TTTATGGC, a site distinct enough to be recognizable. PDX1 is a different case: its in vitro motif is plain TAATTA, indistinguishable from the generic Q50 homeodomain site, so PDX1 specificity in vivo comes from partners rather than from the sequence it prefers. CDX2 patterns the posterior gut and is the standard immunohistochemical marker of intestinal epithelium; PDX1 is required for pancreas development and its loss causes pancreatic agenesis and MODY4.
families.long:
## The factors

Four human proteins: CDX1, CDX2 and CDX4, the vertebrate relatives of *Drosophila* caudal, and PDX1 (also IPF1, IDX1, STF1), the vertebrate Xlox gene. All four are ParaHox genes. The ParaHox cluster - Gsx, Xlox/PDX1 and Cdx - is an evolutionary sister of the Hox cluster [PMID:9582071], which explains why these proteins carry ordinary 60-residue three-helix homeodomains with the same helix 3 recognition chemistry as HOX proteins, and no second DNA-binding domain [PMID:2572327]. CDX1 and CDX2 are expressed throughout the intestinal epithelium, CDX2 most strongly and persisting into adulthood [PMID:11040183]; CDX4 is largely embryonic, with a role in hematopoiesis; PDX1 is restricted to the pancreatic buds and then to beta cells, duodenum and antral stomach [PMID:7935793]. Unlike most families in this group, specificity here does not come from an extra domain in the same polypeptide - it comes either from the extended site that the CDX homeodomain itself prefers, or, for PDX1, from a protein complex.

## The motif

The CDX site is written in the literature as TTTAT(G/A) and in these databases as an extended TTTATGGC, equivalently GCCATAAA on the other strand. CDX2 and CDX1 HT-SELEX models both read TTTATggC, CDX4 gives TTTTATGaC, and the JASPAR models for CDX1, CDX2 and CDX4 render the reverse complement GC(a)ATAAAA. The 5' TTTAT is the homeodomain core - the same TAAT-type element every Q50 homeodomain reads, here with a 3' extension [PMID:2572327] - and the discriminating information sits in the GGC/TGC that follows. Methyl-HT-SELEX models for CDX1, CDX2 and CDX4 instead read TTTACGAC, a CpG-containing variant, so a subset of CDX sites is methylation-sensitive [PMID:28473536,29638214]. The pooled consensus is TTTATggC with cohesion 0.84. PDX1 is the exception, and it is worth being explicit about it: the A-grade HOCOMOCO model PDX1.H14CORE.1.PSM.A reads cTAATtA and JASPAR MA0132.3 reads TAATTA - a bare Q50 homeodomain site with no extension at all. The nearest neighbours of those models across all four databases lie in the anterior HOX/Q50 groups, and the data flags them as such. A second PDX1 model, the ChIP-derived PDX1.H14CORE.0.P.B, reads TGATTgATGg, whose nearest neighbours are in the TALE family; that is almost certainly the PBX half-site, because PDX1 works in a trimeric complex with PBX1b and MEIS2/MRG1 on the elastase enhancer [PMID:9710595], so PBX-type sequence is expected in PDX1 ChIP peaks. Neither flagged model means the database entry is wrong; both mean the label is more specific than the sequence.

## Where it acts

CDX sites sit in intestine-specific promoters and enhancers - sucrase-isomaltase, lactase-phlorizin hydrolase, the CDX1 and CDX2 genes themselves - and in posterior HOX cluster enhancers, where CDX factors feed into anteroposterior patterning [PMID:9052785,17855634]. The site is 6-8 bp and AT-rich, so exact TTTATGGC matches are expected in the 10^4-10^5 range in 3.1 Gb and most are not occupied. PDX1 sites are concentrated in beta-cell enhancers, for insulin, GCK and SLC2A2, and in acinar enhancers, where PDX1 acts with PBX1 and MEIS2 [PMID:9710595]; PDX1 also co-occurs with NKX6-1, NKX2-2, NEUROD1, FOXA2 and the HNF factors, so an islet regulatory element typically carries several of these motifs together. Because CDX and PDX1 are expressed in adjacent but different gut segments, genomic context and tissue usually resolve which factor is plausible.

## Biology and disease

Cdx2 heterozygous mice show homeotic shifts of the axial skeleton and develop intestinal tumors with gastric-type mucosa [PMID:9052785], and Cdx2 is required for intestinal identity. In humans, CDX1 and CDX2 are ectopically expressed in intestinal metaplasia of the stomach and in gastric carcinoma [PMID:12474224], and CDX2 immunohistochemistry is routine for identifying intestinal-lineage adenocarcinoma. Ectopic CDX2 perturbs HOX gene expression in murine progenitors and is associated with acute myeloid leukemia [PMID:17855634]. PDX1 loss is severe: Pdx1-null mice fail to form a pancreas [PMID:7935793], a homozygous frameshift in human IPF1/PDX1 causes pancreatic agenesis with neonatal diabetes [PMID:8988180], and heterozygous mutations cause MODY4 [PMID:9326926].

## Reading a hit

A TTTATGGC-type match is reasonable evidence for a CDX factor, but it cannot distinguish CDX1, CDX2 and CDX4, whose models are interchangeable; use expression, since CDX2 dominates in adult intestine. Do not use this family's PDX1 models as evidence for PDX1 specifically. TAATTA matches every Q50 homeodomain in the genome, so a TAATTA hit is a homeodomain hit and nothing more, and the ChIP-derived TGATTGATGG model is better read as a PBX/TALE site that happens to lie in PDX1 peaks. In practice, a PDX1 claim should rest on islet chromatin data and co-occurring beta-cell motifs, not on the motif alone. Four of the 17 members of this family are flagged as having nearest neighbours in another family, all four of them PDX1 or short TAAT models - this is a systematic pattern here, not a one-off.
families.caveats: CDX1, CDX2 and CDX4 share one motif; a hit identifies the CDX group, not a member. PDX1 is the real hazard: its in vitro motif is plain TAATTA, indistinguishable from the whole Q50 homeodomain group, and its ChIP-derived model reads a PBX/TALE half-site, consistent with PDX1 acting in a complex with PBX1 and MEIS2. Four of 17 members of this family have nearest neighbours in the HOX/Q50 or TALE families, all of them PDX1 or bare TAAT models, so treat PDX1 matches as unassignable without islet chromatin evidence. CDX sites are short and AT-rich, so chance matches are common.

timeline.finding: Methyl-HT-SELEX shows CDX proteins among the many homeodomain factors that prefer a CpG-methylated variant site (TTTACGA), and a CDX2 structure on methylated DNA shows a direct hydrophobic contact with the 5-methyl group.

timeline.finding: Structures and calorimetry of CDX2 and HOXB13 on their two optimal sites, CAATAAA and TCGTAAA, show both are bound with similar free energy, one enthalpy-driven and one entropy-driven, so the second site is a true optimum rather than a weaker variant.
timeline.methods: X-ray crystallography, isothermal titration calorimetry

open: How much CDX2 occupancy in cells uses the CpG-containing TTTACGA site is unsettled: in vitro it is bound about as well as the canonical TTTATG form and better when methylated, but the databases and the literature still define the CDX site by the TTTAT(G/A) form alone.

Whether PDX1 has any intrinsic sequence preference that distinguishes it from other Q50 homeodomains is open: its in vitro models are a bare TAATTA, its ChIP-derived model reads a PBX half-site, and it is unresolved whether its specificity comes from an extension not yet captured or entirely from PBX-MEIS partners and co-bound islet factors.

families.name: ETV2 / ETV6-type
families.def: ETS sites with tandem GGAA repeats favoured by ETV2 and the ETV6 repressor.
families.short: ETV2 (ER71), ETV6 (TEL) and ETV7 (TEL2) are ETS-domain proteins that read the same GGA(A/T) core as the rest of the family. ETV2 is a transient activator required for the specification of blood and endothelium; ETV6 and ETV7 are repressors, and ETV6 spreads repression by polymerizing through its PNT/SAM domain. They are grouped here because their motif models cluster together, not because they share a distinct binding preference: ETV2's selected sequence is the ordinary class I ETS site and ETV6/ETV7 differ from it only marginally. What does recur among these models is arrangement - several are two GGAA cores in tandem or head-to-head. ETV6 is one of the most frequently rearranged genes in leukemia, most famously as ETV6-RUNX1 in childhood B-lineage acute lymphoblastic leukemia.
families.long:
## The factors

Three genes sit in this family. ETV2 (also ER71 or ETSRP) is a transient transcriptional activator
expressed in a narrow window in nascent mesoderm and hemogenic endothelium and essentially silent
in adult tissues. ETV6 (TEL) and ETV7 (TEL2) are transcriptional repressors; ETV6 is broadly
expressed [PMID:9250681], ETV7 more narrowly and largely in hematopoietic cells. All three carry one ETS domain of
about 85 residues, the family's winged helix-turn-helix fold, and bind DNA as monomers [PMID:21548782]. ETV6 and
ETV7 additionally carry a PNT domain (a SAM domain) that self-associates head-to-tail into an
open-ended polymer [PMID:12193272,21548782], so one DNA-bound ETV6 molecule can nucleate a long repressive assembly; the
polymer interface and its regulation have been mapped biophysically [PMID:33450226]. ETV6 also has an
autoinhibitory element that damps its DNA binding [PMID:21548782]. It is worth stating plainly that this family is
not a biochemical class. Systematic profiling of every human and mouse ETS protein put ETV6 and
ETV7 in a small subclass of their own (class IIb) [PMID:20517297] and did not group ETV2 with them; ETV2's
preference is the ordinary class I preference.

## The motif

The consensus is ACCGGAAGT - the same nine-mer as ETS class I, read the same way, by two invariant
arginines in recognition helix H3 that hydrogen-bond the two guanines of GGA, with wing and turn
lysines contacting the flanks [PMID:21548782]. The in vitro models differ only at the margins: JASPAR's HT-SELEX
model for ETV2 (MA0762.2) is ACCGGAAAT, with A rather than G immediately 3' of the core, while the
ETV6 (MA0645.2) and ETV7 (MA1708.2) HT-SELEX models are plain CCGGAAGT and CGGAAGTG. There is no
sequence that belongs to this family and not to ETS class I. What is distinctive in part of the
collection is arrangement rather than composition: three models here are doubled sites - CIS-BP
M02990 (CCGGAAGCGGAAGT), CIS-BP M04712 (CGGAAGTACTTCCG) and the ETV7 in vitro model
(CCCGGAAGTACTTC) - that is, two ETS cores in tandem or head-to-head. That is consistent with
ETV6's ability to polymerize [PMID:21548782,33450226] and with the reported preference of these factors for repeated GGAA [PMID:21548782],
but doubled and repeated GGAA matrices also occur in ETS class I, where the EWS-FLI1 fusion's GGAA
microsatellite matrices live [PMID:18626011], so a tandem arrangement does not on its own assign a motif here.

## Where it acts

ETV2 binds enhancers of endothelial and hematopoietic genes during a short developmental window,
acting downstream of BMP, Notch and Wnt signals [PMID:18462699,21548782]. ETV6 and ETV7 occupy ETS sites at promoters and
enhancers and repress them, recruiting corepressors rather than activating [PMID:21548782]. The functional point
this family illustrates is competition: because ETV6, ETV7, ERF and ETV3 read the same sequence as
ETS1, ERG, FLI1 and GABPA, the output of a given ETS site depends on which family member happens to
occupy it, not on the sequence. That is also why sites bound by these repressors are not
distinguishable in a scan from sites bound by activators. Notably, the genome-wide footprint
archetypes derived from DNase data contain no archetype for this family [PMID:32728250]: every archetype whose name
includes ETV clustered instead with ELF, ELK or ETS archetypes that are assigned elsewhere in this
atlas.

## Biology and disease

Etv2-null mouse embryos fail to make blood and endothelium [PMID:18462699], placing ETV2 at the top of the
hematoendothelial program; the gene is now widely used to force endothelial fate in reprogramming
experiments. Mice lacking Tel/Etv6 die around mid-gestation with a yolk sac angiogenic defect and
intra-embryonic apoptosis [PMID:9250681], and ETV6 is required for adult bone marrow hematopoiesis [PMID:9694803]. ETV6 is among
the most frequently rearranged genes in human leukemia: the t(12;21) fusion ETV6-RUNX1 (TEL-AML1)
is the most common recurrent fusion in childhood B-lineage acute lymphoblastic leukemia [PMID:7761424], and ETV6
has many other partners including kinases [PMID:7761424,12193272]. Germline heterozygous ETV6 mutations cause autosomal
dominant thrombocytopenia with predisposition to hematologic malignancy [PMID:25581430].

## Reading a hit

This is the family in this atlas where the label deserves the least weight. The motifs assigned
here are not separable from ETS class I, and the data say so directly: for all 16 models in
this family, most of the nearest neighbours across the four databases are labelled with a different
family, usually ETS class I, and for 14 of them the single best match anywhere is a motif from another
family rather than one from this family - including the CIS-BP model that this atlas picks as the
family's representative. One JASPAR entry, the heterodimer model ETV2::FIGLA (MA1941.2), is flagged
outright as belonging with class I. Practical consequences: read a hit as "an ETS site"; use
expression to decide the factor, remembering that ETV2 is effectively absent outside early mesoderm
and engineered endothelial systems, so an ETV2 call in an adult tissue dataset is far more likely a
generic ETS site; and do not try to tell ETV6 from ERF or ETV3, all repressors reading the same
sequence. Four of the seven JASPAR models here are CAP-SELEX heterodimers (ETV2::HOXB13,
ETV2::FIGLA, ETV2::DRGX, ETV2::FOXI1) in which much of the matrix is a HOX, bHLH or FOX site rather
than an ETS site [PMID:26550823].
families.caveats:
Treat the family label as provisional. Its separation from ETS class I is largely a
clustering outcome: all 16 models here have most of their cross-database nearest neighbours
labelled with another family, usually class I, 14 match a motif outside the family better than any
inside it, and one JASPAR entry (ETV2::FIGLA) is flagged as belonging with class I. The published classification also does not support the grouping - ETV6 and ETV7
form their own small subclass while ETV2 behaves like a class I factor. No genomic-footprint
archetype corresponds to this family. Four of seven JASPAR models are CAP-SELEX heterodimers whose
matrices are partly a HOX, bHLH or FOX site. A hit therefore means "an ETS site"; which of ETV2,
ETV6, ETV7, ERF or ETV3 is bound has to come from expression and ChIP data.

timeline.finding: Cloning of the t(12;21) breakpoint in childhood pre-B acute lymphoblastic leukemia shows the amino-terminal HLH domain of TEL (later recognized as the PNT domain) fused to the DNA-binding and transactivation domains of AML1 (RUNX1); TEL had already been found fused to the PDGFRB kinase in chronic myelomonocytic leukemia.
