timeline.methods: X-ray crystallography
timeline.open: The construct did not include DNA, so base-specific contacts remained unresolved.

timeline.finding: Genome-wide ChIP-seq across the circadian cycle in mouse liver put most confident CLOCK:BMAL1 sites near transcription start sites, at roughly one to three thousand per time point, with occupancy itself cycling ahead of the RNA polymerase II and histone-modification rhythms it drives.
timeline.methods: ChIP-seq time course, nascent-RNA and chromatin profiling
timeline.open: Why only a small fraction of genomic CACGTG matches is ever occupied.

timeline.finding: A structure of the human CLOCK:BMAL1 bHLH domains on an E-box, with accompanying affinity measurements, showed that BMAL1 Ile80 contacts the base pair immediately 3' of the core, making the recognized unit 7 bp (CACGTGA), and defined two high-affinity non-canonical boxes, AACGTGA and CATGTGA.
timeline.methods: X-ray crystallography with substitution series
timeline.open: Whether the non-canonical boxes are used at endogenous rhythmic promoters.

open: Whether the non-canonical boxes AACGTGA and CATGTGA are used at endogenous clock sites is unsettled: they bind with high affinity in vitro and the methyl-HT-SELEX models in this family recover the CATGTG form, but the grade-A models and ChIP-derived sites are dominated by CACGTG.

It is not resolved what selects the one to three thousand occupied sites from the roughly 7 x 10^5 CACGTG matches in the genome; tandem spacing, pre-existing chromatin accessibility and partner factors have each been proposed, and no model predicts occupancy from sequence alone.

Whether CLOCK and NPAS2 regulate distinguishable target sets is open: they cannot be separated by sequence and NPAS2 can sustain behavioral rhythms without CLOCK, yet their tissue distributions differ.

A substantial share of CLOCK:BMAL1 ChIP peaks contains no recognizable E-box, and whether these reflect tethering through partner proteins or binding to degenerate sites below the detection threshold of current models has not been settled.

families.name: SPI1 / SPIB / SPIC (PU.1)
families.def: Purine-rich AGAGGAAGTG. SPI1, SPIB, SPIC; EICE composite with IRF.
families.short: SPI1 (PU.1), SPIB and SPIC are the class III branch of the ETS family. They read the same GGA(A/T) core as other ETS proteins but demand a purine-rich 5' flank, giving the hematopoietic PU-box AAAGAGGAAGTG - the one ETS subfamily that a scan can usually tell apart from the rest. SPI1 is required for macrophage, neutrophil, dendritic cell and B-cell development; SPIB acts in B cells and plasmacytoid dendritic cells; SPIC specifies red pulp macrophages. PU.1 also nucleates the ETS-IRF composite element (EICE), GGAAGTGAAAC, by recruiting IRF4 or IRF8 to DNA it has already bound. Reduced PU.1 dosage causes acute myeloid leukemia in mice, and SPI1 fusions occur in high-risk pediatric T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia.
families.long:
## The factors

Three human genes - SPI1 (PU.1, Spi-1), SPIB (Spi-B) and SPIC (Spi-C) - form the SPI subfamily.
Each carries one ETS domain of about 85 residues with the family's winged helix-turn-helix fold and
binds DNA as a monomer [PMID:8602247]; outside the domain they have acidic and glutamine-rich activation regions
and, in PU.1, a PEST region whose Ser148 must be phosphorylated for cooperative assembly with IRF
partners [PMID:7797077]. Systematic profiling of all human and mouse ETS proteins puts these three in their own
class (class III), the most sequence-distinct group in the family [PMID:20517297,21548782]; a tyrosine that sets specificity
at the position immediately 3' of the core in other ETS proteins is replaced by asparagine here [PMID:20517297].
Expression is hematopoietic and essentially non-overlapping with the rest of the family: SPI1 in
myeloid cells, macrophages, dendritic cells, microglia and B cells; SPIB in B cells and
plasmacytoid dendritic cells; SPIC narrowly in splenic red pulp macrophages, with none detected in monocytes, dendritic cells or the
other tissue macrophages examined [PMID:19037245], and later also in a heme-induced, VCAM1-positive bone
marrow macrophage subset [PMID:24630724].
The first crystal structure of any ETS domain on DNA was PU.1's, which established the
loop-helix-loop mode of DNA contact for the whole family [PMID:8602247].

## The motif

The site is usually written AAAGAGGAAGTG, and the models grouped here agree on AAAGAGGAAGT. The
invariant part is the same GGA(A/T) core all ETS proteins read, contacted by two invariant
arginines in recognition helix H3 that hydrogen-bond the two guanines, with a wing lysine 5' of the
core and a turn lysine on the opposite strand 3' of it [PMID:8602247]. What sets this family apart is the 5' flank.
Class I ETS proteins prefer ACC immediately 5' of GGA [PMID:20517297]; the SPI proteins prefer purines - AGA, with
a marked preference for G two bases 5' of the core - and tolerate a run of As further out [PMID:2180582,20517297,21548782]. Because
that difference spans three or four positions rather than one, class III motifs are the only ETS
subfamily that a sequence scan separates from the rest with any reliability [PMID:20517297]. Within the family,
SPI1, SPIB and SPIC are not separable: their models are near-identical, and the Vierstra archetype
that represents them is named for two of the three factors at once (AC0642:SPIB/SPI). Note that
the published PU.1 site contains no CpG, so unlike the class I CCGGAAGT it is insensitive to
CpG methylation. The composite EICE, GGAAGTGAAAC, is a PU.1 site fused to an IRF half-site [PMID:7797077,12453417] and is
captured by only one model in this family - the CIS-BP entry M07944, whose consensus AAAGAGGAAGTGAAA
runs from the PU.1 site into the IRF half-site.

## Where it acts

PU.1 sites are found at myeloid and B-lineage promoters and, more heavily, at the enhancers that
define those lineages; the classic example is the macrophage colony-stimulating factor receptor
(CSF1R) promoter, where PU.1 directs macrophage-specific expression [PMID:8264604]. PU.1 behaves as a lineage
"pioneer" in the sense that its binding precedes and is required for much of the accessible
chromatin landscape of myeloid cells [PMID:20513432], so its motif is enriched in macrophage and B-cell DNase and
ATAC footprints far more than in other cell types. Two named composite elements dominate its
cooperative biology. The EICE (ETS-IRF composite element, GGAAGTGAAAC) was defined at
immunoglobulin light-chain enhancers, where DNA-bound and Ser148-phosphorylated PU.1 recruits IRF4
(originally Pip) or IRF8 [PMID:7797077,12453417]; cooperativity between the two DNA-binding
domains has been measured at 20- to 40-fold [PMID:12453417]. The
crystal structure of the PU.1/IRF4/DNA complex shows the DNA bent into an S shape that juxtaposes the two domains across the
central minor groove, and explains why IRF1 and IRF2 are anti-cooperative with PU.1 at the same
element [PMID:12453417]. PU.1 sites also cluster with CEBP, RUNX and GATA sites in myeloid enhancers.

## Biology and disease

Spi1-null mice lack macrophages, neutrophils and B cells and have severely disrupted myeloid and
lymphoid development [PMID:8079170,8896458], the most striking single-gene hematopoietic phenotype among the ETS family.
Dosage matters as much as presence: reducing PU.1 expression to roughly a fifth of normal in mice
causes acute myeloid leukemia [PMID:15146183], placing SPI1 among the transcription factors whose partial loss is
leukemogenic. SPIC is required for red pulp macrophage development and splenic iron recycling [PMID:19037245].
In human disease, recurrent SPI1 fusions (STMN1-SPI1, TCF7-SPI1) define a high-risk subgroup of
pediatric T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia [PMID:28671687], and PU.1 activity is a recurring theme in myeloid
leukemia biology more broadly.

## Reading a hit

A purine-rich AAAGAGGAAGTG match is one of the few ETS hits that genuinely localizes the signal to
a subfamily - but only to the subfamily. SPI1, SPIB and SPIC cannot be told apart by sequence, and
the atlas's representative model for this family is itself named for two factors. The distinction
from class I ETS is real but not absolute: degenerate members of this family, such as HOCOMOCO's
short SPI1.H14CORE.1.S.B model whose consensus is only GGAAGT, will match generic ETS sites, and
the GGAA core alone is expected millions of times per strand in a 3.1-Gb genome. Cell type carries
much of the inference: outside myeloid, B-lineage or microglial contexts a PU-box match is far more
likely to be a chance GGAA than a bound PU.1 site. Two caveats specific to this family: only one of its
twelve models (CIS-BP M07944, AAAGAGGAAGTGAAA) reaches into the IRF half-site, so scanning with the
rest will find the PU.1 half of an EICE without flagging the composite - look explicitly for GTGAAAC
a few bases 3' of the core; and the JASPAR
SPIB model (MA0081.3) is stored on the reverse strand as CACTTCCTCTT, the same site as AAGAGGAAGTG.
families.caveats:
This is one of the few ETS subfamilies a scan can separate from the others, because
its purine-rich 5' flank differs over three or four positions rather than one. It cannot separate
its own members: SPI1, SPIB and SPIC share one motif, and the atlas representative is a Vierstra
archetype named for two of them. Expression usually decides - SPIC is confined to iron-recycling macrophages of the splenic red pulp
and bone marrow, SPIB to B cells and plasmacytoid dendritic cells - so a PU-box hit outside a
hematopoietic context deserves scepticism. The family is small (12 models) and includes short,
degenerate entries that behave like a generic ETS site. Only one of the twelve models reaches into the IRF half-site of
the EICE composite, so a scan will usually register the PU.1 half-site and miss the element that
gives it specificity.

timeline.finding: PU.1 is cloned as a macrophage- and B-cell-specific activator that recognizes the purine-rich PU box, GAGGAA, through a carboxy-terminal DNA-binding domain related to the ets oncogene.
timeline.methods: cDNA cloning, methylation interference, DNase I protection, deletion mapping
timeline.open: How the domain read the PU box, and what set it apart from other ETS sites, was unknown.

timeline.finding: Two Spi1 knockouts establish PU.1 as essential for blood development: one gives late-gestation lethality with a multilineage defect in lymphoid and myeloid progenitors; the second (1996) gives live-born pups lacking macrophages, neutrophils, B and T cells, in which T cells and a few neutrophils later appear while B cells and macrophages never do.
timeline.methods: Gene targeting in mice
timeline.open: The two lines disagreed on whether PU.1 acts at lineage commitment of a multipotential progenitor or only at later B-cell and macrophage differentiation.

timeline.finding: Pip (IRF4) is cloned as the lymphoid partner that binds the immunoglobulin light-chain enhancer composite element only alongside DNA-bound PU.1, and complex formation requires phosphorylation of PU.1 Ser148.
timeline.methods: cDNA cloning, EMSA, co-transfection reporter assays

timeline.finding: The PU.1 ETS domain-DNA crystal structure, the first for the family, shows a winged helix-turn-helix contacting ten base pairs through a loop-helix-loop, with two recognition-helix arginines on the GGA core and conserved wing and turn lysines on either side.
timeline.methods: X-ray crystallography
timeline.open: The structure did not explain the purine-rich 5' flank that distinguishes the SPI proteins.

timeline.finding: The PU.1/IRF4/DNA ternary structure shows the composite element bent into an S shape that juxtaposes the two DNA-binding domains across the central minor groove, accounting for cooperativity with IRF4 and IRF8 and anti-cooperativity with IRF1 and IRF2.
timeline.methods: X-ray crystallography

timeline.finding: Hypomorphic alleles that lower PU.1 to about 20% of normal cause acute myeloid leukemia in mice, whereas complete or 50% loss does not, so graded reduction rather than absence of PU.1 is leukemogenic.
timeline.methods: Hypomorphic knock-in mice, retroviral rescue

timeline.finding: PU.1, together with small sets of lineage-determining partners (C/EBP in macrophages, E2A, EBF and Oct-2 in B cells), establishes most promoter-distal H3K4me1 regions; PU.1 binding initiates nucleosome remodeling followed by H3K4 monomethylation.
timeline.methods: ChIP-seq, histone-mark profiling, motif analysis, genetic complementation
timeline.open: Whether PU.1 can open closed sites alone, or only with its collaborating factors, was not resolved.

timeline.finding: Recurrent STMN1-SPI1 and TCF7-SPI1 fusions mark 3.9% (7 of 181) of pediatric T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemias, a distinct subgroup with uniformly poor survival; the fusion proteins keep transcriptional activity and block maturation of mouse progenitors.
timeline.methods: Transcriptome and targeted capture sequencing, transduction of mouse stem/progenitor cells

open: The base immediately 5' of the GGA core is reported inconsistently: the PU box and the ChIP-derived models read GAGGAA, whereas systematic in vitro profiling characterizes class III by G at -2 and C at -1, and one HT-SELEX SPIB model here reads AAAAGCGGAAGT; if C is genuinely favored, the site can contain a CpG, and the methylation insensitivity of the classic PU.1 site would not extend to it.

How much PU.1 alone selects myeloid and B-cell enhancers is unsettled: its binding initiates nucleosome remodeling and H3K4 monomethylation at many distal sites, yet those sites are established together with lineage partners such as C/EBP in macrophages and E2A in B cells, and whether PU.1 can open closed chromatin without them is not settled by the studies cited here.

families.name: ZBTB7A/B/C (LRF)
families.def: GC-rich GACCCCCCCC. ZBTB7A, ZBTB7B, ZBTB7C.
families.short: ZBTB7A, ZBTB7B and ZBTB7C are BTB/POZ zinc-finger proteins that read short GC-rich sites through four C2H2 fingers and repress or reorganize promoters through the dimerizing BTB domain. ZBTB7A, also called LRF, Pokemon or FBI-1, competes with SP1 at GC boxes, represses the ARF tumor suppressor and the fetal hemoglobin genes, and acts more broadly as a promoter-accessibility factor for other transcription factors. ZBTB7B, better known as ThPOK or cKrox, directs CD4 rather than CD8 T-cell fate and has been proposed as the vertebrate GAGA factor. Because the recognition sites are short, GC-rich and shared with the large SP/KLF motif class, hits in this family are easy to obtain and hard to attribute.
families.long:
## The factors

Three paralogues: ZBTB7A (LRF, Pokemon, FBI-1, OCZF), ZBTB7B (ThPOK, cKrox, Zfp67) and the much less studied ZBTB7C (APM-1). Each is 500-600 residues with an N-terminal BTB/POZ domain and four C-terminal C2H2 fingers. The BTB domain homodimerizes and also serves as the corepressor-docking surface, so DNA-bound ZBTB7 proteins arrive as dimers carrying NCoR/SMRT- and HDAC-containing complexes; for ZBTB7B the BTB domain is specifically required for its CD4-lineage function [PMID:15750595]. Expression patterns diverge sharply. ZBTB7A is broadly expressed, with well-characterized roles in hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells, erythroid cells and B versus T lineage choice. ZBTB7B is induced in CD4-committed thymocytes during positive selection [PMID:15750595,20307210] and is also expressed in cartilage and skin, where it was first described as c-Krox, a regulator of type I collagen genes. ZBTB7C is expressed at low levels in many tissues and has essentially no dedicated functional literature.

## The motif

The in vitro consensus supported by the matrices here is a short GC-rich element, CGACCACC, or GGTGGTCG read on the other strand. HT-SELEX models for ZBTB7B (JASPAR MA0694.2) and ZBTB7C (MA0695.2), the CIS-BP entries for both, and the Vierstra archetype AC0529:ZBTB7A/ZBTB7B all converge on it, with 10-14 bits over eight positions [PMID:23332764]. Four adjacent zinc fingers would be expected to read about 12 bases, so this consensus is shorter than the domain can in principle cover, and the flanks are weakly specified. Two other renderings circulate and should not be conflated with it. First, ZBTB7A models in HOCOMOCO and CIS-BP extend the same GACC core into a run of cytosines - written GGGGGGGTC or GACCCCYSCC - and the GC-rich "GACCCCCCCC" form is what much of the ZBTB7A literature quotes [PMID:12750370,18801742]; whether ZBTB7A genuinely prefers a longer C-run than its paralogues, or whether this reflects the different experiments used, is not resolved by these data. Second, ZBTB7B has been identified as the vertebrate homologue of the Drosophila GAGA factor and reported to associate with purine-rich GAGA sequences, a description that does not match CGACCACC at all [PMID:28856379]. The atlas reports the HT-SELEX consensus because that is what the collections agree on, but a reader should know that three different sequence descriptions exist for this family. Within the family, ZBTB7A, ZBTB7B and ZBTB7C models are 0.96-0.98 similar where they overlap, so the paralogues are not separable by sequence.

## Where it acts

These are promoter factors. ZBTB7A binds a substantial fraction of human promoters and enhancers, including many NF-kappaB p65 targets, and it associates with promoters independently of the client factor; prebinding by ZBTB7A marks which promoters can undergo factor-induced changes in accessibility [PMID:29813070]. On its own it does not activate. ZBTB7A also competes directly with SP1 for overlapping GC boxes - documented at the RB1 promoter, where it displaces SP1 and recruits corepressors [PMID:18801742] - which is a general hazard for interpreting GC-box hits. Because the site is GC-rich and CpG-containing, matches concentrate in CpG-island promoters. Known target loci include CDKN2A/ARF, RB1, MCAM, BCL2L11 (BIM) and the fetal globin genes HBG1/HBG2.

## Biology and disease

Zbtb7a-null mouse embryonic fibroblasts resist oncogene-driven transformation, and ZBTB7A overexpression transforms cells in vitro and in transgenic mice, effects attributable in part to direct repression of ARF [PMID:15662416]; ZBTB7A is overexpressed in several human cancers. In hematopoiesis, ZBTB7A antagonizes Notch to enforce B-cell over T-cell fate [PMID:17495164], and it is an essential GATA1 target in erythroid development, restraining BIM-dependent apoptosis [PMID:19853566]. ZBTB7A and BCL11A independently repress fetal hemoglobin, making ZBTB7A a target of interest for sickle cell disease and beta-thalassemia therapy [PMID:26816381]. Recurrent ZBTB7A mutations occur in acute myeloid leukemia with t(8;21), where they behave as loss-of-function cooperating lesions [PMID:27252013]. For ZBTB7B, transgenic expression forces MHC class I-restricted thymocytes into the CD4 helper program instead of the CD8 cytotoxic program [PMID:15750595], and a human multimorphic ThPOK variant has been reported to cause an inborn error of immunity with T-cell defects and fibrosis [PMID:40392549].

## Reading a hit

This family sits in the most crowded part of motif space. CGACCACC and the GC-rich GACCCCC variants overlap the recognition space of SP1-SP4, the KLFs, MAZ, PATZ1, E2F and other CpG-island factors, and ZBTB7A is documented to compete with SP1 for the same sites, so sequence cannot assign a GC-box hit to this family with any confidence [PMID:18801742]. Within the family, the three paralogues are indistinguishable; the Vierstra archetype AC0529:ZBTB7A/ZBTB7B is explicit that ZBTB7A and ZBTB7B were not resolved. Provenance is mixed. The ZBTB7B and ZBTB7C JASPAR matrices are HT-SELEX, which supports direct binding [PMID:23332764], and HOCOMOCO's ZBT7B and ZBT7C models carry in vitro evidence codes (SM and S). The ZBTB7A situation is worse: the JASPAR ZBTB7A matrix MA0750.3 is ChIP-seq-derived and reads CCGGAAGTG, an ETS-family site with no resemblance to any other ZBTB7A model in the family and with its best cross-database match in a different family altogether. That matrix should be treated as reporting a co-bound or indirectly bound ETS element, not ZBTB7A's own preference. Finally, ZBTB7A occupancy is common and largely permissive rather than instructive [PMID:29813070], so even a correct ZBTB7A call says little about whether the promoter is regulated by it.
families.caveats: The sites are eight or fewer informative bases, GC-rich and CpG-island-associated, and overlap SP/KLF, MAZ and E2F motif space; ZBTB7A is documented to compete with SP1 for the same GC boxes. ZBTB7A, ZBTB7B and ZBTB7C cannot be told apart from sequence, and the Vierstra archetype merges ZBTB7A with ZBTB7B by name. Three different sequence descriptions exist in the literature for this family (CGACCACC, GC-rich GACCCCCCCC, and purine-rich GAGA for ThPOK/vGAF), which are not reconciled. Most importantly, JASPAR MA0750.3 for ZBTB7A is a ChIP-derived ETS-like matrix (CCGGAAGTG) unrelated to the rest of the family; do not scan with it as if it were ZBTB7A.

timeline.finding: FBI-1 (ZBTB7A) was shown to bind GGGG-rich repeats with the per-repeat consensus G(A/G)GGG(T/C)(C/T)(T/C)(C/T) arranged as direct, inverted or everted copies with no preferred spacing or rotational alignment, so the dimeric protein tolerates site geometries that a single position weight matrix cannot express.
timeline.methods: EMSA with viral and cellular sites, spacing and orientation variants
timeline.open: Which of the many tolerated arrangements, if any, is the physiological site.

timeline.finding: ZBTB7A was identified as an oncogenic repressor: null mouse fibroblasts resisted oncogene-driven transformation, overexpression transformed cells in vitro and in transgenic mice, and the ARF tumor suppressor was shown to be a direct repressed target.
timeline.methods: mouse knockouts and transgenics, transformation assays, promoter binding

timeline.finding: cKrox/ThPOK (ZBTB7B) was shown to be upregulated in CD4-committed thymocytes and sufficient to redirect MHC class I-restricted thymocytes into the CD4 helper program, with the BTB domain required - a lineage-instructive role for a paralogue that reads the same sequence as ZBTB7A.
timeline.methods: expression profiling during selection, transgenic mice

timeline.finding: Two hematopoietic requirements were established for ZBTB7A: repression of Notch-driven T-cell instruction to enforce B-cell fate, and, as a direct GATA1 target, repression of BIM to keep late erythroblasts alive.
timeline.methods: conditional mouse alleles, lineage reconstitution, genetic rescue by Bim loss

timeline.finding: HT-SELEX gave ZBTB7B and ZBTB7C the compact eight-base site CGACCACC, which the collections adopted as the family consensus; it does not look like the C-run form the ZBTB7A literature quotes, and the two descriptions were never reconciled.
timeline.methods: HT-SELEX on a large panel of human transcription factors
timeline.open: Whether ZBTB7A truly prefers a longer C-run than its paralogues or the difference is an assay artifact.

timeline.finding: ZBTB7A was shown to silence the fetal globin genes through nucleosome density, independently of BCL11A, and recurrent truncating and missense ZBTB7A mutations were found in 23 percent of t(8;21) acute myeloid leukemias, where they disable repression - evidence that the factor is dosage-critical in blood.
timeline.methods: erythroid knockouts and ChIP, patient exome sequencing with functional assays

timeline.finding: ZBTB7A was found at a large share of promoters and enhancers, binding independently of the client factor and determining which promoters can be opened by NF-kappaB p65 and other factors without activating them itself, which reframes a ZBTB7A match as a permissive mark rather than a regulatory instruction.
timeline.methods: genome-wide binding and accessibility profiling, depletion experiments

timeline.finding: A de novo ThPOK variant, K360N, was reported in a patient with CD4 T-cell deficiency and fibrosis and shown to be multimorphic: it fails to bind the wild-type ThPOK consensus, interferes with the wild-type protein, and acquires a novel DNA-binding specificity, the first human allele to alter this family's sequence preference directly.
timeline.methods: patient genomics, protein binding microarray-style specificity assays, single-cell RNA sequencing, transduction experiments

open: Three sequence descriptions are in circulation for this family - the HT-SELEX site CGACCACC, the GGGG/C-run repeats from the ZBTB7A literature, and purine-rich GAGA sequences attributed to vertebrate GAF/ThPOK - and nothing in the published work establishes whether these are paralogue differences, assay differences, or several binding modes of one flexible BTB dimer.

Whether ZBTB7A occupancy is driven by sequence at all is unresolved: it binds a large fraction of promoters, does not activate them, and competes with SP1 for the same GC boxes, so its binding profile may be set mainly by accessibility and by partner factors.

The JASPAR ZBTB7A matrix MA0750.3 reads an ETS-like CCGGAAGTG that resembles nothing else in the family, and it is unknown whether this reflects reproducible co-binding of ZBTB7A with ETS factors at shared promoters or simply a peak set dominated by another protein.
ZBTB7C has a motif in three collections and almost no functional literature, so whether it has any distinct target set or acts only redundantly with ZBTB7A and ZBTB7B has not been tested.

families.name: ROR
families.def: RORE: AT-rich half-site AAAGTAGGTCA. RORA, RORB, RORC.
families.short: RORA, RORB and RORC (RORalpha/beta/gamma) are nuclear receptors that bind DNA as monomers to the ROR response element, or RORE: an AGGTCA nuclear-receptor half-site preceded by a 5-6 bp AT-rich extension, most often written AAAGTAGGTCA. The extension is read by a C-terminal extension of the DNA-binding domain lying in the minor groove, and it is the only feature that distinguishes a RORE from the half-site shared by many other nuclear receptors. ROREs form the second transcriptional loop of the mammalian circadian clock, where RORs activate Bmal1 in competition with the REV-ERB repressors at the same sites. RORgammat, a thymus-restricted RORC isoform, drives the Th17 program and is a drug target in autoimmune disease.
families.long:
## The factors

The ROR (RAR-related orphan receptor) group is encoded by three human genes: *RORA* (NR1F1, RORalpha), *RORB* (NR1F2, RORbeta) and *RORC* (NR1F3, RORgamma; the symbol *RORG* is used for it in HOCOMOCO and in the Vierstra archetypes). Each protein has the standard nuclear-receptor layout — an N-terminal A/B region, a DNA-binding domain (DBD) built from two zinc-coordinating modules, a hinge, and a ligand-binding domain (LBD) ending in an AF-2 helix. Unlike the steroid and RXR-partnered receptors, RORs bind DNA as monomers, using a C-terminal extension (CTE) of the DBD in addition to the zinc modules [PMID:7926749,7739535]. Alternative promoters and splicing generate isoforms with different N-termini (RORalpha1-4; RORgamma and the thymus-restricted RORgammat), and these N-termini change DNA-binding behavior rather than just transactivation [PMID:7926749]. Expression differs sharply: *RORA* is broad (cerebellum, liver, many tissues), *RORB* is largely restricted to retina, pineal gland and specific brain regions, and *RORC* is expressed in liver, muscle and skeletal tissue, with RORgammat confined to thymocytes and to T-helper and innate lymphoid subsets. RORalpha and RORgamma are constitutively active in reporter assays, with cholesterol and oxysterol derivatives occupying the LBD pocket [PMID:24577401].

## The motif

The ROR response element (RORE) is a single nuclear-receptor half-site with a 5' extension, conventionally written as an AT-rich stretch of 5-6 bp followed by RGGTCA. The canonical monomeric site established for RORalpha1 is often quoted as the 11-mer AAAGTAGGTCA [PMID:7926749,7739535]; the motif models in this family converge on a slightly shorter 10-mer, A(A/T)NTAGGTCA (the pooled data consensus here is AAbTAGGTCA). Both renderings describe the same element — the discrepancy is only how many of the weakly constrained AT positions a given model retains.

Structurally, the split is clean. The zinc modules place a recognition helix in the major groove of AGGTCA, which supplies most of the information content; the CTE (the A-box/T-box region) lies along the minor groove of the AT-rich 5' extension and is what converts a generic half-site into a RORE [PMID:7739535]. The crystal structure of the closely related REV-ERBalpha DBD plus CTE on a direct repeat, and the structure of the monomeric receptor NGFI-B, both show this arrangement directly [PMID:9660968,10331876]. Without the 5' extension the motif is just the half-site shared by dozens of nuclear receptors [PMID:31175293].

RORs also bind extended sites: HT-SELEX models in this family include ~18-bp tandem arrangements (AAGTAGGTCAGTAGGTCA), i.e. two half-sites in direct repeat with a 2-bp gap. All eleven motifs assigned here collapse onto the same core (family cohesion 0.87), and none is flagged as mislabelled. RORA, RORB and RORC are not distinguishable from sequence.

## Where it acts

ROREs sit in promoters and enhancers, not preferentially in CpG islands. The best-characterized examples are the two ROREs in the *Bmal1* (*ARNTL*) promoter, with further sites at *Cry1*, *Npas2* and *Nfil3* [PMID:12152080,15312651]. In immune cells, RORgammat acts through ROREs in the *IL17A*/*IL17F* locus and its conserved non-coding regions, alongside RUNX1, BATF and IRF4. In the circadian cis-regulatory grammar, the RORE is one of three elements — E-box (CLOCK:BMAL1), D-box, and RORE — whose combination sets the phase of a rhythmic promoter; the RORE contributes the late-night/early-morning component [PMID:12152080]. Because the informative part is a 10-mer with several degenerate positions, matches are common: expect on the order of 10^5 hits genome-wide at permissive thresholds, so genomic occurrence alone carries little weight.

## Biology and disease

The *staggerer* mouse, a spontaneous *Rora* deletion, loses cerebellar Purkinje cells and is ataxic [PMID:8602221], and RNAi and mutant analyses place Rora in the mammalian clock, where loss shortens or destabilizes period [PMID:15312651]. *Rorb* is required for photoreceptor and pineal gene programs [PMID:9670004]. *Rorc*-null mice lack lymph nodes and Peyer's patches and show increased thymocyte apoptosis [PMID:10875923], and RORgammat is required for the Th17 program [PMID:16990136], making it a drug target in psoriasis and other autoimmune disease; RORgamma inverse agonists and RORalpha/gamma agonists have both been pursued clinically [PMID:24577401].

## Reading a hit

A RORE match identifies the family, not the member: nothing in the sequence separates RORA from RORB from RORC. More importantly, it does not separate ROR from REV-ERB. NR1D1 and NR1D2 bind the same RORE and the same 2-bp-spaced direct repeat [PMID:9660968,24577401], and the Vierstra archetype AC0123:NR1D/RORC states this by naming both groups. The two are told apart by tissue, circadian phase and cofactor (coactivator versus NCoR-HDAC3), not by motif [PMID:24577401,26044300].

Second, check that your hit includes the AT-rich extension. A bare AGGTCA is shared with ESRRA, NR5A, NR4A and the RXR heterodimer partners; scanning with the full 10-11-mer is the only way to make the call specific. Third, weigh the evidence code. RORB.H14CORE.0.SM.B rests on in vitro selection (HT-SELEX plus methyl-HT-SELEX) and supports a direct binding claim; RORA.H14CORE.0.P.C is ChIP-only at grade C and its consensus drifts at the 3' end. Finally, ChIP-derived versions of this motif can be contaminated by indirect binding: in mouse liver, most REV-ERBalpha ChIP peaks reflect tethering to HNF6 rather than direct RORE occupancy [PMID:26044300], and the same mechanism is available to RORs.
families.caveats: Treat a RORE hit as a family-level call, and remember the family boundary is porous: REV-ERB (NR1D1/NR1D2) binds the same element, so a match is really a 'ROR/REV-ERB site' unless expression or phase data break the tie. RORA, RORB and RORC are not separable from sequence — all eleven motifs here collapse onto one core. Matches to the bare AGGTCA half-site are not ROREs; require the AT-rich 5' extension. Prefer the in vitro-derived models (HOCOMOCO evidence S/M, e.g. RORB.H14CORE.0.SM.B) over ChIP-only entries such as RORA.H14CORE.0.P.C, which is grade C. The 10-mer is common enough that occurrence alone is weak evidence.

timeline.finding: Binding-site selection with in vitro-made RORalpha shows that it binds DNA as a monomer to a 6-bp AT-rich sequence preceding an RGGTCA half-site, defining the RORE; the alternative N-termini of RORalpha1 and RORalpha2 change which ROREs are bound.
timeline.methods: In vitro binding-site selection, EMSA, reporter assays
timeline.open: Which part of the protein reads the AT-rich extension was not yet known.

timeline.finding: Methylation and ethylation interference plus mutagenesis place RORE specificity in a C-terminal extension of the second zinc module, as in the monomeric receptors NGFI-B and FTZ-F1, though through different subdomains.
timeline.methods: Interference footprinting, mutagenesis, domain swaps

timeline.finding: Positional cloning shows that the ataxic staggerer mouse carries a deletion in Rora, the first in vivo phenotype for the family.
timeline.methods: Positional cloning, mouse genetics

timeline.finding: The 2.3 A crystal structure of the REV-ERB DNA-binding region on its DR2 element reveals a second protein-DNA interface in the minor groove beside the half-site; the NGFI-B monomer structure (1999) shows the same C-terminal-extension contact on a single half-site.
timeline.methods: X-ray crystallography
timeline.open: The ROR arrangement was inferred from these relatives, not observed in a ROR-DNA complex.

timeline.finding: Genome-wide expression profiling of SCN and liver, combined with promoter searches, identifies the REV-ERB/ROR element as the cis-element for circadian-night expression, in phase with Bmal1.
timeline.methods: Expression profiling, promoter motif search, reporter assays

timeline.finding: A cell-based screen for Bmal1 activators identifies Rora; Rora is required for normal Bmal1 expression and consolidated locomotor rhythms, establishing the ROR-activates/REV-ERB-represses loop at shared ROREs.
timeline.methods: Functional genomics screen, reporter assays, mutant mouse behavior

timeline.finding: RORgammat is shown to direct the differentiation of IL-17-producing T helper cells, making RORC a drug target in autoimmune disease.
timeline.methods: Knockout mice, retroviral overexpression, T-cell differentiation

timeline.finding: Comparing wild-type and DNA-binding-defective REV-ERBalpha in liver shows that clock genes are controlled by direct binding at ROREs in competition with RORs, whereas metabolic genes are regulated through tethering to lineage factors such as HNF6; ChIP peaks at these sites therefore mix direct and indirect binding.
timeline.methods: ChIP-seq, DNA-binding mutant, transcriptomics
timeline.open: The study tested REV-ERBalpha; how much ROR ChIP signal is tethered was left open.

open: Whether RORs use two-half-site sites in vivo is unresolved: the literature describes them as monomers on a single extended half-site, yet three of the eleven motifs in this family model two AGGTCA half-sites (two as a 2-bp-spaced direct repeat from HT-SELEX, one as a palindrome), which could reflect a cooperative binding mode or only the extra avidity of two monomers in vitro.

It is not settled whether RORs are regulated by a physiological ligand or are effectively constitutive: cholesterol, cholesterol-biosynthetic intermediates and several oxysterols all occupy the RORgamma pocket and act as agonists in vitro, but which of them, if any, sets ROR activity in cells is debated.

How much ROR ChIP signal reflects direct RORE binding is unknown: for REV-ERBalpha a DNA-binding mutant showed that metabolic-gene sites are reached by tethering to HNF6 and other lineage factors, but the equivalent partition for RORs has not been established.

families.name: NR2E (TLX / PNR)
families.def: AAGGTCA monomeric sites. NR2E1, NR2E3.
families.short: NR2E is a small orphan nuclear-receptor group with two human members: NR2E1 (TLX, the homolog of Drosophila tailless) and NR2E3 (PNR, photoreceptor-specific nuclear receptor). Unusually for the superfamily, they prefer the hexamer AAGTCA rather than the AGGTCA half-site read by most nuclear receptors, a switch traced to a residue in the P-box of the recognition helix; the fuller models add a 5' A/T-rich extension and a tandem repeat of the core. The two factors are expressed in different cell types: TLX regulates neural stem and progenitor cells in the forebrain and retina, while PNR acts in rod photoreceptors with CRX and NRL. NR2E3 mutations cause enhanced S-cone syndrome, a retinal cell-fate disorder.
families.long:
## The factors

NR2E is a two-member orphan group within the nuclear receptor superfamily: NR2E1, usually called TLX (the vertebrate homolog of *Drosophila* tailless), and NR2E3, usually called PNR (photoreceptor-specific nuclear receptor) [PMID:8047143,10220376]. Both have the canonical receptor layout — a short N-terminal region, a DNA-binding domain (DBD) built from two zinc-coordinating modules with a C-terminal extension, and a ligand-binding domain. No endogenous ligand is established for either, which is why they remain formally orphan. The two are expressed in different cell types, although both act in the retina. TLX is expressed in the neuroepithelium of the developing brain and in adult neural stem and progenitor cells of the subventricular zone and dentate gyrus, where it maintains the undifferentiated state [PMID:8047143,14702088]; it is also expressed in the optic cup, in retinal progenitors and later in Muller glia and retinal astrocytes [PMID:10706625,15371513]. PNR is essentially retina-specific, restricted to rod photoreceptors, where it works downstream of NRL and alongside CRX [PMID:10220376,19823680]. Neither is broadly expressed, and neither has a large paralogue set — with two genes, this is one of the smallest nuclear-receptor groups in the human genome. TLX represses target genes through the atrophin/LSD1 and HDAC corepressor machinery [PMID:16702404,17873065,20123967]; PNR can both activate rod genes and repress cone genes, depending on context and partner [PMID:19823680].

## The motif

The NR2E group is unusual in the superfamily for what it reads. Most nuclear receptors recognize the hexamer AGGTCA; tailless and PNR instead prefer AAGTCA, and the switch has been traced to a subclass-specific residue in the P-box, the part of the recognition helix that reads the core [PMID:8047143,10220376,18179707]. The consensus given here, AAGTCA with a 5' A/T-rich extension (i.e. AAAGTCAA in the fuller models), reflects that. This is where the literature disagrees with itself, and with some database annotation: the group is frequently described as binding "AAGGTCA monomeric sites", which is the ordinary extended half-site. The difference is one base in the core, and the in vitro selection data assembled here fall on the AAGTCA side, including a tandem form AAGTCAATAAGTCA from HT-SELEX. Both renderings are in print; the shorter core is the better supported one for these two proteins specifically.

The family is loosely cohesive (0.67, low for this atlas). Models split into an AAGTCA-centered set (the HOCOMOCO NR2E1 in vitro entries, JASPAR Nr2e1, two Vierstra archetypes) and a second set centered on GGGATCA/AAAGATCA. One CIS-BP entry labelled NR2E1 (M02394_2.00, GAGGTCA) is flagged here as a probable member of the RXR-heterodimer family instead, and the JASPAR profile Nr2e3 (MA0164.2) has a consensus (AAGCTT) that resembles nothing else in the family. Work reported for NR2E3 indicates it binds only dimeric arrangements, while NR2E1 tolerates both monomeric and dimeric sites [PMID:18179707] — a real difference between the two, but not one you can read off a single match.

## Where it acts

Because both factors are cell-type restricted, so is the useful signal. PNR sites cluster at rod photoreceptor gene promoters and enhancers, typically adjacent to CRX (the OTX-family site) and NRL (a Maf-family site), and PNR physically interacts with CRX through its DBD [PMID:19823680]. TLX sites are found at neural stem cell and cell-cycle genes, including *PTEN* and *CDKN1A*, in neural stem cells and retinal progenitors [PMID:17873065,16702404]. Neither motif is CpG-island associated. The bare AAGTCA hexamer is far too short to be informative on its own; at any usable threshold a 6-mer occurs hundreds of thousands of times in the human genome, so only the extended or tandem forms are worth scanning.

## Biology and disease

*NR2E3* mutations cause enhanced S-cone syndrome (Goldmann-Favre syndrome), in which S-cone photoreceptors are overproduced at the expense of rods — a cell-fate disorder rather than a simple degeneration [PMID:10655056] — and also account for a share of autosomal recessive retinitis pigmentosa. The naturally occurring *rd7* mouse carries an *Nr2e3* mutation and reproduces the phenotype [PMID:34561487], and gene supplementation in that model is an active therapeutic line. Disease-associated substitutions in the NR2E3 DBD impair both dimerization and the interaction with CRX, which is consistent with a dimer-only binding mode [PMID:19823680]. *Nr2e1*-null mice have a defective limbic system, with a hypoplastic amygdala and cortical and hypothalamic abnormalities, aggressive behavior, and impaired maintenance of adult neural stem cells [PMID:9394001,14702088]. Their retinas are thin, overproduce S-cones and degenerate early, with progressive optic nerve degeneration and blindness [PMID:10706625,16702404].

## Reading a hit

An NR2E match should be read cautiously. The core is short, the family is only loosely cohesive, and the two members are expressed in different cell types, so context does much of the work: a PNR call in brain is almost certainly wrong regardless of motif score [PMID:10220376]. The retina is the exception: TLX acts there in progenitors and glia and PNR in photoreceptors [PMID:15371513,10220376], so in retinal data only the cell type separates them. Nothing in the sequence distinguishes NR2E1 from NR2E3, and the AAGTCA core overlaps the AGGTCA half-site used by much of the nuclear receptor superfamily, so a permissive scan will pull in ESRRA, NR4A, NR5A and RXR-partner sites [PMID:31175293]. Prefer the extended or tandem models, and prefer the HOCOMOCO entries with in vitro evidence codes (`S`, `SM`) over the archetype and ChIP-derived profiles. Treat the two Vierstra archetypes whose consensus is GGGATCA or AAAGATCA as separate observations that happen to be labelled NR2E rather than as confirmation of the AAGTCA site; archetypes are named after the majority of the factor labels that clustered, not after a demonstrated binding protein.
families.caveats: This is a weak family to call from sequence. The core is a 6-mer, family cohesion is only 0.67, and the assigned motifs split into an AAGTCA-centered set and a GGGATCA/AAAGATCA set. One CIS-BP entry labelled NR2E1 is flagged here as belonging with the RXR heterodimers, and the JASPAR Nr2e3 profile does not resemble the rest of the family. NR2E1 and NR2E3 are not separable by motif, but they are expressed in different cell types, so expression is the more informative discriminator — except in the retina, where both act and only the cell type (progenitors and glia for TLX, photoreceptors for PNR) separates them. Note also that the group is often described as binding AAGGTCA; the in vitro data here favor AAGTCA, one base shorter in the core.

open: Whether the NR2E receptors read AAGTCA or AGGTCA is not fully settled: biochemical work on tailless, TLX, PNR and their nematode orthologues points to AAGTCA, with a single P-box residue able to shift the preference to AGGTCA, while the family is widely annotated as binding AAGGTCA and one CIS-BP NR2E1 model (GAGGTCA) clusters with the RXR heterodimers instead.

What the GGGATCA/AAAGATCA-centered motifs labelled NR2E represent is unresolved: one CIS-BP NR2E3 model and three Vierstra archetypes share this core, which differs from the AAGTCA half-site described for TLX and PNR, and it has not been established whether it is a second binding mode or a labelling or assay artifact.

Whether human NR2E3 binds only dimeric sites is not established: the dimer-only rule comes from the nematode orthologue FAX-1, human NR2E3 has mainly been studied by cell-based dimerization and partner assays, and the JASPAR Nr2e3 profile (AAGCTT) resembles neither monomeric nor tandem AAGTCA sites.

families.name: Thinly characterized small families
families.def: Factors with a measured motif but almost no dedicated literature: MSANTD1/3/4, DNTTIP1, FLYWCH1, FAM200B (= ZBED11), ELYS/AHCTF1, NACC2, and XPA, which is a DNA repair protein rather than a transcription factor. BANP is named in older drafts of this entry, but its only matrix is a joint Vierstra archetype filed under ZBTB_OTHER.
families.short: This is not a motif family. It is a holding pen for small, thinly characterized factors that needed somewhere to go, and it currently holds eleven matrices for nine unrelated proteins: MSANTD1, MSANTD3 and MSANTD4, DNTTIP1, FLYWCH1, FAM200B, ELYS/AHCTF1, NACC2 and XPA. Internal cohesion is 0.47, the lowest of any group in this atlas. Two warnings about the label. The name mentions SCAN and SSX domains, but no SCAN-domain or SSX protein has a motif here; and BANP, named in the definition, is not here either - its only model sits in the other-BTB-zinc-finger bucket. XPA is the central scaffold of nucleotide excision repair, not a transcription factor. The motifs themselves are mostly well supported.
families.long:
## The factors

Nine proteins, eleven models, no shared biology; read the list, not the label, which mentions SCAN and SSX domains that are not represented.

BANP is named in the definition and is the most interesting protein in the set, but its motif is filed elsewhere. The CGCG element was for years an orphan promoter motif, enriched near the start sites of a subset of CpG-island promoters and associated with highly expressed genes; single-molecule footprinting combined with interaction proteomics identified BTG3-associated nuclear protein as its binder [PMID:34234345]. Methylation of the motif repels BANP, confining it to unmethylated CpG islands, and on binding it opens chromatin, phases nucleosomes and activates essential metabolic genes [PMID:34234345]. Structures of BEN domains later showed that oligomerization lets BANP select unmethylated CGCG [PMID:39225042]. Here that motif rides on a Vierstra archetype with a joint ZBTB/BANP label, so it went to the other-BTB-zinc-finger entry instead.

The BEN domain reaches one protein that is here: of nine human BEN-domain proteins, NACC1 prefers CATG-containing sequence [PMID:39225042], and the NACC2 model here reads ACATGC. DNTTIP1, originally TdT-interacting factor 1, is a subunit of the mitotic deacetylase complex MiDAC; its C-terminal SKI/SNO/DAC-like domain binds DNA and nucleosomes, making it a chromatin-binding module rather than an activator [PMID:25653165]. FLYWCH1 is a FLYWCH-type zinc finger studied as a suppressor of nuclear beta-catenin in colorectal cancer [PMID:30097457]. FAM200B, also called ZBED11, is transposase-derived, of the hAT/ZBED lineage with an RNase H-like fold. MSANTD1, MSANTD3 and MSANTD4 carry Myb/SANT-like DNA-binding domains and almost no documented function [PMID:29425488]. ELYS/AHCTF1 was named a transcription factor when cloned from mouse foetal haematopoietic tissue [PMID:11952839], then shown to be a nucleoporin that seeds Nup107-160 assembly and doubles as a kinetochore protein [PMID:17098863]. XPA was cloned in 1990 as an excision-repair gene "containing a zinc-finger domain" [PMID:2234061]; the 2018 census of human transcription factors nevertheless lists it because of a strong HT-SELEX motif, not because of that domain [PMID:29425488]; it is the scaffold of nucleotide excision repair and reads splayed-arm junction geometry, not sequence [PMID:27247238].

## The motif

There is no consensus: the reported CACTCAc is only the MSANTD3 medoid of eleven unrelated matrices, and cohesion is 0.47.

HOCOMOCO v14 encodes assays in the model name: P is ChIP-seq, S HT-SELEX, M methyl-HT-SELEX, G genomic HT-SELEX, I SMiLE-seq, B protein-binding microarray, and grade A means at least two assay types agreed [PMID:37971293]. Most are good on that scale. FLYWCH1 gives aTTCGAhcCGATTCGA, a 19-bit tandem TTCGA repeat, from PSGB at grade A. FAM200B gives the 13-bp palindrome TGGGTCGCGaCCC, 16 bits, PSGIB grade A, the shape a dimeric domesticated transposase should give. MSANTD4 gives acTTACTACtcg (13.8 bits, SGIB, A), MSANTD1 CACTTAAG (10.8 bits, PSGIB, A), DNTTIP1 GcatGCAC (PSG, A) and NACC2 ACATgc (PSGIB, A). Six of the seven HOCOMOCO models are grade A from up to five platforms, the assay set used by the recent systematic effort on poorly characterized human factors that produced motifs for 177 of 332 candidates [PMID:42557334]. A protein with no literature can still have a well-measured motif.

Three entries are weaker. MSANTD3 appears twice, as JASPAR MA1523.2 and CIS-BP M01259, both reading CACTCAc and both flagged as resembling the NKX homeodomain family at 0.94-0.97, so that hexamer is not separable from an NKX site. ELYS contributes AAAT, 8.5 bits, from PBM alone at grade B, with a best match outside the bucket of 0.99: an AT-rich four-mer indistinguishable from any other AT-rich model. XPA appears twice, as CIS-BP M05827 and the Vierstra archetype AC0333:XPA:Unknown, whose domain label is literally "Unknown"; neither carries an assay label here.

## Where it acts

Unmapped for almost everything here; BANP, filed elsewhere, is the exception, at unmethylated CpG-island promoters near transcription start sites, with binding lost where those promoters are aberrantly methylated in cancer [PMID:34234345]. For the rest, the systematic work on understudied factors found in vitro motifs enriched at cellular binding sites concentrated in promoters, making promoter-proximal the prior [PMID:42557334]. Scan arithmetic matters more than location: ACATGC or CACTCA is expected several hundred thousand times per strand in 3.1 Gb and AAAT tens of millions of times, so the ELYS and MSANTD3 models cannot localise anything, while FLYWCH1's or FAM200B's long matrices are genuinely rare.

## Biology and disease

XPA is the only member with a Mendelian disease of its own, and it is a repair disease: biallelic mutations cause xeroderma pigmentosum group A, with extreme ultraviolet sensitivity and, in severe alleles, neurodegeneration [PMID:2234061,27247238]. MiDAC, the complex DNTTIP1 assembles, is essential for mouse embryonic development [PMID:32591534]. MSANTD3 appears as an HTN3-MSANTD3 fusion defining a subset of salivary acinic cell carcinoma [PMID:30520817]. ELYS loss blocks nuclear pore assembly and chromosome segregation [PMID:17098863]. MSANTD1, MSANTD4, FAM200B and NACC2 have no established disease link.

## Reading a hit

Name the matrix, not the family: a hit here is on one of eleven unrelated models. Then triage. If you came for the BANP motif, it is TCTCGCGAGA on archetype AC0312:ZBTB/BANP in the other-BTB-zinc-finger entry, and it matches the ZBTB33/Kaiso archetype at 0.99, so sequence alone will not say which of the two bound - use methylation state and expression. If the hit is XPA, discard it: XPA has no sequence specificity [PMID:27247238]. If it is ELYS AAAT, discard it as AT-rich background. If it is MSANTD3 CACTCA, check the NKX entry first. If it is FLYWCH1, FAM200B, MSANTD1, MSANTD4, DNTTIP1 or NACC2, the matrix is reasonable evidence and the protein is not: treat the site as a candidate for an understudied factor, confirm the gene is expressed, and note that on structure FAM200B belongs with the ZBED entry and the MSANTD proteins with MYB.
families.caveats: This is an administrative holding pen, not a family. Eleven matrices for nine unrelated proteins, cohesion 0.47, the lowest in the atlas; there is no consensus and none should be quoted. The label misleads twice: no SCAN-domain or SSX protein has a motif here, and BANP, named in the definition, has its only model filed under other BTB-zinc-fingers as the joint ZBTB/BANP archetype. XPA is a nucleotide excision repair scaffold that binds DNA by shape, so its two models should not be scanned at all, and the ELYS model is a PBM-only AT-rich four-mer. Conversely, do not dismiss the whole group: six of the seven HOCOMOCO models are grade A from several independent assay platforms.

timeline.finding: Human and mouse XPAC cDNAs are cloned by complementing the ultraviolet sensitivity of xeroderma pigmentosum group A cells; the 273-residue human protein carries a zinc-finger motif.
timeline.methods: cDNA cloning, complementation of UV sensitivity, mRNA analysis of patient cell lines
timeline.open: Whether the zinc finger conferred any DNA sequence preference was not addressed.

timeline.finding: ELYS is cloned from mouse embryonic haematopoietic tissue and described as a nuclear transcription factor, on the strength of a predicted AT-hook DNA-binding domain, nuclear localization signals and transcriptional activity of GAL4-fusion constructs.
timeline.methods: cDNA cloning, expression analysis, GAL4-fusion reporter assays
timeline.open: The transcription-factor label rested on domain prediction and fusion assays rather than on a mapped binding site or target gene.

timeline.finding: ELYS copurifies with the Nup107-160 complex in Xenopus and human extracts, localizes to nuclear pores and, at mitosis, to kinetochores, and is required for nuclear pore assembly. The putative transcription factor is recast as a nucleoporin.
timeline.methods: Immunoprecipitation and mass spectrometry, immunofluorescence, RNAi

timeline.finding: NACC2, reported under the name RBB, is described as a BTB- and BEN-domain transcriptional repressor that binds a specific DNA motif as a homodimer, interacts with the NuRD complex and represses HDM2 from its internal promoter.
timeline.methods: SELEX, ChIP-seq, protein interaction and reporter assays

timeline.finding: Crystal structures of two DNTTIP1 domains show an N-terminal dimerization domain of a new fold that assembles the HDAC1:MIDEAS complex, and a C-terminal domain related to SKI/SNO/DAC that binds DNA and nucleosomes. DNTTIP1 is a dimeric chromatin-binding module of MiDAC, not a classical activator.
timeline.methods: X-ray crystallography, DNA and nucleosome binding assays
timeline.open: How MiDAC is directed to particular loci was not established.

timeline.finding: The human transcription factor census keeps XPA as a transcription factor with a known motif, noting that it functions in DNA repair but has a strong HT-SELEX-derived motif. It lists DNTTIP1, ELYS/AHCTF1, FAM200B, FLYWCH1, MSANTD1, MSANTD4 and NACC2 as likely sequence-specific factors with no motif, and comments that MSANTD4, with a single Myb-like domain, is likely non-specific.
timeline.methods: Expert curation of candidate transcription factors
timeline.open: Why a repair scaffold yields a strong HT-SELEX motif was not explained.

timeline.finding: The Codebook effort assays 332 putative and poorly characterized human transcription factors in more than 4,000 experiments on multiple in vitro and in vivo platforms and obtains motifs for 177, most tied to a single protein. In vitro motifs are strongly enriched at cellular binding sites concentrated in promoters. Six of the seven HOCOMOCO models in this bucket carry grade-A, multi-platform evidence of this kind, among them a 13.8-bit model for MSANTD4, the protein the census had expected to bind non-specifically.
timeline.methods: HT-SELEX, genomic HT-SELEX, SMiLE-seq, protein-binding microarrays and ChIP-seq, cross-validated
timeline.open: Nearly half of the 332 targets still yielded no motif.

open: Why XPA has a strong sequence motif is unexplained. The repair literature describes a scaffold that recognizes damaged-DNA junction geometry rather than sequence, yet HT-SELEX gave it a 10-bit TGTGAGGTG matrix that CIS-BP and a Vierstra archetype carry, and the human transcription factor census kept it as a transcription factor on the strength of that motif.

NACC2's specificity is inconsistent across sources. The 2013 description of NACC2 as RBB reported a homodimer-bound SELEX motif, which the human transcription factor census records as TGTCRSWWYYGWC, whereas the grade-A HOCOMOCO model reads ACATGC, in line with the CATG preference of the BEN domain of its paralogue NACC1; the work cited here does not reconcile the two.

Whether MSANTD3 has a specificity of its own is unresolved. Both of its models read CACTCA and match NKX homeodomain models at 0.94-0.97, and unlike MSANTD1 and MSANTD4 it has no multi-platform HOCOMOCO model against which to check them.

families.name: EBF / COE
families.def: Palindromic Olf-1/EBF site TCCCNNGGGA, read by a Rel-like DNA-binding domain with a zinc knuckle rather than by a bHLH. EBF1-4 (COE1-3).
families.short: EBF1-EBF4 (COE1-COE4, also Olf-1 and O/E-1 to O/E-3) bind a 10-base palindrome, TCCCNNGGGA, as homodimers. Despite being filed with the bHLH proteins, their DNA-binding domain is a pseudo-immunoglobulin fold structurally similar to the Rel homology domains of NF-κB and NFAT, contacting DNA through two loops and a unique zinc-coordination motif, with each subunit reaching across both half-sites; the HLH they carry is used for dimerisation, not DNA contact. EBF1 is required at the earliest committed step of B-lymphocyte development and shows pioneer-like activity on closed chromatin; EBF2 establishes brown adipocyte identity; de novo EBF3 variants cause a hypotonia-ataxia-developmental-delay syndrome. The motif is long enough that scans for it are relatively clean.
families.long:
## The factors

EBF1, EBF2, EBF3 and EBF4 — also called COE1-COE4, and in the olfactory literature Olf-1 and O/E-1 to O/E-3 — make up the vertebrate COE (Collier/Olf-1/EBF) family. They were discovered twice in the same year: EBF1 as a regulator of the B-cell-specific *mb-1*/*Cd79a* promoter, and Olf-1 as the factor binding a conserved element in olfactory neuron gene promoters [PMID:8491377,8321284]. The family is conventionally filed with the bHLH proteins, and the atlas inherits that placement, but structurally it is not one. Crystallography shows that the EBF DNA-binding domain adopts a pseudo-immunoglobulin fold with novel topology that is structurally similar to the Rel homology domains of NF-κB and NFAT, and that it contacts DNA through two loop-based modules plus a unique zinc-coordination motif, the "zinc knuckle", with each monomer reaching across to touch both halves of the palindrome [PMID:20876732]. Biochemistry had already identified that zinc motif and multiple dimerisation and activation domains [PMID:7796816]. The proteins also carry an IPT/TIG domain and an atypical helix-loop-helix with its own novel dimerisation motif — an HLH used for dimerisation, not for DNA contact [PMID:20592035]. The Vierstra archetype covering this family is named `AC0500:EBF:Rel_homology_region_(RHR)_factors`, which reflects the structure better than the bHLH label does. EBF1 acts in B lymphocytes, olfactory neurons, adipocytes, striatal neurons and osteoblasts; EBF2 in brown adipocytes, olfactory epithelium and cerebellum; EBF3 broadly in the central nervous system; EBF4 is the least characterised. They function as homodimers and can heterodimerise with each other.

## The motif

The site is a 10-base palindrome, TCCCNNGGGA: two inverted TCCC half-sites separated by two degenerate positions [PMID:8491377]. The databases' versions fill those central positions in slightly different ways — HOCOMOCO EBF1 reads TCCCCTGGGA, HOCOMOCO EBF3 and JASPAR EBF1 read TCCCCAGGGA/TCCCCAGGGGA, the CIS-BP EBF1 model reads AKTCCCTWGGGAAT with extended flanks — but they are all the same element, and the representative model is the archetype consensus TCCCTGGGGA. Because the palindrome is read symmetrically by a dimer, with each subunit contacting both half-sites, the two central bases are the tolerant ones and the TCCC/GGGA blocks are essentially invariant [PMID:20876732].

Two practical consequences follow. First, this is an information-rich motif by the standards of a transcription factor site: eight effectively fixed positions rather than the four or five of an E-box. An exact TCCCNNGGGA is expected around 47,000 times in a 3.1-Gb genome, and because the pattern is its own reverse complement that count is not doubled — roughly one site per 65 kb, against roughly one per 4 kb for a six-mer. Scans for this motif are correspondingly cleaner. Second, the motif resembles nothing else in the atlas: the best match of any member to a motif outside the family is 0.93 and typically much lower, while within-family similarities run 0.91-1.00 (cohesion 0.91). The four paralogues are completely indistinguishable from sequence.

One provenance note: the CIS-BP EBF2 model `M03721_2.00` is inherited from a *Drosophila melanogaster* protein (Collier/Knot) at 91% DNA-binding-domain identity. Because COE proteins are deeply conserved and the fly motif (AATTCCCTAGGGAATT) matches the human models closely, this transfer is benign, but it is a transfer.

## Where it acts

EBF1 in B cells binds thousands of sites, mostly at enhancers of the B-lineage programme — *Cd79a*, *Pax5*, *Cd19*, *Igll1*, *Vpreb*, *Blnk*, *Foxo1* — and acts by activation, by repression, and by a transcription-independent poising of chromatin at genes that only become active later [PMID:20451411]. Its C-terminal domain confers pioneer-like activity, letting EBF1 engage closed and nucleosomal chromatin and open it for subsequent factors, which is unusual and consistent with the extended DNA contact area seen in the structure [PMID:26982363]. In B cells EBF1 sites co-occur with E2A/TCF3, PAX5, FOXO1 and RUNX1 motifs. In brown fat, EBF2 occupies and activates the PPARG/PRDM16 thermogenic enhancer programme [PMID:23499423]. In olfactory sensory neurons the same element sits in promoters of olfactory marker and signalling genes [PMID:8321284].

## Biology and disease

*Ebf1*-null mice arrest B-cell development before the pro-B stage, with no immunoglobulin heavy-chain DJ rearrangement — EBF1 is required at the earliest committed step of the B lineage [PMID:7542362]. EBF2 is required to establish and maintain brown adipocyte identity, and forced EBF2 expression imposes a brown-fat programme [PMID:23499423]. In human genetics, de novo variants in *EBF3*, largely missense changes in the DNA-binding domain, cause a neurodevelopmental syndrome with hypotonia, ataxia, developmental delay and expressive language impairment, reported independently by two groups in the same issue; the mutations reduce DNA binding and transactivation, consistent with a dominant-negative or haploinsufficient mechanism [PMID:28017372,28017370].

## Reading a hit

Because the site is long, palindromic and unlike any other family's, a TCCCNNGGGA hit is unusually trustworthy at the family level: if you find a good match, EBF-family binding is a reasonable hypothesis. What it will not tell you is which EBF, since all four share the motif, and in most tissues only one or two are expressed, so expression data resolve the question that sequence cannot. Two cautions. All three HOCOMOCO models here are ChIP-derived (evidence letter `P`, grade B), so the in vitro support for the recognition sequence comes from the original biochemistry and the crystal structure rather than from SELEX models in the current collection. And the family label "bHLH" is misleading: EBF has an HLH, but it is a dimerisation module, and an E-box search will neither find EBF sites nor be found by them.
families.caveats: The site is long, palindromic and unlike any other family's, so a good match is reasonable evidence for EBF-family binding — unusual in this atlas. It is no evidence at all about which EBF: all four paralogues share one motif (cohesion 0.91) and only expression can separate them. All three HOCOMOCO models here are ChIP-derived (evidence letter P, grade B), so the sequence preference rests on the original biochemistry and the crystal structure rather than on in vitro models in the current collection. One CIS-BP EBF2 model is inherited from a Drosophila protein at 91% domain identity, which is benign but is a transfer. The "bHLH" class label is structurally wrong; do not expect E-box searches to find these sites.

timeline.finding: The same factor is cloned twice in one year from unrelated tissues: EBF as the regulator of the B-cell-specific mb-1/Cd79a promoter, and Olf-1 as the protein binding a conserved element in olfactory neuron gene promoters, both reading a palindromic TCCC...GGGA site.
timeline.methods: biochemical purification and cloning; yeast genetic selection
timeline.open: How a protein with no recognisable DNA-binding fold of a known class reads that palindrome.

timeline.finding: Protein dissection identifies a novel zinc-coordination motif required for DNA binding plus separate dimerization and activation domains, and the Ebf-null mouse shows B-cell development arrested before the pro-B stage with no immunoglobulin heavy-chain DJ rearrangement.
timeline.methods: deletion and mutagenesis biochemistry; mouse gene targeting

timeline.finding: Two structural studies show the EBF DNA-binding domain is a pseudo-immunoglobulin fold structurally similar to the Rel homology domains of NF-kB and NFAT, binding DNA through two loop modules and a zinc knuckle with each monomer contacting both halves of the palindrome, and that the atypical HLH serves dimerization rather than DNA contact — the family's bHLH label is structurally wrong.
timeline.methods: X-ray crystallography of an Ebf1:DNA complex and of isolated domains

timeline.finding: Genome-wide analysis in B cells shows Ebf1 acts by activation, by repression, and by a transcription-independent poising of chromatin at genes expressed only at later stages; the poising works in T cells but not in fibroblasts, so the pioneer-like behaviour is context dependent.
timeline.methods: ChIP-seq, expression profiling and ectopic expression in several cell types
timeline.open: What limits the poising activity to a haematopoietic chromatin context.

timeline.finding: EBF2 is shown to determine and maintain brown adipocyte identity by occupying and activating the PPARG/PRDM16 thermogenic enhancer programme, extending the family well beyond lymphocytes and olfactory neurons.
timeline.methods: ChIP-seq, knockdown and ectopic expression in adipocytes

timeline.finding: The pioneering activity is mapped to the EBF1 C-terminal domain, which is required for de novo gain of chromatin accessibility at a specific target set independently of the protein's activation and repression functions.
timeline.methods: domain deletion with ATAC-seq and ChIP-seq in B-cell progenitors
timeline.open: Whether the C-terminal domain engages nucleosomal DNA directly or recruits remodelling activity.

timeline.finding: Two groups report in the same issue that de novo EBF3 variants, mostly missense changes at conserved DNA-binding residues including the zinc motif, cause a neurodevelopmental syndrome with hypotonia, ataxia and expressive language impairment, and reduce DNA binding and transactivation.
timeline.methods: trio exome sequencing with binding and reporter assays; structural modelling
timeline.open: Whether the variants act by haploinsufficiency or dominant-negatively through mixed dimers was not settled.

open: No comparative in vitro measurement separates EBF1, EBF2, EBF3 and EBF4: their models are near-identical, every HOCOMOCO model here is ChIP-derived, and whether the paralogues differ at all in sequence preference or only in expression domain is untested.

The two central positions of TCCCNNGGGA are filled differently by different databases (TCCCCTGGGA in HOCOMOCO EBF1, TCCCCAGGGA in EBF3 and JASPAR EBF1), and whether those bases carry a real, measurable preference or are genuinely unconstrained has not been resolved.

How EBF1 opens closed chromatin is unknown: the activity maps to the C-terminal domain and works in haematopoietic and T-cell but not fibroblast chromatin, leaving open whether the domain engages nucleosomal DNA directly or depends on a lineage-restricted cofactor.

Whether pathogenic EBF3 variants act by haploinsufficiency or as dominant negatives through heterodimers with wild-type EBF3 and other COE proteins is unresolved, and the two mechanisms predict different consequences for occupancy at the palindromic site.

families.name: Estrogen-related receptors
families.def: ERRE TNAAGGTCA extended half-site. ESRRA, ESRRB, ESRRG.
families.short: The estrogen-related receptors ERRalpha (ESRRA), ERRbeta (ESRRB) and ERRgamma (ESRRG) are orphan nuclear receptors with no established natural ligand; their activity is set by coactivators such as PGC-1alpha rather than by a hormone. Unlike most nuclear receptors they bind DNA as monomers, on a single AGGTCA half-site carrying a three-base 5' extension: TNAAGGTCA, usually seen as TCAAGGTCA. The extension is read by a C-terminal extension of the DNA-binding domain in the minor groove, and it is what allows a monomer to bind with high affinity. The three paralogues share one motif and are not distinguishable from sequence. ERR sites sit at nuclear-encoded mitochondrial and oxidative-metabolism genes, at pluripotency enhancers, and in the placenta and inner ear.
families.long:
## The factors

Three paralogues make up subfamily NR3B: ESRRA (ERRalpha, NR3B1), ESRRB (ERRbeta, NR3B2) and ESRRG (ERRgamma, NR3B3). They were found by homology to the estrogen receptor but are not activated by estradiol; no endogenous ligand is established, the ligand-binding pocket is small and largely filled, and transcriptional output is controlled by coactivator availability, chiefly PGC-1alpha and PGC-1beta (Giguere 2008) [PMID:18664618]. Architecturally they resemble other nuclear receptors - a C4 double-zinc-finger DNA-binding domain (DBD) and a ligand-binding domain - but they bind DNA as monomers [PMID:12654265], and can also homodimerize. ERRalpha is broadly expressed with highest levels in heart, kidney, skeletal muscle and brown adipose tissue [PMID:9271417]; ERRgamma is enriched in heart, brain and kidney; ERRbeta is the most restricted, appearing in extraembryonic ectoderm and trophoblast, the inner ear and pluripotent stem cells [PMID:9285590,18179891,23040477]. Ten motif models fall here (JASPAR 3, HOCOMOCO 3, CIS-BP 3, Vierstra 1), covering all three genes.

## The motif

The ERR response element is an extended half-site, not a repeat. Binding-site selection with ERRalpha defined it as TNAAGGTCA: the canonical nuclear receptor hexamer AGGTCA preceded by three bases, of which the two immediately 5' are almost always AA (Sladek et al. 1997) [PMID:9271417]. In practice the models here read TCAAGGTCA or CAAGGTCA, and the family's data consensus is CAAGGTCA.

The 5' extension is functional, not decorative. The solution structure of the ERRbeta DBD bound to its site showed that monomeric high-affinity binding requires base-specific minor-groove contacts from a modified guanosine-binding AT-hook in the C-terminal extension (CTE) that flanks the core DBD; the CTE is stabilized by packing against the DBD surface that other receptors use for dimerization, a pseudo-dimer interface (Gearhart et al. 2003) [PMID:12654265]. That is the structural reason why ERRs need three extra 5' bases while a GR or ER dimer needs a second hexamer instead. Dimeric arrangements do occur: the CIS-BP ESRRG model M03412 is two extended half-sites in tandem (AAGGTCAttTcAAGGTCA), the highest-information model in the family at 22 bits.

Spacing and orientation are what separate this family from its neighbours, and they separate it imperfectly. An inverted AGGTCA repeat with a 3 bp spacer is an ERE; direct repeats with 1-5 bp spacers are RXR-heterodimer elements; a single 5'-extended half-site is an ERR element - but it is also the SF-1/LRH-1 response element (SFRE), and the Vierstra archetype in this family is labelled ESRRA/NR5A for exactly that reason. ERRalpha and ERRbeta also bind and activate through consensus EREs, while ERbeta does not reciprocate (Vanacker et al. 1999) [PMID:10428965]. The family data marks one CIS-BP model labelled ESRRA (M07988) as a full ERE belonging with ESR. ESRRA, ESRRB and ESRRG themselves are indistinguishable: their models are 0.96-0.99 similar to one another.

## Where it acts

ERR sites are found at both promoters and distal enhancers, with a strong bias towards nuclear-encoded mitochondrial genes: oxidative phosphorylation subunits, TCA cycle enzymes and fatty-acid beta-oxidation genes, where ERRalpha works with PGC-1alpha [PMID:15100410,18664618]. The founding example was an ERRE in the promoter of the medium-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase gene (Sladek et al. 1997) [PMID:9271417]. Genome-wide mapping in heart showed ERRalpha and ERRgamma occupying an overlapping program of cardiac metabolic and contractile genes (Dufour et al. 2007) [PMID:17488637]. At such promoters ERR elements co-occur with NRF1 [PMID:17488637], GABPA [PMID:15100410] and YY1 sites. In mouse embryonic stem cells Esrrb sits at pluripotency enhancers with OCT4, SOX2 and NANOG, and is itself a direct Nanog target that can substitute for Nanog (Festuccia et al. 2012) [PMID:23040477].

## Biology and disease

The ERRs are best understood as regulators of oxidative capacity. Esrra-null mice are lean, resistant to diet-induced obesity and impaired in cold adaptation; ERRalpha and ERRgamma together are required for the perinatal switch of the heart to fatty-acid oxidation [PMID:18664618]. Esrrb-null embryos die from placental failure with abnormal chorion development (Luo et al. 1997) [PMID:9285590]. In humans, recessive ESRRB mutations cause nonsyndromic hearing loss DFNB35 (Collin et al. 2008) [PMID:18179891]. ERRalpha expression is associated with poor outcome in breast cancer, where it supports the metabolic and biosynthetic demands of proliferation and interacts with ERBB2 signalling (Deblois and Giguere 2013) [PMID:23192231]. ERRgamma has been studied in prostate cancer and hepatic gluconeogenesis, and inverse agonists of ERRalpha are in preclinical development.

## Reading a hit

The practical warning is length. TCAAGGTCA is a 9-mer with roughly eight informative positions, so an exact match occurs on the order of 10^4 times in the haploid human genome by chance alone, and near-matches many times more. A hit therefore carries very little weight on its own, and far less than a 13-15 bp dimeric element would. Measure the 5' extension explicitly: without the AA at positions -2 and -3 you have a bare half-site that anything in the superfamily could touch, and with an inverted second hexamer three bases downstream you have an ERE instead. A match cannot distinguish ESRRA, ESRRB and ESRRG, nor reliably distinguish ERRs from NR5A1/NR5A2, whose element is the same 9-mer. All three HOCOMOCO models here are grade A with combined ChIP, HT-SELEX and methyl-SELEX evidence (PSM), so direct binding to this sequence is well supported; the uncertainty is about which family member and which site is used, not about the sequence.
families.caveats: The ERR element is a 9 bp extended half-site, which is short: expect on the order of 10^4 chance matches per haploid genome, so a hit alone is weak evidence. It does not distinguish ESRRA, ESRRB and ESRRG, whose models are 0.96-0.99 similar, and it does not distinguish ERRs from NR5A1/NR5A2, which use the same TCAAGGTCA element - the Vierstra archetype here is labelled ESRRA/NR5A. Cross-recognition with the estrogen receptor is real, not just a labelling artefact: ERRs activate through consensus EREs, and one CIS-BP model labelled ESRRA in this family is a full ERE flagged as belonging with ESR. Require the 5' AA extension before calling an ERR site.
