families.name: NR5A (SF-1 / LRH-1)
families.def: SF-1 response element (T)CAAGGTCA. NR5A1, NR5A2.
families.short: NR5A1 (steroidogenic factor 1, SF-1) and NR5A2 (liver receptor homolog 1, LRH-1) are the mammalian relatives of Drosophila FTZ-F1. Like the NR4A receptors they bind DNA as monomers rather than dimers, occupying one AGGTCA half-site plus a short 5' extension read by a separate protein surface called the A box, which gives the nine-base SF-1 response element TCAAGGTCA. NR5A1 drives adrenal and gonadal development and the steroidogenic enzyme genes; NR5A2 works in liver, pancreas, intestine and the early embryo. The two proteins have indistinguishable motifs but almost non-overlapping tissue distributions, so cell type, not sequence, tells them apart. The element differs from the NR4A site at a single base and is contained inside the NR6A1 direct repeat.
families.long:
## The factors

The subfamily has two human members: NR5A1 (SF-1, Ad4BP, STF-1, ELP) and NR5A2 (LRH-1, FTF, CPF, hB1F), both mammalian homologs of the Drosophila regulator FTZ-F1 (Lala et al. 1992) [PMID:1406703]. Their DNA-binding domain is the usual pair of C4 zinc modules plus a carboxy-terminal extension carrying the A box, or FTZ-F1 box, and a terminal helix required for a stable complex on DNA (Little et al. 2006) [PMID:16339274]. The ligand-binding domain has a large hydrophobic pocket: crystal structures identify bound phosphatidylinositols, making these receptors phospholipid sensors rather than true orphans (Krylova et al. 2005) [PMID:15707893], although LRH-1 adopts an active conformation with the pocket essentially empty (Sablin et al. 2003) [PMID:12820970]. The paralogues occupy largely non-overlapping tissues: NR5A1 in adrenal cortex, gonadal somatic cells, pituitary gonadotropes, spleen and ventromedial hypothalamus; NR5A2 in liver, pancreas, intestine and the preimplantation embryo. Six motifs are collected here, two each from JASPAR, HOCOMOCO and CIS-BP; HOCOMOCO files the NR5A1 model under the symbol STF1.

## The motif

The element is usually written (T)CAAGGTCA, the SF-1 response element or SFRE: one AGGTCA half-site with a short 5' extension, bound by a single receptor molecule. Domain swaps placed SF-1 and NGFI-B (NR4A1) in the same monomeric paradigm, zinc modules on the half-site and A box in the minor groove 5' of it; the SF-1 sequence requires an amino group in the minor groove and the SF-1 A box supplies an asparagine (Wilson et al. 1993) [PMID:8395013]. The consequence for sequence analysis is stark: the NR4A element is AAAGGTCA and the NR5A element is CAAGGTCA, a difference of one base. The collected models are tight: both HOCOMOCO models, STF1.H14CORE.0.PSM.A and NR5A2.H14CORE.0.PSM.A, are tCAAGGtCA and the CIS-BP NR5A1 model is CAAGGtCA, so the paralogues cannot be separated by sequence. Three entries need care. JASPAR Nr5A2 (MA0505.3) is written TGACCTTGA, the reverse complement of TCAAGGTCA and so the same element on the other strand. CIS-BP M05589_2.00 is TCAAGGTCATGACCTTGA, 21 bits, a head-to-head pair of SF-1 elements with no spacer; its best within-family similarity is only 0.71, so it is an outlier. And JASPAR NR5A1 (MA1540.3) is the 12-mer AGTTCAAGGTCA, which can be read either as the SF-1 element with an extended 5' flank or as a DR0 pair of AGTTCA and AGGTCA half-sites. That ambiguity is real rather than an artifact: the DR0 bound by NR6A1 is AAGTTCAAGGTCA, and its 3' nine bases are exactly the SF-1 element, so every NR6A1 site contains an SFRE match.

## Where it acts

SF-1 sites sit in promoters of the steroidogenic machinery, including STAR, CYP11A1, CYP17A1, CYP19A1 and HSD3B2, and of hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal genes such as INHA, MC2R and NR0B1/DAX1; SF-1 cooperates with SOX9 at the anti-Mullerian hormone promoter and is antagonized by DAX-1, which binds the protein rather than DNA (Ferraz-de-Souza et al. 2011) [PMID:21078366]. LRH-1 acts on bile acid and cholesterol genes such as CYP7A1, CYP8B1 and NR0B2/SHP and on pancreatic and intestinal programs. An eight- to nine-base element is expected tens of thousands of times in a mammalian genome, so almost every match lies in a cell expressing neither receptor. Cell type is the strongest filter here, and an unusually effective one: the two cistromes barely overlap because the tissues do not.

## Biology and disease

Sf1-null mice lack adrenal glands and gonads entirely, undergo male-to-female sex reversal and have an abnormal ventromedial hypothalamus (Luo et al. 1994) [PMID:8187173]. The first reported human NR5A1 mutation was a heterozygous DNA-binding-domain change causing 46,XY sex reversal with adrenal failure (Achermann et al. 1999) [PMID:10369247]; the spectrum now includes 46,XY differences of sex development without adrenal insufficiency, hypospadias, male infertility and primary ovarian insufficiency (Ferraz-de-Souza et al. 2011) [PMID:21078366]. SF-1 is overexpressed, and the gene amplified, in adrenocortical tumors, more frequently in children than in adults (Almeida et al. 2010) [PMID:20080844]. Mouse embryos lacking Nr5a2 die early with defects in cholesterol homeostasis (Pare et al. 2004) [PMID:15014077], and common variants at NR5A2 on 1q32.1 are an established pancreatic cancer susceptibility signal (Petersen et al. 2010) [PMID:20101243].

## Reading a hit

A monomeric half-site is much harder to call than a spaced dimer. A DR3, DR4 or DR5 element constrains two half-sites plus a defined spacer, 13-15 positions, and the arrangement is itself evidence; the SFRE constrains eight or nine positions, six of which are the AGGTCA half-site shared across the nuclear receptor superfamily, leaving two or three bases of family-level information and no spacer to check. One substitution turns an SFRE into an NR4A NBRE, and any NR6A1 DR0 contains an SFRE, so a hit may belong to a different family or be one half of a genuine dimeric site. Prediction improves substantially when dimer configuration can be modeled, which is not possible here (Sandelin and Wasserman 2005) [PMID:15563547]. The sequence evidence is strong: both HOCOMOCO models are grade A with ChIP-seq, HT-SELEX and methyl-HT-SELEX support, so TCAAGGTCA is well supported as directly bound, unlike the ChIP-only models common elsewhere in this atlas. What a hit cannot do is name the receptor. Use expression: outside adrenal, gonad, gonadotrope and hypothalamus an SF-1 call is implausible, as is an LRH-1 call outside liver, pancreas, intestine and early embryo. Note also that databases report this element on either strand, as TCAAGGTCA or TGACCTTGA.
families.caveats: The motif is well measured but weakly diagnostic. Both HOCOMOCO models carry grade-A in vitro support, so TCAAGGTCA really is bound directly, yet it constrains only eight or nine positions, six of them the AGGTCA half-site used across the nuclear receptor superfamily. One substitution converts it into the NR4A element AAAGGTCA, and every NR6A1 DR0 contains an exact SFRE, so family assignment from sequence alone is unreliable. NR5A1 and NR5A2 have identical motifs; only tissue distinguishes them, which in practice works well because their expression barely overlaps. Watch for presentation differences across databases: one JASPAR model is the reverse complement, one CIS-BP model is a head-to-head pair of elements, and HOCOMOCO files NR5A1 under the symbol STF1.

open: Whether the phospholipids found in the NR5A ligand pocket act as regulatory signals or merely as structural occupants is unresolved: crystal structures identify bound phosphatidylinositols, yet LRH-1 adopts an active conformation with the pocket essentially empty.

Whether NR5A1 and NR5A2 differ in DNA preference at all is untested at the resolution that would matter; the grade-A models for the two proteins are the same nine-base element, so any difference would have to lie in flanking positions that no current model resolves.

How to read the 12-mer AGTTCAAGGTCA is genuinely ambiguous: it can be taken as the SF-1 element with an extended 5' flank or as a DR0 pair of half-sites, and because the NR6A1 direct repeat contains an exact SFRE, sequence alone cannot assign such a match to one family.

It is unclear whether the head-to-head pair of SF-1 elements in the CIS-BP model M05589_2.00 reflects cooperative occupancy by two receptor molecules or an artifact of motif discovery on sequences containing two independent sites.

families.name: NR6A1 (GCNF)
families.def: DR0 direct repeat TCAAGGTCA. NR6A1.
families.short: NR6A1, better known as germ cell nuclear factor (GCNF), is the only mammalian member of nuclear receptor subfamily 6: one gene with no paralogue. It binds a DR0, two nuclear receptor half-sites in direct repeat with no intervening bases, and it does so as a homodimer without an RXR partner. That makes it the odd one out among the orphan receptors here, because a two-half-site element of 13 to 15 base pairs is far more specific than a monomeric half-site. Its best-characterized job is repressing the pluripotency gene Oct4 during differentiation, which it does by recruiting methyl-CpG-binding proteins and DNA methyltransferases. Mouse mutants show posterior truncation, the gene underlies a vertebral-number locus in pigs, and human variants cause an oculo-vertebral-renal syndrome.
families.long:
## The factors

NR6A1 was cloned as GCNF, germ cell nuclear factor, from developing germ cells and is also called RTR (Chen et al. 1994) [PMID:7854358]. It is the sole mammalian member of nuclear receptor subfamily 6, so unlike most families here it has no paralogue to be confused with; zebrafish carries two copies (Neelathi et al. 2025) [PMID:40610405]. The protein has the standard layout: a DNA-binding domain of two C4 zinc modules with a carboxy-terminal extension, then a ligand-binding domain with no established ligand. It behaves predominantly as a repressor, recruiting methyl-CpG-binding domain proteins and DNA methyltransferases at its best-studied target (Gu et al. 2011) [PMID:21608077]. Expression is developmentally restricted: germ cells during spermatogenesis and oogenesis, the early post-implantation embryo, embryonic stem cells and parts of the developing nervous system, with little in adult tissue. Six motifs are collected here from all four sources, all labeled NR6A1; the family is the most internally consistent of the orphan receptor groups.

## The motif

The element is a DR0: two nuclear receptor half-sites arranged as a direct repeat with zero intervening bases. In vitro translated GCNF binds autonomously to a direct repeat of AGGTCA; sequences beyond the core DNA-binding domain are needed for specific binding; antibody-shift experiments place two GCNF molecules on one repeat, so the complex is a homodimer; and no RXR interaction is detectable (Borgmeyer 1997) [PMID:9063454]. That homodimeric, two-half-site mode separates NR6A1 from NR4A and NR5A, which bind a single extended half-site as monomers (Wilson et al. 1993) [PMID:8395013]. The collected models agree closely. Four of the six, from HOCOMOCO, JASPAR, CIS-BP and the Vierstra archetypes, converge on AAGTTCAAGGTCA or the longer TCAAGTTCAAGGTCA at 15 to 20 bits. One detail is worth stating rather than smoothing over: the measured upstream half-site is the AGTTCA variant, not AGGTCA, so the data consensus AAGtTCAAGgTCA differs from the textbook description of a direct repeat of AGGTCA. The architecture is the same; the databases capture which variant of the upstream half-site is preferred. Two further points matter for scanning. The 3' nine bases, TCAAGGTCA, are exactly the NR5A/SF-1 response element, so every genuine NR6A1 site contains an exact SF-1 match. And one of the two ChIP-only HOCOMOCO models, NR6A1.H14CORE.1.P.C, is nothing more than tCAAGgtCA, a bare half-site indistinguishable from the NR5A motif; the other, NR6A1.H14CORE.0.P.C, is a degenerate aAggtCAAGgtCA.

## Where it acts

The best-characterized site is a DR0 in the proximal promoter of Oct4 (POU5F1). GCNF restricts Oct4 to the germline in the mouse embryo (Fuhrmann et al. 2001) [PMID:11702949], is required to repress Oct4 and other pluripotency genes when embryonic stem cells differentiate in response to retinoic acid (Gu et al. 2005) [PMID:16166633], and initiates promoter DNA methylation there by recruiting MBD proteins and DNMTs (Gu et al. 2011) [PMID:21608077]. Occupancy is developmentally gated and largely absent from adult tissue. The element's length changes the arithmetic: a specific 13-mer is expected only about 50 times per strand in a 3-Gb genome, against roughly 47,000 for a specific eight-mer, so a full DR0 match is genuinely rare and the limiting question becomes whether NR6A1 is expressed rather than whether the match is chance.

## Biology and disease

Mouse embryos lacking Gcnf develop an ectopic tail bud and a posterior truncation (Chung et al. 2001) [PMID:11134352] and fail to silence Oct4 outside the germline (Fuhrmann et al. 2001) [PMID:11702949]. In domestic pigs, NR6A1 underlies a major quantitative trait locus for the number of vertebrae (Mikawa et al. 2007) [PMID:17416745]. In humans, rare heterozygous NR6A1 variants in six families cause an autosomal dominant oculo-vertebral-renal syndrome of colobomatous microphthalmia, missing vertebrae and congenital kidney abnormalities; knockdown of either or both zebrafish paralogues gives abnormal eye, kidney and somite development, rescued by wild-type but not variant mRNA (Neelathi et al. 2025) [PMID:40610405]. The vertebral phenotype in both pig and human is consistent with a role in somitogenesis.

## Reading a hit

This family is the encouraging case among the orphan receptors, but only if the hit came from the right model. A match to the full 13- to 15-base DR0 is informative: the pattern is long enough that chance occurrences are rare, and the strongest model, NR6A1.H14CORE.2.SM.B, has HT-SELEX and methyl-HT-SELEX support at grade B [PMID:37971293], so it is in vitro evidence of direct binding rather than mere occupancy. A match to the two ChIP-only grade-C models is different: one is a bare nuclear receptor half-site and should be reported as such, not as NR6A1. Always check which model produced the hit. Two confusions follow from the sequence. Because the DR0 contains an exact SF-1 element, NR5A scanners will score NR6A1 sites, and a hit that looks like NR5A inside a longer direct repeat may be NR6A1. And a DR0 is not unique to NR6A1: the NR2F/COUP-TF group and RXR heterodimers also bind direct repeats with short spacers, so the arrangement narrows the candidates without naming one. Prediction of nuclear receptor elements is much better when the dimer configuration can be modeled, which here it can (Sandelin and Wasserman 2005) [PMID:15563547]. The Vierstra entry AC0133:NR6A is a footprint archetype named after the factor group whose motifs clustered together (Vierstra et al. 2020) [PMID:32728250]. Expression is the practical gate: outside germ cells, early embryos and stem cell models, an NR6A1 call needs independent support.
families.caveats: The full DR0 is long enough to be reasonably specific, and the strongest model has in vitro support, so a good 13- to 15-base match is more trustworthy than most nuclear receptor hits. The risk is model choice: two of the six collected models are ChIP-only at grade C, and one of those is just the nine-base half-site tCAAGgtCA, which is identical to the NR5A/SF-1 element. Hits from that model say nothing specific about NR6A1. Conversely, every real NR6A1 site contains an exact SF-1 match, so the two families cross-annotate each other. A direct repeat is not unique to NR6A1 either, since NR2F/COUP-TF and RXR heterodimers also read closely spaced repeats. Note finally that the measured upstream half-site is AGTTCA rather than the textbook AGGTCA, and that expression is confined largely to germ cells and early embryos.

timeline.finding: GCNF was cloned from developing germ cells as an orphan receptor with no close mammalian relative, establishing nuclear receptor subfamily 6 as a single-gene group.
timeline.methods: Molecular cloning with expression analysis in germ cells
timeline.open: Neither a ligand nor a response element was known.

timeline.finding: In vitro translated GCNF was shown to bind a direct repeat of AGGTCA with no spacer, with two molecules placed on one repeat by antibody shift and no detectable RXR interaction, making this a homodimeric DR0-binding receptor rather than a monomer or an RXR partner.
timeline.methods: Gel-shift with antibody supershift and deletion constructs

timeline.finding: Gcnf-null mouse embryos were found to develop an ectopic tail bud and a posterior truncation, giving the receptor a role in axial development well outside the germ cell compartment it was named for.
timeline.methods: Mouse germline knockout with embryological analysis

timeline.finding: GCNF was shown to restrict Oct4 expression to the germline in the mouse embryo, identifying the pluripotency gene as its central target and the receptor as a repressor.
timeline.methods: Mouse genetics with expression analysis and promoter studies

timeline.finding: GCNF was found to be required for repression of Oct4 and other pluripotency genes when embryonic stem cells differentiate in response to retinoic acid, moving the DR0 from an embryonic curiosity to a component of the exit from pluripotency.
timeline.methods: Knockout embryonic stem cells with differentiation assays and expression profiling

timeline.finding: Fine mapping of a swine quantitative trait locus for the number of vertebrae implicated NR6A1, tying the gene to somitogenesis in a second species and in a non-laboratory setting.
timeline.methods: Linkage fine mapping and candidate-gene analysis in pigs

timeline.finding: Repression at Oct4 was shown to proceed through recruitment of methyl-CpG-binding domain proteins and DNA methyltransferases, so occupancy of the DR0 initiates promoter DNA methylation rather than acting only through transient repression.
timeline.methods: Chromatin immunoprecipitation, methylation analysis, knockdown

timeline.finding: Rare heterozygous NR6A1 variants in six families were reported to cause an autosomal dominant oculo-vertebral-renal syndrome of colobomatous microphthalmia, missing vertebrae and congenital kidney abnormalities, with zebrafish knockdown phenotypes rescued by wild-type but not variant mRNA.
timeline.methods: Human genetics across families with zebrafish knockdown and rescue
timeline.open: Whether the variants act by haploinsufficiency or as dominant negatives on the homodimer.

open: The preferred upstream half-site is unsettled between the literature and the data: the receptor is described as binding a direct repeat of AGGTCA, while four independent models converge on AAGTTCAAGGTCA, so the measured upstream half-site is the AGTTCA variant and scanners built on the textbook description will score real sites lower.

Whether NR6A1 ever occupies a bare nuclear receptor half-site in vivo is unresolved: two ChIP-only grade-C models for this factor encode little more than TCAAGGTCA, which is also the NR5A element, so those peaks may reflect a different receptor or indirect binding.

The target set beyond the pluripotency network is essentially unmapped; a specific 13-mer is expected only about 50 times per strand in the genome, but no survey has established how many of those matches are occupied when the receptor is expressed.

How the human NR6A1 variants cause the oculo-vertebral-renal syndrome is open, since a dominant phenotype in a homodimeric receptor is compatible both with haploinsufficiency and with a variant subunit poisoning the dimer, and the published rescue experiments do not separate the two.
Whether the ligand-binding domain has a physiological ligand at all remains unknown, and the receptor is still treated as an orphan on the basis of absence of evidence.

families.name: THAP-type zinc finger
families.def: THAP1, THAP12 and other THAP-type zinc fingers. THAP11 is covered by the ZNF143 entry, whose site it shares.
families.short: THAP-type zinc fingers are C2CH modules whose closest known relative is the site-specific DNA-binding domain of the Drosophila P-element transposase, making this a family of domesticated transposase DNA-binding domains. The atlas files six motifs for two proteins, THAP1 and THAP12. THAP1 recognizes a bipartite site - a GCCATCTT-like half and a GGGCA half separated by a short variable spacer - which the trimmed JASPAR model reduces to GCAGGGCA. Crystallography of the fly THAP domain explains the bipartite pattern: a beta-sheet inserts into the major groove while a basic C-terminal loop reads the adjacent minor groove. THAP1 is the DYT6 dystonia gene. THAP11 is deliberately not filed here; it shares the ZNF143 SBS element and is covered by the ZNF143 entry.
families.long:
## The factors

The THAP domain was defined in 2003 as a roughly 90-residue module whose sequence resembles the site-specific DNA-binding domain of the Drosophila melanogaster P-element transposase, carrying a putative metal-coordinating signature of the form CX(2-4)CX(35-53)CX(2)H [PMID:12575992,15863623]. A survey across model animals catalogued about 100 distinct THAP proteins, including the human proapoptotic factors THAP1 and DAP4/THAP0, the transcriptional repressor THAP7, and the Caenorhabditis elegans chromatin protein HIM-17 and cell-cycle regulators LIN-36 and LIN-15B [PMID:15863623]. The domain is therefore one of the clearest cases of molecular domestication: a transposase recognition module retained by the host after the mobile element that carried it was lost, a route to new transcription factors seen repeatedly in animal genomes [PMID:19132291,28844698].

The atlas family itself is small. Six motifs cover two named proteins, THAP1 and THAP12, plus two unnamed Vierstra archetypes labelled only THAP. THAP1 is a ubiquitously expressed nuclear protein encoded at 8p11.21. THAP12 is the protein also known as DAP4 or PRKRIR. THAP11, better known as Ronin, is excluded by design: it binds the same element as ZNF143 and is described in the ZNF143 entry, so a THAP11-labelled motif should be read there, not here.

## The motif

In vitro binding-site selection with the THAP domain of human THAP1 yielded an 11-nucleotide consensus, and single-nucleotide substitutions within it abolished binding; chelating zinc with 1,10-o-phenanthroline also abolished binding, confirming the domain is a zinc-dependent member of the zinc-finger superfamily [PMID:15863623]. The structural basis came from a crystal structure of the fly P-element transposase THAP domain bound to a natural ten-base-pair site [PMID:20010837]. Unlike a C2H2 finger, the THAP domain docks a conserved beta-sheet into the major groove and a basic C-terminal loop into the adjacent minor groove, and sequence analysis of natural and selected sites suggested a shared bipartite TXXGGGX(A/T) consensus for the fly domain and for human THAP1 and THAP9 [PMID:20010837].

The atlas models match that description at two different trimmings. The long models keep both halves: HOCOMOCO THAP1.H14CORE.0.P.B reads gccGCCATcTTbgntvcGGGCa over 22 positions, and CIS-BP M08020 gives CGCCATcTTggnTrhGGGCAg at 21.5 bits. The short models keep only the downstream half: JASPAR MA0597.3 and Vierstra archetype AC0141 are both GCAGGGCA, and a second Vierstra archetype AC0478 is the still shorter tnhGGGCA. Family cohesion is moderate at 0.58, driven entirely by this difference in trimming rather than by disagreement about the site. The remaining motif, CIS-BP M02538 for THAP12, carries 3.8 bits of information and is not usable. Label agreement across databases is very low, between 0 and 0.1, which is what an eight-base-pair GC-containing model will always produce: its nearest neighbours in other databases belong to other families.

## Where it acts

THAP1 occupancy is concentrated at promoters and CpG islands rather than distal enhancers. The best-characterised direct target is TOR1A, the DYT1 dystonia gene, whose promoter THAP1 binds and represses [PMID:20976771]. Because the site includes a GGGCA half that overlaps GC-box-like sequence, matches cluster in the same promoter-proximal, CpG-rich compartment occupied by SP/KLF factors, and work in rats and patient-derived neurons indicates THAP1 acts on that same regulatory space [PMID:35015830]. Note the separation of labour within the wider domain family: the hyperconserved promoter element bound by Ronin/THAP11 together with HCF-1 at genes controlling embryonic stem cell growth [PMID:20581084] is the ZNF143 SBS, not the THAP1 site.

## Biology and disease

Heterozygous THAP1 mutations cause DYT6, an autosomal dominant primary torsion dystonia with prominent cranio-cervical and laryngeal involvement [PMID:19182804]. Many of the pathogenic substitutions fall inside the THAP domain and reduce DNA binding directly [PMID:19182804], which is why this family is one of the few where a motif model maps onto a molecular disease mechanism. THAP1 represses TOR1A, linking the DYT6 and DYT1 loci in one pathway [PMID:20976771]. DYT6-mutant THAP1 behaves as a cell-type-dependent regulator of the SP1 family [PMID:35015830], and mouse Thap1 loss produces transcriptional deficits that converge on pathways shared with other dystonic syndromes [PMID:30590536]. Elsewhere in the domain family, Ronin/THAP11 is essential for mouse embryogenesis and for embryonic stem cell pluripotency [PMID:18585351].

## Reading a hit

Use the long model if you can. GCAGGGCA is eight base pairs of partly GC-rich sequence and will match tens of thousands of times in a 3.1 Gb genome, most of them meaningless; the 22-base-pair bipartite HOCOMOCO model is far more specific because it requires both halves and the spacer. A hit identifies a THAP-domain site, not a protein: the bipartite consensus is shared by THAP1, THAP9 and the fly P-element transposase itself [PMID:20010837]. Condition on a promoter or CpG island context and on THAP1 expression. If your hit instead resembles the ACTACA-containing SBS element, you are looking at THAP11 and should read the ZNF143 entry. Ignore the THAP12 model entirely.
families.caveats: The family carries only six motifs for two proteins, and one of them, CIS-BP M02538 for THAP12, has 3.8 bits and no usable information. The HOCOMOCO THAP1 model is ChIP-only (evidence code P, grade B), so within the atlas there is no in vitro support for it, although independent binding-site selection and a crystal structure of the homologous fly domain support the same bipartite site in the literature. Short GCAGGGCA-style matches are common and largely uninformative on their own. Nothing in the motif separates THAP1 from THAP9 or from the ancestral P-element transposase domain. THAP11 is intentionally absent from this family: its site is the ZNF143 SBS and belongs to that entry.

timeline.finding: Sequence analysis defined the THAP domain as an N-terminal C2CH module resembling the site-specific DNA-binding domain of the Drosophila P-element transposase, proposing it as a DNA-binding domain shared between cellular proteins and a mobile element.
timeline.methods: Comparative sequence analysis
timeline.open: Whether the cellular THAP domain binds DNA at all, and with what specificity, had not been tested.

timeline.finding: The THAP domain of human THAP1 was shown to be a zinc-dependent, sequence-specific DNA-binding domain: in vitro binding-site selection gave an 11-nucleotide consensus in which single substitutions abolished binding, and about 100 THAP proteins were catalogued across model animals.
timeline.methods: In vitro binding-site selection, site-directed mutagenesis, zinc chelation, sequence survey
timeline.open: How a single C2CH module of about 90 residues achieves base-specific recognition.

timeline.finding: A THAP1 mutation segregating in three Amish-Mennonite families, and a second mutation in a German family, identified THAP1 as the DYT6 primary torsion dystonia gene; the missense change impaired DNA binding.
timeline.methods: Family genetics and sequencing, DNA-binding assay
timeline.open: Which THAP1 target genes mediate the dystonia.

timeline.finding: The crystal structure of the Drosophila P-element transposase THAP domain on a natural 10 bp site showed a beta-sheet docked in the major groove and a basic C-terminal loop in the adjacent minor groove, and natural and selected sites gave a shared bipartite TXXGGGX(A/T) consensus for the fly domain, THAP1 and THAP9.
timeline.methods: X-ray crystallography, mutagenesis, DNA-binding assays

timeline.finding: THAP1 was shown to bind the core promoter of TOR1A, the DYT1 dystonia gene, and repress it, with DYT6-mutant THAP1 repressing less, placing two dystonia genes in one pathway.
timeline.methods: Promoter characterization, DNA-binding and reporter assays
timeline.open: Whether TOR1A repression accounts for DYT6 dystonia in vivo.

timeline.finding: Conditional deletion of Thap1 in the mouse CNS delayed myelination through a cell-autonomous requirement in the oligodendrocyte lineage, and loss of THAP1 reduced the DNA occupancy of YY1 at oligodendrocyte maturation genes, identifying YY1 as a working partner of THAP1.
timeline.methods: Conditional mouse knockout, oligodendrocyte progenitor assays, chromatin occupancy measurements
timeline.open: Whether THAP1 and YY1 bind adjacent sites in a composite element or separate elements within the same promoters.

timeline.finding: Germline Thap1 deletion in mice was embryonic lethal, heterozygotes had no discernible phenotype because the intact allele was upregulated, and nestin-conditional deletion caused locomotor deficits with expression changes converging on pathways shared with other dystonias.
timeline.methods: Mouse germline and conditional knockouts, transcriptomics, behavioral testing

timeline.finding: Across patient cortex, patient iPSC-derived midbrain dopaminergic neurons, a heterozygous knockout rat and knockout cell lines, THAP1 directly targeted only a minority of the genes dysregulated by its mutation; most changes ran through SP1 and SP4 in a cell-type-dependent way, revising the picture of THAP1 as a direct regulator of a few promoters such as TOR1A.
timeline.methods: Epigenomic and transcriptomic profiling across human and rat model systems, behavior and electrophysiology
timeline.open: How much of the disease depends on THAP1 binding its own site rather than on the SP1-family cascade.

open: The upstream GCCATCTT block of the long ChIP-derived THAP1 models (HOCOMOCO and CIS-BP) matches the YY1 core consensus GCCATnTT, and THAP1 is known to work with YY1; the in vitro selection and structural data define only the GGGCA-containing half, so whether the 22-position model is one THAP1 site or a THAP1-YY1 composite has not been tested.

How much of THAP1's transcriptional effect requires its own DNA site is disputed: TOR1A repression was explained by direct promoter binding, whereas a multi-system study found that THAP1 directly binds only a minority of the genes its mutation dysregulates and acts mostly through SP1 and SP4.

Why heterozygous THAP1 loss causes dystonia in humans but no discernible phenotype in mice is unresolved; upregulation of the intact mouse allele is one explanation, and it is not known whether human THAP1 is buffered in the same way.
Whether THAP12 (DAP4) binds DNA sequence-specifically at all is unknown: its only model carries 3.8 bits, and no in vitro selection or structure exists for it.

families.name: ZNF263
families.def: Long GA-rich/GGAGGA repeat motif. ZNF263.
families.short: ZNF263 is a nine-finger C2H2 zinc-finger protein that also carries a KRAB repression domain and a SCAN oligomerization domain. Its binding site is unusually long: genome-wide mapping in K562 cells recovered a roughly 24-nucleotide GA-rich element built from tandem GGAGGA-like units, which differs in several positions from what the zinc-finger recognition code predicted for this protein. Unlike most KRAB zinc-finger proteins it does not sit mainly on transposable elements, and many of its thousands of target sites lie inside transcribed regions rather than at promoters; knockdown both raises and lowers target genes. The GA-rich character makes this motif easy to confuse with purine-rich sites read by ETS and SP1-like factors on the opposite strand.
families.long:
## The factors

ZNF263 is the only member of this family. It combines three modules found in the KRAB zinc-finger protein superfamily: nine tandem C2H2 fingers, a KRAB domain that recruits TRIM28/KAP1 and associated silencing machinery [PMID:28765213], and a SCAN domain, a protein-protein interaction module that mediates selective homo- and hetero-oligomerization among SCAN-domain zinc fingers [PMID:28740726]. Because of the KRAB domain ZNF263 was expected to be a repressor, but knockdown experiments changed expression of target genes in both directions, so it is better described as a context-dependent regulator [PMID:19887448]. It is broadly expressed. Its nine fingers are the reason the recognized element is so long, and it is one of the relatively few C2H2 proteins for which the whole array appears to be used for base reading rather than for anchoring or for protein contacts.

## The motif

The element is long and internally repetitive. ChIP-seq in K562 cells recovered more than 5000 binding sites and a 24-nucleotide consensus assembled from tandem GA-rich units [PMID:19887448], written here as GGAGGAGGAGGAGGA and equivalently as CTCCTCCTCCTCCTCC on the complementary strand. Notably, the observed motif differed at several positions from the site predicted for ZNF263 by the zinc-finger recognition code, which was one of the early demonstrations that prediction from finger sequence is not a substitute for measurement [PMID:19887448]. The matrices in this family capture different amounts of the repeat: the ChIP-derived HOCOMOCO matrix spans 20 base pairs (GGGAGGAGGGVGAGGAGGAG), while JASPAR MA0528.3, the CIS-BP matrix and the two Vierstra archetypes cover only seven or eight (GGGAGGA, CTCCTCCC, GTGCTCCC). The short versions are not different motifs; they are windows on the same repeat, and because the repeat is periodic a short matrix will match at many registers within one site, so one genomic element can generate several overlapping matches. There is no half-site and no spacing rule, and no paralogue to confuse ZNF263 with.

What distinguishes this from other purine-rich motifs is length and periodicity. ETS-class motifs are built on a GGA(A/T) core needing the flanking ACCGGAAGT-type context and are much shorter; SPI1/PU.1 reads a purine-rich AGAGGAAGTG with a defined 3' half; ZNF281/ZNF148 and ZBTB7 read C-rich CCCCACCC-type words rather than GA-rich ones; VEZF1 reads CT/GC-rich vascular promoter sites. A genuine ZNF263 element is a long, uninterrupted GGAGGA-type repeat rather than a single core with flanks, so a short GGGAGGA match inside a mixed-sequence promoter more likely belongs to one of the shorter families, while a repeat of 20 base pairs or more is the ZNF263 signature.

## Where it acts

ZNF263 sites are not concentrated at transcription start sites in the way most promoter motifs are. A striking fraction of the ChIP-seq peaks fall within the transcribed region of the target gene, including introns and exons, which is atypical both for a KRAB zinc-finger protein and for a promoter factor [PMID:19887448]. Many targets are expressed at high levels despite the KRAB domain [PMID:19887448]. Reported biology places sites at genes of heparan sulfate and heparin biosynthesis, where ZNF263 regulates the pathway [PMID:32277030], and at SIX3 in glioblastoma, where an EGFR-ZNF263 axis silences the gene [PMID:32051553]. GA-rich and CT-rich simple repeats of this kind are also enriched in short tandem repeat-based silencer elements [PMID:36929452], so the sequence class has regulatory functions that are not necessarily ZNF263-dependent. The motif is not a CpG-island signature and has no named composite element.

## Biology and disease

The functional literature is modest, and it is better to say so than to pad it. ZNF263 has been reported as a transcriptional regulator of heparin and heparan sulfate biosynthesis [PMID:32277030], as the effector of an EGFR-driven axis that epigenetically silences SIX3 in glioblastoma [PMID:32051553], and as a regulator of adipocyte gene expression in cattle. There is no described knockout phenotype in a mammalian model, no Mendelian disease, and no recurrent somatic driver mutation. Broader surveys of human KRAB zinc-finger proteins place ZNF263 among the members whose targets are not dominated by transposable elements, which distinguishes it from the large group of primate-specific KRAB proteins that control endogenous retroviruses. The motif is considerably better characterized than the biology.

## Reading a hit

Ask how long the match is. A 20-base-pair or longer GA repeat is good evidence for the ZNF263 element; a seven- or eight-base match is weak, because the short matrices in this family are windows on a repeat and because several other families read short purine-rich cores. Expect multiple overlapping hits within one real element and do not count them as independent observations. The primary matrices are ChIP-derived; the single HOCOMOCO matrix carrying in vitro support is the short eight-base version, so the long consensus rests on genome-wide occupancy rather than on purified binding, and indirect binding cannot be excluded for individual peaks. A hit inside a gene body is not a reason to discount it here, since that is where much of the reported occupancy lies. Simple repeats are also prone to mapping and assembly artefacts, so confirm that a hit lies in uniquely mappable sequence before building on it.
families.caveats: Two problems. First, length: the long GA repeat is distinctive, but the short seven- and eight-base matrices in this family match promiscuously and overlap ETS, PU.1 and other purine-rich families on one strand and CT-rich families on the other. Only a match of about 20 base pairs or more should be attributed to ZNF263. Second, evidence: the long consensus comes from ChIP-seq in a single cell line, and the ChIP-derived matrix differs from the sequence predicted by the zinc-finger recognition code, so individual peaks could reflect indirect binding or the intrinsic properties of simple repeats. Because the element is periodic, one real site produces several overlapping matches, which inflates naive hit counts.

timeline.finding: Genome-wide ChIP-seq in K562 cells finds more than 5000 ZNF263 sites and a 24-nucleotide GA-rich consensus that differs at several positions from the site predicted by the zinc-finger recognition code; many sites lie in transcribed regions, and siRNA knockdown changes target expression in both directions.

timeline.open: Whether ZNF263 binds the long repeat directly, and with which of its nine fingers, was not tested in vitro.

timeline.finding: A ZNF263 motif is found in the promoters of heparin/heparan sulfate biosynthesis genes; CRISPR targeting or knockdown of ZNF263 sharply raises expression of the 3-O-sulfotransferases HS3ST1 and HS3ST3A1, increasing antithrombin binding of the resulting heparan sulfate.
timeline.methods: Promoter motif analysis, CRISPR knockout, siRNA knockdown, glycan and binding assays

timeline.finding: In glioblastoma, EGFR-ERK signaling stabilizes ZNF263, which binds the SIX3 core promoter and recruits a KAP1-containing corepressor complex with DNA methyltransferases to silence the gene.
timeline.methods: ChIP, co-immunoprecipitation, knockdown and overexpression, tumor tissue analysis
timeline.open: A single-locus study; whether KAP1 recruitment explains ZNF263 repression genome-wide was not tested.

timeline.finding: A STARR-seq-based screen for silencers in a mouse T-cell line finds silencers enriched for ZNF263 motifs and short tandem repeats that are potential KZFP binding sites, including for ZNF263.
timeline.methods: High-throughput silencer reporter assay, motif enrichment, CRISPR deletions
timeline.open: Motif enrichment does not show that ZNF263 itself occupies or represses through these repeats.

timeline.finding: A survey of ChIP-exo profiles for human KRAB zinc-finger proteins lists ZNF263 among the KZFPs whose binding is enriched over SVA retrotransposons.
timeline.methods: ChIP-exo/ChIP-seq survey of KZFPs, repeat-family enrichment

open: Whether ZNF263 reads the full 20-24-base-pair GA repeat directly is not established: the long consensus rests on ChIP-seq, while the only in vitro-supported matrix in this family (HOCOMOCO, methyl-HT-SELEX) is an eight-base GGGAGGA core, so how many of the nine fingers contact DNA is unknown.

Whether ZNF263 acts mainly as a KRAB-dependent repressor is unresolved: knockdown in K562 changed targets in both directions, the heparan sulfate and SIX3 studies describe repression, and no study has tested whether the gene-body sites where much of its occupancy lies repress transcription or simply mark highly transcribed genes.

How much of ZNF263 occupancy lies in transposable elements has not been quantified: the first ChIP-seq study emphasized gene bodies, but a 2023 survey of KZFP binding lists ZNF263 among those whose signal is enriched over SVA retrotransposons.

families.name: ZNF281 / ZNF148 (ZBP-89)
families.def: GC-rich CCCCACCCC sites. ZNF281, ZNF148, ZNF219.
aka: TFClass: more than 3 adjacent zinc finger factors
families.short: ZNF148 (better known as ZBP-89) and ZNF281 (ZBP-99) are broadly expressed four-fingered C2H2 proteins that bind GC- and GA-rich promoter elements, most often written GGGGGAGGGG or, on the opposite strand, CCCCTCCCCC; longer models add a CCCCACCCC module. Both were cloned as factors that occupy GC-rich elements already known to bind Sp1, and that competition is the point: the same element is a legitimate site for several families. ZNF219 is grouped with them on domain similarity but has no matrix here. The two proteins are not distinguishable from each other by sequence, and only weakly distinguishable from MAZ, PATZ1 and VEZF1. Human ZNF148 truncating variants cause a recognized developmental syndrome.
families.long:
## The factors

ZNF148 was cloned as ZBP-89, an 89-kDa zinc-finger protein, by screening a rat expression library with a multimer of the GC-rich element GGGGCGGGGTGGGGGG that confers epidermal growth factor responsiveness on the human gastrin promoter - an element already known to bind Sp1. The protein was 89% identical to a previously described 49-kDa human factor, ht-beta, and acts as a repressor of that promoter (Merchant et al. 1996) [PMID:8943318]. ZNF281 was then cloned as ZBP-99, a second member of the same family, also a GC-box binder and also a repressor, this time characterized on the ornithine decarboxylase promoter; its four Kruppel-type zinc fingers share 91% similarity and 79% identity with those of ZBP-89 (Law et al. 1999) [PMID:10448078]. Four fingers predicts a footprint of roughly 12 bp, not the long arrays of CTCF-like proteins. ZNF219 is placed here by domain similarity and assembles with Sox9 to drive chondrocyte differentiation (Takigawa et al. 2010) [PMID:20940257], but contributes no matrix, so everything said about the motif comes from ZNF148 and ZNF281. Mouse orthologs are Zfp148 and Zfp281. Both are broadly expressed and both act predominantly as repressors, frequently at elements that Sp1 also occupies.

## The motif

The two JASPAR profiles are one sequence in opposite orientations: ZNF281 (MA1630.3) is GGGGGAGGGG, ZNF148 (MA1653.2) is CCCCTCCCCC, as is CIS-BP M08321_2.00. The HOCOMOCO models are longer and add a module: ZN281.H14CORE.0.P.B is GGGTGGGGGAGGGG and ZN148.H14CORE.0.P.B is the same 14-mer, placing a GGGTGGGG (CCCCACCCC on the other strand) immediately 5' of the GGGGGAGGGG core [PMID:37971293]. At 20.3 and 19.9 bits these are the most information-rich matrices in the family, and they are also where the CCCCACCCC form of the consensus comes from. One matrix here carries in vitro evidence - ZN281.H14CORE.1.SM.B, from HT-SELEX and methyl-HT-SELEX - and it is instructive: it is a 21-position near-uniform G-run, GGGGGGGGGGGGAGGGDGGGG [PMID:37971293]. In other words, the in vitro data for ZNF281 support "long G-rich tract" rather than a crisp, positionally defined site. Family cohesion is high at 0.90, but that is cohesion among six matrices from two gene labels and does not make the family distinctive. Label agreement runs from 0.2 to 0.4, and for the JASPAR ZNF148 profile the best-scoring neighbor anywhere in the four databases (0.95) lies outside this family, beating its best within-family match (0.88). Concretely: GGGAGGG, the MAZ site, is contained inside GGGGGAGGGG, so MAZ and ZNF281 differ only in the length of the run and its flanks; VEZF1's informative model is the same shape; and the ChIP-derived WT1 models fall in the same cluster. The only sequence-level discriminator available in this neighborhood is against the SP1/KLF GC-box - an A in the middle of the run where the GC-box has a C, GGGAGGG versus GGGCGG (Song et al. 2001) [PMID:11395515] - and even that fails when the match spans a G-rich tract long enough to accommodate both.

## Where it acts

These are promoter-proximal factors, at GC-rich elements in CpG-island promoters - gastrin, ornithine decarboxylase and similar targets - usually shared with Sp1. ZBP-89 is butyrate-inducible and binds GC-rich DNA elements in gastrointestinal epithelium (Essien et al. 2013) [PMID:23395646]. Zfp281 in mouse embryonic stem cells occupies the Nanog locus, where its function depends on recruited complexes rather than on the motif: it brings in the NuRD complex to mediate Nanog autorepression (Fidalgo et al. 2012) [PMID:22988117] and recruits Polycomb repressive complex 2 to restrict extraembryonic endoderm potential (Huang et al. 2021) [PMID:32812113]. The pattern recurs: the motif places the protein, the partner determines the output.

## Biology and disease

The role of Zfp281 in ES cells has been reported in opposite directions. Knockdown indicated that it maintains pluripotency and activates Nanog directly (Wang et al. 2008) [PMID:18757296]; a null allele then showed that ES cells are established and maintained without it but differentiate abnormally, and that it mainly represses pluripotency genes, Nanog included (Fidalgo et al. 2011) [PMID:21915945], by mediating Nanog autorepression through NuRD, which also hinders somatic cell reprogramming (Fidalgo et al. 2012) [PMID:22988117]. ZNF281 is induced by genotoxic stress and contributes to the DNA damage response by controlling expression of the homologous-recombination and non-homologous-end-joining factors XRCC2 and XRCC4 (Pieraccioli et al. 2016) [PMID:26300006], and is reported as an oncogene in colorectal and other carcinomas, in association with epithelial-mesenchymal transition. On the ZNF148 side, conditional deletion of Zfp148 in mice alters tryptophan hydroxylase I expression and impairs mucosal defense against Salmonella typhimurium (Essien et al. 2013) [PMID:23395646]. The clearest human link is Mendelian: de novo truncating variants in ZNF148 cause a syndrome of corpus callosum defects, developmental delay, short stature and dysmorphic features (Stevens et al. 2016) [PMID:27964749], since named GDACCF and delineated in a cohort of 22 patients (Szakszon et al. 2024) [PMID:37580113].

## Reading a hit

A match identifies a G-rich promoter element and nothing narrower. ZNF148 and ZNF281 share one motif, so the hit cannot choose between them; ZNF219 has no matrix at all, so a claim about ZNF219 from sequence is pure inference from domain similarity. Three of the six matrices are ChIP-only at grade B, and the one in vitro model is effectively a poly-G tract, which means the family's own evidence does not define a sharp site. Long G-runs are common in GC-rich promoters and in G-quadruplex-forming sequence, so expect chance matches. Most importantly, the neighbors: MAZ and PATZ1 sites are nested inside this consensus, VEZF1's model has the same shape, the ChIP-derived WT1 models cluster here, and the SP1/KLF GC-box is one base away. Which protein occupies a site is answered by ChIP, knockdown or expression - not by a score.
families.caveats: ZNF148 and ZNF281 share a single motif, and ZNF219 - also assigned to this family - contributes no matrix, so nothing can be said about it from sequence. Three of the six matrices rest on ChIP-seq alone at grade B, and the one HT-SELEX/methyl-SELEX model is essentially a 21-base poly-G tract, so the in vitro evidence does not define a sharp site. For the JASPAR ZNF148 profile the best-matching matrix anywhere in the four databases lies outside this family. MAZ and PATZ1 sites are nested inside this consensus, VEZF1's model has the same shape, and the SP1 GC-box is one base away. Treat a hit as G-rich promoter sequence.

timeline.finding: ZBP-89 (ZNF148) is cloned with a multimer of the gastrin EGF-response element GGGGCGGGGTGGGGGG, which also binds Sp1; it is 89% identical to human ht-beta, a factor reported to bind a GTGGG/CACCC element in T-cell receptor promoters, and represses gastrin expression.
timeline.methods: Expression-library screening with a promoter element, gel shift, co-transfection
timeline.open: Which part of the composite GC-rich element ZBP-89 reads, as opposed to Sp1, was not mapped.

timeline.finding: ZBP-99 (ZNF281) is cloned as a second family member whose four fingers are 79% identical to ZBP-89's; it binds the GC-rich gastrin and ornithine decarboxylase promoter elements and represses ODC expression.
timeline.methods: cDNA cloning, gel shift, co-transfection

timeline.finding: Knockdown experiments indicate that Zfp281 is required to maintain mouse ES-cell pluripotency; it binds 2,417 target genes and activates Nanog directly through a promoter site next to the Oct4 and Sox2 sites.
timeline.methods: Knockdown, ChIP-chip, expression microarrays, co-immunoprecipitation
timeline.open: Knockdown could not show whether Zfp281 is needed to maintain ES cells or only to regulate them, nor whether activation or repression is its main mode at Nanog.

timeline.finding: A null allele shows Zfp281 is dispensable for establishing and maintaining ES cells but required for their differentiation, and that it mainly represses pluripotency genes, Nanog included; in 2012 it was shown to mediate Nanog autorepression by recruiting NuRD and to impede reprogramming. Both results reverse the 2008 knockdown picture.
timeline.methods: Knockout ES cells, expression profiling, ChIP, protein interaction, reprogramming assays

timeline.finding: Recurrent de novo truncating ZNF148 variants, all creating stop codons in the last exon, are found in 4 of 2,172 exome trios with intellectual disability and corpus callosum defects, defining a ZNF148-associated syndrome.
timeline.methods: Trio exome sequencing
timeline.open: Whether the variants act through haploinsufficiency or a truncated protein was not determined.

timeline.finding: ZFP281 recruits PRC2 to restrict extraembryonic endoderm potential in ES cells, another case where the output depends on the recruited complex rather than on the site.
timeline.methods: ES-cell genetics, ChIP-seq, protein interaction

timeline.finding: A cohort of 22 further patients redefines GDACCF: developmental delay, growth retardation, microcephaly and dysmorphism are core, corpus callosum anomalies are less constant than first reported, variants are mostly last-exon truncations, and one patient has a whole-gene deletion.
timeline.methods: Multicenter clinical and exome/genome data

timeline.finding: HOCOMOCO v14 gives ChIP-derived ZNF281 and ZNF148 14-mers, GGGTGGGGGAGGGG, and one in vitro ZNF281 model (HT-SELEX and methyl-HT-SELEX) that is a near-uniform 21-position G-run.
timeline.methods: ChIP-seq, HT-SELEX and methyl-HT-SELEX motif models
timeline.open: Whether the CACCC-type module in the ChIP models is read by these proteins was not addressed.

open: Whether Zfp281 is required for ES-cell pluripotency, and in which direction it regulates Nanog, is contested: knockdown data indicated that it maintains pluripotency and activates Nanog directly, whereas a null allele showed ES cells self-renew without it, Nanog rises when it is lost, and it mediates Nanog autorepression through NuRD.

Whether ZNF281 and ZNF148 read a defined site or long G-tracts in general is unresolved: the ChIP-derived 14-mers carry a GGGTGGGG (CACCC-type) module 5' of the core, in line with the GTGGG/CACCC element reported for the human ZBP-89 homolog, whereas the one in vitro model is a near-uniform G-run.

How ZNF148 variants cause GDACCF is unsettled: most are nonsense or frameshift changes in the last exon, which would be expected to escape nonsense-mediated decay and yield a truncated protein, yet one patient carries a deletion of the whole gene, which points to haploinsufficiency.

families.name: Transposase-derived / TE-binding zinc fingers
families.def: Zinc fingers whose motif is a transposable-element sequence (ZNF91/93 on SVA/L1, ZNF445, ZFP57 on imprinted TGCCGC, ZNF808, ZNF780A).
families.short: A small entry for KRAB zinc fingers whose recognized sequence is itself a piece of a transposable element. The best-documented cases are ZNF91, which binds the VNTR region of SVA elements, and ZNF93, which binds a segment of the 5' untranslated region of primate L1 retrotransposons. Both changed as those element families began to spread, and the L1PA3 subfamily escaped ZNF93 by deleting its binding site. The atlas holds six matrices for three proteins, ZNF93, ZNF808 and ZNF780A; ZNF91 itself has no motif in any of the four source databases. Because these motifs are copies of element sequence rather than compact regulatory words, a match usually tells you which repeat you are inside rather than which protein is bound there.
families.long:
## The factors

All three labelled proteins are KRAB zinc-finger proteins (KZFPs): an N-terminal KRAB domain that recruits TRIM28/KAP1 and through it SETDB1 and H3K9me3 heterochromatin, plus a tandem array of C2H2 fingers. ZNF93 (19p12, formerly ZNF505) is primate-restricted and represses L1 elements roughly 12 to 20 million years old (Forey et al. 2025) [PMID:40828019]. ZNF808 (19q13.41) is primate-specific and silences a set of primate-specific transposable elements during pancreas development (De Franco et al. 2023) [PMID:37973953]. ZNF780A has almost no functional literature; it appears here because its ChIP-derived motif clusters with the others, and the only concrete report about it is as the partner of a RUNX1::ZNF780A fusion in one case of T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukaemia (Panagopoulos et al. 2023) [PMID:36581344]. ZNF91, the fourth gene named in this family's definition, has no motif in JASPAR, HOCOMOCO, CIS-BP or the Vierstra archetypes, so it cannot be scanned for at all; it is covered here because its biology defines the category. ZFP57 and the bulk of the KZFP family have their own entries.

## The motif

There is no family consensus: three proteins, three unrelated sequences, cohesion 0.60. ZNF93 is given as GGCAGCGGCAGCGG in JASPAR (MA1721.2) and as GCAGCAGSGNCTGCTGCTDCC in CIS-BP, a tandem GCAGC/CTGCT repeat rather than a compact site, which is what a long finger array tiling a repeated element looks like. ZNF780A is CWGACBGCCTGCC in CIS-BP and in the matching Vierstra archetype AC0167, but GGCAGGCAGTTAGGGAAG in HOCOMOCO. ZNF808 is GGTCTVTAAAGDGCCTGBT. Median consensus length is 16 bp and median information content 15 bits. More important, the primary literature does not describe these proteins with short consensus words at all: ZNF91 is mapped to the VNTR region of SVA elements (Haring et al. 2021) [PMID:33722937] and ZNF93 to a segment of the L1 5' untranslated region whose deletion in the L1PA3 subfamily released those elements from repression (Jacobs et al. 2014) [PMID:25274305]. The matrices here are partial models of long element segments, so scanning for them behaves much like scanning for the element.

## Where it acts

Copies of the target element, usually in heterochromatin. SVA is one of three still-mobile human element families, with roughly 2,800 insertions in the reference genome and about half of those human-specific (Haring et al. 2021) [PMID:33722937]; recognizable L1PA 5' untranslated regions number in the thousands. Occupancy is concentrated in early embryonic and pluripotent contexts, where TRIM28 and SETDB1 deposit H3K9me3. Many KZFP-bound element copies remain in closed chromatin in differentiated cells, which is why sites of this kind are systematically missed by accessibility-based assays (Razavi et al. 2026) [PMID:42557260]. Where repression is relieved, the same elements can act as cis-regulatory modules for neighbouring genes, the route by which element sequence becomes host regulatory DNA (Imbeault et al. 2017; Davis et al. 2026) [PMID:28273063,41720928].

## Biology and disease

Deleting ZNF91 in human embryonic stem cells activates SVA transcription, shifts evolutionarily young SVAs toward activating chromatin marks, mildly upregulates nearby genes, and triggers coordinated upregulation of KZFP genes across their clusters. Deleting ZNF611, another strong SVA binder, does not activate SVAs, so binding and functional repression are not the same thing (Haring et al. 2021) [PMID:33722937]. Biallelic loss of ZNF808 causes pancreatic agenesis: the primate-specific elements it normally silences gain regulatory activity during pancreas specification and liver-identity genes are induced instead (De Franco et al. 2023) [PMID:37973953]. ZNF93 has been co-opted in cancer, where it limits the mutagenic enzyme APOBEC3B; ZNF93 depletion impairs DNA synthesis, activates replication and damage checkpoints, and provokes proinflammatory phenotypes (Forey et al. 2025) [PMID:40828019]. The general pattern, of an arms race followed by domestication, is reviewed by Bruno et al. 2019 and Davis et al. 2026 [PMID:31518518,41720928], and the correlation between retroelement load and zinc-finger gene number across vertebrates is quantified by Thomas and Schneider 2011 [PMID:21784874].

## Reading a hit

Check the repeat annotation before interpreting anything. A ZNF93 match inside an L1PA 5' untranslated region mainly tells you the approximate age of that L1 copy; whether ZNF93 is bound there in your cell type is a separate question these matrices cannot answer. Occurrence counts scale with element copy number, so genome-wide enrichment of one of these motifs is usually a statement about repeat content rather than about regulation. The evidence base is thin: the family contributes one HOCOMOCO model, ChIP-only (evidence code P) and graded C, and no member has an HT-SELEX or methyl-SELEX model in HOCOMOCO. ZNF91's absence from all four databases is a hard limitation. And because ZNF93's matrix is essentially a GCAGC repeat, it will also score well on unrelated GCAGC- and CTGCT-rich sequence, including trinucleotide-repeat tracts.
families.caveats: These motifs are transposable-element sequence, so scanning for them is close to scanning for the element: check repeat annotation first, and expect occurrence counts to track element copy number rather than regulatory activity. The family contributes a single HOCOMOCO model, ChIP-only and graded C, and no member has in vitro support there. ZNF91, the best-characterized member of this category, has no matrix in any source database and cannot be scanned. The literature describes the ZNF91 and ZNF93 sites as long element segments, not short consensus words, so these matrices are approximations. Binding also does not imply repression: ZNF611 binds SVAs without silencing them.

timeline.finding: Across vertebrate genomes the number of LTR retroelements was found to correlate specifically with the number of tandem zinc-finger genes, and on primate branches the appearance of new endogenous retrovirus families predicted new KRAB zinc-finger duplicates, giving the first genome-scale evidence for a host-element coevolutionary model.
timeline.methods: comparative genomics across vertebrates, dN/dS analysis of duplicate pairs
timeline.open: No individual human zinc finger had been shown to repress a currently active element family.

timeline.finding: ZNF91 was shown to have acquired structural changes 8 to 12 million years ago that let it repress SVA elements, and ZNF93 to have repressed the primate L1 lineage until about 12.5 million years ago, when the L1PA3 subfamily escaped by deleting the ZNF93-binding site: the first demonstrated cycle of restriction and escape in the human lineage.
timeline.methods: comparative genomics, ancestral reconstruction, reporter and repression assays in cells
timeline.open: Whether the bound sequences could be described as compact motifs, rather than as element segments, was not addressed.

timeline.finding: Genome-wide mapping of KZFP binding found that most of their transposable-element targets have lost all transposition potential, so for most of the family the arms race is over and the conserved element fragments now serve as regulatory platforms.
timeline.methods: ChIP-exo in human cells, phylogenetics

timeline.finding: CRISPR deletion of ZNF91 in human embryonic stem cells activated SVA transcription and shifted young SVAs toward activating marks, while deletion of ZNF611, an equally strong SVA binder, did not, separating binding from functional repression.
timeline.methods: ChIP-seq, CRISPR-Cas9 deletion in human embryonic stem cells, epigenetic and transcriptional profiling
timeline.open: What distinguishes a binding event that silences an element from one that does not remains unexplained.

timeline.finding: Homozygous loss-of-function variants in the primate-specific ZNF808 were identified as a cause of pancreatic agenesis, with the primate-specific elements it silences gaining regulatory activity and inducing liver-identity genes, the first human developmental disease traced to failure of transposable-element silencing by a KZFP.
timeline.methods: human genetics, directed differentiation of stem cells, chromatin and expression profiling

timeline.finding: ZNF93 was shown to also limit the mutagenic enzyme APOBEC3B, with its depletion impairing DNA synthesis and activating damage checkpoints and its overexpression conferring resistance to genotoxic stress, an example of an element-restricting KZFP being co-opted by tumor cells.
timeline.methods: depletion and overexpression in cancer cell lines, expression correlation across tumor types
timeline.open: Whether this control of APOBEC3B is direct or a downstream consequence of L1 derepression was not resolved.

open: ZNF91, the best-characterized member of this category, has no matrix in any source database and its site is described as the SVA VNTR rather than as a short word, so whether its specificity can be represented by a position-weight matrix at all is unresolved.
Why ZNF91 deletion activates SVAs while deletion of ZNF611, an equally strong SVA binder, does not is unexplained, leaving no general rule for predicting which KZFP-element contacts are repressive.
The two ZNF780A models disagree outright, HOCOMOCO giving GGCAGGCAGTTAGGGAAG and CIS-BP CWGACBGCCTGCC, and with no functional study of the protein there is nothing to adjudicate between them.
It is unknown whether ZNF93's control of APOBEC3B is exerted directly at an element-derived site or indirectly through the L1 elements it represses.

families.name: AHR / AHRR
families.def: Xenobiotic response element TNGCGTG. AHR, AHRR (with ARNT).
families.short: The xenobiotic response element is the site bound by the aryl hydrocarbon receptor, AHR, paired with ARNT. Both are bHLH-PAS proteins. AHR sits in the cytoplasm in a complex with HSP90 and XAP2 until it binds a ligand: dioxins and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, or endogenous tryptophan metabolites such as kynurenine. It then enters the nucleus, exchanges its chaperones for ARNT, and binds an asymmetric half-site pair in which AHR reads the 5' TNGC and ARNT reads the 3' GTG, giving the core TNGCGTG. The paralogue AHRR is induced by AHR and represses it by competing for ARNT and for the same element. Occupied sites drive the cytochrome P450 genes CYP1A1, CYP1A2 and CYP1B1, so this motif is the entry point of the classical xenobiotic-metabolism response.
families.long:
## The factors

AHR (aryl hydrocarbon receptor, also called the dioxin receptor) and AHRR (AHR repressor) are bHLH-PAS proteins: a basic helix-loop-helix DNA-binding domain followed by PAS-A and PAS-B. Unliganded AHR is cytoplasmic in a complex with HSP90, p23 and XAP2/AIP1, whose architecture has been resolved by cryo-EM with agonist bound (Gruszczyk et al. 2022) [PMID:36385050]. Ligand binding in the PAS-B pocket triggers nuclear translocation and heterodimerization with ARNT, the same beta subunit used by HIF, SIM1/2 and the NPAS factors; ARNT is the shared partner of the whole class, and its loss in mice is embryonic lethal (Maltepe et al. 1997) [PMID:9121557]. AHRR is an AHR-induced gene lacking a functional ligand pocket; it represses by competing with AHR for ARNT and for the response element, a negative-feedback circuit that helps set tissue-specific sensitivity to pollutants (Mimura et al. 1999) [PMID:9887096]. AHR is widely expressed, with highest levels in liver, lung, placenta and immune cells. This atlas family is small: five motifs, one from JASPAR, two from HOCOMOCO and two Vierstra archetypes, with no CIS-BP entry.

## The motif

The element has several names: xenobiotic response element (XRE), dioxin response element (DRE) and AH response element (AHRE). Its core was defined as 5'-TA/TGCGTG-3' in the dioxin-responsive enhancers of the CYP1A1 locus, with flanking bases needed for full enhancer function (Denison et al. 1988) [PMID:2846558]; it is conventionally written TNGCGTG. The two half-sites are not equivalent. Selection experiments assign high-affinity 5' half-sites T(C/T)GC to AHR and GT(G/A)C to SIM, and the 3' half-site GTG to ARNT, so ARNT contributes the same GTG in every complex and the partner supplies the discriminating 5' half (Swanson et al. 1995) [PMID:7592839]. Within that scheme the invariant string is GCGTG, and a single position, the base immediately 5' of CGTG, separates the XRE (G) from the hypoxia response element (A) and from the palindromic E-box CACGTG that ARNT homodimers prefer. The crystal structure of the AHR-ARNT heterodimer on the DRE shows ARNT curling around AHR in an intertwined, asymmetric architecture; specificity is set locally by the DNA-contacting residues that discriminate the DRE from the HRE and globally by the dimerization and interdomain interfaces (Seok et al. 2017) [PMID:28396409]. Systematic measurements across the family report 12-15 bp footprints in which flanking preferences, not the core, separate members that share a core (Bersten et al. 2026) [PMID:41495897]. Two presentation issues matter when reading the collected models. The pooled consensus for this family is CACGCaA, which is the reverse complement of TTGCGTG: the Vierstra archetypes here are written on the minus strand, and CACGCAA is not a separate motif. And de novo discovery in AHR ChIP-seq recovers a symmetrical variant, GTGCGTG (Lo and Matthews 2012) [PMID:22903824]. AHR and AHRR are not distinguishable: their HOCOMOCO models are TGCGTGC and TGCGTGCcA. The long archetype AC0516:AHR:bHLH (about 20 bits) is an outlier whose best within-family similarity is only 0.66, so it encodes flanking or composite information absent from the other four.

## Where it acts

In TCDD-treated MCF-7 cells, ChIP-seq found 2,594 AHR-bound, 1,352 ARNT-bound and 882 co-bound regions; about 60% of the co-bound regions contained at least one core GCGTG. Peak density was highest within 1 kb of transcription start sites, though some sites lay up to 100 kb away, and the same regions were enriched for FOXA1 and SP1 motifs, placing AHR in cell-type-specific enhancer contexts (Lo and Matthews 2012) [PMID:22903824]. Canonical targets are CYP1A1, CYP1A2, CYP1B1, NQO1, ALDH3A1, TIPARP and AHRR itself; the CYP1A1 enhancer carries several XREs. Occupancy is ligand-dependent, so in untreated cells most matches are unbound. The core contains a CpG and is methylation-sensitive; relatedly, a CpG in AHRR (cg05575921) is the strongest and most reproducible blood DNA-methylation marker of cigarette smoking (Joehanes et al. 2016) [PMID:27651444].

## Biology and disease

AHR mediates the toxicity of dioxins and related planar aromatic pollutants. Ahr-null mice have reduced liver size, hepatic fibrosis and immune defects, and are resistant to TCDD (Fernandez-Salguero et al. 1995) [PMID:7732381]. It also responds to endogenous and diet-derived tryptophan metabolites: kynurenine produced by TDO in gliomas activates AHR and promotes tumor growth and immune suppression, making AHR an immuno-oncology target (Opitz et al. 2011) [PMID:21976023]. AHR contributes to barrier immunity and intestinal lymphocyte programs, and AHRR behaves as a candidate tumor suppressor in several epithelial cancers.

## Reading a hit

TNGCGTG carries roughly six informative base pairs, so chance matches are frequent and a hit alone licenses no conclusion. Separating an XRE from an HRE rests on one base plus weak flanking preferences, and the two are routinely confused by scanners. A hit cannot distinguish AHR from AHRR. Provenance here is thin: both HOCOMOCO models are ChIP-only (letter P) at grades B and C, the JASPAR entry is a dimer model, and the other two are Vierstra footprint archetypes, so nothing in the collection is in vitro evidence that AHR binds this sequence. That support comes from the older selection work and the crystal structure, not from these models. Roughly 40% of AHR/ARNT co-bound regions have no core AHRE, so indirect and tethered binding is common in ChIP-derived versions. Finally, the archetype label AC0073:AHR:bHLH names the factor group whose motifs clustered together [PMID:32728250]; it is not a claim that AHR is separable from other bHLH-PAS proteins.
families.caveats: Every model in this family is ChIP-derived or footprint-derived, at grade B or C, so it evidences occupancy in cells rather than direct AHR binding; the in vitro anchor for TNGCGTG is the older selection literature and the AHR-ARNT crystal structure. About 40% of AHR/ARNT co-bound regions lack any core element, so indirect binding is well documented. AHR and AHRR share one motif and cannot be told apart. The XRE differs from the hypoxia response element at a single base 5' of CGTG, so XRE and HRE calls are easily swapped. Note also that the pooled consensus CACGCAA is simply TTGCGTG on the opposite strand, not a different site. Occupancy requires a ligand, so an unbound match in untreated cells is expected.
